notes.text: yea of Angels. Heb. 2.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Not only al reasonable creatures, but al beastes, and other thinges obey him. The sea and the windes obey him. Mat. 8.

verses.text: The birdes of the ayre, and fishes of the sea; that walke the pathes of the sea.
<na>(l)</na> O Lord our Lord, how meruelous is thy name in the whole earth!

notes.label: l
notes.text: The same end & beginning signifie, that as God was meruelous in creating man in so happie state, that if he would, he might haue auoyded both sinne & death: so he is meruelous in that he so rewardeth the blessed in the resurrection, that they can neither sinne non dye.

chapters.summary: God is magnified & praised for his meruelous worke of creatures, 5. but especially of mankind, singularly exalted by the Incarnation of Christ. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's Incarnation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for the <na>(a)</na> secrets of the sonne, the Psalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Christs coming in humilitie, and Christians afflictions, are hidden from the world, in Gods prouidence.

verses.text: I WIL <na>(b)</na> confesse to thee ô Lord with al my hart: I wil tel al thy meruelous thinges.

notes.label: b
notes.text: geue thanks.

verses.text: I wil be <na>(c)</na> glad and <na>(d)</na> reioyce in thee: I wil sing to thy name ô most High.

notes.label: c
notes.text: in mind.

notes.label: d
notes.text: and bodie.

verses.text: In <na>(e)</na> turning mine enemie backward: they shal be weakened, and perish before thy face.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God repelleth the enemie, when man is not able to resist.

verses.text: Because thou hast done <na>(f)</na> my iudgement and my cause: thou hast sitte vpon the throne which iudgest iustice.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A iust man doth his endeuour, not of him selfe, but by Gods grace ouercometh the enemie.

verses.text: Thou hast rebuked the <na>(g)</na> Gentiles, and the impious hath perished: their <na>(h)</na> name thou hast destroyed for euer, and for euer and euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Al sinners called gentils, because they were generally accounted wicked.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The vaine glorious fame of sinners partly decayeth in this world but most especially in the world to come.

verses.text: The swordes of the enemie haue fayled vnto the end: and their cities thou hast destroyed.
Their memorie hath perished wirh a sound: and our Lord abideth for euer. He hath prepared his throne in <na>(i)</na> iudgement:

notes.label: i
notes.text: Iudicial seates of men are often corrupted but Gods neuer.

verses.text: & he wil iudge the whole world in equitie, he wil iudge the people in iustice.
And our Lord is made a refuge for the poore: an helper <na>(k)</na> in opportunities, in tribulation.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God doth not presently deliuer the good from afflictions: but when it is to their spiritual profite.

verses.text: And let them hope in thee that know thy name: because thou hast not forsaken them that seeke thee ô Lord.
Sing to our Lord, which dwelleth in Sion: declare his <na>(l)</na> studies among the Gentiles:

notes.label: l
notes.text: His precepts which men ought chiefly to studie.

verses.text: Because he <na>(m)</na> requiring bloud remembred them: he hath not forgotten the crie of the poore.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God reuengeth the blood of Martyrs.

verses.text: Haue mercie on me ô Lord: See my humiliation <na>(n)</na> by my enemies.

notes.label: n
notes.text: procured by mine enemies.

verses.text: Which exaltest me from the gates of death, that I may declare al thy prayses in <na>(o)</na> the gates of the daughter of Sion.

notes.label: o
notes.text: In the publique view of the Church.

verses.text: I wil reioyce in thy saluation: the Gentiles are <na>(p)</na> fastened in the destruction, which they made. In this snare, which they hid, is their foote taken.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The wicked are intangled in the snares which they lay for others.

verses.text: Our Lord shal be knowen doing iudgements: the sinner is taken in the workes of his owne handes.
<na>(q)</na> Let sinners be turned into hel, al nations that forget God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: As the first workes of Christ in al humility and patience were strange, and hidden to the world: (v. 1.) so his last iudgement shal be in maiesty and manifest to al in exalting the blessed and suppressing the wicked.

verses.text: Because to the end there shal not be obliuion of the poore man: the patience of the poore, shal not perish in the end.
Arise Lord, let not man be strengthned: let the <na>(r)</na> Gentiles be iudged in thy sight.

notes.label: r
notes.text: By Gentiles is often vnderstood al great sinners. For the Iewes despised Gentiles: as the Romans did al Barbarous nations.

verses.text: Appoint Lord <na>(s)</na> a lawgeuer ouer them: that the Gentiles may know that they be men.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Suffer a tyrant to rule ouer them that thereby they may lerne what it is to vse others vniustly. It semeth to S. Augustine a prophecie, that such as receiue not Christ, shal beleue Antichrist.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Why Lord hast thou departed far of, despisest in opportunities, in tribulation?

notes.label: v
notes.text: In great persecution it semeth to the weake, that God differreth his assistance very long.

verses.text: Whiles the impious is proude, the poore is <na>(w)</na> set on fyre: <na>(x)</na> they are caught in the counsels which they deuise.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Extremely vexed & tormented.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The Prophet answereth to the complaint of the iust, that in deede the wicked are caught in their owne snares.

verses.text: Because the sinner is praysed in the desires of his soule: and the vniust man is blessed.
The sinner hath exasperated our Lord, according to the multitude of his wrath he shal <na>(y)</na> not seeke.

notes.label: y
notes.text: not seeke to recouer Gods fauour.

verses.text: There is no God in his sight: his waies are defiled at al time. Thy iudgementes are taken away from his face: he shal <na>(z)</na> rule ouer al his enemies

notes.label: z
notes.text: The wicked doth dominier for a time, and thinketh he shal do so stil.

verses.text: For he hath sayd in his hart: I wil not be moued from generation vnto generation, <na>(a)</na> without euil.

notes.label: a
notes.text: and neuer fal into any aduersitie but stil remaine without miserie or anie euil.

verses.text: Whose mouth is ful of cursing, and bitternesse, and guile: vnder his tongue labour and sorrow. <cr>[1]</cr>
He sitteth in waite with the rich in secrete places, to kil the innocent.
His eyes looke vpon the poore: he lyeth in wayte in secret, as a lyon in his denne.
He lyeth in wayte to take the poore man violently: violently to take the poore man whiles he draweth him. In his snare he wil humble him selfe, and shal fal when he shal haue dominion ouer the poore.
For he hath sayed in his hart; God hath forgotten, he hath turned away his face not to see for euer.
<na>(b)</na> Arise Lord God, let thy hand be axalted: forget not the poore.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The prayer of the iust in tribulation.

verses.text: Wherfore hath the impious prouoked God? for he hath said in his hart; He wil not enquire.
Thou seest, that thou considerest labour and sorrow: that thou mayest deliuer them into thy handes. To thee is the poore left: to the orphane thou wilt be an helper
Breake the arme of the sinner and malignant: his sinne shal be sought, and shal not be found.
Our Lord shal reigne for euer, and for euer and euer: ye <na>(c)</na> Gentiles shal perish from his land.

notes.label: c
notes.text: ye vilest men.

verses.text: Our Lord hath heard the desire of the poore: thy eare hath heard the <na>(d)</na> preperation of their hart,

notes.label: d
notes.text: The iust ought alwayes to be readie prepared in hart, to suffer patiently al that shal happen vnto them.

verses.text: To iudge <na>(e)</na> for the pupil and the humble, that man adde no more to magnifie him selfe vpon the earth.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As the first workes of Christ in al humility and patience were strange, and hidden to the world: (v. 1.) so his last iudgement shal be in maiesty and manifest to al in exalting the blessed and suppressing the wicked.

notes.text: S. Augustin applieth it to heretikes, perswading Catholiques to repare vnto their separate congregation, falsly calling it the montayne.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Ye my freindes say thus.

notes.label: d

verses.text: Our Lord is in his holy temple, our Lord his seat is in heaven. <cr>[1]</cr>
His eies haue respect vnto the poore: his <na>(f)</na> eieliddes examine the sonnes of men.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Though God seme to winke or sleepe, yet his prouidence stil watcheth, and obserueth al mens actions.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(g)</na> examineth the iust, and the impious: but he that <na>(h)</na> loueth iniquity, hateth his owne soule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Proueth by tribulations.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Continuance in sinne bringeth damnation to the soule.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> He shal rayne snares vpon sinners: fyre and brimstone, and blast of stormes the portion of their cuppe.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God sparing for the time at last must needes of iustice punish seuerely.

verses.text: Because our Lord is iust and hath loued iustice: his countenance hath seene equitie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: It more perteyneth to the new testament then to the old.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Carful and almost perplex cogitatiōs by reason of long persecution and mans weaknes.

notes.label: c

verses.text: How long shal mine enemies be exalted ouer me? Regard and heare me ô Lord my God.

notes.label: d

notes.text: wicked men drowned in sinne are at last so besotted in their vnderstanding, that they thinke in their hart (though they dare not vtter it) that there is no God: that is, none that hath diuine prouidence in gouerning the world, nor that wil iudge al in the end.

Their throte is an open sepulchre: with theit tongues they did deceitfully, the poyson of aspes vnder their lippes. Whose mouth is ful of cursing and bitternesse: their feete swift to sheed bloud. <na>(e)</na> Destruction and infelicitie in their waies, and the way of peace they haue not knowen: there is no feare of God before their eies. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.text: Without faith in Christ none had meritorious workes. · These three verses being not in the Hebrew, nor Greke, yet are in the English. an. 1577. and are three distinct verses in other psalmes. 5. 9. & 35.

notes.label: i
notes.text: who in dede can not hurt Gods seruants.

From them that resist <na>(l)</na> thy right hand keepe me, as the apple of the eie. Vnder the shadowe of thy winges protect me:

notes.label: l
notes.text: against thy omnipotent powre.

verses.text: from the <na>(m)</na> face of the impious, that haue afflicted me. Mine enemies haue compassed my soule,

notes.label: m
notes.text: from their cruel and furious countenance.

verses.text: they haue shut vp their <na>(n)</na> fatte; their mouth hath spoken pride.

notes.label: n
notes.text: they haue shut out al pittie or commiseration.

verses.text: Casting me forth now haue they compassed me: they haue sette their eies to bend them <na>(o)</na> vnto the earth.

notes.label: o
notes.text: They intend vtterly to destroy me euen to the ground.

verses.text: They haue taken me as a lion readie to the pray: and as a lions whelpe dwelling in hid places.
Arise Lord, <na>(p)</na> preuent him, and supplant him: deliuer my soule from the impious, <na>(q)</na> thy sword

notes.label: p
notes.text: Except God preuent, mans industry is not sufficient.

notes.label: q
notes.text: restraine their powre, which they haue by thy permission, that they may not persecute so much as they intend.

verses.text: from the enemies of thy hand. Lord from <na>(r)</na> a few out of the land diuide them, <na>(s)</na> in their life: their bellie is filled of <na>(t)</na> thy secretes. They are filled with children: and they haue leaft their remnantes to their litle ones.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This is a prophecy, that the wicked which are many, shal at the day of iudgement be separated from the elect.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Which iudgement beginneth sometimes in this life.

notes.label: t
notes.text: the pleasures of this world, which God approueth not, nor acknowledgeth amongst good thinges.

verses.text: But <na>(v)</na> I in iustice shal appeare to thy sight: I shal be <na>(w)</na> filled when thy glorie shal appeare?

notes.label: v
notes.text: the iust shal be approued.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Nothing doth satiate mans mind, but the sight of God in eternal glorie.

chapters.summary: A iust mans prayer in tribulation, 10. describing his enemies cruelty, 13. by way of imprecation foresheweth their destruction, 15. and declareth that the iust shal be satisfied in glorie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence protecting the just.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> to the seruant of our Lord Dauid, who spake to our Lord the wordes of this canticle, in the day, that our Lord deliuered him out of the hand of al his enemies, and out of the hand of <na>(c)</na> Saul, and he said: (2. Reg. 22.) <na>[1]</na> I wil <na>(d)</na> loue thee ô Lord <na>(e)</na> my strength:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though literally this Psalme perteyned to Dauid, yet in figure of Christ: and of the Church, or euerie iust soule.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Holie Ghost inspired Dauid to render these thankes for his often deliuerie from dangers.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Saul is specially named because he was his most potent worldlie enimie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: These first wordes ( as also diuers others ) are added, and many changed in this and other Psalmes by the Septuagint, who often leauing the Hebrew text render the sense, and so this agreeth in substance with the same Psalme recorded. 2. Reg. 22.

notes.label: e
notes.text: by whom I am strong.

verses.text: Our Lord is my firmament, and my refuge, and my deliuere.
My God is my helper, and I wil hope in him. My protectour and the <na>(f)</na> horne of my saluation, and my receiuer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: high & firme saluation.

verses.text: Praysing I wil inuocate our Lord: and I shal be saued from mine enemies.
The <na>(g)</na> sorrowes of <na>(h)</na> death haue compassed me: and <na>(i)</na> torrentes of iniquitie haue trubled me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: This is aptly applied to al mankind after his fal, declaring our state in sinne, and inducing to penance, in the office of Masse on Septuagesima sunday.

notes.label: h
notes.text: mortal flesh subiect to death.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Violent incursions of tentions to sinne.

verses.text: The sorrowes of <na>(k)</na> hel haue compassed me: the <na>(l)</na> snares of death haue preuented me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: exceding great afflictiōs of mind, like to torments of hel, which I also feare.

notes.label: l
notes.text: secrete tentations haue deceiued me.

verses.text: In my tribulation I haue inuocated our Lord, and haue <na>(m)</na> cried to my God: And <na>(n)</na> he hath heard my voice from his holie temple: and my crie in his sight, hath entered into his eares.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Earnest prayer is the best remedie in al tribulations.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As it is certaine that God heard Dauids prayers; so he assuredly heareth al that sincerly flee vnto him.

verses.text: The earth was shaken & trembled: the fundations of mountaines were trubled, and were moued, <na>(o)</na> because he was wrath with them.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods anger against sinne maketh high and loftie thinges to shake, euen the most obstinate presumptuous sinners.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Smoke arose in his wrath: and fire flamed vp from his face: coles were kindled from him.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Diuine wrath is like to smoke of the nosethrles, or flaming fire, and burning coles.

verses.text: He <na>(q)</na> bowed the heauens, and descended: and <na>(r)</na> darkenesse vnder his feete.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Gods punishment sometimes cometh so swiftly, as if the heauens bowed towards the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Gods furie is as a darke desolate night, or horrible mist.

verses.text: And he <na>(r)</na> ascended vpon the cherubs, and flew: he flew vpon the wings of windes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Yet whẽ sinners repēt God most speedely, as fleing with winges of mercie, comforteth & protecteth them.

verses.text: And he put darkenesse his <na>(s)</na> couert, his tabernacle is round about him: darkesome water in the cloudes of the aire.

notes.label: s
notes.text: God being in him selfe incõprehensible, is also secret in his determinations, and couert in his procedinges or actes.

verses.text: Because of the <na>(t)</na> brightnesse in his sight the cloudes passed, hayle and coles of fire.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Gods splēdor oppressing mãs sense, yet instructeth him by his meruelous vvorkes. VVhich mystically signifieth, that Christ illuminateth the vvorld by his Apostles, and other preachers denouncing his iustice, peace, and his vvil in al thinges perteyning to man.

verses.text: And our Lord thundered from heauen, and the Highest gaue his voice: haile and coles of fire.
And he shot his arrowes, and dissipated them: he multiplied lightnings, and trubled them.
And the fountaynes of waters appeared, and the fundations of the world were reueled. At thy rebuke ô Lord, at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.
He sent from on high, and tooke me: and he receiued me out of manie <na>(v)</na> waters.

notes.label: v
notes.text: from tribulations.

verses.text: He deliuered me <na>(w)</na> from my most strong enemies, and from them that hated me: because they were made strong ouer me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: From Saul, Absolō, Moabites, Ammonites, and al temporal and spiritual enemies.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> They preuented me in the day of mine affliction: and our Lord was made my protectour.

notes.text: So in the rest of this Psalme the Prophet speaketh for most part in proper termes, vvithout Metaphores or other figures. Yet in the mystical sense of Christ, and Christians.

verses.text: And he brought me out into largenesse: he saued me, because he <na>(x)</na> would me.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Of his good pleasure without my desertes.

verses.text: And our Lord wil reward me according to my iustice, and according to the purity of my handes he wil reward me.
Because I haue kept the waies of our Lord, neither haue I done impiously from my God.
Because al his iudgementes are in my sight: and his iustices I haue not repelled from me.
And I shal be immaculate <na>(y)</na> with him; and shal keepe me from mine iniquitie.

notes.label: y
notes.text: by his grace

verses.text: <na>(z)</na> And our Lord wil reward me according to my iustice: and according to the puritie of my handes in the sight of his eies.

notes.label: z
notes.text: He repeteth the 21. verse, inculcating that God wil render to euerie one as they deserue.

verses.text: With the holie thou shalt be holie, and with the innocent man thou shalt be innocent.
And with the elect thou shalt be elect: and with the peruerse thou shalt be peruerted.
Because thou wilt saue the humble people: and the eies of the proud thou wilt humble.
Because thou dost illuminate my lampe ô Lord: my God illuminate my darkenesse.
Because in thee I shal be deliuered from tentation, and in my God I shal <na>(a)</na> goe ouer the wal.

notes.label: a
notes.text: passe ouer al difficulties.

verses.text: My God his <na>(b)</na> way is vnpolluted: the wordes of our Lord are examined by fire: he is protector of al that hope in him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gods precepts.

verses.text: For <na>(c)</na> who is God but our Lord? or who is God but our God?

notes.label: c
notes.text: One only God, Creator and Sauiour of al.

verses.text: God that girded me with strength: and made my way immaculate.
That perfited my feete as it were of hartes: and setting me vpon high thinges.
That teacheth my handes to battel: and hast put mine armes, <na>(d)</na> as a bow of brasse.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Amongst other actes, Dauid killed a lion, and a beare, & Goliath. 1. Reg. 17.

verses.text: And hast geuen me the protection of thy saluation: and thy right hand hath receiued me: And thy discipline hath corrected me vnto the end: and thy discipline the same shal teach me.
Thou hast enlarged my pases vnder me: and my steppes are not weakened:
I wil pursew myne enemies, and ouertake them: and wil not returne til they faile.
I wil breake them, neither shal they be able to stand: they shal fal vnder my feete.
And thou hast girded me with strength to battel: and hast supplanted them that rise against me vnder me.
And <na>(e)</na> myne enemies thou hast geuen me their backe, and them that hate me thou hast destroyed.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As God geueth streingth to his seruāts; so he diminisheth the natural streingth and corage of his enemies.

verses.text: They cried, neither was there that would saue them, to our Lord; neither did he heare them.
And I wil breake them to powder, as the dust before the face of winde: as the durt of the streates I wil destroy them.
Thou wilt deliuer me from the contradictions of the people: thou wilt appoynte me to be head of the Gentiles.
A people, <na>(f)</na> which I knew not, hath serued me: in the hearing of the eare it hath obeyed me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Conuersion of Gentiles to Christ, as the Moabites, Idumeans, and others were subdued by Dauid. 1. Par. 11. 14. 18. 19. 20.

verses.text: The <na>(g)</na> children being alienes haue lyed to me, the children alienes are inueterated, and haue halted from their pathes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The reuolting and reprobation of the Iewes prefigured by Absolons rebellion and others. 2. Reg. 15. 16.

verses.text: Our Lord liueth, and blessed be my God, and the God of my saluation be exalted.
O God <na>(h)</na> which geuest me reuenges, & subdewest peoples vnder me, my deliuerer from mine angrie enemies.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God stil protecteth the Church of Christ, as he preserued Dauid.

verses.text: And from them that rise vp against me thou wilt exalt me: from the vniust man thou wilt deliuer me.
Therfore wil I confesse to thee among nations ô Lord: and wil say <na>(i)</na> a psalme to thy name,

notes.label: i
notes.text: Vse of Psalmes is most frequent in the Church of Gentiles. See the proemial Annotations. page. 12.

verses.text: Magnifying the saluations of his king, and doing mercie to his Christ Dauid, and to his seede for euer.

chapters.summary: King Dauids thankes to God for his often deliuerie from great dangers, first in general, 9. then more particularly describeth Gods terrible maner of fighting for him, 18. against his cruel, and otherwise potent enimies: 22. attributing the same to Gods good pleasure, and iustice of his cause, 31. praiseth God, 33. his only protector. 41. and depresser of his enemies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David singularly protected by God.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the psalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: perteyning to the beloued of the new Testament.

verses.text: THE <na>(b)</na> heauens shew forth the glorie of God, and the firmament declareth the workes of his handes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The silent workes of God declare his Maiestie to them that consider therof; his preachers declare the same by wordes, to al that wil heare.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Day vnto day vttereth word: and night vnto night sheweth knowledge.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The constant course of times sheweth that the same was disposed by Gods powre, and dayly propagation of faith, especially of Christian doctrine sheweth Christs powre, & assured perpetuitie of his Church.

verses.text: There are <na>(d)</na> no languages, nor speaches, whose voyces are not heard.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Some of euery language or natiõ haue beleued in Christ, receiuing the Catholique Religion.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Their sound hath gone forth into al the earth; and vnto the endes of the round world the wordes of them.

notes.label: e
notes.text: S. Paul affirmeth that this hath bene fulfilled by the Apostles preaching in al the world. Rom. 10.

verses.text: He put his tabernacle in <na>(f)</na> the sunne: & himself as a <na>(g)</na> bridgrome coming forth of his bridechamber. He hath reioyced as a giant to runne the way,

notes.label: f
notes.text: By the sunne a most excellent and superelemental creature, the Prophet describeth Christ, making his course through this world, illuminating, comforting and streingthning the Church his tabernacle, wherein he perpetually dwelleth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Christ the bridgrome, and the Church his bride are neuer diuorsed; his loue, wisdome, and powre, euer conseruing her by his immaculute law.

verses.text: his comming forth from the toppe of heauen: And his recourse euen to the toppe therof: neither is there that can hide him selfe from his heate.
The law of our Lord is immaculate <na>(h)</na> conuerting soules: the testimonie of our Lord is faithful, geuing wisedome to litle ones.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The old law was likewise pure in it selfe and holy, but the new also maketh the obseruers immaculate.

verses.text: The iustices of our Lord be right, making hartes ioyful: the precept of our Lord lightsome; illuminating the eies.
The feare of our Lord is holie, permanent for euer and euer: the iudgmentes of our Lord be true, iustified in themselues.
To be desired aboue gold and much pretious stone: and more sweete aboue honie and the honie combe.
For thy seruant <na>(i)</na> keepeth them, in keeping them is <na>(k)</na> much reward.

notes.label: i
notes.text: How swete the law of God is, his seruantes finde not by reading, or by hearing only, but by keping it.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Conformably to this text the prophete professeth (Psal. 118. v. 12.) that he kept them for reward, in which place the heretikes translation is corrupted.

verses.text: Sinnes <na>(l)</na> who vnderstandeth? from my secrete sinnes cleanse me:

notes.label: l
notes.text: None in this life knoweth and feareth perfectly his owne estate, whether he be worthie of loue or hate, Eccle. 9 but hopeth.

verses.text: and from other mens spare thy seruant. If <na>(m)</na> they shal not haue dominion ouer me, then shal I be immaculate; and shal be cleansed from the greatest sinne.

notes.label: m
notes.text: If mortal sinnes haue not dominion in the soule it is iust: and shal be in time immaculate from al sinne.

verses.text: And the wordes of my mouth shal be such as may please: and the meditation of my hart in thy sight alwayes. O Lord <na>(n)</na> my helper, and my <na>(o)</na> redemer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Gods helping grace is stil necessarie to perseuer,

notes.label: o
notes.text: as his first grace redeeming man is nessarie for our first conuersion,

chapters.summary: Gods perfect goodnes and glorie is shewed by his great workes, and by his Apostles sent with heauenlie commission, to preach in al tongues to al nations. 6. Christ coming into the world, and returne vnto heauen. 8. his immaculate Law: 13. Wherin notwistanding the iust shal haue nede to pray for remission of smaller and daylie sinnes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: Propagation of the Catholic faith.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Psalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though such a prayer was very fitly made for Dauid, Ezechias, or other kinges of Iuda, yet it more properly serueth for Christian Kinges and Prelates.

verses.text: OVr Lord heare <na>(b)</na> thee in the day of tribulation: the name of the God of Iacob protect thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The king, or other superior praying for him selfe, his subiects pray with him, and for him. It may also be applied to Christ, praying whiles he vvas mortal, or novv praying for his mystical body the Church, but in both these cases, our prayers are only necessary for his seruantes not for him.

verses.text: Send he ayde to thee from the holie place: and from Sion defend he thee.
Be he mindeful of al thy <na>(c)</na> sacrifice: and be thy holocaust made <na>(d)</na> fatte.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Hebrevv vvord MINCA signifieth sacrifice of floure, and vnbloudy, so perteyneth to the Eucharist, in forme of bread, and vvine.

notes.label: d
notes.text: be acceptable for him, for vvhom it is offered.

verses.text: Geue he vnto thee according to thy hart: and confirme he al thy counsel.
We shal reioyce <na>(e)</na> in thy saluation: and in the name of our God we shal be magnified.

notes.label: e
notes.text: in the prosperous state of thee our superiour.

verses.text: Our Lord accomplish al thy petitions: now haue I knowen that our Lord hath saued <na>(f)</na> his <sc>CHRIST</sc>. He shal heare him from his holie heauen: the saluation of his righthand is, <na>(g)</na> in powers.

notes.label: f
notes.text: his anointed king, or Priest, Mystically faithful people acknovvlege the victory of Christ our Sauiour ouer death and al enemies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: in great streingth, or heauenlie forces.

verses.text: These in chariotes, and these in horses: but we wil inuocate in the name of the Lord our God.
<na>(i)</na> They are bound, and haue fallen: but we haue risen and are set vpright.

notes.label: i
notes.text: men trusting in humane and worldly powre fal into captiuitie.

verses.text: Lord <na>(k)</na> saue the king, and heare vs in the day, that we shal inuocate thee.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By protection of the head the body is also conserued.

chapters.summary: Faithful people ioyne their prayer, for their Prince or Prelate, 4. with sacrifice offered for his preseruation, and prosperous successe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The subiects prayer for their superior.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Psalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the nevv Testament, principally to Chrrist, partly to godly and victorious kinges, and generally to al the blessed, vvhich ouercome spiritual enemies.

verses.text: LOrd in <na>(b)</na> thy power the king shal be glad: and vpon thy saluation he shal reioyce excedingly.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Christ our king as man ouercoming his enemies by his diuine povvre, reioyceth in victorie.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> desire of his hart thou hast geuen him: and of the wil of his lippes thou hast not defrauded him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Christs most special desire was the saluation of his people.

verses.text: Because thou hast <na>(d)</na> preuented him in blessinges of sweetnesse: thou hast put on his head a crowne of pretious stone.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This most principally verified in Christ, is also applied to Martyres, vvhich suffer or are readie in preparation of mind to suffer death for the truth.

verses.text: He asked life of thee: and thou gauest him length of daies for euer, and for euer and euer.
Great is his glorie in thy saluation: glorie and great beautie thou shalt put vpon him.
Because thou shalt geue him <na>(e)</na> to be a blessing for euer and euer: thou shalt make him ioyful in gladenesse with thy countenance.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Al Sainctes receiue blessing of glorie, but only Christ imperteth such grace to others: for in him al are blessed that are eternally glorified. Gen. 21. Ioan. 1.

verses.text: Because the king hopeth in our Lord: and in the mercie of the Highest he shal not be moued.
Let <na>(f)</na> thy hand be found of al thy enemies: let thy righthand find al, that hate thee.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The iust conforming their desires to Gods vvil, do pray that the vvicked may be punished. It is also a prophecie, that so it shal come to passe.

verses.text: Thou <na>(g)</na> shalt put them as an ouen of fyre <na>(h)</na> in the time of thy countenance: our Lord in his wrath <na>(i)</na> shal truble them, and fyre shal deuoure them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And so it folovveth in the next verse: Thou shalt put them &c.

notes.label: h
notes.text: This also can not be vnderstood of anie but of Christ, vvho in the general or particular iudgement shal geue sentence vpon the vvicked.

notes.label: i
notes.text: And immediatly hel fire shal deuoure them.

verses.text: Their <na>(k)</na> fruite thou shalt destroy from the land: and their seede from the children of men.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Al the wicked, and namely the Iewes who persecuted Christ, faile in their deuises.

verses.text: Because they haue turned the euils vpon thee: they haue deuised counsels, which they could not establish.
Because thou shalt put them backe: in thy remnantes thou shalt prepare their countenance.
Be exalted Lord in thy powre: <na>(l)</na> we wil chaunte and sing thy powers.

notes.label: l
notes.text: whiles the wicked perish, the iust reioyce and praise God in songue and Psalme.

chapters.summary: Praise to God for Christs exaltation after his passion: 9. and depression of his enemies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's exaltation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end for the <na>(a)</na> morning enterprise, the Psalme <na>(b)</na> of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Redemptiõ of mankind vndertakē by Christ, and performed by his death, beganne to be shewed by his Resurrection in the morning of the third day. S. Aug.

notes.label: b
notes.text: in figure of Christ the beloued of God.

verses.text: GOD <na>(c)</na> my God haue respect to me: <na>(d)</na> why hast thou forsaken me? <na>(e)</na> far from my saluation are the wordes of my sinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God is God of al his creatures, but in more peculiar sorte God of Christ by personal vnion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Thou neither deliuerest me frõ dying: nor yeldest me such comforth, as thou voutsafest to other Sainctes. · v. 6. Mat. 27.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am neither deliuered from dying, nor comforted in my passion, hauing vndertaken to dye for the sinnes of mankind, & reputed them as myn owne wordes or factes.

verses.text: My God I shal crie <na>(f)</na> by day, <na>(g)</na> and thou wilt not heare: and by night, and <na>(h)</na> not for follie vnto me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Albeit I crie by day,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and by night, on the crosse and in the garden, to haue the chalice of death remoued from me, and shal not be heard,

notes.label: h
notes.text: Yet there is no follie, nor fault in this petition, which is with submission of mans wil to Gods wil.

verses.text: But <na>(i)</na> thou dwellest in the holie place, <na>(k)</na> the prayse of Israel.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou from heauen wilt heare when it is conuenient.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Whose wisdome and goodnes the Church worthely praiseth.

verses.text: In thee <na>(l)</na> our fathers haue hoped: they hoped, and thou didst deliuer them.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Patriarkes, Prophets, and other holy mẽ praying in their distresses obtained their requestes.

verses.text: They cried to thee, and were <na>(m)</na> saued: they hoped in thee, and were <na>(n)</na> not confounded.

notes.label: m
notes.text: VVere temporally deliuered by thy mightie hand from their persecuters.

notes.label: n
notes.text: not frustrate of their humble prayers.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> But I am a <na>(p)</na> worme and no man: a <na>(q)</na> reproch of men and <na>(r)</na> outcast of the people.

notes.label: o

verses.text: Whiles the harmeful approch vpon me, to eate my flesh. Mine enemies that truble me, them selues are weakened and are fallen.
If campes stand together against me, my hart shal not feare. If battel rise vp against me, in this wil I hope.

One thing I haue asked of our Lord, this wil I seeke for, that I <na>(e)</na> may dwel in the house of our Lord al the dayes of my life. That I may see the pleasentnes of our Lord, and visite his temple.

notes.label: e
notes.text: How special a benefite Dauid estemed it to be in the Catholique Church the only true house of God!

verses.text: Because he hath <na>(f)</na> hid me in his tabernacle: in the day of euils he hath protected me, in <na>(g)</na> the secrete of his tabernacle.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Albeit the spiritual or carnal enemie seke to ouerthrow me, yet I am secure in the Catholique Church.

notes.label: g
notes.text: God either suffereth not the enemie to find his seruant.

verses.text: In <na>(h)</na> a rocke he hath exalted me: and now he hath <na>(i)</na> exalted my head ouer mine enemies. I <na>(k)</na> haue gone round about, and haue immolated in his tabernacle an host of iubilation: I <na>(l)</na> wil sing, and say a Psalme to our Lord.

notes.label: h
notes.text: or not to be able to hurt him spiritually

notes.label: i
notes.text: when a martyr or confessour dieth, then he getteth the victorie against the persecutors.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Diligently recounting al thy benefites, I render thankes by sacrifice and praise.

notes.label: l
notes.text: not only in hart, but also singing with loud voice and instrument.

verses.text: Heare ô Lord my voice, wherwith I haue cried to thee: haue mercie on me, and heare me.
My <na>(m)</na> hart hath sayd to thee, my face hath sought thee out: <na>(n)</na> thy face ô Lord I wil seeke.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In my inward sincere cogitation I desire, and seeke that I may see thee,

notes.label: n
notes.text: face to face 1. Cor. 13. v. 12.

verses.text: Turne <na>(o)</na> not away thy face from me: <na>(p)</na> decline not in wrath from thy seruant. Be <na>(q)</na> thou my helper: forsake me not, neither despise me ô God my Sauiour.

notes.label: o
notes.text: In the meane time ô Lord, grant me thy fauour,

notes.label: p
notes.text: leaue me not though thou be angrie with me.

notes.label: q
notes.text: He speaketh in the person of orphanes.

verses.text: Because <na>(r)</na> my father and my mother haue forsaken me: but our Lord hath taken me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Though carnal parentes forsake the iust man in tribulation, yet God hath then most special care of him.

verses.text: Geue me <na>(s)</na> a law ô Lord in thy way: <na>(t)</na> and direct me in the right path, because of mine enemies.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Establish my hart in thy law.

notes.label: t
notes.text: conserue me in the right way, which thou hast already taught me, and it is the more necessarie, because myne enemies labour to peruert me.

verses.text: Deliuer me not into <na>(v)</na> the soules of them that truble me: because <na>(w)</na> vniust witnesses haue risen vp against me, and iniquity hath lyed <na>(x)</na> to it selfe.

notes.label: v
notes.text: the willes.

notes.label: w
notes.text: false witnesses accused Dauid, others accused Christ: Mat. 26. others do stil accuse the iust Mat. 5.

notes.label: x
notes.text: the wicked please themselues in lying, but the chief hurt finally turneth vpon themselues.

verses.text: I <na>(y)</na> beleue to see the good things of our Lord, in the land of the liuing.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The prophet and al iust men are comforted by God, and hope of reward in heauen.

verses.text: <na>(z)</na> Expect our Lord, doe manfully: and <na>(a)</na> let thy hart take courage, and <na>(b)</na> expect thou our Lord. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: z
notes.text: The iust exhorteth his owne soule to patience,

notes.label: a
notes.text: fortitude,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and longanimitie. · Psal. 30.

chapters.summary: Dauid being in great distresse through persecution, and hauing assured confidence in God, describeth the great securitie of Gods protection. 7. sheweth the same experienced in him self. 12. prayeth for continuance therof 13. and incorageth his owne soule, in hope of life euerlasting, to perseuer in vertue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
An other confident prayer of David in tribulation.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A Psalme to Dauid him selfe. TO THEE ô Lord I wil crie, my God <na>(a)</na> keepe not silence from me: lest at any time thou hold thy peace from me, and I shal be like to them that goe downe into the lake.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Omitte not to comfort me.

verses.text: Heare ô Lord the voice of my petition whiles I pray to thee: whiles I lift vp my handes to thy holie temple.
<na>(b)</na> Draw me not together with sinners: and with them that worke iniquitie destroy me not. Which speake peace with their neighbour, but euils in their hartes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Suffer me not to be ouercome: for God tempteth none to euil. Iac. 1.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Geue them according to their workes, and according to the wickednesse of their inuentions. According to the workes of their handes geue vnto them: render them their retribution.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The iust in zele of iustice pray that sinne may be punished.

verses.text: Because they haue <na>(d)</na> not vnderstood the workes of our Lord, and in the workes of his handes thou shalt destroy them, and <na>(e)</na> not build them vp.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Ignorance doth not excuse when men may and wil not vnderstand.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God saueth not without our cooperation with his grace.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord: because he hath heard the voice of my petition.
Our Lord is my helper, and my protectour: in him my hart hath hoped, and I was holpen. And <na>(f)</na> my flesh florished againe: and <na>(g)</na> with my wil I wil confesse to him.

notes.label: f
notes.text: being comforted in spirite my bodie is as it were refreshed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: freely and gladly.

verses.text: Our Lord is the strength of his people: and he is <na>(h)</na> the protector of the saluations of his annoynted.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God protecteth and prospereth the kings good endeuoures for his people.

verses.text: Saue <na>(i)</na> thy people ô Lord, and blesse thine inheritance: and rule them, and extol them for euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: As Psal. 19. and often elswhere the subiectes pray for their Superior: so mutually the superior prayeth for the subiectes.

chapters.summary: Dauid prayeth to be defended from the eternal destruction of the wicked, 4. which ( by way of imprecation, or conformitie to Gods iustice ) he prophecieth 6. Feeling by inspiration that his prayer is heard, rendereth thankes to God, 9. and prayeth for al the people. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Another prayer of David for delivery from evils.
The 8. key.

verses.text: The Psalme of Dauid, in the consummation <na>(a)</na> of the tabernacle. BRING <na>(b)</na> to our Lord ye children of God: bring to our Lord <na>(c)</na> the sonnes of rammes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Offer sacrifice of thankes for the singular benefites after recounted in this Psalme.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Rammes were of the more principal thinges that were offered in the law of Moyses. But the sonnes of rammes importe in mystical sense better hostes then rammes.

verses.text: Bring to our Lord <na>(d)</na> glorie and honour, bring to our Lord glorie vnto his name: adore ye our Lord <na>(e)</na> in his holie court.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The first thing in sacrifice is to glorifie, honour, and adore God in sinceritie of spirite,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in his holie Catholique Churh.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(f)</na> vpon waters, the God of <na>(g)</na> maiestie hath <na>(h)</na> thundered: Our Lord vpon <na>(i)</na> manie waters.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Here is a greater matter intimated then happened in the bringing of the Arke into a tabernacle prepared in Sion, when Dauid danced, and offered hostes for sacrifice, others ioyning with him in that solemnitie. But this voice of out Lord vpon waters is rather verified of our Blessed Sauiours owne preaching with

notes.label: g
notes.text: maiestie

notes.label: h
notes.text: thundering, & by his Apostles vpon

notes.label: i
notes.text: manie waters, manie nations:

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(k)</na> in powre: the voice of our Lord <na>(l)</na> in magnificence.

notes.label: k
notes.text: in powre of miracles.

notes.label: l
notes.text: in magnificence preaching as hauing in dede powre, not as the Scribes and Pharises. Mat. 7. v. 29.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(m)</na> breaking ceders: and our Lord shal breake the <na>(n)</na> ceders of Libanus:

notes.label: m
notes.text: breaking cedars among innumerable others, conuerting highest Potentates

notes.label: n
notes.text: of Libanus, Emperoures, kinges and greatest Princes of the world:

verses.text: And he shal breake them in peeces as a <na>(o)</na> calfe of Libanus. <na>(p)</na> and the beloued as <na>(q)</na> the sonne of vnicornes.

notes.label: o
notes.text: as a calfe of Libanas so meekly submitting them selues to Christs yoke, and spiritual obedience of his Church.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Al which is done by Christ our Lord the beloued of God,

notes.label: q
notes.text: as the sonne of vnicornes, is most tenderly beloued by the parentes.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(r)</na> diuiding the flame of fire:

notes.label: r
notes.text: This voice of our Lord diuiding the flame of fire. the Holie Ghost proceding from the Father and the Sonne, came vpon the Apostles, as in diuided tongues of fire.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(s)</na> shaking the desert; and our Lord shal moue <na>(t)</na> the desert of Cades.

notes.label: s
notes.text: wherwith the desert, the Gentiles of the wide and wild world, were shaken and moued,

notes.label: t
notes.text: the desert of Cades, some of the Iewes also compunct in hart with remorse of conscience hearing the voice of S. Peter, and other Apostles.

verses.text: The voice of our Lord <na>(v)</na> preparing <na>[1]</na> hartes, and he shal <na>(w)</na> discouer thicke woodes: and <na>(x)</na> in his temple al shal say glorie.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The same voice of our Lord preparing hartes, inspiring the mindes of men with spede, like hyndes and does, to ascend the high hilles of free and perfect life, in contemplatiue vertues.

notes.label: w
notes.text: So our Sauiour shal discouer the thicke woodes, reueile the hidden Mysteries of the old Law, by preaching Christian doctrine, and vse of Christian Religion.

notes.label: x
notes.text: in his holie Temple, the Catholique Church, wherin al true Christians shal glorifie God.
ceruos.

verses.text: Our Lord maketh <na>(y)</na> to inhabite the floud: and our Lord <na>(z)</na> shal sit king for euer.

notes.label: y
notes.text: making the great abundance of people, who are like the sea when it ouerfloweth the land, to dwel in the same Church.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Christ our Lord sitting, & ruling king ouer al foreuer:

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(a)</na> will give strength to his people: our Lord <na>(b)</na> will bless his people in peace.

notes.label: a
notes.text: by his grace geuing streingth to his people, to passe through the tentations of this life;

notes.label: b
notes.text: and blesse the iust with eternal peace in heauen.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet seing in spirite the most sacred Mysteries, brought by Christ into this world, inuiteth al to offer their best thinges, euen themselues wholly, as sacrifice of thankes, for so excellent benefites, preached with magnificence. 5. VVherby innumerable are gethered into his Church here replenished with grace, and in heauen with glorie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Christ endowed with excellent mysteries.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A <na>(a)</na> Psalme of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> in the dedication of Dauids house.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The general name of Psalme common to this whole booke conteyning in al 150. is more particularelie appropriated to some, which more specially were playde vpon musical instruments as on the Psalter, Harpe, &c. Others are called Canticles, which were most vsuallie songue with humaine voices. So this, called a Psalme of Canticle, signifieth that voyces begane the musike and instruments were adioyned. As contrariwise others are called Canticles of Psalmes, where instruments begane and voices folowed.

notes.label: b
notes.text: After manie great tribulations, King Dauid prospering built an excellent house or palace. (2. Reg. 5. v. 11. Paralip. 14. v. 1.) And at his first dwelling therein, made this Psalme, beginning himselfe to sing the same with voice, other musitians ioyned with him in the praises of God and thankesgeuing for his benefites.

verses.text: I WIL <na>(c)</na> exalt thee ô Lord, <na>(d)</na> because thou hast receiued me: neither hast <na>(e)</na> delighted myne enemies ouer me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though God in himselfe is most high, and neither nedeth, nor can be exalted by men, yet the royal prophet knew it vvas his dutie to sing thankes and praises to him,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for his deliuerie from manie trubles, and dangers.

notes.label: e
notes.text: not suffering his enemies to be delighted in his ruine.

verses.text: O Lord my God I haue cried to thee, and thou hast <na>(f)</na> healed me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: conserued my bodie in health amõgst innumerable dangers.

verses.text: Lord thou hast <na>(g)</na> brought forth my soule out of hel: thou hast saued me from them that goe downe into the lake.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Preserued my soule from greater dãgers of sinnes, and so from hel.

verses.text: Sing to our Lord <na>(h)</na> ye his sainctes: and <na>(i)</na> confesse to the memorie of his holines.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Ye that are iust and holie praise God for it, from vvhom it cometh, and not from your selues:

notes.label: i
notes.text: confesse his mere goodnes vvithout your desertes.

verses.text: Because <na>(k)</na> wrath is in his indignation: <na>(l)</na> and life in his wil. At <na>(m)</na> euening shal weeping abide: and in the morning gladnesse.

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvhen he is angrie,

notes.label: l
notes.text: yet he meaneth vvel vnto vs.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The state of a iust mans life is often changed from sorovv to comforte, and from comforte to sorovv.

verses.text: And I said in my abundance: <na>(n)</na> I wil not be moued for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Though vve suppose our selues firmly established:

verses.text: O Lord <na>(o)</na> in thy wil, thou hast geuen strength to my beautie. Thou hast <na>(p)</na> turned away thy face from me, and I became trubled.

notes.label: o
notes.text: yet God of his good vvil tovvardes vs sometimes geueth strength, and corege,

notes.label: p
notes.text: sometimes suffereth vs to our ovvne vveakenes,

verses.text: To thee ô Lord <na>(q)</na> I wil crie: and I wil pray to my God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: therfore we must stil crie and pray for Gods helpe,

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> What profite is in my bloud, whiles I descend into corruption? Shal dust confesse to thee, or declare thy truth?

notes.label: r
notes.text: in manner here expressed or the like.

verses.text: Our Lord hath heard, and had mercie on me: our Lord is become my helper.
Thou hast turned my mourning into ioy vnto me: thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladnes.
That <na>(s)</na> my glorie may sing to thee: and I be not compunct: Lord my God for euer <na>(t)</na> wil I confesse to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: finally in this my good state

notes.label: t
notes.text: I shal alvvayes confesse and praise thee.

chapters.summary: King Dauid by voice and instrument rendereth thankes to God for his peaceable state in the kingdom, 5. inuiteth others to reioyce in Gods benefites, teaching by his owne example that God sometimes geueth more conforth sometimes sheweth his wrath, but al for our good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David rendereth thanks for his establishment in his Kingdom.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, the Psalme of Dauid, for <na>(b)</na> excesse of minde.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Testament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: especially to the iust trubled and almost distracted in mind in great affliction. See v. 23.

verses.text: IN THEE ô Lord <na>(c)</na> haue I hoped, <na>(d)</na> let me not be confounded for euer: in thy iustice deliuer me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: How greuously soeuer I am afflicted yet I trust in thee,

notes.label: d
notes.text: therfore I pray thus.

verses.text: Incline thine eare to me, make hast to deliuer me. Be vnto me for a God protector: and for a house of refuge, that thou mayst saue me.
Because thou art my strength, and my refuge: and for thy name thou wilt conduct me, and wilt nourish me.
Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they haue hid for me: because thou art my protector.
Into <na>(e)</na> thy handes I commend my spirit: thou hast <na>(f)</na> redeemed me ô Lord God of truth. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: I offer and resigne my selfe to thee:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Luc. 23. · Thou hast often deliuered me. This verse is most aptly applied in al resignatiõs of our soules to Gods wil, namely whensoeuer we receiue the B. Sacrament; likewise in the houre of death, and at manie other times.

verses.text: Thou hast hated them that obserue vanities, vnprofitably. But I haue hoped in our Lord:
I shal reioyce and be ioyful in thy mercie. Because thou hast respected my humilitie, thou hast saued my soule out of necessities.
Neither <na>(g)</na> hast thou shut me vp in the handes of the enemie: thou hast set me feete in a large place.

notes.label: g
notes.text: not suffered me to be shut vp.

verses.text: Haue mercie vpon me ô Lord because I am in tribulation: myne eie is trubled for wrath, my soule, and my bellie:
Because <na>(h)</na> my life is decayed for sorrowe: and my yeares for gronings. My strength is weakened for pouertie; and by bones are trubled.

notes.label: h
notes.text: al my partes external and internal, body and mind are trubled.

verses.text: Aboue al myne enemies I am made a reproch both to my neighbours excedingly: and <na>(i)</na> a feare to my acquantance. They that saw me, fled forth from me:

notes.label: i
notes.text: My freindes dare not conuerse with me, lest they incurre displeasure for my sake.

verses.text: I am forgotten, from the hart as one dead. I am made as a vessel destroyed:
because I haue heard the reprehension of manie that abide round about: In that whiles, they assembled together against me, they consulted to take my soule.
But I haue hoped in thee ô Lord: I sayd: Thou art my God:
my lottes are in thy handes. Deliuer me out of the handes of my enemies, and from them that persecute me.
<na>(k)</na> Illustrate thy face vpon thy seruant, <na>(l)</na> saue me in thy mercie:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Make thy light so shine in my soule, that I may vnderstand that is right.

notes.label: l
notes.text: and through thy mercie deliuer me from the force of myne aduersaries.

verses.text: Lord let me not be confounded, because I haue inuocated thee. Let the impious be ashamed, and brought downe into hel:
let the deceitful lippes be made mute. Which speake iniquitie against the iust, <na>(m)</na> in pride, and <na>(n)</na> abuse.

notes.label: m
notes.text: so proudly behauing them selues, as if they had no superior, neither in earth nor in heauen, to whom they shal at last render account:

notes.label: n
notes.text: and abusing their present powre and authoritie, which they haue of God.

verses.text: How great is the multitude of thy sweetnesse ô Lord, which thou <na>(o)</na> hast hid for them that feare thee. Thou hast perfited it for them that hope in thee, <na>(p)</na> in the sight of the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: As yet in this present life the reward of the iust is hidde:

notes.label: p
notes.text: but shal be made manifest in sight of al men.

verses.text: Thou <na>(q)</na> shalt hide them in the secrete of <na>(r)</na> thy face from the disturbance of men. Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.

notes.label: q
notes.text: In the meane time the iust is in great estimation in the secrete knowledge of God.

notes.label: r
notes.text: title of honoure, as we speake to a king; your maiestie: or to a noble man, your Lordshippe.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord: because he hath made his mercie merueilous to me in the fensed citie.
But I haue said in <na>(s)</na> the excesse of my minde: I am cast away from the sight of thine eies. Therfore thou hast heard the voice of my praier, whiles I cried to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: in myn extreme affliction being almost distracted in my mind, I said that in reason I would not haue sayd. Holie Iob spake some thinges in such state of affliction. ch. 3. & 42.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Loue our Lord al ye his sainctes: because our Lord wil require truth, & wil repay them abundantly that doe proudly.

notes.label: t
notes.text: the prophet, or other iust person exhorteth al the seruants of God

verses.text: Do ye <na>(v)</na> manfully, and let your <na>(w)</na> hart take courage, al ye that <na>(x)</na> hope in out Lord.

notes.label: v
notes.text: to constancie.

notes.label: w
notes.text: longanimitie,

notes.label: x
notes.text: and final perseuerance to the end.

chapters.summary: A prayer of a iust man excedingly afflicted stil confident in God, 11. describing his manie calamities (in respect of his enemies) vndeserued, 18. prayeth for his owne deliuerie, and their iust punishment. 20. praiseth and thanketh God for his goodnes. 24. exhorteth al others to do the same. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
How to pray in affliction.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid him selfe vnderstanding. BLESSED are they, <na>(b)</na> whose iniquities are forgeuen: and whose sinnes <na>(c)</na> be couered. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme sheweth how Dauid was brought to vnderstand his sinnes, to confesse, bewayle, and obtaine remission of them.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The first blessing of a sinner is the forgeuenes of his sinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: by charitie, which couereth the multitude of sinnes. 1. Pet. 4.

verses.text: Blessed is the man, to whom <na>(d)</na> our Lord hath not imputed sinne, neither is there <na>(e)</na> guile in his spirit.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Satisfaction being made.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhen sinners repent sincerly without guile, then God forgeueth: without which cooperation none is iustified.

verses.text: Because <na>(f)</na> I held my peace, my bones are <na>[1]</na> inueterated, <na>(g)</na> whiles I cried al the day.

notes.label: f
notes.text: because I acknowledged not my greuous sinnes, I was stil sore afflicted.

notes.label: g
notes.text: though otherwise I ceased not to pray but without any fruict or good effect.
vvaxed as if they vvere old.

verses.text: Because day and night thy hand is made heauie vpon me: I <na>(h)</na> am turned in my anguish, whiles <na>(i)</na> the thorne is fastened.

notes.label: h
notes.text: thy diuine prouidence reducing me,

notes.label: i
notes.text: by remorse of myn owne conscience which telleth me that I deserue al this affliction.

verses.text: I <na>(k)</na> haue made my sinne knowen to thee: and my iniustice I haue not hid. I said: I wil confesse against me my iniustice to our Lord: and thou hast forgeuen the impietie of my sinne.

notes.label: k
notes.text: therfore I do no longer dissẽble with men nor am silent to thee, but expresly acknowlege my sinnes.

verses.text: For this <na>(l)</na> shal euerie holie one pray to thee, in time conuenient. But yet <na>(m)</na> in the floud of manie waters, they shal <na>(n)</na> not approche to him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: As I do now recal my selfe being stricken with Gods heauie hand; so must euerie one that wil be purged from his sinnes and sanctified pray to thee, when he is afflicted.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Though calamities be meruelous great like to a diluge:

notes.label: n
notes.text: yet they shal not opresse him, that relieth vpon God.

verses.text: Thou art my refuge from tribulation, which hath compassed me: my exultation, deliuer me from them that compasse me.
I <na>(o)</na> wil geue thee vnderstanding, and wil instruct thee in the way, that thou shalt goe; I <na>(p)</na> wil fasten mine eies vpon thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God speaketh: promising by these tribulations to geue his seruants vnderstanding, and instruction:

notes.label: p
notes.text: with perpetual protection.

verses.text: Doe <na>(q)</na> not become as horse and mule, which haue no vnderstanding. In <na>(r)</na> bit and bridle binde fast their cheekes, that approch not to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Be not therfore careles, like to brute beastes, but consideratiue of your actions.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The Prophet or anie iust soul besecheth God to hold this straict hand of discipline ouer sinners, for their conuersion.

verses.text: Manie <na>(s)</na> are the scourges of a sinner, but <na>(t)</na> him that hopeth in our Lord mercie shal compasse.

notes.label: s
notes.text: sinners deserue much punishment.

notes.label: t
notes.text: but repenting, and trusting in God shal finde his mercie.

verses.text: Be <na>(v)</na> ioyful in our Lord and reioyse ye iust, and glorie al ye right of hart.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The end of true penance is ioy to which therfore the prophet inuiteth al penitents.

chapters.summary: Forgeuenes of sinnes is a happie thing: 3. wherto manie are brought by affliction geuing them vnderstanding, so mouing them to confesse their sinnes, 6. pray for remission, 10, not despaire, but hope in Gods mercie, and so reioyce with sincere hart. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The second penitential Psalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: REIOYCE ye iust <na>(a)</na> in our Lord: <na>(b)</na> praysing becometh the righteous.

notes.label: a
notes.text: not in your selues

notes.label: b
notes.text: praise is not comelie in the mouth of a sinner. Eccli. 15.

verses.text: Confesse ye to our Lord on <na>(c)</na> the harpe: on <na>(d)</na> a psalter of ten strings sing to him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: in mortificacion offering your bodies a liuing hoste, Rom. 12.

notes.label: d
notes.text: of this instrument this booke is called the Psalter and it signifieth the obseruation of the tenne commandments, withoutwhich no praise pleaseth God.

verses.text: Sing ye to him <na>(e)</na> a new song: sing wel to him in iubilation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: praising God for the grace of Christ in the new testament.

verses.text: Because the <na>(f)</na> word of our Lord is right, and al his workes are <na>(g)</na> in faith.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Gods rules and precepts are most iust and right.

notes.label: g
notes.text: he performeth whatsoeuer he promiseth.

verses.text: He loueth <na>(h)</na> mercie and iudgement: the earth is ful of the mercie of our Lord.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God euer ioyneth these vertues together.

verses.text: By <na>(i)</na> the word of our Lord the heauens are established: and by the spirit of his mouth al the power of them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Gods word is omnipotent.

verses.text: Gathering together the waters of the sea, as it were in a bottel: putting the depthes <na>(k)</na> in treasures.

notes.label: k
notes.text: vnknowen, as riches hid in secrete places.

verses.text: Let al the earth feare our Lord: and let al the inhabitantes of the world be moued at him.
Because he said, and they were made: he commanded and they were created,
Our Lord <na>(l)</na> dissipateth the counsels of nations: and he reproueth the cogitations of people, and he reproueth the counsels of princes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: As in Babylon he confounded their tongues.

verses.text: But the counsel of our Lord abydeth for euer: the cogitations <na>(m)</na> of his hart in generation and generation.

notes.label: m
notes.text: his absolute wil is alwayes fulfilled.

verses.text: Blessed is the nation, whose God is our Lord: the people <na>(n)</na> whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: the people of Israel in the old testament: and Christians of al nations in the new.

verses.text: Our <na>(o)</na> Lord hath looked from heauen: he hath sene al the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods perpetual prouidence.

verses.text: From his prepared habitation he hath looked vpon al, that inhabite the earth.
Who <na>(p)</na> made their hartes seuerally: who vnderstandeth al their workes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Gods wisdom infinite.

verses.text: The <na>(q)</na> king is not saued by much powre: and the gyant shal not be saued in the multitude of his strength.

notes.label: q
notes.text: No powre in earth is of anie force without God.

verses.text: The horse fayleth <na>(r)</na> to safetie, <na>(s)</na> and in the abundance of his force he shal not be saued.

notes.label: r
notes.text: of his maister

notes.label: s
notes.text: or of him selfe.

verses.text: Behold the eies of our Lord be vpon them that feare him: and on them, that hope vpon his mercie.
That he may deliuer their soules from death: and nourish them in famine.
Our soule expecteth our Lord: because he is our helper and protector.
Because in him our hart shal reioyce: and we haue trusted in his holie name.
<na>(t)</na> Let thy mercie ô Lord be made vpon vs: as we haue hoped in thee.

notes.label: t
notes.text: O God which hast al perfection, shew thy mercie in protecting, and sauing al that trust in thee.

chapters.summary: The prophet exhorteth to praise God, 4. describing his powre, prouidence, mercie, and wisdom. 16. no saluation but by him. 20. and therfore prayeth for his helpe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The perfection of God's works described.
The 2. key.

verses.text: To <na>[1]</na> Dauid, when he changed his countenance before <na>(a)</na> Abimelech, and he dismist him, and he went away. (1. Reg. 21.) <na>[2]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: His proper name was Achis 1. Reg. 21. but al kinges of Palestina were called Abimelech, as Pharao in Ægypt, Nabuchodonosor in Babylon.
This Psalme is also composed in order of the Alphabet.

verses.text: I <na>(b)</na> WIL blesse our Lord at <na>(c)</na> al time: his prayse alwayes in my mouth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I prayse God

notes.label: c
notes.text: both in prosperitie and aduersitie.

verses.text: In our Lord <na>(d)</na> my soule shal be praised: let the milde heare, and reioyce.

notes.label: d
notes.text: when I serue our Lord, my soule shal be praised in his seruice.

verses.text: Magnifie ye our Lord with me: and let vs exalt his name for euer.
I haue sought out our Lord, and he hath heard me: and from al my tribulations he hath deliuered me.
Come ye to him, and be illuminated: and your faces shal not be confounded.
This <na>(e)</na> poore man hath cried, and our Lord hath heard him: and from al his tribulations he hath saued him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Euerie man be he how poore soeuer when he prayeth shal be heard.

verses.text: The <na>(f)</na> Angel of our Lord shal put in him selfe about them that feare him: and shal deliuer them.

notes.label: f
notes.text: the proper guardian Angel of euerie one.

verses.text: Tast ye, and see that our Lord is sweete: blessed is the man, that hopeth in him.
Feare <na>(g)</na> ye our Lord al ye his sainctes: because there is no lacke to them that feare him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: with filial feare.

verses.text: The <na>(h)</na> rich haue wanted, and haue bene hungrie: but they that seeke after our Lord shal not be diminished of any good.

notes.label: h
notes.text: the rich of this world setting their mind vpon their wealth, are poore in spiritual giftes.

verses.text: Come children, heare me: I wil teach you the feare of our Lord.
Who is the man <na>(i)</na> that wil haue life: loueth to see good daies.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Euerie one desireth to be happie, but he in dede shal be happie, that fleeth from euil, and doth good.

verses.text: Stay thy tongue from euil: and thy lippes that they speake not guile.
Turne away from euil, and do good: seeke after peace, and pursewe it.
The eies of our Lord vpon the iust: and his eares vnto their prayers
But the <na>(k)</na> countenance of our Lord is vpon them that doe euil things: to destroy their memorie out of the earth.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God seing al mens actiõs & intentions, wil render as they deserue.

verses.text: The iust haue cried, and our Lord hath heard them: and out of al their tribulations he hath deliuered them.
Our Lord is nigh to them, that are of a contrite hart: and the humble of spirit he wil saue.
Manie are the tribulations of the iust: and out of al these our Lord wil deliuer them.
Our Lord keepeth al their <na>(l)</na> bones: there shal not one of them be broken.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though the iust seme for a time to be forsaken, yet God that geueth them internal streingth, wil at last reward and crowne in them his owne giftes.

verses.text: The death of sinners is verie il: and they that hate the iust <na>(m)</na> shal offend.

notes.label: m
notes.text: for their sinne they are suffered to fal into more sinne.

verses.text: Our Lord wil redeme the soules of his seruantes: and al that hope in him <na>(n)</na> shal not offend.

notes.label: n
notes.text: contrariwise those that accept of his grace, shal finally not offend.

chapters.summary: King Dauid by his owne example being deliuered from danger, exhorteth al men to render thankes for Gods benefites. 12. shewing wherin iustice consisteth, 16. and Gods special prouidence towards the iust. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himself. IVDGE <na>(b)</na> bô Lord them that hurt me: ouerthrow them that impugne me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dauid signifieth beloued desiderable, or strong of hand, that is Christ, aboue al beloued of God, desired of man, the strong conquerour of death and hel. S. Aug. in hunc locum.

notes.label: b
notes.text: By way of imprecation he prophecieth that God wil ouerthrow the persecutors of Christ, and of Christians.

verses.text: Take <na>(c)</na> armour and <na>(d)</na> shield: and rise vp to helpe me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: offensiue

notes.label: d
notes.text: denfensiue.

verses.text: Bring forth the sword, and <na>(e)</na> shut vp against them, that persecute me: say to my soule: I am thy saluation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: preoccupate and preuent the malice of the persecutor.

verses.text: Let them <na>(f)</na> be counfounded & ashamed, that seeke my soule. Let them be turned backward, and be confounded that thinke euil against me

notes.label: f
notes.text: Such a punishment and confusion shal fal in the end vpon al the malicious, after that the iust shal haue ouercome tribulations.

verses.text: Be they made as dust before the face of winde; and the angel of our Lord straictning them.
Let their way be made darkenesse and slippernes: and the angel of our Lord pursewing them.
Because they haue hid the destruction of their snare for me without cause: in vaine haue they vpbrayded my soule.
Let the snare which he knoweth not, come on him; and the net, which he hath hid, catch him: and let him fal into the verie same snare.
But <na>(g)</na> my soule shal reioyce in our Lord: and shal be delighted vpon <na>(h)</na> his saluation.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In the time of truble in hope,

notes.label: h
notes.text: after deliuerie, in eternal saluation,

verses.text: Al my bones shal say: Lord, who is like to thee? Deliuering the needie from the hand of them that are stronger then he: the needie and poore from them that spoile him.
<na>(i)</na> Vniust witnesses rysing vp, asked me things that <na>(k)</na> I knew not.

notes.label: i
notes.text: such false witnesses did rise against Christ Mat. 26.

notes.label: k
notes.text: thinges that were not; for God himselfe, that knoweth al thinges knoweth not that which neither was, is, nor can be.

verses.text: They repayed me euil things for good, <na>(l)</na> sterilitie to my soule.

notes.label: l
notes.text: they made priuation of my life, verified in Christ, not in Dauid, for he was killed by his enemies.

verses.text: But I when they were trublesome to me, <na>(m)</na> did put on cloth of heare. I humbled my soule in fasting: and my prayer shal be turned into my bosome.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Al our Sauiours life was penance for others, needing none for himselfe.

verses.text: As a <na>(n)</na> neighbour, as our brother, so did I please: as mourning and sorowful so was I humbled.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Christ the good Samaritane that releeued the wounded man. Luc. 10.

verses.text: And they <na>(o)</na> reioyced against me, and <na>(p)</na> came together: <na>(q)</na> scourges were gathered together vpon me, and I was <na>(r)</na> ignorant.

notes.label: o
notes.text: al this was fulfilled according to the letter in our Sauiours passion.

notes.label: p
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: q
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: r
notes.text: Our Lord knoweth not anie iust cause, why the Iewes so persecuted him, for they had no iust cause but meere malice.

verses.text: They were dissipated, and not compunct, they tempted me, they scorned me with scorning: they gnashed vpon me with their teeth.
Lord <na>(s)</na> when wilt thou regard? <na>(t)</na> restore thou my soule from their malignitie, myne only one from the lions.

notes.label: s
notes.text: as Psal. 21. and Mat. 27. God why hast thou forsaken me? not deliuered me from temporal death, nor yelded me such consolation, as thou gauest other Sainctes in their agonies?

notes.label: t
notes.text: a prophecie of Christs resurrection.

verses.text: I wil confesse to thee in <na>(v)</na> the great Church, in a graue people I wil prayse thee.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Prophecie of the Catholique Church. as Psal. 21.

verses.text: Let them not reioyce ouer me that are my aduersaries vniustly: <na>(w)</na> that hate me without cause, and twinckle with the eies.

notes.label: w
notes.text: This place is applied by our Sauiour to himselfe. Ioan. 15.

verses.text: Because they spake in deede <na>(x)</na> peaceably to me: and in the anger of the earth speaking they meant guiles.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The Pharises and Herodians said: Master we know that thou art a true speaker &c. meaning to intrappe him with treason. Mat. 22.

verses.text: And they <na>(y)</na> opened their mouth a wide vpon me: they said; Wel, wel, our eies haue seene.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The same Pharises and Priestes iudged him woorthy of death, and procured the people to crie: Crucifie him, crucifie, him.

verses.text: Thou hast sene ô Lord, keepe not silence: <na>(z)</na> Lord depart not from me.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Againe his Resurrection is prophecied.

verses.text: Arise and attend to my iudgement: my God, and my Lord vnto my cause.
Iudge me according to thy iustice ô Lord my God, and let them not reioyce ouer me
Let them not say in their hartes: Wel, wel, to our soule: neither let them say: We haue deuoured him.
Let <na>(a)</na> them blush and be ashamed together, that reioyce at my euils. Let them be clothed with confusion and shame; that speake great things vpon me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: At the day of iudgement the Wicked shal receiue sentence of damnation.

verses.text: Let <na>(b)</na> them reioyce and be glad, that wil my iustice: and let them say alwayes: Our Lord be magnified, that wil the peace of his seruant.

notes.label: b
notes.text: the blessed of eternal glorie.

verses.text: And my tongue shal meditate thy iustice, thy prayse al the day.

chapters.summary: Dauid, in figure of Christ, prophetically by way of inuocating Gods helpe, forsheweth his persecution, and the iust reuenge vpon his persecutors, 9. with praise to God. 13. his charitie towards his cruel aduersaries. 17. whom neuertheles God punisheth, 20. for pretending peace in wordes, and in fact persecuting, 23. rendering to al as they deserue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's persecution.
The 5. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Vnto the end, to <na>(b)</na> the seruant of our Lord Dauid him selfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: More specially describing the state of men in the new testament, then in the old.

notes.label: b
notes.text: instruction for Dauid not as a king, or a prophet, but as the poore seruant of God.

verses.text: THE vniust hath said within him selfe, that he <na>(c)</na> would sinne: there is no feare of God before his eies

notes.label: c
notes.text: wittingly and resolutely preferring wicked life before vertuous.

verses.text: Because he hath done deceitfully in his sight: <na>(d)</na> that his iniquitie may be found vnto hatred.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God so hateth sinne committed of meere malice, that he commonly reiecteth such sinners, and more often offereth new grace to those, that sinne of frailitie, or ignorance.

verses.text: The wordes of his mouth are iniquitie, and guile: he <na>(e)</na> would not vnderstand that he might doe wel.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some ignorance is inuincible whē one hath a good wil to lerne, doing his endeuour to knovv the truth in doctrin, & his dutie in manners, but can not get knowlege therof, and then he is excused before God; though he erre in opinion, or in fact: others are negligent to lerne, and their error is grosse ignorance and is a sinne, greater or lesse, according to the importance of the thing, which they ouhgt to knovv. Others are more vvilful, desiring to be ignorant; that they may sinne vvith the lesse remorse, or repining of their ovvne conscience, and this is affected ignorance, and most hainous, and odious sinne. For which God often leauing them destitute of ordinarie grace, which he geueth to others, they fal into reprobate sense, and into more horrible sinnes.

verses.text: He hath meditated iniquitie in his bed: he hath set himselfe on euery way not good, and malice he hath not hated.
Lord <na>(f)</na> thy mercie is in heauen: and <na>(g)</na> thy truth euen to the clowdes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God doth not vtterly shut vp his mercie from the most wilful & wicked sinners, but geueth them sometimes good motions, and sufficient helpe, thar they may repent, be iustified & saued, if they do not wittingly harden their owne hartes, and stil wilfully repel Gods grace.

notes.label: g
notes.text: For so God pomiseth (vvho is most faithful) that he vvil forgeue sinners, and receiue them into his fauoure againe, whensoeuer they resoluing to serue him, repent and cease to sinne.

verses.text: Thy iustice as the hilles of God: thy iudgementes are great depth. Men & <na>(h)</na> beastes thou wilt saue ô Lord:

notes.label: h
notes.text: Thou ô God that hast care of al creatures, not only of men but also of brute beastes, art euer readie of thy part to saue both moderate men, in vvhom the light of reason remaineth, and also grosse senseles persons, vvhich are become brutish like horse and mule or other beastes.

verses.text: as thou <na>(i)</na> hast multiplied thy mercie ô God. But <na>(k)</na> the children of men, <na>(l)</na> shal hope in the couert of thy winges.

notes.label: i
notes.text: For so our Lord multiplieth his mercie.

notes.label: k
