notes.text: Yet with condition that sensles or brutish men, must become reasonable men, the children of men, not coltes, whelpes, pigges &c.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Sinners thus conuerted shal not only haue al necessaries in this life, as al liuing creatures haue in this world, but also shal hope of spiritual, heauenly, & eternal glorie prepared for Angels, and children of men: as in the verses folovving.

verses.text: They shal be inebriated with the plentie of thy house: and with the torrent of thy pleasure thou shalt make them drinke,
Because with thee is the fountaine of life: and in thy light we shal see light.
Extend thy mercie to them that know thee, and thy iustice to them, that are of a right hart.
Let <na>(m)</na> not the foote of pride come to me: and let not <na>(n)</na> the hand of a sinner moue me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Lest anie impediment hinder the obtayning and possession of eternal revvard, the iust must specially pray not to be infected vvith pride:

notes.label: n
notes.text: nor be ouercome by the forcible tentations of other sinners, by persvvasion, nor euil example.

verses.text: There <na>(o)</na> haue they fallen that worke iniquitie: they were expelled, <na>(p)</na> neither could they stand.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The first sinne, tovvit of diuels, vvas pride, and mans sinne vvas by persvvasion of the diuel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: neither of which could escape punishment.

chapters.summary: The prophet describeth the wicked malice of obstinate sinners 6. Against which he opposeth Gods infinite goodnes, 9. with his prouident mercie towards the worst, and iust reward of the good; 12. praying to escape the dangerous gulfe of pride. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> A Psalme <na>(a)</na> to Dauid him self. HAVE <na>(b)</na> no emulation toward the malignant: neither enuie them that doe iniquitie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Dauids and euery iust mans instruction.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither be thou offended that the wicked do prosper in this world, nor imitate them that thou maist also prosper.
This Psalme is composed in order of the Alphabet, euerie distick beginning vvith a diuers letter, to moue the reader to diligent attention, which may serue in place of a larger cōmentarie,

verses.text: Because <na>(c)</na> they shal quickely wither as grasse: and as the blossomes of herbes they shal soone fal.

notes.label: c
notes.text: For al this life, and consequently the prosperitie therof is shorte, and vncertaine.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Hope in our Lord and doe good: and inhabite the land, and thou <na>(e)</na> shalt be fed in the riches therof.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Put thy trust in God, liuing content in this world:

notes.label: e
notes.text: & he wil geue thee that is necessarie.

verses.text: Be delighted in our Lord: and he wil geue thee the petitions of thy hart.
<na>(f)</na> Reuele thy way to our Lord, and hope in him: and he wil doe it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Commend al thyn affaires to God.

verses.text: And he wil <na>(g)</na> bring forth thy iustice as light: and thy iudgement as midday:

notes.label: g
notes.text: Partly making vertue appeare to the comfort of the vertuous, and example of others in this life, but especially in the next world.

verses.text: be subiect to our Lord, and pray him. Haue no emulation in him, that prospereth in his way: in a man that doth iniustices.
Cease from wrath, and leaue furie: haue not emulation that thou be malignant.
Because they that are malignant, shal be cast out: but they that expect our Lord, the same shal inherite <na>(h)</na> the land.

notes.label: h
notes.text: the land of the liuing.

verses.text: And yet a litle while, and the sinner shal not be: and thou shalt seeke his place, and shal not find it.
<cr>[1]</cr> But the meeke shal inherite the land, and shal be delighted in multitude of peace.
The sinner shal obserue the iust: and shal gnash vpon him with his teeth.
But our Lord shal scorne him: because he foreseeth that his day shal come.
Sinners haue drawen out the sword; they haue bent their bowe; That they may deceiue the poore and needie: that they may murder the right of hart.
Let <na>(i)</na> their owne swordes enter into their hartes: and let their bowe be broken.

notes.label: i
notes.text: By way of imprecation (as in manie other places) the prophet forsheweth that wicked men shal fal into the euils, which they prepare for others.

verses.text: Better is a litle to the iust, aboue much riches of sinners.
Because the armes of sinners shal be broken in pieces: but our Lord comfirmeth the iust.
Our Lord knoweth the daies of the immaculate: and their inheritance shal be for euer.
They shal not be confounded in the euil time, and in the dayes of famine they shal be filled:
because the sinners shal perish. But the enemies of our Lord forthwith as they shal be honoured and exalted, vanishing shal vanish as smoke.
The sinner shal borrow, and not pay: but the iust is merciful and wil geue.
Because they that blesse him shal inherite the land: but they that curse him shal perish.
With our Lord the steppe of man shal be directed: and he shal like wel of his way.
When <na>(k)</na> he shal fal, he shal not be brused: because our Lord putteth his hand vnder.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though the iust fal of frailtie or ignorance into venial sinne, yet Gods grace shal stay him that he fal not into mortal. The iust falleth seuen times in the day, & riseth. Prou. 24.

verses.text: I haue bene yong, for I am old: and I haue not sene the iust forsaken, <na>(l)</na> nor his seede seeking bread.

notes.label: l
notes.text: So king Dauid obserued: and it very rarely happeneth, that the iust or their children are destitute of necessarie sustenance in this vvorld. If it chance in some, it is to their greater merite, and is manifestly recompensed in spiritual giftes. In which sense S. Basil expoundeth, that it is alwayes verified For God euer rewardeth good workes either temporally, or spiritually, or both wayes. S. Augustin also (conc. 3. in hunc Psal.) exemplifieth in Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob with al his familie, who were forced to goe into other countries by reason of famine, and by Gods prouidence were there sustained, Gen. 12. 26. 46. and S. Paul among his other tribulations mentioneth famine and thirst. 2. Cor. 11. v. 27. Seing therfore these so iust persons sought their bread in necessitie, he expoundeth this holie Scripture in the Allegorical sense, that the Church from her beginning in Ierusalem to the end of the world, neuer wanteth the true word of God, true faith and doctrin, which is the spiritual bread vvhervvith the soule is nourished.

verses.text: Al the day he is merciful and lendeth: and his seede shal be in blessing.
<na>(m)</na> Decline from euil, and doe good: and <na>(n)</na> inhabite for euer and euer.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In these tvvo prīciples, declining from euil and doing good, true iustice consisteth.

notes.label: n
notes.text: and he that finally obserueth these tvvo pointes, meriteth and shal possesse heauen.

verses.text: Because our Lord loueth iudgement, and he wil not forsake his sainctes: they shal be preserued for euer. The vniust shal be punished: and the seede of the impious shal perish.
But the iust shal inherite the land: and shal inhabite for euer and euer vpon it.
The mouth of the iust shal meditate wisedome, and his tong shal speake iudgement. <cr>[1]</cr>
The law of his God in his hart: and his steppes shal not be supplanted.
The sinner considereth the iust: and seeketh to <na>(o)</na> murder him.

notes.label: o
notes.text: to draw him to mortal sinne, which is death of the soule.

verses.text: But our Lord wil not leaue him in his handes: neither wil he condemne him, when iudgement shal be geuen of him.
Expect our Lord, and keepe his way: and he wil exalt thee, that thou mayst inherite the land: when the sinners shal perish thou shalt see.
I haue seene the impious highly exalted, and aduanced as the ceders of Libanus.
And I passed by, and behold he was not: and I sought him, and his place was not found.
Keepe innocencie, and see equitie: because there are <na>(p)</na> remaynes for the peaceable man.

notes.label: p
notes.text: rewardes.

verses.text: But the vniust shal perish together: the remaines of the impious shal perish.
But the saluation of the iust is <na>(q)</na> of our Lord: and he is their potector in the time of tribulation.

notes.label: q
notes.text: mans iustice and wel doing is not of his owne powre but of Gods grace.

verses.text: And our Lord wil helpe them, and deliuer them: and he wil take them away from sinners, and saue them: because they haue hoped in him.

chapters.summary: An exhortation not to enuie nor imitate the euil, who for most part prosper in this world, and are damned eternally: but to flee euil and doe good, duly considering that God diuersly permitteth and punisheth the wicked, and likewise comforteth and afflicteth the iust, al for their good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
An exhortation to contempt of this world.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Psalme of Dauid, in <na>(a)</na> recordation of the sabbath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In remembrance that by sinne we lost the rest and peace, which man had in the state of innocencie; secondly we lost the peace of conscience; thirdly the rest and peace of eternal felicitie.

verses.text: LORD <na>(b)</na> rebuke me nor in thy furie: <na>(c)</na> nor chastise me in thy wrath.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Condemne me not to eternal paine:

notes.label: c
notes.text: nor punish me in purgatorie fire; but purge me so in this life, that the purging fire be not needful. By which fire (saith S. Augustin) though some shal be saued ( grauior tamen erit ille ignis, quam quicquid potest homo pati in hac vita) yet that fire shal be more greuous, then whatsoeuer a man can suffer in this llife. S. Gregory also expoundeth this same place, as if Dauid sayd thus: I know it wil come to passe, that after the end of this life, some shal be cleansed by purging flames, some shal be vnder the sentence of eternal damnation. But because I do esteme that transitorie fire more intolerable then al present tribulation, I desire not only not to be rebuked in furie of eternal damnation, but also I feare to be purged in the wrath of transitorie correption. Thou therfore ô Lord whom I serue in my spirite, whom I know to be the Sauiour of al men, rebuke me not in furie of perpetual damnation, nor chatise me in wrath of purging punishment. See Annotat. Psal. 6.

verses.text: Because <na>(d)</na> thy arrowes are fast sticked in me: and thou hast <na>(e)</na> fastened thy hand vpon me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Afflictions of mind and bodie sent by thy iust iudgement.

notes.label: e
notes.text: thou hast strooke me with an heauie hand.

verses.text: There is <na>(f)</na> no health in my flesh, at <na>(g)</na> the face of thy wrath: my bones haue no peace at <na>(h)</na> the face of my sinnes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I already feele in my flesh, in al my bones, and powres great affliction,

notes.label: g
notes.text: considering thy iustice,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and my sinnes.

verses.text: Because mine iniquities are gone <na>(i)</na> ouer my head: and as a <na>(k)</na> heauie burden are become heauie vpon me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: which are excedingly increased, almost ouerwhelming my spirite.

notes.label: k
notes.text: sinnes not washed away by penance by their weight carie the soule into more and more wickednes.

verses.text: My <na>(l)</na> scarres are putrified and corrupted, because of my folishnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: stil corrupting those partes which were whole before, as a pestered sore that is not cured.

verses.text: I am become miserable, and am made <na>(m)</na> crooked euen to the end: I went sorowful al the day.

notes.label: m
notes.text: not able to goe streight to do anie good worke, being guiltie of greuous sinne.

verses.text: Because <na>(n)</na> my loynes are filled with illusions: and there is no health in my flesh.

notes.label: n
notes.text: concupiscence striuing in me.

verses.text: I am afflicted and am humbled excedingly: I <na>(o)</na> rored for the groning of my hart.

notes.label: o
notes.text: from the sorrow of my hart, my voice hath broken out into clamour.

verses.text: Lord, <na>(p)</na> before thee is al my desire: and my groning is not hid from thee.

notes.label: p
notes.text: ô God thou knowest my desire, to be restored to thy fauour.

verses.text: My hart is trubled, my strength hath forsaken me: and the light of mine eies, and the same is not with me.
My <na>(q)</na> frendes, and my neighbores haue approched, & stood against me. And they that were neere me, stood far of:

notes.label: q
notes.text: those that were my freindes and companions in sinne are become myn enemies, because I forsake them:

verses.text: and they did violence which sought my soule. And they that sought me euils, <na>(r)</na> spake vanities: and meditated guiles al the day.

notes.label: r
notes.text: sought by al meanes to intangle me againe.

verses.text: But I as <na>(s)</na> one deafe did not heare: and as one dumme not opening his mouth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: I now renoũce al sinne.

verses.text: And I became as a man not hearing: and not hauing reproofes in his mouth.
Because <na>(t)</na> in thee ô Lord haue I hoped, thou wilt heare me ô Lord my God.

notes.label: t
notes.text: I now relie vpon thee ô God.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Because I said: Lest sometime mine enemies reioyce ouer me: and whiles my feete are moued, they speake great thinges vpon me.

notes.label: v
notes.text: for this cause I am returned to thee and doe pray that mine enemies may not preuail against me.

verses.text: Because I <na>(w)</na> am readie for scourges: and my sorow is in my sight alwaies:

notes.label: w
notes.text: I resigne my selfe to thee.

verses.text: Because <na>(x)</na> I wil declare my iniquitie: and I wil <na>(y)</na> thinke for my sinne.

notes.label: x
notes.text: though thou knowest al yet with mouth confession is made to saluation.

notes.label: y
notes.text: and I meditate of that which my sinne hath deserued.

verses.text: But mine enemies liue, and are confirmed ouer me: and they are multiplied that hate me vniustly.
They that repay euil thinges for good, <na>(z)</na> detracted from me: because I folowed goodnes.

notes.label: z
notes.text: one kind of detraction is in reueling secrete faultes, an other in feaning and imputing false crimes, the third ( here mentioned ) in calling vertue vice, as penance, hypochrisie.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Forsake me not ô Lord my God, depart not from me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Graunt me Lord final perseuerãce in thy grace, and seruice.

verses.text: Attend vnto my help, ô Lord the God of my saluation.

chapters.summary: King Dauid, or anie other penitent, earnestly prayeth God to remitte his sinnes, and mitigate the paines which he acknowledgeth him selfe to haue deserued, 12. lamenting the afflictions which he suffereth by such as sometimes were his freindes, 14. whose tentations he now resisteth, trusting in God, resigning himselfe to Gods wil, confessing his owne iniquitie, and humbly praying for Gods helpe. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The third penitential Psalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, to <na>(b)</na> Idithun him selfe, a canticle of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Some expound this Psalme of the Iewes in captiuitie in Babylon, but this title, and the matter conteyned shew, that it rather peteineth to the new Testament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: to be songue by Idithun and his scholars & successors, or rather by Christianes.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> HAVE said: I wil keepe my waies: that I offend not in my tongue. I haue set a gard to my mouth, when the sinner stood against me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: weake men in affliction not able to deliuer them selues, seeke reuenge, by murmuring and other euil speaches, but the perfect resolue to rule their tongues:

verses.text: I was dumme and humbled, and kept silence <na>(d)</na> from good thinges: and <na>(e)</na> my sorrow was renewed.

notes.label: d
notes.text: euen to forbeare sometimes from their owne iust defence:

notes.label: e
notes.text: though therby they indure more persecution.

verses.text: My <na>(f)</na> hart waxed hote within me: and in my meditation a fyre shal burne.

notes.label: f
notes.text: sorow suppressed maketh the hart to burne with zele, and indignation.

verses.text: I haue spoken in my tongue: Lord <na>(g)</na> make mine end knowne to me. And the number of my daies what it is: that I may know what is lacking to me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: If it may please thee let me know how long I shal liue, desiring to dye; as Elias desired. 3. Reg. 19.

verses.text: Behold thou hast put my daies measurable, and my <na>(h)</na> substance is as nothing before thee. Doubtles al things are vanitie, euerie man liuing.

notes.label: h
notes.text: my life and al that I haue is as nothing compared to thy eternitie.

verses.text: Surely man passeth as <na>(i)</na> an image; yea and he is trubled <na>(k)</na> in vayne. He gathereth treasure; and knoweth not to whom he shal gather them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: as a shadow or image appearing in a glasse, which is quickly forgotte.

notes.label: k
notes.text: therfore there is no cause man should be trubled in mind for temporal miseries.

verses.text: And now what is my expectation? is not our Lord? and my substance is with thee.
From al mine iniquities deliuer me: <na>(l)</na> a reproch to the foolish thou hast geuen me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou hast suffered me to be reproched by the foolish that prosper in this world.

verses.text: I was dumme, and opened not my mouth, <na>(m)</na> because thou didst it:

notes.label: m
notes.text: I know my tribulation is by thy prouidence.

verses.text: Remoue thy scourges from me.
By the strength of thy hand I haue faynted in reprehensions: for iniquitie thou hast chastised man. And thou hast made his <na>(o)</na> soule pyne away as a spider: but vaynly is euerie man trubled.

notes.label: o
notes.text: my life decayeth as a spider hauing spent al her moysture.

verses.text: Heare my prayer ô Lord, and my petition; with thyne eares receiue my teares. Keepe not silence: because I am a <na>(p)</na> stranger with thee, and a pilgrime, as my fathers.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Al men are strangers in this life, heauen being our home.

verses.text: Forgeue me, that I may <na>(q)</na> be refreshed before I depart: and <na>(r)</na> shal be no more.

notes.label: q
notes.text: that I may recouer spiritual streingth in this life:

notes.label: r
notes.text: after which I shal not be in state to do free workes of satisfaction nor merite.

chapters.summary: A iust man in remediles persecution resolueth to suffer al with peace and silence: 5. praying God to take him from this world, confessing the vanitie therof. 8. and relying on Gods prouidence (11. who punisheth man for his sinnes) prayeth for release. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gods prouidence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Redemption of mankind, and to denounce the same in the whole world: 12. prayeth for his seruantes, vndertaking to satisfie for their sinnes. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Christs comming and redeming of mankind The 5 key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Psalme to Dauid himselfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: perteyning vnto the new Testament.

verses.text: EXPECTING <na>(b)</na> I expected our Lord, and he hath attended to me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: the faithful of the old and new Testament reioyce in the coming of Christ.

verses.text: And he heard my prayers, and brought me out of the lake of miserie, and from the myre of dregges. And hath set my feete vpon a rocke: and hath directed my steppes.
And he hath put a new canticle into my mouth: a song to our God. Manie shal see, and shal feare: and they shal hope in our Lord.
Blessed is the man, whose hope is in the name of our Lord: and hath not had regard to vanities and false madnes.

Thou hast done manie thy meruelous thinges ô Lord my God: & in thy cogitations there is none that may be like to thee. I <na>(c)</na> haue declared and haue spoken: they <na>(d)</na> multiplied aboue number.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Christ by him selfe and by others preached the Gospel of saluation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: the multiplication of Christians therby.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Sacrifice and oblation thou wouldest not: but <na>(f)</na> eares thou hast perfited to me. <cr>[1]</cr> Holocaust and for sinne thou didst not require:

notes.label: e
notes.text: No sacrifice of the old testament sufficed to satisfie Gods iustice for the sinne of man.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christ by the eare of obedience performed the redemption of man by his death, as was determined from eternitie. S. Paul for [eares] saith [bodie] See Annotations. Heb. 10.

verses.text: then said I, Behold I come. In the <na>(g)</na> head of the book it is written of me,

notes.label: g
notes.text: The summe of holie Scripture is of Christs Incarnation & death for redemption of man.

verses.text: that I should doe thy wil: my God I would, and thy law in the middes of my hart.
I haue <na>(h)</na> declared thy iustice in the great Church, loe I wil not stay my lippes: Lord thou hast knowen it.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Againe Christ inculcateth the preaching and receiuing of his Gospel in the whole world.

verses.text: Thy iustice I haue not hid in my hart: thy truth and thy saluation I haue spoken. I haue not hid thy mercie, and thy truth from the <na>(i)</na> great councel.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In the greatest and wisest congregations of this world, Christ concealeth not his mercie and truth. So himselfe professed before Annas, Caiphas, Pilate, and their councels. S. Paul preached Christ at Athens, and in manie nations, and so the other Apostles. For their voice went into al the coastes of the earth.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> But thou ô Lord make not thy commiserations farre from me: thy mercie and thy truth haue alwayes receiued me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet now speaketh in the name of Christs mystical bodie the Church: praying to be made partaker of mercie, and to be deliuered from euiles.

verses.text: Because euils haue compassed me, which haue no number: mine iniquities haue ouertaken me, & I was <na>(l)</na> not able to see. They are multiplied aboue the heares of my head: and <na>(m)</na> my hart hath forsaken me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: the sinnes also of those which beleue in Christ are so manie, that they can not be fully sene in particular.

notes.label: m
notes.text: I almost faint in considering so manie and so great iniquities amongst those that professe Christ.

verses.text: It may please thee ô Lord to deliuer <na>(n)</na> me: Lord haue respect to helpe me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The whole Church prayeth in the name of al for the infirme members.

verses.text: Let <na>(o)</na> them be confounded and ashamed together, that seeke my soule, to take it away. Let them be turned backward, and be ashamed that wil me euils.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The prophet foresheweth that the reprobate for their obstinate malice, seeking to hurt others shal be confounded.

verses.text: Let them forthwith receiue their confusion, that <na>(p)</na> say to me: Wel, wel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: that skornfully say: wel, wel: wishing al euil to good men.

verses.text: Let al <na>(q)</na> that seeke thee, reioyce and be glad vpon thee: and let them that loue thy saluation, say alwayes: Our Lord be magnified:

notes.label: q
notes.text: which not only in mouth and outward profession, but also in sinceritie of hart seeke thee, may with confidence reioyce, and praise God.

verses.text: But <na>(r)</na> I am a begger, and poore: Our Lord is careful of me. Thou art <na>(s)</na> my helper, & my protector: my God be not slacke.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Christ speaketh in the name of sinners truly repenting, whose sinnes he vndertaketh to redeme, and wash away by his passion.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The faithful of the old testament pray for Christs first coming into this world, and the faithful now pray for his second coming to purge his Church, and to reward the good.

chapters.summary: Christs faithful members after long expectation congratulate his coming in flesh. 6. He directing his speach to his Father, professeth to performe the

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Psalme to Dauid him selfe. <cr>[1]</cr>

cross_refs.text: Io. 13. v. 18. This Psalm is also applied by the Church in the office of the sick, whom whosoever assisteth in that case, may hope to have assistance in their own like necessity.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new testament, as appeareth by the 10. verse alleaged by our Sauiour. This Psalme is also applied by the Church in the office of the sick, whom whosoeuer assisteth in that case, may hope to haue assistance in their owne like necessitie.

verses.text: BLESSED is the man that vnderstandeth concerning <na>(b)</na> the needie, and the poore: in <na>(c)</na> the euil day our Lord wil deliuer him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He is happie that is not scandalized in Christ (Luc. 7 v. 23.) coming in pouertie, and suffering extreme afflictions.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that trusteth in Christ, notwithstanding the contrarie motiues of his wordlie miserie, shal be deliuered by him in al distresse.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(d)</na> preserue him, and geue him life, and make him blessed in the land: and <na>(e)</na> deliuer him not vnto the wil of his enemies.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Our Lord wil geue to such seruantes more grace in this life, and glorie in the next.

notes.label: e
notes.text: not suffer him to be ouercome in tentations.

verses.text: Our Lord helpe him <na>(f)</na> vpon the bed of his sorow: thou hast turned al his couche in his infirmitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: When such constant seruantes are sick to death, Christ wil most especially comforte and helpe them.

verses.text: I said: <na>(g)</na> Lord haue haue mercie on me: heale my soule, because I haue sinned to thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Christ in the behalf of his mystical bodie confesseth their sinnes, and prayeth for them.

verses.text: Mine enemies haue spoken euils to me: When shal he die, <na>(h)</na> and his name perish?

notes.label: h
notes.text: After death suffered for mankind Christ riseth, and his name and kingdom is glorious.

verses.text: And if <na>(i)</na> he came in to see, he spake vayne thinges: his hart hath gathered together iniquitie to him selfe. He went forth. and spake together.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Those that came not of good wil, but of malice to obserue Christs deedes and wordes, carped at both, sometimes saying, he taught against the law, and against Moyses; sometymes that he cast out diuels in the powre of Beelsebub.

verses.text: Al mine enemies whispered against me: they did thinke euils to me.
They <na>(k)</na> haue determined an vniust word against me: <na>(l)</na> Shal not he that sleepeth adde to ryse againe?

notes.label: k
notes.text: At last they resolued that he should die.

notes.label: l
notes.text: But they could not so suppresse his powre, for he rose againe in glorie.

verses.text: For <na>(m)</na> the man also of my peace, in whom I hoped: who did eate my breades, hath greatly troden me vnder foote <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: m
notes.text: By our Sauiours application of this verse, it is certaine that the traitor Iudas is here described. Ioa. 13. v. 18.

verses.text: But thou ô Lord haue mercie vpon me, and raise me vp againe: and I <na>(n)</na> wil repay them.

notes.label: n
notes.text: in the day of iudgement Christ Iudge of al wil render to euerie one as they deserue.

verses.text: In this I haue knowen that thou wouldest me: because mine enemie shal not reioyce ouer me.
But me thou hast receiued <na>(o)</na> because of innocencie: and thou hast confirmed me in thy sight for euer.

notes.label: o
notes.text: As before in respect of sinners, Christ Iudge of al wil render to euerie one: so here in his owne person he auoucheth his owne innocencie, which made him apt to satisfie for others.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord the God of Israel <na>(p)</na> from the beginning of the world, and for euermore: <na>(q)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: p
notes.text: For this mercie of Almightie God in sauing the elect by his Sonnes death, he is to be praised for euer eternally.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Al the blessed agree in this, that God is eternally to be praised and therto say Amen, So be it, so be it. Some diuide the Psalmes into fiue bookes, supposing the first booke to end here with these wordes; Be it, be it: not obseruing that the last Psalme hath not this ending. S Ierom confuteth this opinion by our Sauiours, and S. Peters naming it the booke, not bookes of Psalmes. Luc 20. v. 42. Act. 1. Moreouer if this were the end of one booke, then the Psalme folowing should not be called the 41. Psalme, but the first Psalme of the second booke.

chapters.summary: The prophet pronounceth them happie that wil beleue in Christ, coming in humilitie and pouertie. 5. Christ describeth his owne poore afflicted state in this life, by reason he is to satisfie for the sinnes of the world; the malice of his aduersaries, 10. especially of Iudas, 11. and by way of prayer, prophecieth his owne Resurrection. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's Passion and Resurrection.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, vnderstanding to the sonnes of <na>(a)</na> Core.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The sonnes of Core repented, and departed from their fathers schisme, and so escaped miraculosly the horrible pitte of damnation, into which their father and his complices fel. Num. 26. v. 10. By which example al seduced, and deceiued Christians are admonished, not to persist in schisme or other sinnes. And wordlie men, ambicious of honour be warned to desire & seke God aboue al thinges, first of al the kingdome of heauen (to be liuing members of the Catholique Church) and the iustice therof: to seke thinges which are aboue, not which are vpon the earth; lest hel deuoure them, as it deuoured the complices of Core. Num. 16 v. 31.

verses.text: EVEN as the harte <na>(b)</na> desireth after the fountaines of waters: <na>(c)</na> so doth my soule desire after thee ô God.

notes.label: b
notes.text: A harte waxing old, and burdened with much heare, and great hornes, draweth a serpent into his nosethrels, so being infected with poyson, desireth most ardently to drinke, and afterwards casteth his hornes, and heare, and becometh as it were yong againe.

notes.label: c
notes.text: with such feruent desire a true penitent, feeling him selfe infected with poysou of sinnes, seeketh the water of Gods grace.

verses.text: My soule hath thirsted after God <na>(d)</na> the strong <na>(e)</na> liuing: <na>(f)</na> when shal I come and appeare before the face of God?

notes.label: d
notes.text: God is omnipotent, and in dede the only-true liuing God: diuels who are honored in idols, can do no more then God permitteth, and so they can kil the soules, that consent vnto their tentations, but can not restore spiritual life againe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: f
notes.text: The soule being iustified, and stil assaulted with new tentations desireth to be with God.

verses.text: My <na>(g)</na> teares haue beene breades vnto me day and night: whiles it is said to me dayly: <na>(h)</na> Where is thy God?

notes.label: g
notes.text: I haue had no other refection, but to lenifie my sorow with weping.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The wicked exprobate the iust, as though God would neuer helpe them, because he suffereth them to be sometimes long in tribulation.

verses.text: These thinges haue I remembred, and haue powred out my soule in me, because I shal passe into the place <na>(i)</na> of a meruelous tabernacle, euen to the house of God. In the yoyce of exultation, and confession: the sound of one feasting.

notes.label: i
notes.text: King Dauid was not permitted to build the temple, much lesse did he enter into anie such meruelous tabernacle in his mortal life, but must nedes be vnderstood, to speake here of the heauenlie tabernacle, prepared by Christ for his seruants.

verses.text: Why <na>(k)</na> art thou sorowful my soule? and why dost thou truble me? Hope in God, because yet I <na>(l)</na> wil confesse to him: the saluation of my countenance,

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet conforteth him selfe, or anie iust soule, in the hope of euerlasting ioy.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I render thankes and praises.

verses.text: and my God. My soule is trubled toward my selfe; therfore wil I be mindful of thee from the land <na>(m)</na> of Iordan, and Hermoniim from the litle mountaine.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Al this life is like to the smal straict place betwene Iordan and a litle hil called Hermoniim; but from this straictnes the hope of the iust is, to be placed in heauen.

verses.text: Depth <na>(n)</na> calleth on depth, in the voice of <na>(o)</na> thy flould-gates. Al thy high thinges, and thy waues haue passed ouer me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: One tentation stil succedeth an other:

notes.label: o
notes.text: and the same so great, as if God opened the gates; and suffered them to ouerflow like fluddes of water.

verses.text: In <na>(p)</na> the day our Lord hath commanded his mercie: and <na>(q)</na> in the night a song of him. With me <na>(r)</na> is prayer to the God of my life:

notes.label: p
notes.text: But God helpeth in opportunitie, not suffering his seruantes to be tempted aboue their streingth, geuing them fruit with tentations:

notes.label: q
notes.text: yea in the greatest tribulation, he geueth ordinarily most comfort, making them sing spiritually in hart, if not also in voice.

notes.label: r
notes.text: one special meanes to procure diuine consolation is prayer in distresse.

verses.text: I wil say to God: Thou art my defender. Why hast thou forgotten me? and why goe I sorowful, whiles mine enemie afflicteth me?
Whiles my bones are broken, mine enemies that truble me haue vpbrayded me: Whiles they say to me day by day: Where is thy God?
Why art thou heauie ô my soule? & why dost thou truble me? <na>(s)</na> Hope in God, because yet I wil confesse to him: the saluation of my countenance, and my God.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Stil the iust soule taketh comforth in assured hope of saluation, the eternal vision of God.

chapters.summary: The feruent desire of the iust, 6. much afflicted in this life, 12. and assured hope of eternal ioy. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal glory.
The 10. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> of Dauid. IVDGE <na>(b)</na> me ô God, & discerne my cause from the nation not holie, from the vniust and deceitful man <na>(c)</na> deliuer me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Holie Dauid often prefiguring Christ, here representeth euerie faithful seruant of God, and particularly when they beginne a great and holie worke; as when Priestes celebrate the diuine Sacrifice, they with their assistantes recite by interchangeable verses this Psalme.

notes.label: b
notes.text: After that we haue examined, and prepared our selues to the most holie Sacrifice and Sacrament, according to S. Paules admonition (let a man proue himselfe, and so eate this bread, and drinke this chalice, 1. Cor. 11.) we pray God, to iudge betwen our true sincere intention, and the vniust deceipful endeuoures of our enimie: and so to deliuer and protect vs from sutle malice.

notes.label: c
notes.text: and so to deliuer and protect vs from sutle malice.

verses.text: Because thou art God <na>(d)</na> my strength: <na>(e)</na> why hast thou repelled me? and why goe I sorowful, <na>(f)</na> whiles the enemie afflicteth me?

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVith thee I can do anie thing, without thee nothing,

notes.label: e
notes.text: thou semest sometimes not to regard me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: whiles tentations are more sensible then thy grace.

verses.text: Send forth <na>(g)</na> thy light and thy truth: <na>(h)</na> they haue conducted me, and haue brought me into thy holy hil, and into thy tabernacles.

notes.label: g
notes.text: As thou hast sent Christ the light and truth into this world, grant vs the same now in particular.

notes.label: h
notes.text: These two giftes of God, the light of knowing our duties and truth, with sincere intention to performe the same, haue brought vs into thy Church, and vnto thy Altar.

verses.text: And <na>(i)</na> I wil goe in to the altar of God: to God, which <na>(k)</na> maketh my youth ioyful.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Accompanied with light of truth, and sincere intention, we confidently approch to thyn Altar ô God,

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvho changest our old corruption into newnes of life.

verses.text: I wil confesse to thee <na>(l)</na> on the harpe <na>(m)</na> ô God <na>(n)</na> my God: <na>(o)</na> why art thou sorowful ô my soule? and dost thou trubel me?

notes.label: l
notes.text: But to this purpose we praise God on the harpe, mortifying our affections.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The former word is of the plural number in hebrevv, Eloim, the other of the singular, signifying the Blessed Trinitie, one God.

notes.label: n
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thou needest not therfore my soule, be pensiue, or desolate.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Hope in God, because yet <na>(q)</na> wil I cõfesse to him: the saluation <na>(r)</na> of my countenance, and <na>(s)</na> my God.

notes.label: p
notes.text: But trust in God,

notes.label: q
notes.text: praise him,

notes.label: r
notes.text: vvhom I hope to see face to face,

notes.label: s
notes.text: the true eternal God.

chapters.summary: The iust inuocateth Gods sentence against the deceiptful, that seeke his spiritual ouerthrow, 4. acknowledgeth his helpe, from almightie God the B. Trinitie, in whose vision glorie consisteth. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
One God the B. Trinity.
The 1. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for the sonnes of <na>(b)</na> Core to vnderstanding.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though this Psalme doth first and literally perteyne to the people of Israel, yet al thinges happening to them, vvere in figure of the Christian Catholique Church, vvhich begane vvith difficulties, aftervvards prospered, and againe suffereth much persecution.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Core signifieth caluus, bauld; also caluaria a scul, or place of sculles: the name of the place vvhere our Sauiour vvas crucified, so the children of Core signifie the children of Christ. S. Aug.

verses.text: O GOD we haue heard with our eares: our fathers haue declared to vs. The <na>(c)</na> worke, that thou hast wrought in their dayes: and in the dayes of old.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The particular calling of Abraham out of Chaldea, protection of him, and Isaac, and Iacob, the deliuerie of al Israel out of Ægypt, and establishing them in the promised land of Chanaan, with innumerable, great, and strange thinges donne for them.

verses.text: Thy hand destroyed the nations, and thou didst plant them: thou didst afflict the peoples, and expel them:

For <na>(d)</na> not by their owne sword did they possesse the land, and their owne arme did not saue them: But thy right hand, and thyne arme, and the illumination of thy countenance: because <na>(e)</na> thou wast pleased in them.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Israelites conquered not by ordinarie povvre, but by the miraculous hand of God.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Not that this people deserued of themselues, but of Gods free election, al the vvorld being vvicked, he gaue peculiar grace to Abraham, Isaac, Iacob and some others, and then for their sakes protected the vvhole people, in them conseruing a visible Church.

verses.text: Thou art the same my king and my God: which commandest the saluations of Iacob.
In <na>(f)</na> thee we shal turne out our enemies with <na>(g)</na> the horne, & in thy name we shal contemne them that ryse vp against vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As in former examples, so in Dauids time, not mans streingth, but Gods hand gaue them great victories.

notes.label: g
notes.text: As an oxe vvith his horne casteth a smal thing into the vvind.

verses.text: For I wil not hope in my bowe: and my sword wil not saue me.
For thou hast saued vs from them that afflict vs: and them that hate vs thou hast confounded. <cr>[1]</cr>
In God we shal be praysed al the day: and in thy name we wil confesse for euer.
But <na>(h)</na> now thou hast repelled and confounded vs: and thou wilt not goe forth ô God in our hostes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The prophet fortelleth that after prosperitie God vvould suffer the Ievves to falle into captiuitie, & manie afflictions, which also signified allegorically diuers states of Christs Church.

verses.text: Thou hast turned vs backe behind our enemies: and they that hated vs, spoyled for themselues.
Thou hast geuen vs as sheepe that are to be eaten: and thou <na>(i)</na> hast dispersed vs among the nations.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The Iewes are now meruelously dispersed, and depressed.

verses.text: Thou hast sold thy people <na>(k)</na> without price: and there was <na>(l)</na> no multitude in the exchanges of them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In the destruction of Ierusalem the remnant of the people were sold for smal, as it wree for no price. They had sold Christ for thirtie pence;

notes.label: l
notes.text: and now no multitude, nor number of money at al was geuen for them, but thirtie of them were sold for one pennie, Iosephus de bello Iudaico.

verses.text: Thou hast made vs a reproche to our neighbours, a scorne and mocking stocke to them, that are round about vs.
Thou hast made vs for a parable to the Gentiles: a wagging of the head among the peoples.
Al the day my shame is against me, and the confusion of my face hath couered me.
At the voyce of the vpbrayder, and the reprocher: at the face of the enemie and persecutor.
Al these thinges haue come vpon vs, <na>(m)</na> neither haue we forgotten thee: and we haue not done wickedly in thy testament.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vntil Christs passion the Iewish people did not wholly fal from God, and true religion. And of them were chosen the Apostles, and manie others, that founded and propagated the Church of Christ.

verses.text: And our hart hath not reuolted backward: and <na>(n)</na> thou hast declined our pathes from thy way:

notes.label: n
notes.text: The negatiue particle is here vnderstood by zeugma, according to the hebrew thus: our hart hath not reuolted backward, neither hast thou suffered our pathes to decline frō thy way.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Because thou hast humbled vs in the place of affliction, and the shadow of death hath couered vs.

notes.label: o
notes.text: An other hebrew phraise, If we haue, for, we haue not.

verses.text: If we haue forgotten the name of our God, and if we haue spred forth our handes to a strange God:
Wil not God enquire of these thinges? For he knoweth the secretes of the hart. Because <na>(p)</na> for thee we are killed al the day: we are estemed as sheepe of slaughter. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: The Prophetes and others persecuted partly before Christ, much more the Apostles, and other Christians in the new Testament:

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Arise why sleepest thou ô Lord? Arise, and expel vs not to the end.

notes.label: q
notes.text: A prayer in affliction.

verses.text: Why dost thou turne away thy face, forgettest our pouertie and our tribulation?
Because <na>(r)</na> our soule is humbled in the dust: our <na>(s)</na> bellie is glewed in the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: we are at deaths dore, readie to become dust.

notes.label: s
notes.text: lying as groueling sorowing on the earth:

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Arise Lord, helpe vs: and redeme vs for thy name.

notes.label: t
notes.text: til thou deliuer vs from these tribulations.

chapters.summary: The prophet describeth the first calling, and difficulte state of the Iewish nation, 6. their prosperitie at other times. 10. Againe their afflictions in captiuitie, and persecutions. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The state of the Jews.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for them, <na>(b)</na> that shal be changed, <na>(c)</na> to the sonnes of Core, <na>(d)</na> for vnderstanding, <na>(e)</na> a Canticle for the beloued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Testament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gentiles conuerted from paganisme to Christianitie:

notes.label: c
notes.text: and al others returning from schisme, or other sinnes,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for their instruction,

notes.label: e
notes.text: this Psalme is a mariage songue of the beloued bridgrome and bride: Christ and his Church.

verses.text: MY <na>(f)</na> hart hath vttered <na>(g)</na> a good word: I tel my workes <na>(h)</na> to the king. My <na>(i)</na> tongue is the penne of a scribe, that <na>(k)</na> writeth swiftly.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I haue receiued by diuine inspirarion in my hart and cogitation,

notes.label: g
notes.text: a most high Mysterie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: To the honour therfore and glorie of this king (vvhom I secretly see in my hart) I vtter and referre al my vvorkes, and this particular Canticle.

notes.label: i
notes.text: From the abundance of my hart, my tongue also speaketh,

notes.label: k
notes.text: & that presently without delay

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Goodly of beautie aboue the sonnes of men, grace is powred abrode in thy lippes: therfore hath God blessed thee for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Description of Christ, most excellent in al internal and external giftes.

verses.text: Be <na>(m)</na> girded with thy sword vpon thy thigh, ô most mightie.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The prophet seing in spirite the perfections vvhich he wisheth in Christ, in maner of congratulating, describeth his fortitude, fighting against the diuel for the Church.

verses.text: With thy beautie and fayrnesse <na>(n)</na> intend, <na>(o)</na> procede prosperously, and <na>(p)</na> reigne, Because of <na>(q)</na> truth, and <na>(r)</na> mildenesse, and <na>(s)</na> iustice: and thy right hand shal conduct thee meruelously.

notes.label: n
notes.text: purposing,

notes.label: o
notes.text: prosecuting,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and perfecting the conquest, and so establishing thy spiritual kingdome.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Not vvith warlike armour of this world, but by assaulting the aduersarie with truth:

notes.label: r
notes.text: defending thyselfe and thy souldiers with the shield of mildnes,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and striking the enemie with the sword of iustice. VVhich right force of spiritual fight hath meruelous good successe.

verses.text: Thy <na>(t)</na> sharpe arrowes, the <na>(v)</na> peoples vnderneth thee shal fal into the hartes of the kings enemies.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Preaching of Christs Gospel, his grace mouing the hartes of the hearers, is liuelie and forcible, more pearcing then anie two edged sword.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The example of people conuerted, shal moue the hartes of the aduersaries to come also vnto the truth.

verses.text: Thy seate ô God <na>(w)</na> for euer and euer: a rod of direction the rod of thy kingdom.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Christs kingdom shal haue no end. Luc. 1. v. 33.

verses.text: Thou <na>(x)</na> hast loued iustice, and hast hated iniquitie: therfore God, <na>(y)</na> thy God, hath annoynted thee with the oile of gladnes <na>(z)</na> aboue thy felowes.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Thou defendest and rewardest the good, finally forsakest and punishest the wicked.

notes.label: y
notes.text: more peculiarly the God of Christ, by hypostatical vnion.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Diuers kinges (as Dauid himselfe, Iosaphat, Ezechias, and Iosias) were as godlie as Salomon, and perseuered good to the end, which is doubted Salomon did not: but Christ incomparably was annointed, & indued with al graces aboue al kinges.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Myrrhe, and <na>(b)</na> Aloes, and <na>(c)</na> Cassia from thy <na>(d)</na> garmentes, from houses of yuorie; out of the which

notes.label: a
notes.text: Mortification which conserueth from putrifying,

notes.label: b
notes.text: humilitie aswaging pride,

notes.label: c
notes.text: being smal in the first spring grovveth great,

notes.label: d
notes.text: humanitie assumpted; and sanctified persons, in vvhom Christ dwelleth as in cleane, shining, odoriferous houses;

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> the daughter of kinges haue delighted thee in thy honour.

notes.label: e
notes.text: sincere faithful soules more deare to their spouse Christ, then daughrers of temporal kinges.

verses.text: The <na>(f)</na> Queene stood on thy right hand in golden rayment: compassed with <na>(g)</na> varietie. <na>(h)</na> Heare daughter, and <na>(i)</na> see, and <na>(k)</na> incline thyne eare: and forget thy people, and the house of thy father.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The Catholique Church, in faith purified as gold:

notes.label: g
notes.text: vvith varietie of states, as Clergie, Laity and diuers sortes of religious Orders, and other professions, al vnited in the same faith, hope, and charitie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: carifully al that Christ thy spouse speaketh to thee by his Spirite.

notes.label: i
notes.text: diligently put the same in practise:

notes.label: k
notes.text: vvith al obedience and readines, and returne not to former infidelitie, nor to corrupt life.

verses.text: And the king <na>(l)</na> wil couet thy beautie: because he is the Lord thy God, and <na>(m)</na> they shal adore him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Christ loueth the Church adorned with his giftes,

notes.label: m
notes.text: and mutually his true children loue and serue him.

verses.text: And the daughters <na>(n)</na> of Tyre with giftes, al the rich of the people shal besech thy countenance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Manie of al nations submitte themselues, and al that they haue to Christ.

verses.text: Al the glorie of that daughter of the king is <na>(o)</na> within, in <na>(p)</na> borders of gold

notes.label: o
notes.text: Internal vertues are most especial ornaments:

notes.label: p
notes.text: exterior are required to edifie others in diuers sortes of vertues.

verses.text: clothed round about with varieties. <na>(q)</na> Virgins shal be brought to the king after her: her <na>(r)</na> neighbours shal be brought to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: By this meanes manie more are conuerted to christianitie:

notes.label: r
notes.text: and one countrie inuiteth and draweth an other.

verses.text: They shal be brought in ioy and exultation: they shal be brought into the temple of the king.
For <na>(s)</na> thy fathers there are borne sonnes to thee: thou shalt make them princes ouer al the earth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: As Apostles came in place of Patriarches and Prophetes: so stil Bishops, and Priestes succede in the Church, pastors, and gouernours therof.

verses.text: They shal <na>(t)</na> be mindeful of thy name in al generation and generation. Therfore shal <na>(v)</na> peoples confesse to thee for euer: and for euer and euer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: These pastores shal stil teach the true Christian doctrin.

notes.label: v
notes.text: and stil there shal be Christian people that wil folow and professe the same.

chapters.summary: Dauid singularly moued in hart and tongue, 3. prophecieth Christs excellencie, indowing his Church with most worthie dowries. 11. by way of exhortation forshewing her internal and external beautie. 17. with perpetual succession of Pastors feeding the flock euen to the worlds end. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ most excellently endowing his Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, to the sonnes of Core, for <na>(b)</na> the secretes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Belonging to the Church of Christ.

notes.label: b
notes.text: As wel the cause, vvhy God suffereth his Church to be persecuted, as his assured protection in difficulties, are hidden secretes to the world.

verses.text: OVr God is a refuge. <na>(c)</na> and strength: an <na>(d)</na> helper in tribulations, which <na>(e)</na> haue found vs excedingly.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al refuge is not secure for one man is not able alwayes to defend an other: but God is a sure and strong refuge.

notes.label: d
notes.text: euer able and in conuenient time vvilling to helpe

notes.label: e
notes.text: This whole vvorld is ful of tribulations, but the Church suffered the greatest in the first persecutions, & shal suffer as great in the time of Antichrist. English Catholiques suffer most of al nations in this age, and can not be suppressed, but stil increase in number and fortitude.

verses.text: Therfore wil we <na>(f)</na> not feare when <na>(g)</na> the earth shal be trubled: and <na>(h)</na> mountaines transported into the hart of the sea.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Therfore al Catholiques may assuredly know, that the whole Church can not faile.

notes.label: g
notes.text: though very manie, as now in England,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and very eminent persons, as some noblemen, and some Priestes haue reuolted, yet al vvil not.

verses.text: Their waters haue sounded, and were trubled: the mountaines were trubled in his strength.
The violence of the riuer <na>(i)</na> maketh the citie of God ioyful: the Highest hath sanctified his tabernacle.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Such bad examples make the good to recollect themselues more diligently, and to reioyce in Gods grace, by which they stand fast.

verses.text: God is in the middes therof, it shal not be moued: God wil helpe it <na>(k)</na> in the morning early.

notes.label: k
notes.text: before the heate of persecution shal inuade al, for the elect the dayes of tribulation are shortned.

verses.text: Nations are trubled, and <na>(l)</na> kingdomes are inclined: he gaue <na>(m)</na> his voice, the earth was moued

notes.label: l
notes.text: Sometimes one nation or kingdome rebelleth against the Church, but can not destroy it.

notes.label: m
notes.text: by the spirite of Christ, Antichrist, and al his members shal be destroyed.

verses.text: The Lord of hostes is with vs: the God of Iacob is our defender.
Come ye, and see the workes of our Lord, what wonders he hath put vpon the earth:
<na>(n)</na> taking away warres euen vnto the end of the earth. He shal destroy bow, & breake weapons: and shields he shal burne with fire.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The Church sometimes hath great peace, and tranquilitie.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Be quiet, and see that I am God: I shal be exalted among the gentiles, and I shal be exalted in the earth.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God himselfe restrayneth the wicked, suddainly abating their furie, or cutting of their forces.

verses.text: The Lord of hostes is with vs: the God of Iacob is our defender.

chapters.summary: The Church in persecution acknowledgeth Gods perpetual defence, 5. making her therby more glorious, 10. sometimes granting rest ( 11. God himself checking the persecuters ) and euer protecting her. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church prospereth also in persecution.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> the sonnes of Core.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Christians that leaue the sinnes of their fathers, and reioyce in Christ crucified: See Annotation. Psal. 41.

verses.text: AL YE Nations <na>(b)</na> clappe handes: make iubilation to God in the voyce of exultation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: True ioy of the hart sheweth it selfe both in voice of exultation, and also in gesture of body, by clapping of handes, dancing ( as king Dauid did before the Arke. 2. Reg. 6.) likevvise vvith instruments.

verses.text: Because our Lord is high, <na>(c)</na> terrible; a great king ouer <na>(d)</na> al the earth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: To al the wicked,

notes.label: d
notes.text: not only of one or few kingdoms, but of al the earth.

verses.text: He hath made peoples subiect <na>(e)</na> to vs: & gentiles vnder our feete.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhen kinges, and countries become Christians, they are made subiectes to the Church that vvas before, not heades and rulers therfore.

verses.text: He hath chosen his inheritance in vs: the beautie of Iacob which he loued.
<na>(f)</na> God is ascended in <na>(g)</na> iubilation: and our Lord in the voice of trumpet.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christ God & man, after his Passion, rose from death and ascended:

notes.label: g
notes.text: not leauing his Church desolate, but making her ioyful by an other comforter the Holie Ghost.

verses.text: Sing ye to our <na>(h)</na> God, sing ye: Sing ye to our <na>(i)</na> king, sing ye.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The same Christ is our God, by his Diuinitie:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and our king by his Humanitie.

verses.text: Because God is king of al the earth: sing ye <na>(k)</na> wisely.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Doe your endeuour to vnderstand vvhat you sing, read, or heare in Gods word. At least to know the principal Mysteries, and pointes of Christian doctrin, euerie one according to their capacitie and state or profession.

verses.text: God shal reigne ouer the gentiles: God sitteth vpon his holie seate.
Princes of peoples are gathered together with <na>(l)</na> the God of Abraham: because the strong <na>(m)</na> goddes of the earth, are excedingly aduanced.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The faithful of the old and nevv Testament are vnited in the seruice of one, and the same eternal God.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In respect of the Blessed Trinitie, holie Scripture here, and in manie places vseth names of the plural number as Eloim Goddes, not diuiding Gods substance, vvhich is one, but insinuating distinction of Diuine Persons. The Father, the Sonne, and the Holie Ghost. VVhich Mysterie is more expresly mentioned in Baptisme, and professed by Christian gentils, then it was by the people of the Ievves.

chapters.summary: Gentiles are called, and inuited to praise God for his magnificence: 6. for Christs Ascension, and powre. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Vocation of Gentiles.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle to the sonnes of Core, the <na>(b)</na> second of the Sabbath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Voices beginning the musike instruments prosecuted;

notes.label: b
notes.text: especially for the second day of the weke, the day after the sabbath, which is our Sunday, called Dominica, our Lords day.

verses.text: GREAT is our Lord, and to be praysed excedingly in <na>(c)</na> the citie of our God, in his holie mount.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Ierusalem, and mount Sion were most obliged to praise God, for greatest benefites receiued, so the Catholique Church therby prefigured, and hauing receiued farre greatter, is most of al bonden to be gratful.

verses.text: Mount Sion is founded with the exultation of <na>(d)</na> the whole earth, <na>(e)</na> the sides of the North, the citie of the great king.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This can not be affirmed of Sion, or Ierusalem, but is only verified of the Catholique Christian Church:

notes.label: e
notes.text: whose coastes do extend to the North, and to al quarters of the round earth.

verses.text: God shal be knowen in <na>(f)</na> the houses therof, <na>(g)</na> when he shal receiue it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The same one God, one Christ, one Faith, and one Religion in al particular Churches of the vvhole militant Church.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And this Vniuersalitie, and Vnitie shal be, after that Christ taking mans nature shal be ascended, and shal send the Holie Ghost, to found & beginne this Church.

verses.text: For behold the kings of the earth <na>(h)</na> were gathered together: they assembled in one.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For the assured certaintie of that is foreshewed, the Prophet speaketh in the pretertence, as if it vvere already done in his time, which he then savv in spirite.

verses.text: They seing it so, were in admiration, were trubled, were moued:
trembling tooke them. Their sorowes <na>(i)</na> as a woman traueling,

notes.label: i
notes.text: Nothing more moueth the hart, & affecteth al the bodie and soule, then spiritual cogitations of faith and religion, and therfore it is compared to a woman traueling with child, who hath most careful and greuous paines.

verses.text: In a vehement spirit <na>(k)</na> thou shalt breake the shippes of Tharsis.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In vvhich great conflict of mans spirite, God by his grace geueth force, to breake through the contrarie assaultes of our enimie, to remoue al impediments, and to ouercome the difficulties.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> As we haue heard, so haue we seene in the citie of the Lord of hostes, in the citie of our God: God hath founded it for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: This consideration that al is now done, that was of old prophecied, is a meruelous confirmation and consolation to Christians.

verses.text: We haue receiued thy mercie, ô God, <na>(m)</na> in the middes of thy temple.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Grace and mercie is only granted to those that are vvithin, or come vnto the Catholique Church.

verses.text: According to thy name ô God, so also is thy prayse vnto the endes of the earth: thy right hand is ful of <na>(n)</na> iustice.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As God is praised for his mercie, so also for his iustice; which do neuer preiudice the one the other.

verses.text: Let mount Sion be glad, and the daughters of Iuda reioyce, because of thy iudgementes ô Lord
Compasse Sion, and embrace ye her: <na>(o)</na> tel ye in her towers.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Consider the fortresses of the Church, which are the holie Fathers, and Doctors, that watch and defend her vvalles.

verses.text: Set your hartes <na>(p)</na> on her strength: and <na>(q)</na> distribute ye her houses, that you <na>(r)</na> may declare it in an other generation.

notes.label: p
notes.text: So rest you assured for al matters of faith in this pillar of truth.

notes.label: q
notes.text: obserue and marke diligently how manie particular Churches were spedely founded in the world,

notes.label: r
notes.text: and declare this to other generations, that they may also hold fast the same faith, or returne vnto it, if they be relapsed; or at last embrace it, if sowner they haue not.

verses.text: Because <na>(s)</na> this is God, our God for euer, and for euer and euer: he <na>(t)</na> shal rule vs euermore.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Christ God incarnate that vvorketh al this, is our very God and Sauiour, not for a few yeares, an hundred, six hundred, or a thousand, but for euer and euer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: he shal rule as a king, and consequently haue a kingdom his militant Church euermore, to the very end of this vvorld. As he shal likevvise haue his triumphant Church in eternitie.

chapters.summary: God most, and euerie where laudable, is especially praised in the Church of Christ ( presigured by Sion, and there begunne ) 9. Al thinges being fulfilled in the Church, euen as they were prophecied, and promised, 12. the faithful are exhorted to consider and congratulate the same. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church founded and protected by God.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> to the sonnes of Core a Psalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In this and diuers other titles, both before and yet ensuing, is said, To the sonnes, or, for the sonnes of Core, a Psalme, or Canticle, or vnderstanding & the like ; but in no place, a Psalme, Canticle &c. of the sonnes of Core, vvhich no way proueth that they vvere the authores of such Psalmes, but rather the contrarie.

verses.text: HEARE these thinges <na>(b)</na> al ye Gentiles: receiue with your eares al ye, that <na>(c)</na> inhabite the earth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al ye nations and sortes of people,

notes.label: c
notes.text: that dwel vpon the earth, lerne this lesson vvhich I wil teach you.

verses.text: Al ye earthly persons, and children of men: together in one the rich and the poore.
My mouth shal speake wisedom, and the meditation of my hart prudence.
I wil <na>(d)</na> incline mine eare vnto a parable: I wil <na>(e)</na> open my proposition <na>(f)</na> on a Psalter.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Holie Dauid harkened to God inspiring him,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and declared to others that vvhich he receiued from God,

notes.label: f
notes.text: not only by his penne or tongue, but also for better instilling it into their mindes he sounded it vpon the instrument called the Psalter, vvhich had tenne stringes, signifying the obseruation of the tenne commandments.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Why shal I feare in the euil day? <na>(h)</na> the iniquitie of my heele shal compasse me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: What especial thing is there in this life, vvhy or for vvhich I or anie haue cause to feare the dreadful day of iudgement?

notes.label: h
notes.text: Marry this we must feare, iniquitie, by which any supplanteth, defraudeth, oppresseth, or anie vvay wrongeth others, for that vvil inuolue the offender in the sentence of eternal damnation.

verses.text: They <na>(i)</na> that trust in their strength: and glorie in the multitude of their riches.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Such be they that trust in their present powre, riches, or other wordlie thing.

verses.text: A <na>(k)</na> brother doth not redeme, <na>(l)</na> man shal redeme: he shal not geue vnto God his reconciliation.

notes.label: k
notes.text: A mans owne brother can not helpe a sinner in that day,

notes.label: l
notes.text: much lesse anie other man; so the Hebrew phraise by zeugma, vnderstandeth an other negatiue particle.

verses.text: And the price of the redemption of his owne soule: and he shal <na>(m)</na> labour for euer,

notes.label: m
notes.text: stil suffer paine,

verses.text: and <na>(n)</na> shal liue yet vnto the end.

notes.label: n
notes.text: and not dye, but liue in eternal torments.

verses.text: He shal not see death, when he shal see <na>(o)</na> the wise dying <na>(p)</na> the vnwise, and <na>(q)</na> the foole shal perish together. And they shal leaue their riches to strangers:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Al both wise and foolish do dye temporally: but the wise liuing in eternal ioy, the foolish liue in eternal paine,

notes.label: p
notes.text: those that beleue not anie other life after this,

notes.label: q
notes.text: and those that beleuing an other life, yet liue badly in this, shal perish in eternal damnation.

verses.text: and their <na>(r)</na> sepulchers their <na>(s)</na> houses for euer. Their Tabernacles in generation and generation: they haue renowmed their <na>(t)</na> names in their landes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: They shal neuer returne from their sepulchers,

notes.label: s
notes.text: to enioy againe their houses and earthlie possessions.

notes.label: t
notes.text: which vainely they labour to establish in their posteritie.

verses.text: And <na>(v)</na> man, when he was in honour, did not vnderstand: he was compared to beasts without vnderstanding, and became like to them.

notes.label: v
notes.text: A most pithie and brief consideration, for man to thinke, how absurdly, he being endewed with reason, vnderstanding, & free wil, like vnto Angels, and capable of eternal glorie, setteth his vvhole studie, and care vpon corporal and temporal thinges, so making himselfe like vnto brute beastes.

verses.text: This their way is <na>(w)</na> a scandal to them: and <na>(x)</na> afterward in their mouth they shal take pleasure.

notes.label: w
notes.text: This care of wordlie thinges is the stumbling block, and cause of eternal ruine:

notes.label: x
notes.text: yet they shal be obstinate, and praise their owne desires, stil persisting therin.

verses.text: As <na>(y)</na> sheepe they are put in hel: death shal feede vpon them. And the iust shal rule ouer them <na>(z)</na> in the morning: and their aide shal waxe old in hel from their glorie.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Amongst other creatures a sheepe can least helpe her selfe in miserie: euen so the damned in hel are altogether vnable to deliuer themselues from thence, or to get any relief,

notes.label: z
notes.text: in the general resurrection they shal be most of al in miserie, as euer dying and neuer dead: the iust vvhom they vvronged, shal be their iudges, al freindes shal faile them, after they haue passed their glorie, and pleasure in this vvorld.

verses.text: Neuerthelesse <na>(a)</na> God wil redeme my soule out of the hand of hel, when he shal take me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The confidence of the iust.

verses.text: Feare not when a man shal be made rich: and when the glory of his house shal be multiplied,
Because when he shal dye, he shal not take <na>(b)</na> al thinges: neyther shal his glorie goe downe with him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He shal leaue al worldlie thinges and take nothing with him.

verses.text: Because his soule in his life shal be <na>(c)</na> blessed: he wil confesse to thee <na>(d)</na> when thou shalt do him good.

notes.label: c
notes.text: temporally:

notes.label: d
notes.text: so long as he enioyeth wordlie profites he wil seme gratful to God;

verses.text: He shal enter in, euen to the progenies of his fathers: and he shal <na>(e)</na> not see light for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: but they shal not see the true light of heauen.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Man, when he was in honour, did not vnderstand: he was compared to beasts without vnderstanding, and became like to them.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Remember and consider ô worldlie man, that God made thee an excellent creature: which thou neglecting makest thyself like to a beast. As, v. 13.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet inuiting al states and sortes of men, to heare him attentiuely, 6 sheweth that al ought to feare eternal damnation, that liue wickedly; 9. vainly and foolishly seeking (13. euen like brute beastes) carnal pleasures, which they can not long enioy, nor long escape hel. 16. confidently animating him selfe, and al good men, that trust not in this world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Exhortation to fly from sin for fear of hell.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> to Asaph. THE <na>(b)</na> God of goddes our Lord hath spoken: and he hath called the earth, from the rysing of the sunne euen to the going downe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: To be songue or tuned by Asaph a maister of musike.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God almightie, who is greater then are al falsly supposed goddes, or holie persons, that participating of his goodnes are called goddes (as Kinges, Priestes, Iudges) coming into this world in mans nature, calleth al men to saluation.

verses.text: Out <na>(c)</na> of Syon the beauty of his comelines.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Church of Christ began in Sion.

verses.text: God wil come <na>(d)</na> manifestly: our God and he wil not kepe silence. <na>(e)</na> Fire shal burne forth in his sight: and round about him a mighty tempest.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Christ that came in humilitie, and more obscurely to suffer, and to redeme vs, wil come in maiestie, and manifestly to iudge.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Immediately before the general iudgement, fire shal burne al transitorie thinges.

verses.text: He shal <na>(f)</na> cal the heauen from aboue: and <na>(g)</na> the earth to discerne his people.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Geue signes in the firmament,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and in earth.

verses.text: Gather ye together his saincts vnto him: which ordaine his testament <na>(h)</na> aboue sacrifices.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Which know that to keepe Gods commandments in folowing vertues, is aboue the oblation of external sacrifice.

verses.text: And the heauens shal shew forth his iustice: because God is Iudge.
<na>(i)</na> Heare ô my people, and I wil speake: Israel, and I wil testifie to thee: God thy God am I.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God instructeth his people.

verses.text: I wil not rebuke thee in thy sacrifices: and thy holocaustes <na>(k)</na> are in my sight alwaies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Sacrifices are gratful to God.

verses.text: I wil <na>(l)</na> not take calues out of thy house: nor buckegoats out of thy flockes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: but in regard that God needeth not these earthly thinges, he rather requireth a gratful mind. For otherwise man in dede can geue nothing to God: seing al that is in the whole world is Gods owne in proprietie.

verses.text: Because al the wilde beasts of the woods be myne, the cattle in the mountaines and oxen.
I haue knowne al the foules of the ayer: and the beauty of the fielde is with me.
If I shal be hungrie, I wil not tel thee: for the round earth is myne, and the fulnes therof.
Wil I eate the flesh of oxen? or wil I drinke the blood of buckegoats?
<na>(m)</na> Immolate to God the sacrifice of praise, and <na>(n)</na> pay thy vowes to the Highest.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Spiritual sacrifice of prayse.

notes.label: n
notes.text: & due payment of voluntarie vowes made in honour of God,

verses.text: And <na>(o)</na> inuocate me in the day of tribulation: I wil deliuer thee, and thou shalt glorifie me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: and praying to him for helpe in tribulation are most gratful.

verses.text: But to the sinner God hath sayde: <na>(p)</na> Why doest thou declare my iustices, and takest my testament by thy mouth?

notes.label: p
notes.text: He that wil teach others, must especially flee from sinne, & serue God sincerly.

verses.text: But thou hast hated discipline: & cast my words behind thee.
If thou didst see a theese, thou didst rune with him: and with adulterers thou didst put thy portion.
Thy mouth hath abounded with malice: and thy tongue fourged guiles.
Sitting thou spakest against thy brother, and against thy mothers sonne thou didst put a scandal:
these things hast thou done, and I haue held my peace. Thou hast thought vniustly that I wil be like thee: I wil reproue thee, and set it against thy face.
Vnderstand these things you that forget God: lest sometime he take you violently and there be none to deliuer you.
The sacrifice of prayse <na>(q)</na> shal glorifie me: and there is the way, by which I wil shew him the saluation of God.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God is honored by mans gratitude, and other good workes.

chapters.summary: Christ in his first coming calleth al Nations. 3. in his second wil iudge the world. 7. In the meane time God exhorteth al men to serue him in puritie of vertue, which he much preferreth before external sacrifice of the old law. 17. reprehending such as professe or teach the right way, and liue wickedly. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
General Judgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Psalme of Dauid, <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Pertayning not only to Dauid, but also to al penitentes, especially of the new testament

verses.text: when Nathan the Prophet came to him, after that he had sinned with Bethsabee. (2. Reg. 12.)
HAVE mercie on me ô God, <na>(b)</na> according to thy great mercie. And according <na>(c)</na> to the multitude of thy commiserations, take away myne iniquitie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: My sinnes being very great, nede thy great mercie.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yea manie sortes of thy mercies: not only remission of the crimes, but also mitigation of the paines due for the same. Thy merciful grace to be truly sorie, to make some part of satisfaction, to beware hereafter not to fal againe, to geue better example of penance, and of vertuous life, and to perseuer to the end.

verses.text: Wash me <na>(d)</na> more amply from mine iniquitie: & <na>(e)</na> cleanse me from my sinne.

notes.label: d
notes.text: O God thou hast forgeuen me, and taken away my sinnes, as thy prophet hath told me (2. Reg. 12. v. 13.) but my soule so fouly polluted, nedeth yet more washing.

notes.label: e
notes.text: cleanse also the dregges that remaine, and al habites and inclinations to sinne. So our Sauiour afterwards taught. (Ioan. 13. v. 10.) He that is washed nedeth not sauing to wash his feete (il affections and reliques of former sinnes) but is cleane wholy.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Because I do know myne iniquitie: and my sinne is <na>(g)</na> before me alwaies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: VVhiles I did not know; not consider nor acknowledge my sinnes, I could not be forgeuen, but now I know and acknowledge them:

notes.label: g
notes.text: and I cease not to consider of them with sorow.

verses.text: To thee <na>(h)</na> onely haue I sinned, and haue done euil before thee: that thou mayst <na>(i)</na> be iustified in thy words, and mayst <na>(k)</na> ouercome when thou art iudged.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Principally (for so this particle [only] here signifieth) the enormities of my sinnes consist, in that I haue offended thy Diuine Goodnes and Maiestie, the King of the worldes, immortal, inuisible, onlie God, to whom is due al honour and glorie for euer and euer. 1. Tim. 1. v. 17.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou which hast promised forgeuenes to al sinners that truly conuert, shal herein be iustified by receiuing me againe to grace:

notes.label: k
notes.text: and ouerthrow thy calumniators, that iudge wickedly of thy proceedings, as if either thy iustice or mercie were peruerted.

verses.text: For behold I <na>(l)</na> was conceiued in iniquities: & my mother conceiued me in sinnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I and al are borne in original sinne, the reliques wherof, concupiscence and weakenes incline vs to other sinnes, which we haue added. In regard of which our infirmitie, thy mercie is readie to recal vs, and help vs.

verses.text: For behold thou <na>(m)</na> hast loued truth: <na>(n)</na> the vncertaine, and hidden thinges of thy wisdome thou hast made manifest to me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Besides thou hast also geuen me knowledge of true faith, and right doctrine, which thou euer louest, and art accustomed to reduce, and direct such into the true way of penance.

notes.label: n
notes.text: yea thou hast moreouer shewed to me thinges vncertaine, or vnknowen to manie others, geuen me the gift and spirit of prophecie, to know hidde mysteries, and to euerie one God geueth some particular benefites, which he loueth in him, and is ready of his part to confirme and maintaine the same, that they be not lost.

verses.text: Thou shalt sprinkle me with <na>(o)</na> hyssope, and I shal be clensed: thou shalt wash me, and I shal be made <na>(p)</na> whiter then snow.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Most merciful Lord thou wilt (as I see in the spirit of prophecie) sprinkle me, and al men with thy bloud, from the Crosse, where they shal geue thee vinegre about hyssoppe to drinke. (Ioan. 19.)

notes.label: p
notes.text: by which washing I shal be cleane from sinne, and become in time pure, yea whiter then snow. A figure of this hyssope was obserued in Moyses Law. Num. 19. signifying the liuelie heat of Christs infinite charitie.

verses.text: To <na>(q)</na> my hearing thou shalt geue ioy and gladnes, and <na>(r)</na> the bones humbled shal reioyce.

notes.label: q
