notes.text: When myn affections shal be cleane purged, I shal take singular great delight to heare of thee,

notes.label: r
notes.text: and al my powres of mind and bodie, which are now afflicted, shal reioyce.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Turne away thy face from my sinnes: and wipe away al mine iniquities.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Leaue of thy cogitation of punishing, to which purpose first take away myn iniquities, for otherwise if they remaine, Gods iustice can not but punish them.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Create a cleane hart in me ô God: and renew a right spirit in my <na>(v)</na> bowels.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Create in me new grace, wherby my hart shal be pure. So S. Paul calleth a iust soul a new creature. Galat. 6. v. 15.

notes.label: v
notes.text: In my inward thoughtes.

verses.text: Cast me not away from thy face: and thy Holie spirit <na>(w)</na> take not from me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: suffer me not so to fal againe, that thy grace depart from me.

verses.text: Render vnto me <na>(x)</na> the ioy of thy saluation? and <na>(y)</na> confirme me with the principal spirit,

notes.label: x
notes.text: which I had before my fal, of Christ promised of my seede, and alter not the same for my sinnes. Dauid also and other penitents pray here, that God wil restore vnto them the ioy, which they had in the state of grace, of eternal saluation promised;

notes.label: y
notes.text: confirme & conserue in me hereafter, a strong, constant, and willing spirite to perseuere.

verses.text: I <na>(z)</na> wil teach the vniust thy waies: and the impious shal be conuerted to thee.

notes.label: z
notes.text: No way can a penitent better shew him self gratful to God, for remission of his sinnes, then by instructing, exhorting, and perswading other sinners to repentance, to leaue their former il wayes, and turne to God.

verses.text: Deliuer me <na>(a)</na> from bloudes ô God, the God of my saluation: and my tongue shal exult [for] thy iustice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: From the guilt and punishment of murder, causing Vrias and others with him to be slaine. Other penitents pray to be deliuered from what sinnes soeuer they haue committed, by sheding bloud, or other wrongs and iniuries; promising to praise Gods iustice, in offering and geuing grace, according to his promise to sinners, that they may repent.

verses.text: Lord, thou <na>(b)</na> wilt open my lippes: & my mouth shal shew forth thy prayse.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Thou ô God first stirring me vp, opening my lippes, which of my selfe I can not do, then my tongue and mouth wil praise thee.

verses.text: Because if thou <na>(c)</na> wouldest haue had sacrifice, I had verily giuen it: with holocaustes thou wilt <na>(d)</na> not be delighted.

notes.label: c
notes.text: If thou wouldest especially legal sacrifice, I would easily haue offered great store:

notes.label: d
notes.text: but the best of that kind is not sufficient:

verses.text: A sacrifice to God is <na>(e)</na> an afflicted spirit: a contrite, and humbled hart, ô God thou wilt not despise.

notes.label: e
notes.text: true contrition of hart pleaseth thee farre better.

verses.text: Deale fauorably ô Lord in thy good wil <na>(f)</na> with Sion: that the walles of Ierusalem may be built vp.

notes.label: f
notes.text: After a penitent hath remission of his owne sinnes, he must pray for the whole Church.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Then shalt thou accept sacrifice of <na>(h)</na> iustice, <na>(i)</na> oblations, & <na>(k)</na> holocaustes: <na>(l)</na> then shal they lay calues vpon thyne altar.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The Church prospering, her faithful children shal offer

notes.label: h
notes.text: the sacrifice of iustice, rendering to euerie one that is due;

notes.label: i
notes.text: also free offeringes without obligation,

notes.label: k
notes.text: yea holocaustes, which is the chiefest,

notes.label: l
notes.text: calues, and like hostes vpon the altar, according to the state of the old law: but in the law of Christ, the most B. Sacrifice by him instituted.

chapters.summary: King Dauid in great sorow for his sinnes of adulterie and murder, most seriously prayeth God of his manifold mercies to remitte and purge al his offences, and paines due for them. 12. to restore vnto him the grace of the Holie Ghost, lost by his sinnes; 15. that he may teach others (as in deede his singular example may teach the whole world true penance) 19. contrition of hart, worthely to offer sacrifice, for the whole Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The fourth penitential Psalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, vnderstanding to Dauid,
when Doeg <na>(a)</na> the Idumeite came and told Saul: Dauid is come into the house of <na>(b)</na> Achimelech. (1. Reg. 22.) <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Of the race of Esau, half a Iew, but either an Infidel, or fautor of Infidels, a spie for Saul, a persecutor of Dauid, & a murderer of Innocents. 1. Reg. 22. v. 9. 18.

notes.label: b
notes.text: High priest, slaine with 84. more Priestes and others, because they were supposed to fauour Dauid. ibidem.

verses.text: WHY doest thou <na>(c)</na> glorie in malice, which art mightie in iniquitie?

notes.label: c
notes.text: Thou persecutor Doeg, why art thou so malicious, to abuse thy credite with king Saul, to the murdering of innocents?

verses.text: Al the day hath thy tongue thought iniustice: as a sharp rasor thou <na>(d)</na> hast done guile.

notes.label: d
notes.text: playing the part of a spie, in betraying to Saul, that I was with Achimelech?

verses.text: Thou hast loued malice more then benignitie: <na>(e)</na> iniquitie rather then to speake equitie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Though he told a truth, yet it was iniquitie to betray innocents.

verses.text: Thou hast loued al wordes of precipitation, a deceitful tongue.
Therfore Wil God destroy thee for euer, he wil <na>(f)</na> plucke thee out, & remoue thee out of thy tabernacle: & <na>(g)</na> thy roote out of the land of the liuing.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Thou shalt vtterly be destroyed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: & al thy race.

verses.text: The iust shal see, and feare, and shal laugh at him, and they shal say:
Behold the man, that hath not put God for his helper. But hath hoped in the multitude of his riches, and hath <na>(h)</na> preualed in his vanitie.

notes.label: h
notes.text: for a short time in this world.

verses.text: But I as <na>(i)</na> a fruitful oliue tree in the house of God, haue hoped in the mercie of God for euer: and for euer and euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Dauid prophecieth his owne exaltation, and conseruation of his seede in the kingdom of Israel.

verses.text: I wil <na>(k)</na> confesse to thee for euer, because thou hast done it: and I wil expect thy <na>(l)</na> name, because it is good in the sight of thy saints:

notes.label: k
notes.text: sing praise, and thankes to thee.

notes.label: l
notes.text: thy Goodnes, which agreeth to thy name.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid inueigheth against wicked Doeg a traitor. 7. prophecieth his ruine. 10. and his owne exaltation. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's invective against Doeg.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Maeleth; <na>(b)</na> vnderstandings of Dauid. THE foole hath said in his hart: There is no God.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Weakenes, or mourning,

notes.label: b
notes.text: S. Augustin expoundeth this Psalme as an instruction to those that suffer persecution and iniuries, especially nere the end of the world.

verses.text: They are corrupte, and become abominable in iniquities: there is not that doth good.
God hath looked forth from heauen, vpon the children of men: to see if there be that vnderstandeth, or seeketh after God.
Al haue declined, they are become vnprofitable together: there is not that doth good, no there is not one.
Shal they not al know that worke iniquitie, that deuoure my people as food of bread?

God they haue not inuocated: there haue they trembled for feare, where no feare was. Because God hath <na>(c)</na> dissipated the bones of them <na>(d)</na> that please men: they are confounded, because God hath despised them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God wil ouerthrow al the counsels, and forces

notes.label: d
notes.text: of worldlie politiques.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Who wil geue out of Sion the saluation of Israel? when God shal conuert the captiuitie of his people: Iacob shal reioyce, and Israel shal be glad.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The true Church afflicted desireth Christs coming to deliuer the oppressed.

chapters.summary: As in the thirtenth Psalme, Christs Incarnation is prophecied, after that sinne abunded in the world: so here is foreshewed that after general wickednes, 5. Christ wil come to iudge the bad, 7. and deliuer the good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The general Iudgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> in songs vnderstanding for Dauid

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though historically this Psalme

notes.label: b
notes.text: was song by Dauid the author therof, shewing how he prayd in danger, and rendered thankes for his deliuerie,

verses.text: when the Zipheites were come, and said to Saul: <na>(c)</na> Is not Dauid hid with vs? (1. Reg. 1. 23. & 26.) <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: c
notes.text: when vpon notice geuen that he abode in the mountaines, Saul straictly beseged him, with a great armie, but the Philistims inuading the countrie, Saul was forced to leaue Dauid, and to turne his forces against them, 1. Reg. 23. yet it perteyneth also literally to al iust men in distresse, especially to the Church of Christ, praying in like dangers, and God by his like prouidence, deliuering his seruantes in extremities.

verses.text: O GOD saue me <na>(d)</na> in thy name: and in thy strength <na>(e)</na> iudge me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: For the glorie of thy name

notes.label: e
notes.text: for the iustnes of my cause defend me.

verses.text: O God heare my prayer with thine eares: receiue the words of my mouth.
Because <na>(f)</na> strangers haue risen vp against me, & the strong haue sought my soule: and they haue not set God before their eies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Barbarous highland men haue betraide the place of myne abode to the persecuters.

verses.text: For <na>(g)</na> behold God helpeth me: and our Lord is the receiuer of my soule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: But I feare them not, because I am in Gods protection.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Turne away the euils to mine enimies: and in <na>(i)</na> thy truth destroy them.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A iust prayer, that God wil turne intended mischief, vpon the deuisers heades,

notes.label: i
notes.text: according to his promise, that he wil defend the innocent.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> I wil voluntarily sacrifice to thee, and <na>(l)</na> wil confesse to thy name ô Lord, because it is good:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Offering voluntarie sacrifice, more then is commanded:

notes.label: l
notes.text: and praise thee ô God,

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Because thou hast deliuered me out of al tribulation: and <na>(n)</na> mine eie hath looked downe vpon mine enimies.

notes.label: m
notes.text: as I am bond

notes.label: n
notes.text: I reioyce in thy iust iudgements against the wicked.

chapters.summary: Dauid in distresse crieth to God for helpe, 6. confidently trusting therin, 8. and promising sacrifice of thankesgeuing. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in distress.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> in songes, <na>(c)</na> vnderstanding to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A song as wel for king Dauid himselfe, as others of al times;

notes.label: b
notes.text: to sing,

notes.label: c
notes.text: and consider Gods prouidence, in suffering one man to afflict an other in this life.

verses.text: HEARE my prayer ô God, despise not my petition,
Attend to me; and heare me.

I am made sorowful in my <na>(d)</na> exercise: and am trubled at the voice of the enimie: and at the tribulation of the sinner. Because they haue <na>(e)</na> wrested iniquities vpon me: & <na>(f)</na> in anger they were trublesome to me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This life is a warefare, and a continual combate.

notes.label: e
notes.text: calumniated me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: and persecuted me in great furie.

verses.text: My hart is trubled in me: and <na>(g)</na> the feare of death is falne vpon me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: so inwardly afflicted, as if death were at hand.

verses.text: Feare and trembling are come vpon me: and <na>(h)</na> darkenes hath couered me.

notes.label: h
notes.text: I haue scarse sense, or discourse of reason, being almost ouerwhelmed with trubles.

verses.text: And I said: <na>(i)</na> Who wil geue me wings as of a doue, and I wil fly: and rest?

notes.label: i
notes.text: would God I could flie, that in the simplicitie of a doue, I might spedely part away from these afflictions.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Loe I haue gone far flying away: and I abode in the wildernes.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I haue fled so farre as I could from trubles:

verses.text: I <na>(l)</na> expected him, that <na>(m)</na> saued me from <na>(n)</na> pusillanimitie of spirit, and <na>(o)</na> tempest.

notes.label: l
notes.text: for the rest I remitted to Gods wil and good pleasure,

notes.label: m
notes.text: and he suffered me not to be ouerthrowne,

notes.label: n
notes.text: though I am weake,

notes.label: o
notes.text: and the tentations are great.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Precipitate ô Lord, and <na>(q)</na> diuide their tongues: because I haue sene <na>(r)</na> iniquitie, and <na>(s)</na> contradiction in the citie.

notes.label: p
notes.text: O God abate the pride of arrogant persecuters,

notes.label: q
notes.text: suffer them not to agree amongst them selues.

notes.label: r
notes.text: They are ful of al iniquitie,

notes.label: s
notes.text: they haue also contentions among themselues, turne the same to our good.

verses.text: Day and night shal iniquitie compasse it vpon the walles therof; and <na>(t)</na> labour in the middest therof, and <na>(v)</na> iniustice.

notes.label: t
notes.text: VVith their continual great iniquitie, they haue their trubles,

notes.label: v
notes.text: but leaue not their iniustice.

verses.text: And there hath not ceased out of the streetes therof <na>(w)</na> vsurie, and guile.

notes.label: w
notes.text: They are stil vsurers, and deceiptful oppressors of the poore.

verses.text: For <na>(x)</na> if myne enimie had spoken euil to me, I would verely haue borne it. And if he that hated me had spoken great thinges vpon me: I would perhaps haue hid myselfe from him.

notes.label: x
notes.text: It is a greater griefe to suffer iniuries of those that seme to be freindes.

verses.text: But <na>(y)</na> thou a man of the same minde: my <na>(z)</na> guide, and my familiar.

notes.label: y
notes.text: A man that was, or semed of the same mind, faith, and religion,

notes.label: z
notes.text: whom I so trusted, that I would haue gone, whithersoeuer he should haue ledde me.

verses.text: Which diddest <na>(a)</na> take swete meats together with me, in the <na>(b)</na> house of God we walked with consent.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Thou that didst participate the same holie sacraments with me,

notes.label: b
notes.text: in the Catholique Church.

verses.text: Let <na>(c)</na> death come vpon them: and let them goe downe quicke into hel. Because there is wickednes in their habitations, in <na>(d)</na> the middes of them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As Core & his complices: spoken of iust zele, not of desire to reuenge: verified in those that sinne wittingly and knowing, for they descend, as it were, aliue into hel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The whole crew of the wicked conspire in iniquitie.

verses.text: But I haue cried to God, and our Lord wil saue me.
In <na>(e)</na> the euening, and morning, & at midday, I wil <na>[1]</na> speake, and declare, and he wil heare my voice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The prophet alludeth to three more specially appointed houres of Diuine seruice, the daylie sacrifice at morning, and euening, and other sacrifices commonly about midday. VVhich also are the three principal times of Diuine Seruice in the Church of Christ. Mattins, Euensong, and the Sacrifice of Masse. VVhich Eutymius and other Grecians cal Lyturgiam. S. Clement also (li 7. c. 25. Apost. Instit) testifieth that the Apostles ordained three set houres of common prayer euerie day.
* or pray

verses.text: He wil redeme my soule in peace from them, that approch to me: because among manie <na>(f)</na> they were with me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Manie enimies combined together approched vnto me, to ouerthrow me.

verses.text: God wil heare, and he <na>(g)</na> which is before the worldes wil humble them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Eternal God.

verses.text: For there is <na>(h)</na> no change with them, & they feared not God: he hath streached forth his hand in repaying.

notes.label: h
notes.text: They wil neuer repent of their wickednes.

verses.text: They haue contaminated his testament, they are <na>(i)</na> diuided by the wrath of his countenance; and <na>(k)</na> his hart hath approched. <na>(l)</na> His wordes are made softer then oile: and <na>(m)</na> the same are dartes.

notes.label: i
notes.text: They harden their hartes against his threatned wrath:

notes.label: k
notes.text: but Gods prouidence illuminateth others to know and teach the truth, whȇ it is impugned, or contemned.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Gods wordes, which in them selues are meke and swete,

notes.label: m
notes.text: are hard to the incredulous, & as dartes that wound them. Christ said (Ioan. 6.) Vnles one eate my flesh, & drinke my bloud, he shal not haue life in him, which the Capharnaites not vnderstanding said one to an other: This is a hard speach, who can abide it? which S. Augustin here saith was the first heresie against our Sauiours preaching. It was not hard to S. Peter, who in the name of the rest, answered, that Christ had the wordes of eternal life. He yet vnderstood not the secrete of our Lords speach, but he piously beleued that the wordes vvere good, vvhich he vnderstood not.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Cast thy care vpon our Lord: and he wil nourish thee: he wil not geue <na>(o)</na> fluctuation to the iust for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Therfore in al doubtes of doctrin, in al distresses of persecution, and other difficulties vvhich surpasse thy vveakenes, cast thy care vpon our Lord, and he vvil nourish thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: He vvil not suffer the iust to remaine alvvayes in fluctuation, that is, in doubtful, dangerous, and vvanering thoughtes or perplexities, as vvhen a shippe is tossed in the vvaues of the sea, but vvil geue quiet repose of mind, as in a sure hauen vvithout danger of drovvning.

verses.text: But thou ô God wilt bring <na>(p)</na> them downe into the pitte of destruction. <na>(q)</na> Bloudy and deceitful men shal not liue halfe their daies. but I wil hope in thee ô Lord.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Coatrariwise, the wicked and obstinate shal fal into destruction.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Often or for most part, bloud-suckers dye before the course of nature requireth, as Saul, Absolon, Achitophel, Achab, Iezabel, and the like.

chapters.summary: The prophet (as wel in his owne, as other iust mens person) describeth great calamities suffered, 10. praieth against the wicked, 13. Lamenting especially that those which professe frendshipe, are aduersaries. 17. and declareth Gods prouidence in protecting the good, and destroying the bad. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence towards the good and bad.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> for a people, that is made far from the Sainctes, Dauid in <na>(c)</na> the inscription of the title, <na>(d)</na> when the foreners held him in Geth. (1. Reg. 12. v. 12.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme perteyneth also to future times,

notes.label: b
notes.text: for the vse of anie iust persons, or people, that are against their wil seperated from the publike diuine Seruice of holie Church :

notes.label: c
notes.text: most worthie to be noted with title, for perpetual memorie,

notes.label: d
notes.text: made by Dauid when the Philistims detected him to their king in Geth.

verses.text: HAVE mercie on me ô God, because <na>(e)</na> man hath troden vpon me: <na>(f)</na> al the day impugning he hath afflicted me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Now one sorte of il disposed men, now an other,

notes.label: f
notes.text: neuer cease to seeke my destruction.

verses.text: Myne enimies haue troden vpon me al the day: because they are <na>(g)</na> manie that warre against me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Saul with his great armie, the Philistimes, and other strangers, some in manifest hostilitie, others detecting and betraing me to myn aduersaries. So al that liue godly in Christ haue manie enimies visible and inuisible,

verses.text: From <na>(h)</na> the height of the day I shal feare: <na>(i)</na> but I wil trust in thee.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Of these most eminent great dangers I am in deede afeard,

notes.label: i
notes.text: but so that my trust and assured confidence is in thee ô God.

verses.text: In God I wil praise <na>(k)</na> my wordes, in God haue I hoped: I wil not feare what flesh may do to me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Wordes and promises made to me; or the good which I speake or do by Gods grace.

verses.text: Al the day did they <na>(l)</na> detest my wordes; against me, <na>(m)</na> al their cogitations are vnto euil.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They calumniate whatsoeuer I say,

notes.label: m
notes.text: wresting al my wordes to euil sense.

verses.text: They wil <na>(n)</na> inhabite and keepe secret: they wil obserue my heele. As they haue expected <na>(o)</na> my soule,

notes.label: n
notes.text: They meete together, and secretly conspire to intreppe me or catch me tripping.

notes.label: o
notes.text: to take my life:

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> for nothing shalt thou saue them: <na>(q)</na> in wrath thou wilt breake peoples. O God,

notes.label: p
notes.text: for this their vaine purpose to destroy me, thou wilt saue them, as they deserue, that is,

notes.label: q
notes.text: thou wilt breake them in peeces.

verses.text: I haue shewed my life to thee: thou hast set my teares in thy sight. As also in thy promise:
then shal mine enemies be turned backward. In what day soeuer I shal inuocate thee: loe I haue knowne that thou art my God.
In God I wil praise <na>(r)</na> the word, in our Lord wil I praise thee saying, I haue hoped in God, I wil not feare what man can do to me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: I wil alwayes gratfully acknowlege thy promises, and sayings, for they are assured.

verses.text: In me, ô God <na>(s)</na> are thy vowes, which I wil render, praises to thee.

notes.label: s
notes.text: I haue purposed and vowed to offer sacrifice of praise, and by thy helpe wil performe it.

verses.text: Because thou hast deliuered my soule from death, and my feete from falling: that I may <na>(t)</na> please before God, in <na>(v)</na> the light of the liuing.

notes.label: t
notes.text: do that pleaseth God,

notes.label: v
notes.text: in true faith and pious workes.

chapters.summary: Dauid being in danger before Achis king of Geth, confidently imploreth Gods helpe, against the great malice and powre of his enimies; 8. foresheweth their ruine, his owne exaltation, 12. and offereth praises and thankes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's prayer in danger.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> destroy not, to Dauid in <na>(c)</na> the inscription of the title; <na>(d)</na> when he fled from the face of Saul into the caue. (1.Reg.22.24.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: The heroical facts of Dauid are for examples to al Christians.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Innocent Dauid hauing opportunitie to kil his vniust persecutor, obeyed the motion of God, suggesting vnto him, not to destroy his enimie; contrarie to the counsel of his freindes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: a thing most worthie to be recorded for perpetual memorie,

notes.label: d
notes.text: being in so great and vniust truble, as to lye in the caue of a mountaine, yet spared to kil, or hurt him, that driue him into such straictes. See the historie 1. Reg. 24.

verses.text: HAVE mercie on me ô God, haue mercie on me: because my soule hath trusted in thee. And I wil hope in the shadow of thy winges, vntil iniquitie passe.
I wil crie to God the highest: God that hath done me good.
He sent <na>(e)</na> from heauen, and deliuered me: he hath geuen into <na>(f)</na> reproche them that trode vpon me. God hath sent his mercie, and his truth,

notes.label: e
notes.text: Extraordinarie diuine helpe, passing mans powre.

notes.label: f
notes.text: It fel reprochfully to Saul, that Dauid might haue slaine him if he would, yet did neither hurt him, nor insult vpon him, but meekely and piously admonished him of his error, and iniurious persecution.

verses.text: and hath deliuered my <na>(g)</na> soule out of the middes of <na>(h)</na> Lions whelpes: I slept trubled. The sonnes of men, their <na>(i)</na> teeth are weapons and arrowes: and their <na>(k)</na> tongue a sharpe sword.

notes.label: g
notes.text: my life.

notes.label: h
notes.text: from most mightie and rauenous persecuters.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Though they haue not lions natural teeth, yet they exercise crueltie by artificial weapons,

notes.label: k
notes.text: and with their cruel tongues incite their folowers to the same furie. 1. Reg. 22. 7. 16.

verses.text: Be exalted aboue the heauens ô God: and thy glorie vpon al the earth.
They prepared a snare for my feete: and bowed downe my soule. They <na>(l)</na> digged a pit before my face: and they are falne into it.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Saul endeuored manie wayes to ouerthrow Dauid, amongst other meanes prouoked him to sette vpon the Philistims, thincking they should haue slaine him, 1. Reg. 18. v. 17. but the same Philistims ouerthrew Saul. 1 Reg. 31.

verses.text: My hart is readie ô God, my hart is readie: I wil sing, and say <na>[1]</na> a Psalme.

notes.text: Psalmes more in vse with Christian Gentils, then they were with the Iewes. See page. 12.

verses.text: Arise my glorie, arise psalter and harpe: I wil arise early.
I wil confesse to thee among <na>(m)</na> peoples ô Lord: and I wil say a Psalme to thee among <na>(n)</na> the Gentiles.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Gods benefites bestowed vpon Dauid, and vpon faithful Christians prefigured by him, are for euer to be praised by al peoples and nations.

notes.label: n
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: Because thy mercie is magnified euen to the heauens, and thy truth euen to the cloudes.
Be axalted aboue the heauens ô God: and thy glorie vpon al the earth.

chapters.summary: The Prophet prayeth in tribulation, 4. testifieth Gods helpe, 6. praiseth his greatnes: 8. promising, and inuiting al nations to praise him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Dauids great patience.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> destroy not, to Dauid in, <na>(c)</na> the inscription of the title.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme was made vpon the same occasion, and to the same purpose as the former,

notes.label: b
notes.text: to exhorte the iust and innocent to patience,

notes.label: c
notes.text: by Dauids memorable example.

verses.text: IF <na>(d)</na> in very dede you speake iustice: iudge right thinges ye sonnes of men.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Few are so wicked, but they speake and pretend iust thinges:

verses.text: For in <na>(e)</na> the hart you worke iniquities: in the earth your <na>(f)</na> handes forge iniustice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: but neither thincke wel,

notes.label: f
notes.text: nor do wel, but both contrarie, which feaned sanctitie is duble iniquitie.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Sinners are alienated from the matrice, they haue erred from the wombe: they haue spoken false thinges.

notes.label: g
notes.text: These wicked sinners that flatter and incite king Saul, seme to haue spent al their life from their infancie in malice.

verses.text: They haue furie according to the similitude of <na>(h)</na> a serpent: as of <na>(i)</na> the aspe that is deafe, and stoppeth his eares.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Their furie is vnquiet, til they may wound the innocent with their poisonful sting,

notes.label: i
notes.text: neither wil they harken to good admonitions, but stoppe their eares like an aspe, that layeth one eare close to the ground, and stoppeth the other with his taile.

verses.text: Which wil not heare the voice of the inchanters, and of the sorcerer inchanting wisely.
God shal breake their <na>(k)</na> teeth in their mouth, the <na>(l)</na> cheeke tooth of the lions, our Lord wil breake in peeces.

notes.label: k
notes.text: But God wil breake their cruel force,

notes.label: l
notes.text: though it semeth most strong, and insuperable.

verses.text: They shal come to nothing as water running downe: he hath <na>(m)</na> bent his bow til they be weakened.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Gods iust determination of punishing the wicked stil remaineth beat and readie, though execution be some while differred.

verses.text: As <na>(n)</na> waxe that melteth, shal they be taken away: <na>(o)</na> fyre hath falne on them, and they haue not scene the sunne.

notes.label: n
notes.text: That force and powre which is now inuincible, hard and strong like a lions strongest teeth, shal then be as impotent and soft as waxe:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Gods wrath, like fire, the most forcible element, shal fal vpon them, and they shal be cast into vtter darkenes, depriued of the sunne and al comfortable light.

verses.text: Before your <na>(p)</na> thornes did vnderstand the old bryar: as liuing so in wrath he swalloweth them.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Before their malice can bring to effect, the great mischieffes which they plette and purpose, God suddainly cutteth them of before they fully vnderstand of, either sicknes or death, casteth them as it were aliue into hel.

verses.text: The iust <na>(q)</na> shal reioice when he shal see reuenge: he shal wash his handes in the bloud of a sinner.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The iust reioyce in the punishment of the wicked for three causes, first in zele of iustice, conforming his wil and mind to Gods iudgement; secondly, for that himselfe through Gods mercie hath escaped that terrible damnation; thirdly, for that he is now deliuered from molestation, and continual tribulation.

verses.text: And man shal say: If certes there be fruite to the iust: <na>(r)</na> there is a God certes iudging them on the earth.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The iust seing, or by faith knowing what punishment remaineth for the wicked, is therby assured that the good shal reape fruict for his wel doing, and that in the meane time God ruleth and iudgeth on the earth, though as yet it appeareth not so euidently.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid inueigheth against dissembling wicked men. 7. describeth their manifold punishment, 11. wherin the iust shal be comforted. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence in suffering evil.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, destroy not, to Dauid in the inscription of the title, <na>(a)</na> when Saul sent, and watched his house to kil him. (1. Reg. 19.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: King Saul hauing thrise attempted in vaine to kil Dauid, (1. Reg. 18. v. 11. & c. 19. v. 9) sent some of his guard to fetch him, from his owne house, that he might be slaine: but God moued the mind of Michol, to admonish him of the danger, and to helpe him away in saftie, though Saul thought she would haue bene a scandal vnto him (or cause of ruine) by the handes of the Philistians 1. Reg. 18. v. 21. Vpon which occasion Dauid made this Psalme. As he also made others, for perpetual memorie of Gods like benefites, in deliuering him in iminent dangers, when Saul sent three troupes of seriants to kil him, and folowed them himselfe. 1. Reg. 19. v. 10. likewise when he was knowen and bewrayed before Achis king of Geth. 1. Reg. 21. also in Ceila, in the deserts of Ziph, and of Maon. c. 23, in Engaddi, c. 24. in Hachila. c. 26. and againe amongst the Philistians. c. 27. and 30.

verses.text: DELIVER me from mine enimies ô my God: and from them that rise vp against me defend me.
Deliuer me from them that worke iniquitie: and from bloudy men saue me.
Because loe they <na>(b)</na> haue taken my soule: the strong haue falne violently vpon me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: They haue so straictly beseged me, that it is now in their handes, to take away my life.

verses.text: Neyther is it mine iniquitie, nor my sinne ô Lord: <na>(c)</na> without iniquitie haue I runne, and gone directly.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Of my part I haue committed no fault against myn enimies, for which they can haue anie iust cause to persecute me.

verses.text: Ryse vp to meete me, and see: and thou ô Lord the God of powres, God of Israel attend to visite <na>(d)</na> al nations: haue <na>(e)</na> no mercie on al that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The prophet foreseing in spirite, that the Catholique Church shal be vniustly persecuted, prayeth, and teacheth others to pray, that God wil mercifully visite his faithful people of al nations:

notes.label: e
notes.text: and not spare obstinate persecuters.

verses.text: They wil returne <na>(f)</na> at euening: and they shal suffer famine <na>(g)</na> as dogges, and shal compasse the citie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Persecuters laboring how much, or how long soeuer, shal at night, that is, in the end of al their wicked endeuoures be vnsatisfied in their desires,

notes.label: g
notes.text: as hungrie dogges that runne hunting al the day, & night also, stil seeking & not finding wherwith to fil their rauenous mouthes and deuouring bellies.

verses.text: Behold they <na>(h)</na> wil speake in their mouth, and a sworde in their lippes: <na>(i)</na> because who hath heard?

notes.label: h
notes.text: They threaten and determine to vse al crueltie,

notes.label: i
notes.text: as if there were no God, that heareth, and wil punish it.

verses.text: And thou ô Lord wilt scorne them: thou wilt bring to naught al the nations.
I wil keepe my strength to thee: <na>(k)</na> because thou art my recciuer:

notes.label: k
notes.text: Through Gods grace the Church is stil strong and the vertuous do perseuere.

verses.text: my God, thy mercie shal preuent.
God wil shew vnto me concerning mine enimies, kil them not <na>(l)</na> lest sometime my peoples forgete. Disperse them in thy strength: and <na>(m)</na> depose them my protector ô Lord.

notes.label: l
notes.text: God suffereth afflictions to fal vpon his seruants to kepe them exercised, lest in prosperitie they forgete their duties to him.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Depriue them of powre, that they may not do so much euil as they desire.

verses.text: The sinne of their mouth, the word of their lippes: and let them be taken in their pride. And for <na>(n)</na> cursing and lying they shal be <na>(o)</na> talked of

notes.label: n
notes.text: After that their iniquitie is complete

notes.label: o
notes.text: they shal be accused and punished for their blasphemies and lies.

verses.text: in consummation: in wrath of comsummation and they shal not be. And they shal know that God wil rule ouer Iacob: and ouer the ends of the earth.
They <na>(p)</na> shal be turned at euening, and shal suffer famine as dogges: and shal compasse the citie.
They shal be <na>(q)</na> dispersed to eate: and if they be not filled, they <na>(r)</na> wil murmur also.

notes.label: q
notes.text: They shal in vaine seeke oyle for their lampes with the foolish virgins, repent with Iudas, and finding no helpe,

notes.label: r
notes.text: shal continually blaspheme in hel.

verses.text: But I wil sing thy strength: and wil exalt thy mercie in <na>(s)</na> the morning. Because thou art become my receiuer, and my refuge, in the day of my tribulation.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In the resurrection.

verses.text: My helper, I wil sing to thee, because thou art God my receiuer: my God, my mercie.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid (being besieged in his owne house by men sent to kil him) confidently prayeth God to deliuer him, 6. and al faithful nations in like danger: 7. and praiseth God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Another prayer of David in danger.
The 8. key.

verses.text: victories, 11. achieved by God's only power. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: King Dauids thankes for victories. the 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for them, <na>(a)</na> that shal be changed, in <na>(b)</na> the inscription of the title <na>(c)</na> to Dauid him selfe, <na>(d)</na> for doctrine,

notes.label: a
notes.text: The change of state from aduersitie to prosperitie in the people of Israel, was a figure of the like change in the Church of Christ,

notes.label: b
notes.text: worthie to be remembred,

notes.label: c
notes.text: for the instruction,

notes.label: d
notes.text: of Gods beloued,

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> when he set fire on Mesopotamia of Syria, and in Sobal, and Ioab returned, and stroke Idumæa in the valley of salt-pittes twelue thousand. (2. Reg. 8. & 10. & 1. Paral. 18.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: as the same are more largely recorded in the bookes of kinges.

verses.text: O GOD thou <na>(f)</na> hast repelled vs, & hast destroyed vs: thou wast angrie <na>(g)</na> and hast had mercie on vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God suffereth his people to be afflicted, as wel for their sinnes, as for exercise in vertue,

notes.label: g
notes.text: after sheweth his mercie in pardoning, and fauour in aduancing them.

verses.text: Thou hast moued the earth, and hast trubled it: heale the breaches thereof, because it is moued.
Thou hast shewed vnto thy people <na>(h)</na> hard thinges: thou hast made vs drinke the wine of compunction.

notes.label: h
notes.text: by punishīg sinners.

verses.text: Thou hast <na>(i)</na> geuen a signification to them that feare thee: they flee from the face of the bow.

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVarning them to amēd.

verses.text: That thy beloued <na>(k)</na> may be deliuered, saue me with thy right hand; and heare me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: and then restoreth them to former good state.

verses.text: God hath spoken in <na>(l)</na> his holie: I shal reioyce, and <na>(m)</na> shal diuide Sichem: and shal mesure the valley of tabernacles.

notes.label: l
notes.text: God also as he hath promised by his holie oracle,

notes.label: m
notes.text: hath aduanced king Dauid, in his temporal kingdom, and doth much more aduance him, and other elect in euerlasting life.

verses.text: Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: and Ephraim the strength of my heade.
Iuda my king: Moab <na>(n)</na> the pot of my hope. Into Edom wil I <na>(o)</na> stretch out my shoe: the foreners are subiect to me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As a vessel for meaner vses

notes.label: o
notes.text: Bring it vnder my dominion.

verses.text: Who shal conduct me into a fensed citie? who shal conduct me euen into Idumea?
Shal not thou ô God, <na>(p)</na> that hast expelled vs: and <na>(q)</na> wilt not thou ô God goe forth in our hostes?

notes.label: p
notes.text: As God doth sometimes punish:

notes.label: q
notes.text: so he also rewardeth.

verses.text: Giue vs aide from tribulation: because mans saluation is vaine.
In God we shal doe <na>(r)</na> strength: and he shal bring to nothing them that afflict vs.

notes.label: r
notes.text: strongly, with fortitude.

chapters.summary: King Dauid after his owne and the peoples manie tribulations, 8. rendereth thankes for their renowmed victories, 11. atchiued by Gods only powre.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> in hyms to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In songues of praise and thankes to God.

verses.text: HEARE ô God my petition: attend to my praier.
From <na>(b)</na> the ends of the earth I haue cried to thee: whiles my hart was in anguish, thou <na>(c)</na> didst exalt me on a rocke.

notes.label: b
notes.text: From al coastes of the earth faithful people pray to God,

notes.label: c
notes.text: the Church builded vpon an assured fundation, is exalted to great powre and dignitie.

verses.text: Thou hast <na>(d)</na> conducted me, because thou art made my hope: a toure of strength from the face of the enimie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God conducteth, defendeth, and deliuereth those that confidently trust in him.

verses.text: I shal inhabite in <na>(e)</na> thy tabernacle for euer: I shal be protected in the couert of thy winges.

notes.label: e
notes.text: in the Church, a place of assured protection.

verses.text: Because thou my God hast heard my prayer: thou hast giuen inheritance to those that feare thy name.
Thou wilt adde <na>(f)</na> dayes vpon the dayes of the king: his years euen vnto the day of generation and generation.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christs kingdome the Church perpetual to the end of this world, and eternal after the general Resurrection.

verses.text: He is permanent for euer in the sight of God: his <na>(g)</na> mercie and <na>(h)</na> truth who shal require?

notes.label: g
notes.text: Who is able to vnderstand, or explicate how great Christs mercie is in redeming vs,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and his truth in performing his promised rewardes?

verses.text: So <na>(i)</na> wil I say a Psalme to thy name for euer and euer: that I may render my vowes <na>(k)</na> from day to day.

notes.label: i
notes.text: For so imestimable benefites, I wil alwayes praise thee with Psalmes, Canticles, or other thankes in this life:

notes.label: k
notes.text: and eternally in the life to come.

chapters.summary: Faithful people of the whole earth pray, and acknowlege that God mercifully heareth their prayer. 6. expect the eternal kingdom of Christ, in which they shal praise him for euermore. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A confident prayer for Christ's Incarnation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Iduthun a Psalme of Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Directed to Idithun, one of the masters of musike, to sing it, or to make tune for it.

verses.text: Shal <na>(b)</na> not my soule be subiect to God? for of him is my saluation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The wicked threating to ruinate others, Dauid, or anie iust man, feareth them not, because his soule is subiect to God.

verses.text: For he is my God, and my sauiour: my receiuer <na>(c)</na> I shal be moued no more.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Therfore I firmely purpose neuer to be moued from God.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> How long set you violently vpon a man: <na>(e)</na> you al doe kil: as it were vpon <na>(f)</na> a wal, that is leaning, and a wal shaken.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In vaine do you myn aduersaries stil assault me,

notes.label: e
notes.text: though ye be al confederate to kil me;

notes.label: f
notes.text: supposing me to be like a ruinous, or shaken wal, that is easily throwne downe.

verses.text: But <na>(g)</na> yet they thought to repel my price, <na>(h)</na> I ranne in thirst: they <na>(i)</na> blessed with their mouth, and cursed with their hart.

notes.label: g
notes.text: They thinck stil to depriue me of my reward, the price of my laboures and merites,

notes.label: h
notes.text: but I runne so much more diligently, as thirsting after righteousnes in this life, and glorie in the next, to finish my course.

notes.label: i
notes.text: A most dangerous tentation, when after threates and crueltie, persecutors endeuour by swete wordes, and promises to perswaed the iust to fal into sinne.

verses.text: But yet my soule be thou subiect to God: because my patience is from him.
Because he is my God, and my sauiour: my helper <na>(k)</na> I shal not remoue.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I resolutly purpose not to yeld to anie tentations.

verses.text: In God is my saluation, and my glorie: the God of my helpe, and my hope is in God.
Hope in him <na>(l)</na> al ye the congregation of people: powre out your harts before him, God is our helper for euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Gods faithful seruantes are not only constant themselues, but also exhorte and perswade al others, as much as in them lieth, to serue God and trust in him.

verses.text: But yet the children of men are vaine, the children of men are <na>(m)</na> liers in balances: that they may deceiue by vanitie together.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vsing false weightes they defraud one an other.

verses.text: Hope not in iniquitie, and couete not robberies: if riches abound set not your hart vpon them.
<na>(n)</na> Once hath God spoken, these <na>(o)</na> two things haue I heard:

notes.label: n
notes.text: God hauing nce spoken it is most assured.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Two especial attributes of God.

verses.text: That <na>(p)</na> powre is Gods, and <na>(q)</na> mercie ô Lord is to thee: because thou wilt render to euery one according to his workes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: God is Omnipotent, so that he can both reward, and punish infinitly;

notes.label: q
notes.text: and Merciful, that he is readie to receiue al sinners into his fauour, if they wil repent and turne vnto him.

chapters.summary: A iust man encoregeth his owne soule to serue God in sincere humilitie, 9. exhorteth also al others to trust in God, not in false and worldlie pollicie, or wealth, because Gods powre and mercie wil render to euerie one as they deserue. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Exhortation to good life, in respect of reward or punishment.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> of Dauid when he was in the desert of Iuda (1. Reg. 22.) <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Holie Dauid made this deuout meditation when he was in the forest of Haret, or desert of Ziph 1. Reg. 22. & 23. and could not come to the tabernacle of God, nor to Ierusalem, where he especially desired to be, in the inheritance of our Lord, which was to him a great affliction. As the like is now to Catholiques, when they are put in close prison for their faith, or otherwise hindered, that they can not be present at the most holie and daylie Sacrifice. In which case we must supplie as we may, this great losse, and comfort ourselues with this, or like Psalme, or prayer, saying : O God my God, to thee I watch.

verses.text: O GOD my God to thee I watch, <na>(b)</na> from the morning light. <na>(c)</na> My soule hath thirsted to thee, <na>(d)</na> my flesh to thee very manie wayes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Euen from the first downing of the morning,

notes.label: c
notes.text: my soule thirsteth after thee,

notes.label: d
notes.text: yea also my very flesh, and whole bodie feeleth great paines, by this affliction of mind, and desireth releese and rest.

verses.text: In a desert land, and inaccessible, and without water, <na>(e)</na> so in the holie haue I appeared to thee, <na>(f)</na> that I might see thy strength, and thy glorie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Being now in case that I can not serue thee, ô God, as I would, yet I exhibite myselfe present in spirite, before thy holie place,

notes.label: f
notes.text: meditating thy powre, and thy glorie.

verses.text: Because <na>(g)</na> thy mercie is better then liues, my lippes shal prayse thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: This consolation in banishment from thy diuine Seruice, is sweeter to me then manie temporal liues, or anie worldlie prosperitie.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> So wil I blesse thee in my life: and in thy name I wil liste vp my hands.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For as the Passions of Christ abound in vs (saith S. Paul 2. Cor. 1.) so also by Christ our comfort aboundeth.

verses.text: As with <na>(i)</na> marrow and fatnes let my soule be filled: <na>(k)</na> and my mouth shal praise with lippes of exultation.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Replenish my soul ô God, with the aboundance of thy grace,

notes.label: k
notes.text: so shal I be more able to praise thee.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> If I haue bene mindful of thee vpon my bedde, <na>(m)</na> in the morning I wil meditate on thee:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seing in the night, also in my bed I meditate of thee;

notes.label: m
notes.text: I wil more diligently do the same in the morning.

verses.text: because thou hast bene my helper.
And in the couert of thy winges I wil reioice, my soule hath cleaued after thee: thy right hand hath receiued me.
But <na>(n)</na> they in vaine haue sought my soule, <na>(o)</na> they shal enter into the inferiour partes of the earth.

notes.label: n
notes.text: My temporal and spiritual enimies:

notes.label: o
notes.text: and they shal be damned for their sinnes.

verses.text: They <na>(p)</na> shal be deliuered into the handes of the sworde, they shal be <na>(q)</na> the portions of foxes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: It happened literally to Saul, that he was slaine in battle, which he made against his enimies;

notes.label: q
notes.text: and his dead bodie was hung on a wal (1. Reg. 31.) exposed to wilde beastes, or birdes, though it was afterwards burnt and buried.

verses.text: But <na>(r)</na> the king shal reioice in God, al shal be praised that sweare by him: because the mouth is stopped of those that speake wicked thinges.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Dauid was presently after Sauls death exalted to the kingdome, in figure of Christ, whose name and glorie was exalted, after the destruction of the Iewes by Pagane Emperours.

chapters.summary: Dauid in banishment with great affection desireth to vnite himselfe with God in meditation, 4. purposing and promising euer to praise him : 10. prophicieth the vaine endeuoures, and condemnation of his enimies; and his owne aduancement. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's devotion in banishment.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Psalme of Dauid.
HEARE ô God my prayer when I make petition: from the feare of my enimie deliuer my soule.
Thou <na>(a)</na> hast protected me from the <na>(b)</na> assemblie of the malignant: from the multitude of them that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: By example of thy former protection,

notes.label: b
notes.text: from the conspiracie of wicked men, I trust most assuredly in thy helpe.

verses.text: Because they haue sharpned their tongues as a sworde: they haue bent the bow a bitter thing,
that they may shoote in secretes at the immaculate.
Sodanely they wil shoote at him, and wil not feare: they <na>(c)</na> haue confirmed to themselues a wicked worde. They haue talked to hide snares: they haue saide, who shal see them?

notes.label: c
notes.text: They are resolued to intrappe me,

verses.text: They haue searched iniquities: they <na>(d)</na> haue failed searching with scrutanie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: But as they haue failed: so they shal stil faile, and be ouerreached in their bad counsels; as Achitophel. 1. Reg. 17.

verses.text: Man shal come to a deepe hart: and God shal be exalted. <na>(e)</na> Childrens arrowes are made their woundes:

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath chosen the weake of this world to confound the strong.

verses.text: and their tongues are weakned against them. Al that saw them <na>(f)</na> were trubled:

notes.label: f
notes.text: much merueled, seing the wicked so punished.

verses.text: and euerie man feared. And they shewed forth the workes of God: and they vnderstood his doinges.
The iust shal reioice in our Lord, and shal hope in him, and al the right of hart <na>(g)</na> shal be praised.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The iust shal be praised, for rightly seruing God.

chapters.summary: A prayer of the iust reposing their whole trust in God: 7. and reioycing that the enimies machinations are frustrate. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A confident prayer in tribulation.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To the end, a Psalme of Dauid, <na>(a)</na> the Canticle of Ieremie, and Ezechiel, to the people of the transmigration, when they begane to goe forth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The seuentie Interpreters seing Dauid here prophecie of the peoples returne from Babylon, added the names of Ieremie and Ezechiel, who being in that captiuitie, prophecied the same more largely. As likewise these and other Prophetes, foresaw in spirite, and more especially prophecied the going forth of al nations from Babylon, that is, forsaking Idolatrie, and embracing true Religion in the Church of Christ, so S. Augustin, Eutymius, and others.

verses.text: AN hymne ô God becometh thee <na>(b)</na> in Sion: & a vow shal be rendered to thee in Ierusalem.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not in Babylon, nor els where, but only in the Church, praises and vowes are gratful to God.

verses.text: Heare my prayer: <na>(c)</na> al flesh shal come to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al nations shal know thee.

verses.text: The wordes of the wicked <na>(d)</na> haue preuailed vpon vs: and thou wilt be <na>(e)</na> propitious to our impieties.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The wicked are insolent in threatning,

notes.label: e
notes.text: but thou mercifully pardoning our sinnes, they shal not hurt vs.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Blessed is he, whom thou hast chosen, and taken: he shal dwel in thy courtes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They are happie to whom thou hast prepared grace, and glorie.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> We shal be replenished in the goods of thy house: holie is thy temple, <na>(h)</na> meruelous in equitie. Heare vs ô God our sauiour, the hope of al the ends of the earth; and in the sea farre.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The voice of the faithful, reioycing in the hope of eternal glorie. Rom. 5.

notes.label: h
notes.text: nothing polluted shal enter into heauen. Apo. 21.

verses.text: Preparing <na>(i)</na> mountanes in thy strength, girded with might:

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou which art al powreful, as appeareth by the huge montaines,

verses.text: which trublest <na>(k)</na> the depths of the sea, the sound of the waues therof.

notes.label: k
notes.text: seas, and other thy workes.

verses.text: The Gentiles shal <na>(l)</na> be trubled, and they that inhabite the borders shal be affraide of thy signes: <na>(m)</na> the outegoinges of the morning and euening thou shalt delight.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou wilt by thy omnipotent powre moue the hartes of obdurate men, and so conuert innumerable of al nations to thee.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Thou wilt draw manie to thee, with ioy and gladnes, from the vttermost coastes of the east and weast.

verses.text: Thou hast visited the earth, and hast inebriated it: thou hast multiplied to inrich it. The <na>(n)</na> riuer of God is replenished with waters, thou hast prepared their <na>(o)</na> meat: because <na>(p)</na> so is the preparation therof.

notes.label: n
notes.text: God wrought diuers miracles in waters (Gen. 7. Exo. 7. 14. 15. Iosue. 3. 4. Reg. 5. 6. &c.)

notes.label: o
notes.text: likewise in prouiding meate for his people. (Exo. 16. 3. Reg. 17. 4. Reg. 4. 7. &c.) which were figures of Baptisme, Eucharist, and other Sacraments of Christ, washing from sinnes, and augmenting grace,

notes.label: p
notes.text: so replenishing the Church with most sacred Mysteries.

verses.text: Inebriate <na>(q)</na> her riuers, <na>(r)</na> multiplie her fruites: in her dropps she shal reioyce springing.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Endewing the Apostles and other preachers with spiritual grace and lerning,

notes.label: r
notes.text: continuing the succession of pastores to watter and feede the faithful people.

verses.text: Thou wilt <na>(s)</na> blesse the crowne of the yeare of thy goodnes: <na>(t)</na> and thy fildes shal be replenished with plentie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: God blesseth the whole course, or circle of time, of the Church militant in this world,

notes.label: t
notes.text: and the crowne, or happie end of euerie iust persons life.

verses.text: The <na>(v)</na> beautiful places of the desert shal be fat: and the <na>(w)</na> litle hilles shal be girded aboute with exultation.

notes.label: v
notes.text: u Euen those which before had only a shew of beautie, but in dede were barren, shal yelde abundant fruict.

notes.label: w
notes.text: those which are more eminent shal particularly reioyce in their owne, and others spiritual progresse in vertue.

verses.text: The <na>(x)</na> rammes of the shepe are clothed, and <na>(y)</na> the valleis shal abounde with corne: <na>(z)</na> they wil crie, yea they wil say an hymne.

notes.label: x
notes.text: The principal pastores shal in proportion reioyce aboue the rest, for the grace and glorie of al their flocke.

notes.label: y
notes.text: the subiectes also and inferior people shal be satiate with their happie lotte.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Al together, prelates and people, higher and lovver shal with vniforme voice sing praises to God, and perpetual hymnes.

chapters.summary: God is rightly praised in Sion and Ierusalem (in his Church only) for his benefites bestowed and promised. 8. Vnto which also in the time of grace, al nations shal be called. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Conversion of Gentiles.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Canticle <na>(a)</na> of resurrection. MAke ye <na>(b)</na> iubilation to God al the earth,

notes.label: a
notes.text: Mystical resurrection, Gentiles succeding in place of the Iewes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Shew your internal ioy by external wordes and deedes.

verses.text: say a psalme to his name: geue glorie to his praise.
Say ye to God: <na>(c)</na> How terrible are thy workes ô Lord! in the multitude of thy strength thine enimies <na>(d)</na> shal lie to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: In drovvning the vvorld, in confounding the tongues in Babel, in burning Sodom and Gomorrha with brimston, in plaging the Ægyptians, in drovvning Pharao and his vvhole armie in the read sea; in destroying the Chananites and other infideles, in punishing the tenne tribes, and aftervvards the other tvvo by captiuitie, and innumerable other punishments, al for sinnes,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for vvhich euen the vvicked, though not sincerly conuerted, yet of seruile feare, feaned and falsly promised to amend, but performed it not: as Pharao afflicted vvith plagues, vvas forced to promise libertie to the children of Israel, vvhich he aftervvards denied.

verses.text: Let al the earth adore thee, and sing to thee: let it sing a psalme to thy name.
Come ye, and see the workes of God: terrible in counsels ouer the chidren of men.
Who turneth <na>(e)</na> the sea into drie land, in <na>(f)</na> the riuer they shal passe on foote, <na>(g)</na> there we shal reioyce in him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The read sea,

notes.label: f
notes.text: when Iosue brought the people ouer Iordan,

notes.label: g
notes.text: in remembring and reciting these singular benefites.

verses.text: Who ruleth in his strength for euer his eyes looke vpon the gentiles: <na>(h)</na> they that exasperate him let them <na>(i)</na> not be exalted in themselues.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Gods chosen people the Iewes did often exasperate God by their ingratitude, murmuring, and other sinnes: whom the prophet therfore admonisheth,

notes.label: i
notes.text: not to be proud, lest they be saboued, and brought lowe.

verses.text: Ye <na>(k)</na> Gentiles blesse our God: and make the voice of his prayse hearde.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By way of inuitation the Psalmist prophecieth the conuersion of Gentiles.

verses.text: Who hath put <na>(l)</na> my soule in life: and hath not geuen my feete to be moued.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The voice of the whole Church: confessing Gods prouidence and protection, that she neuer faleth; for the Iewes falling from Christ the Gentiles beleued in him; and some nations, or countries failing from Religion, others are conuerted.

verses.text: Because thou <na>(m)</na> hast proued vs ô God: by fire thou hast tried vs, as siluer is tried.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God suffereth his Church to be persecuted with al kindes of tribulation, as some are here recited.

verses.text: Thou hast brought vs into a snare, thou hast laide tribulations on our backe: thou hast set men vpon our heades.
<na>(n)</na> We haue passed through fire and water: and thou hast brought vs out into refreshing.

notes.label: n
notes.text: But through Gods assistance his seruants passe through, and ouercome al tentations.

verses.text: I wil goe into thy house with <na>(o)</na> holocaustes: I wil render thee <na>(p)</na> my vowes:

notes.label: o
notes.text: Sacrifice of thankes,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and voluntarie vowes,

verses.text: which my lippes haue distinguished. And <na>(q)</na> my mouth hath spoken in my tribulation.

notes.label: q
notes.text: that which anie promiseth to God in tribulation, they must performe accordingly.

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> Holocaustes with marrow wil I offer to thee, with incense of rammes: I wil offer to thee oxen with bucke goates.

notes.label: r
notes.text: These were the best external sacrifices of the old law.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Come ye, heare, and I wil tel al ye that feare God, what great things he hath done for my soule.

notes.label: s
notes.text: But both then and now the internal sacrifices of contrite hart, of iustice, and of diuine praise best please God.

verses.text: To him haue I cried with my mouth, and haue exulted <na>(t)</na> vnder my tongue.

notes.label: t
notes.text: from the hart, which is vnder the tongue, and directeth the tongue what to speake.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> If I haue beheld iniquitie in my hart, our Lord wil not heare.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Whosoeuer wil be heard in prayer, must repent of his sinnes.

verses.text: Therfore hath God heard, and hath attended to the voice of my petition.
Blessed be God who hath not remoued my prayer, and his mercie from me.

chapters.summary: The prophet inuiteth al men to praise God for his meruelous workes, and benefites donne to the Iewes. 7. Who being vngratful, 8. Gentiles are called, 16. and bring forth better fruict. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gentiles succeed the Jews.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, in hymes, a Psalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme beginning to be songue by voices, instruments were adioyned.

verses.text: GOd <na>(b)</na> haue mercie vpon vs, and <na>(c)</na> blesse vs: <na>(d)</na> illuminate his countenance vpon vs, and <na>(e)</na> haue mercie on vs.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God first remitte our sinnes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: then geue vs thy manifold graces,

notes.label: d
notes.text: grant faith and repentance,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and so forgeuenes of sinnes.

verses.text: That we may know thy way vpon earth: in al nations thy saluation.
Let peoples ô God, confesse to thee: <na>(f)</na> let al peoples confesse to thee.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al nations shal be conuerted.

verses.text: Let nations be glad & reioice: because thou iudgest peoples in equitie, and the nations in earth thou doest direct.
Let peoples ô God confesse to thee, let al peoples confesse to thee:
the earth hath yelded her fruite. <na>(g)</na> God, <na>(h)</na> our God blesse vs,

notes.label: g
notes.text: God the Fater,

notes.label: h
notes.text: God the Sonne,

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> God blesse vs: and let al the endes of the earth feare him.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God the Holie Ghost, saue the peoples of al nations, by Euangelical preaching of thee, the most Blessed Trinitie.

chapters.summary: The prophet prayeth for (and withal foresheweth) the propagation of the Church of Christ. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Propagation of the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Psalme of Canticle, to Dauid himself.
LEt <na>(a)</na> God arise, and let his enimies be dispersed, and let them that hate him <na>(b)</na> flee from his face.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In maner of praying that God wil vouchsafe to defend the Church, the Psalmist prophecieth that God wil arise,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and the enimies shal flee away, not daring to abide the combate.

verses.text: As smoke vanisheth, let them vanish away: as waxe melteth at the presence of fire, so let sinners perish at the presence of God.
And <na>(c)</na> let the iust make merrie, and reioyce in the sight of God: and let them be delighted in mirth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As God is terrible to the wicked: so he is comfortable to the iust.

verses.text: Sing to God, say a Psalme to his name: <na>(d)</na> make way to him, who <na>(e)</na> mounteth vpon the west, <na>(f)</na> Lord is his name. Reioyce ye in his syght, they shal be trubled at the presence of him:

notes.label: d
notes.text: Resist not Gods inspiration, but receiue it with ioy and thankes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: who triumpheth ouer death

notes.label: f
notes.text: God is Lord, not only of these or those nations, countries or other creatures, but absolutly and vniuersally of al.

verses.text: the father of orphanes, and iudge of widowes. God in his <na>(g)</na> holie place:

notes.label: g
notes.text: That is the true holie Church, which hath

verses.text: God that maketh men to inhabite <na>(h)</na> of one manner in a house. That bringeth forth them, <na>(i)</na> that be bound, in strengh, likewise them, that <na>(k)</na> exasperate, that dwel <na>(l)</na> in sepulchers.

notes.label: h
notes.text: vnitie in doctrin, touching faith and maners. · S.Cypr.ep.76.

notes.label: i
notes.text: That be bond in sinne.

notes.label: k
notes.text: euen rebellious willes are altered by Gods mercie, and freely embrace his law

notes.label: l
notes.text: also the dead and drie hartes that cared not for spiritual thinges, are softened, and quickned with new grace.

verses.text: O God <na>(m)</na> when thou wentest forth in the sight of thy people, when thou didst passe through the desert.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The benefites bestowed on the Israelites, are written in the bookes of Moyses, Iosue, and Iudges.

verses.text: The earth was moued, and the heauens also distilled, at the presence of the God of Sina, at the face of the God of Israel.
<na>(n)</na> Voluntarie rayne shalt thou seperat ô God to thine inheritance: and it was <na>(o)</na> weakned, but thou hast perfited it.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Not mans deseruing, but Gods mere good wil, and free grace caused Christ to come, and by himselfe and his Apostles to preach the Euangelical doctrin, which watereth the whole world,

notes.label: o
notes.text: God chose the weake, but made them strong.

verses.text: Thy <na>(p)</na> liuing creatures shal dwel in it: thou hast prepared <na>(q)</na> in thy swetnes for the poore, ô God.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Those whom thou hast chosen, and so made thyn owne peculiar people, shal enioy this grace.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Thou gauest Manna in the desert, the B. Sacrament in the new testament.

verses.text: Our Lord shal geue <na>(r)</na> the word to them that euanglize, <na>(s)</na> with great powre.

notes.label: r
notes.text: God geueth to the preacher what to speake,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and to some he geueth also powre to worke miracles, in confirmation of their doctrin. Mar. 16.

verses.text: The <na>(t)</na> king of hoastes the beloued of the beloued: and <na>(v)</na> to the beautie of the house, to diuide the spoyles.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Some potent king, or ( as it is in the Hebrew ) kinges being beloued, of the beloued of God, the only Sonne of God, shal yeld themselues to the same beloued Sonne of God:

notes.label: v
notes.text: which shal redound to the glorie and beautie of his Church, gayning such spiritual prayes from the diuel.

verses.text: If ye <na>(w)</na> sleepe among the middest of the lottes, the winges of a doue layde ouer with siluer, and the hinder parts of her backe in the palenes of gold.

notes.label: w
notes.text: If you be in such danger, that the aduersaries cast dice, or lottes for your persons, and goodes, yet you shal be deliuered, as if a doue, with her glistering fethers, like siluer and gold, flie away into a secure place, without losse or diminution, but rather with increase of vertues.

verses.text: Whiles <na>(x)</na> the heauenlie discerneth kings ouer her, <na>(y)</na> with snow they shal be made white in Selmon.

notes.label: x
notes.text: VVhen the heauenlie king determineth thus of earthlie kinges,

notes.label: y
notes.text: they shal be purged from their sinnes, and made white like snow, that falleth in mount Selmon, which is a shadowed hil, thicke with trees, in mount Ephraim nere to Iordan.

verses.text: The <na>(z)</na> mountane of God a fat mountane. A mountane <na>(a)</na> crudded as cheese, a <na>(b)</na> fatte mountane:

notes.label: z
notes.text: The Church of God is visible, and durable like to a mountane.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Combined, or ioyned together, as when milke is turned into curde, and so into cheese.

notes.label: b
notes.text: fructful, enriched by spiritual giftes of the Holie Ghost.

verses.text: why <na>(c)</na> suppose you crudded mountanes? A mountane, in which it hath wel pleased God to dwel therin: for in dede our Lord wil dwel euen to the end.

notes.label: c
notes.text: ye that are not of this Church, do in vaine and erroniously imagine, that anie other mountaines are vnited.

verses.text: The <na>(d)</na> chariote of God is ten thousand folde, thousands of them that reioyce, our Lord in them, <na>(e)</na> in Sina in the holie place.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Innumerable Angels ministers of Gods wil, do continually attend vpon his Diuine Maiestie, as if he ( who otherwise nedeth no seruice ) were caried by them, as in a chariotte of infinite magnificence. Dan 7.

notes.label: e
notes.text: So God appeared in Maiestie, when he gaue his law in mount Sinai.

verses.text: Thou art <na>(f)</na> ascended on hygh, thou <na>(g)</na> hast taken captiuitie: thou <na>(h)</na> hast receiued gifts in men: for euen those <na>(i)</na> that do not beleue, our Lord God to inhabite. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christ ascended with innumerable Angels attending vpon him,

notes.label: g
notes.text: caried with him the fathers of the old testament, that had benne captiue,

notes.label: h
notes.text: as man he receiued giftes of God, in and for men, his faithful seruantes,

notes.label: i
notes.text: yea also he receiued for his merite, that innumerable, which before were incredulous, were conuerted, and God dwelt in their soules.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord day by day: the God of our saluations wil make vs a prosperous iourney.
Our God is the God of sauing: and <na>(k)</na> the issues of death are of our Lord, our Lord.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Our Lord, I say, our Lord, and none but he could ouercome death by dying.

verses.text: But yet God <na>(l)</na> stil breake the heads of his enimies: the hearie croune of them, that walke in their sinnes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though Christ died to deliuer al men from death. yet he wil geue capital sentence of eternal death to al that obstinatly remaine his enimies, and multiplie sinnes vpon sinnes, to the end of their temporal life.

verses.text: Our Lord Said: Out <na>(m)</na> of Basan I wil conuert, I wil conuert <na>(n)</na> into the depth of the sea.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Euen of the rudest barbarous nations, manie shal be conuerted to Christiantie

notes.label: n
notes.text: namely Gods grace is extended into the Ilandes of the Ocean, and other seas.

verses.text: That thy foote (o) may be dipped in bloude: the tongue of thy dogges [made redde] with the same [bloud] of the enimies. [1]

notes.label: o
notes.text: But such seuere slaughter shal fal vpon the obstinate contemners of this grace, that mens feete shal be defiled in their bloud, and dogges shal lappe it.
Ex inimicis ab ipso.

verses.text: They <na>(p)</na> haue seene thy entringes in ô God, the entrings of my God: of my King Who is <na>(q)</na> in the holie place.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Manie haue sene, or knowen in general, but the faithful more exactly know how Christ came into this world, his conuersation therin, and his going forth:

notes.label: q
notes.text: his reigning now in heauen our Mediatour, by whom al other intercessors haue accesse to God.

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> Princes came before <na>(s)</na> ioyned with them that sang, in the middes <na>(t)</na> of young wemen plaing on tymbrels.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The Apostles sowing the first seede of Euangelical doctrin,

notes.label: s
notes.text: with whom other Apostolical men,

notes.label: t
notes.text: and other soules of al nations conuerted by their preaching, most ioyfully sing together in hart, voice, and instruments: especially in good workes, shew their gratful affections to our Redeemer.

verses.text: In <na>(v)</na> churches blesse ye God our Lord, of <na>(w)</na> the fountains of Israel.

notes.label: v
notes.text: And al this in the particular Churches of diuers Kingdomes, and partes of the world:

notes.label: w
notes.text: beginning with the Israelites in Ierusalem, and so proceding into al Iurie, and Samaria, and to the vtmost of the earth. Act. 1.

verses.text: There <na>(x)</na> Beniamin a youngman, in excesse of minde. <na>(y)</na> The Princes of Iuda: their leaders: the Princes of Zabulon, the Princes of Nephthali.

notes.label: x
notes.text: S. Paul of Iacobs yongest sonne Beniamin, last called to Apostleship, was chiefly sent to the Gentiles.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Other Apostles of diuers tribes sent first to the Iewes, secondarily to Gentiles.

verses.text: Command thy strength ô God: <na>(z)</na> confirme this ô God, which thou hast wrought in vs.

notes.label: z
notes.text: As the Church begane by the omnipotent powre of God; so by the same only powre it is conserued.

verses.text: From thy temple in Ierusalem, kinges shal offer giftes to thee.

Rebuke <na>(a)</na> the wilde beasts of the reede, the congregation <na>(b)</na> of bulles in the kine of thy peoples: <na>(c)</na> that they may exclude them, which are tried with siluer. Dissipate the nations that wil warres:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Chastice therfore ô God, al persecuters of thy Church, who are but as weake wauering reedes, in comparison of thy powre:

notes.label: b
notes.text: no better then bulles, with kyne, that is, captaines and popular people,

notes.label: c
notes.text: endeuoring to alienate the constant proued confessors from their faith.

verses.text: Legates shal come <na>(d)</na> out of Ægypt: Æthiopia shal preuent his handes to God.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A prophecie that manie should be conuerted to Christ in Ægypt, and Æthiopia: as appeareth by the innumerable multitude of religious Monkes, & Nunnes in those countries, shortly after the Apostles dayes.

verses.text: Ye kingdomes <na>(e)</na> of the earth sing to God: sing to our Lord:

notes.label: e
notes.text: The like afterwards in al other nations, whom therfore the prophet inuiteth to praise God, for so inestimable benefites in the whole world.

verses.text: Sing ye to God, that mounteth vpon the heauen of heauen, to the East. Behold he wil giue to his voice <na>(f)</na> the voice of strength,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christ will come to judge, in terror of voice, and with magnificence, accompanied with holy Angels and other Saints.

verses.text: giue you glorie to God vpon Israel, his magnificence, and his powre in the cloudes.
God is meruelous in his saintes, the God of Israel he wil giue powre, and strength to his people, God be blessed.

chapters.summary: Notwithstanding great persecutions the Church prospereth. 10. Especially in the new testament, by Apostolical function, 18. ministerie of Angels, Christs Ascension, coming of the Holie Ghost, 31. confirming the faithful, repressing the insolent, and conuerting manie. 35. For al which the prophet inuiteth al men to praise God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church still conserved.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, <na>(b)</na> for them that shal be changed, <na>(c)</na> to Dauid.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Testament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: for gentiles conuerted to Christianitie, and from vice to vertue,

notes.label: c
notes.text: prefigured in Dauid.

verses.text: SAve me ô God: because <na>(d)</na> waters are entered into my soule.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Vehement afflictions inuiron my hart.

verses.text: I <na>(e)</na> sticke fast in the myre of the depth: and there is no sure standing. I am come into the depth of the sea: and a tempest hath ouerwhelmed me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am as one intangled with quickesand, or quadmyre in the bottom of a great water.

verses.text: I haue <na>(f)</na> labored crying, my iawes are made hoarse: my eies haue failed, whiles I hope in my God.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Our Lord sweat bloud for anguish in his prayer, and was not deliuered from his Passion, neither are his seruantes presently deliuered from tribulations, but as is most to Gods honour and their owne good.

verses.text: They are multiplied aboue the heares of my head, that hate me without cause. <cr>[1]</cr> Mine enimies are made strong, that haue persecuted me vniustly: <na>(g)</na> then did I pay the thinges that I tooke not.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Ioan. 15. · Our Sauiour who had no sinne, payde the ransom for al sinnes.

verses.text: O God thou knowest my <na>(h)</na> foolishnes: and <na>(i)</na> mine offences are not hide from thee.

notes.label: h
notes.text: O God thou knowest, that this which semeth follie to worldlie men, is true wisdom;

notes.label: i
notes.text: and though men charge me with offences, thou knowest that I am innocent.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> Let them not be ashamed vpon me, which expect thee ô Lord, Lord of hostes. Let them not be confounded vpon me that seeke thee, ô God of Israel.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Suffer not the weake to be scandalized in my passions.

verses.text: Because for thee haue I sustained reproch, confusion hath couered my face.
I am become a forener to my brethren, and a stranger to the sonnes of my mother.
Because <na>(l)</na> the zele of thy house hath eaten me: and the reproches of them that reproched thee, fel vpon me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: l
notes.text: Ioan. 2. Rom. 15. · The zele of seeking Gods honour, in propagating and aduancing his Church, is the cause of persecution. As we see those are lesse persecuted, which haue lesse godlie zele.

verses.text: And I couered my soule in fasting: and iton <na>(m)</na> was made a reproch to me.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The wicked do reproch those that mortifie themselues.

verses.text: And I put heare cloth my garment, & I became a parable to them.
They spake aganst me <na>(n)</na> that sat in the gate; and they soong aganst me that dranke wine.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The great men and iudges, also the drunkards and rascalitie of the people.

verses.text: But I, <na>(o)</na> my prayer to thee ô Lord: a time of thy good pleasure ô God. <na>(p)</na> In the multitude of thy mercie heare me, in the truth of thy saluation:

notes.label: o
notes.text: But I direct my prayer to thee.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Expecting the time of thy good pleasure.

verses.text: Deliuer me out of the myre, that I stick not fast: deliuer me from them that hate me, and from the depthes of <na>(q)</na> waters.

notes.label: q
