notes.text: tribulations.

verses.text: Let not the tempest of water drowne me, nor the depth swallowe me: <na>(r)</na> neyther let the pit shut his mouth vpon me.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Though Christ died and was buried, and in soule descended into hel, yet he could not be holden in his sepulchre, nor in limbo, but rose againe.

verses.text: Heare me ô Lord because thy mercie is benigne: according to the multitude of thy commiserations haue respect to me.
And turne not away thy face from thy seruant: because I am in tribulation, heare me speedily.
Attend to my soule and, deliuer it: <na>(s)</na> because of mine enimies deliuer me.

notes.label: s
notes.text: That they may either be conuerted, or confounded, and so do no more hurt.

verses.text: Thou knowest my reproch, & my confusion, & my shame.

In thy sight are al they that afflict me, my hart hath looked for reproch and miserie. And I expected some bodie that would be sorie together with me, and there <na>(t)</na> was none: and that would confort me, and I founde not.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Not anie that could mitigate our Sauiours affliction, would shew compassion towards him.

verses.text: And they gaue <na>(v)</na> gal for my meate: & in my thirst they gaue me vinegre to drinke.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Mat. 27. Ioan. 19. · But contrariwise when he complained of thirst, they gaue him gal and vinegre to drinke.

verses.text: <na>(w)</na> Let their table be made a snare before them, & for retributions, and for a scandal. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: w
notes.text: Rom. 11. · A prophecie of the destruction of the Iewes, at the time of Pasch, when they should thinke to eate their paschal lamb with ioy.

verses.text: Let <na>(x)</na> Their eies be darkned that they see not: and make <na>(y)</na> their backe crooked alwaies.

notes.label: x
notes.text: They are also blinde in hart, that they wil not see the truth of Christs doctrine:

notes.label: y
notes.text: but bow themselues to earthlie thinges, and worldlie gaines euen to this day.

verses.text: Poure out thy wrath vpon them: and let the furie of thy wrath ouertake them.
Let their habitation be made desert: and in their tabernacles let there be none to dwel. <cr>[1]</cr>
Because <na>(z)</na> whom thou hast striken, they haue persecuted: and vpon the sorrow of my wounds they haue added.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Christ, whom God of this mercie designed to suffer death, for redemption of mankind, the Iewes of mere enuie and malice persecuted to death.

verses.text: Adde thou <na>(a)</na> iniquitie vpon their iniquitie: and let them not enter into thy iustice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A prophecie that God would suffer them, to fal from one iniquitie to an other.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Let them be put out of the booke of the liuing: and with the iust let them not be written.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In the end of their liues, they shal not be found in the booke of life, where they suppose themselues to be written.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> I am poore and sorowful: <na>(d)</na> thy saluation ô God hath receiued me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The voice of Christ, humbling himselfe to death, euen to death of the Crosse:

notes.label: d
notes.text: from which he rose againe.

verses.text: I wil praise the name of God with canticle: and wil magnifie him in prayse.
And <na>(e)</na> it shal please God more then a young calfe: that bringeth forth hornes and hoofes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Deuout praise and thankesgeuing please God more then sacrifices of the most tender calues, which were otherwise also gratful sacrifices.

verses.text: Let the poore see and reioyce: seeke ye God, and your soule shal liue.
Because our Lord hath heard the poore: and he hath not despised <na>(f)</na> his prisoners.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God doth assuredly comfort al such, as are imprisoned for professing the truth.

verses.text: Let <na>(g)</na> the heauens and earth praise him, the sea, and al the creeping beastes in them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Al the creatures of God.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Because God wil saue Sion: and <na>(i)</na> the cities of Iuda shal be built vp. And they shal inhabite there, & by inheritance they shal get it.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God wil alwayes establish and protect the Catholique Church:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and particular Churches, members of the vniuersal shal also prosper.

verses.text: And <na>(k)</na> the seede of his seruants shal possesse it, and they that loue his name shal dwel in it.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Perpetual succession of the Catholique Church.

chapters.summary: Christ in middes of afflictions (as one in dangerous waters) 5. describing the malice of persecutors, and his owne true zele, 14. prayeth his heauenlie Father for helpe. 23. By way of iust imprecation, forsheweth the seuere punishment of his aduersaries, 30. his owne glorious Resurrection, and prosperous building of his Church. For which he inuiteth al creatures to praise God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's afflictions and victory.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Psalme of Dauid, in remembrance, that our <na>(b)</na> Lord saued him.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An apt prayer also for the afflicted in the new Testament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: from the danger of Absolom. (2. Reg. 18.) or from anie persecutor.

verses.text: O God <na>(c)</na> intend vnto my helpe: Lord <na>(d)</na> make hast to helpe me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al men at al times nede Gods helpe:

notes.label: d
notes.text: but most present nede, in present dangers. The rest of this Psalme is conteyned in the 39. Psalme, from the 15. verse. but there the whole Church prayeth for helpe, the world being almost drowned in sinnes; here Dauid, or other particular persons, or peoples pray in their seueral distresses,

verses.text: Let them be confounded, and be ashamed, that seeke my soule. <cr>[1]</cr>
Let them be turned away backeward, and be ashamed that wil me euils. Let them be turned away forthwith ashamed, that say to me: Wel, wel.
Let al that seeke thee reioyce, and be glad in thee, and let them say alwayes: Our Lord be magnified: which loue thy saluation.
But I am needie and poore: ô God helpe me thou art my helper, and deliuerer: ô Lord be not slacke.

chapters.summary: An other prayer of Dauid, when he was persecuted by Absolom : made in a Psalme after his deliuerie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David's prayer in persecution.
The 8. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> for Dauid, <na>(b)</na> of the sonnes of Ionadab, and <na>(c)</na> the former captiues. IN thee ô Lord <na>(d)</na> I haue hoped, let me not be confounded for euer:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though this Psalme (as also diuers others) is intitled to, or for Dauid, it proueth not that some other was the author therof, but the Seuentie Interpreters insinuate hereby, that it perteyneth in more particular sorte to Dauid, growing old;

notes.label: b
notes.text: they adde also the sonnes of Ionadab a most holie familie,

notes.label: c
notes.text: who for their singular pietie, were suffered to remaine in Ierusalem, in the first captiuitie. Ierem. 35.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The wordes of Dauid, or anie faithful iust person.

verses.text: in <na>(e)</na> thy iustice deliuer me, and receiue me. Incline thine eare to me, and saue me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God of his iustice reuengeth the iniuries done to his seruantes.

verses.text: Be vnto me for a God protector, and for a fensed place: that thou maist saue me: Because thou art my firmament, and my refuge.
My God deliuer me out of the hand of the sinner, and out of the hand of him that doth aganst the law, and of the vniust.
Because thou art <na>(f)</na> my patience ô Lord: ô Lord my hope from my youth.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Through thy grace I haue patience to expect thy pleasure, when I shal be releeued.

verses.text: Vpon thee haue I bene confirmed from the wombe: from my mothers bellie thou art my protector. In thee is my singing alwaies:
I was made to manie as <na>(g)</na> a wonder: and thou art a strong helper.

notes.label: g
notes.text: It semeth strange to most men, why the iust haue more trubles then the wicked.

verses.text: Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glorie: <na>(h)</na> al the day thy greatnes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A necessarie prayer for perseuerance, which none can haue without special and continual helpe of grace.

verses.text: Reiect me not in the time of olde age: <na>(i)</na> when my strength shal faile, forsake me not.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Against this special danger, and last assaultes of the enimie, Christ hath instituted the Sacrament of Extreme Vnction.

verses.text: Because mine enimies haue said to me: and they that watched my soule, consulted together,
Saying: God hath forsaken him, pursew, and take him: because there is none to deliuer.
O God be not farre from me: my God haue respect to mine ayde.
Let them be confounded, and fayle that detract from my soule: let them be couered with confusion, and shame, that seeke euils to me.
But I wil alwaies hope: and <na>(k)</na> wil adde vpon al thy praise.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The best meanes to conserue vertue, is to exercise the same, adding good workes towardes our neighbours, and praises to God.

verses.text: My mouth shal shew forth thy iustice: al the day thy saluation. Because <na>(l)</na> I haue not knowne lerning, <na>(m)</na> I wil enter into the <na>(n)</na> powres of our Lord:

notes.label: l
notes.text: I professe not exact knowlege of natural thinges;

notes.label: m
notes.text: but I consider and contemplate the infinite powre of God, which appeareth in his workes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and his iust iudgements, as partly haue appeared in punishing, and rewarding some in this life, but especially wil be manifest in the end of this world.

verses.text: ô Lord I wil be mindful of thy iustice onely.
O God thou hast taught me from my youth: and vntil now I wil pronounce thy meruelous workes.
And vnto ancient age, and olde age: ô God forsake me not? Vntil I shew forth thy arme to al the generation, that is to come. Thy might,
and thy iustice ô God euen to the highest, great meruailes which thou hast done: ô God who may be like to thee?
How great tribulations hast thou shewed me, manie and euil: and turning thou <na>(o)</na> hast quickened me: and from the depthes of the earth thou hast brought me backe againe.

notes.label: o
notes.text: After tribulations recreated me.

verses.text: Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence: and being turned thou hast comforted me.
For I also wil confesse to thee in the instruments of Psalme thy truth: ô God I wil sing to thee on the harpe, holie one of Israel.
My <na>(p)</na> lippes shal reioyce when I shal sing to thee; and my soule, which thou hast redemed.

notes.label: p
notes.text: I wil praise thee with mouth and hart.

verses.text: Yea and my tongue al the day shal meditate thy iustice: when they shal be confounded and ashamed that seeke euils to me.

chapters.summary: King Dauid, or anie other iust person, prayeth God to continew his grace, and protection against the malice of the enimie. 5. Recounteth Gods mercie in deliuering him from falling into tentations. 6. prayeth for the same in old age, or weakenes of bodie and spirite, 20. and promiseth perpetual gratitude and praises. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for perseverance in virtue.
The 7. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Concerning Salomon.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme is of Christ, perfigured by Salomon, whose kingdom was most glorious of al the kinges of Gods people; for of king Salomon himselfe manie thinges in this Psalme can not be truly vnderstood. S. Aug.

verses.text: O God giue thy iudgement to <na>(b)</na> the king: and thy iustice to <na>(c)</na> the sonne of the king. To iudge thy people in <na>(d)</na> iustice, and thy poore in iudgement.

notes.label: b
notes.text: O God most blessed Trinitie, geue powre and authoritie, to the Sonne of Man, God incarnate, King of al kinges,

notes.label: c
notes.text: the Sonne of king Dauid, to iudge for mankind against the diuel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Christ paying ransom for al mankind, and so man renouncing the diuel, and seruing God iustly, not iniuriously deliuered from captiuitie of sinne, and of the diuel.

verses.text: Let <na>(e)</na> the mountains receiue peace for the people: and <na>(f)</na> the litle hilles iustice.

notes.label: e
notes.text: A prophecie of the Apostles receiuing powre to preach Christs Gospel, of peace and reconciliation of men to God by penance;

notes.label: f
notes.text: and of other Apostolical men that folow their steppes.

verses.text: He <na>(g)</na> shal iudge the poore of the people, and shal saue the children of the poore: and he shal humble the calumniator.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Salomon in figure of Christ was for a time a iust and good king.

verses.text: And he shal <na>(h)</na> continew with the sunne, and before the moone in generation and generation.

notes.label: h
notes.text: But only Christ, not Salomon, nor anie other king of that people, contineweth, or reigneth for euer.

verses.text: He <na>(i)</na> shal descend as rayne vpon a fleece: and as droppes distilling vpon the earth.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The maner of Christs incarnation most silent, sweete, and gratful.

verses.text: There shal rise in his dayes iustice, and aboundance of peace, <na>(k)</na> vntil the moone be taken away.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Agane the prophet inculcateth that Christs kingdom, his Church, shal continew for euer.

verses.text: And he shal rule <na>(l)</na> from sea vnto sea: and from the riuer euen to the ends of the round world.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The Church is not only vniuersal in al times, but also in places.

verses.text: Before him shal the Æthiopians fal downe: and his enimies shal lick the earth. <cr>[1]</cr>
The <na>(m)</na> kinges of Tharsis, and <na>(n)</na> the Ilands shal offer presentes: the kings of the Arabians, and of Sabá shal bring giftes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: m
notes.text: The three Sages or Kinges, which adored our Sauiour, and offered gold, frankencense, and myrrh, were the first that fulfilled this prophecie : and afterwards Constantin the great, and other Emperors, Kinges, and Princes.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Amongst other Ilandes great Bryttannie (the greatest of Europe) was conuerted to Christ, according to this prophecie : first some few in the Apostles time (Metaphrastes apud Surium, Theodoret, epist. ad Timoth. Sophronius, Ser. de Nat. Apost, & alij.) More in the time of Eleutherius. Lastly our Englise nation by S. Augustin and others sent by S. Gregorie.

verses.text: And al kinges of the earth shal adore him: al nations shal serue him.
Because he shal deliuer the poore from the mightie: and the poore which had no helper.
He shal spare the poore and needy: and he shal saue the soules of the poore.
From vsuries and iniquitie he shal redeme their soules: and their name shal be honorable before him.
And <na>[1]</na> he shal liue, and there shal be giuen him of the gold of Arabia, and they shal adore it alwaies: al the day they shal blesse him.

notes.text: How is this prophecie verified, except the Church be alwayes visible?

verses.text: And there shal be a firmament in the earth, in the toppes of mountanes, the fruite therof shal be extolled farre aboue Libanus: and they shal florish of the citie, as the grasse of the earth.
Be his name blessed for euer: before the sunne his name is permanent. And al the tribes of the earth shal be blessed in him: al nations shal magnifie him.
Blessed be our Lord the God of Israel, <na>(o)</na> who only doth meruelous thinges.

notes.label: o
notes.text: No miracles can be donne but by Gods powre.

verses.text: And blessed be the name of his maiestie for euer: and al the earth shal be filled with his maiestie. <na>(p)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Aboue al other desires the holie prophet wished Gods glorie, and praises in al the earth, as it is in heauen.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> The praises of Dauid, <na>(r)</na> the sonne of Iesse are ended.

notes.label: q
notes.text: It semeth by this appendix added by Esdras, that this Psalme was last composed, though not put in the last place, but as it came to his handes.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Dauid the natural sonne of Iesse, made no more Hymnes, that is, no more musical praises of God after this Psalme, but the prefigured Dauid Christ our Sauiour, the Sonne of God, in his bodie the Church, singeth stil new praises. S. Aug. in enarrat. Psal. sequentis. 72.

chapters.summary: By way of prayer the Psalmist prophecieth Christs coming, our King and Iudge: 4. the deliuerer of mankind from the thraldom of the diuel. 8. the greatnes of his spiritual kingdom in the Gentiles. 16. and his continual glorie and praise. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ our King & Judge.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> to Asaph. HOw <na>(b)</na> good is God to Israel, to them, that are of a right hart! <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: To be songue by Asaph the master of musike, and his companie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God is so excellent good, as no tongue can expresse, no hart can conceiue.

verses.text: But <na>(c)</na> my feete were almost moued, my steppes almost slipped.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The peace and prosperitie of the wicked tempted me, to leaue the right narrow way, and to goe the brode easie way with them.

verses.text: Because I haue had zele vpon the wicked, seing the peace of sinners.
Because there is <na>(d)</na> no respect to their death: and <na>(e)</na> stabilitie in ther plague.

notes.label: d
notes.text: They neuer thincke of death;

notes.label: e
notes.text: and if they suffer some affliction, they quickly remoue it from them.

verses.text: In <na>(f)</na> the labours of men they are not, and with men they shal not be scourged.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They trauel not so much as good men do, neither are they so often punished.

verses.text: Therfore <na>(g)</na> hath pride helde them, they are couered with their iniquitie and impietie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Which maketh them proud, and so they runne into al sortes of iniquitie.

verses.text: Their iniquitie hath proceded as it were of fatte: they haue passed into <na>(h)</na> the affection of the hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Whatsoeuer mischief came in their mind, they feared not to committe it in fact.

verses.text: They haue thought, and haue spoken wickednes they haue spoken iniquitie <na>(i)</na> on high.

notes.label: i
notes.text: boldly extolling their owne wordes and workes, and despising others.

verses.text: They haue sette their mouth vnto heauen: ãd their tongue hath passed in the earth.
Therfore wil my people <na>(k)</na> returne here: and <na>(l)</na> ful daies shal be found in them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: For this prosperitie of the wicked, some of Gods people wil fall from the right way,

notes.label: l
notes.text: and their dayes wil abound with calamities.

verses.text: And they haue saide: <na>(m)</na> How doth God know, and is there knowledge in the highest?

notes.label: m
notes.text: The voice of the weake, inclining to diffidence, and doubt of Gods knowlege, and prouidence.

verses.text: Loe the sinners them selues, and they that abounde in the world, haue obtained riches.
And I saide: Then haue I iustified my hart without cause, and haue washed my handes amongst innocentes:
And haue bene scourged al the day, and my chastising in the morninges.
If I saide: I wil speake this: behold <na>(n)</na> I reproued the nation of thy children.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The prophet in his owne person answereth, that if he should say such thinges, he should reproue Gods children, as faultie, vnworthie of his protection, and to be neglected; wheras it is Gods prouidence to chastice his children whom he loueth.

verses.text: I <na>(o)</na> thought to know this thing, it is labour before me:

notes.label: o
notes.text: In this life we can not know the particular causes, why the iust are afflicted, and manie wicked prosper in this world.

verses.text: Vntil I may enter into the sanctuarie of God: and may vnderstand concerning their latter endes.
But yet <na>(p)</na> for guiles thou hast put it to them: thou hast cast them downe whiles they <na>(q)</na> were eleuated.

notes.label: p
notes.text: But only in general we are taught, that euils are prepared for the guiles, or deceptes,

notes.label: q
notes.text: pride, and other sinnes of the wicked.

verses.text: How are they brought into desolation, they haue failed sodanely: they haue perished for their iniquitie.
As the dreame of them that rise ô Lord, in thy citie thou shalt bring their <na>(r)</na> image to nothing.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Not real but imaginarie felicitie.

verses.text: Because my hart is <na>(s)</na> inflamed, and my reynes are changed:

notes.label: s
notes.text: Almost burned vp with afflictions.

verses.text: And I am brought to nothing, and knew not.
As <na>(t)</na> a beast am I become with thee: and I <na>(v)</na> alwaies with thee.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Charged with heauie burdens, without knowlege how long, or to what end,

notes.label: v
notes.text: yet not destitute of thy protection.

verses.text: Thou hast helde my right hand: and in thy wil thou hast conducted me, and with glorie thou hast receiued me.
For what is to me <na>(w)</na> in heauen? and besides thee what would I vpon the earth?

notes.label: w
notes.text: Nothing to be desired in heauen, nor in earth but God.

verses.text: My <na>(x)</na> flesh hath fainted, and my hart: God of my hart, and God my portion for euer.

notes.label: x
notes.text: In bodie and mind I thirst after thee, my true inheritance.

verses.text: For behold, they <na>(y)</na> that make them selues farre from thee, shal perish: thou <na>(z)</na> hast destroyed al, that fornicate from thee.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Men by their freewil make themselues enimies to God.

notes.label: z
notes.text: determined their damnation, forseing their final sinnes.

verses.text: But it is good for me to cleaue to God: to put my hope in our Lord God: That I may shew forth al thy prayses, in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet, first professing the vnspeakable goodnes of God, 2. in the person of the weake complaineth, that the wicked prosper, and the iust are afflicted. 15. reprehendeth the murmuration, for though we can not comprehend the secrete iudgements of God. 18. yet they are most iust. 25. So with desire to rest in God, he promiseth euer to praise him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Affliction in this world is recompensed in the end.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnderstanding <na>(a)</na> to Asaph. WHy hast thou ô God <na>(b)</na> repelled for euer: is thy furie wrath vpon the sheepe of thy pasture?

notes.label: a
notes.text: Instruction for the congregation of the faithful in distresse, not to seeke temporal rewardes and prosperitie, but to expect spiritual and eternal. S. Aug.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In long persecution the weake beginne to feare, or suspect, that God hath vtterly abandoned them.

verses.text: Be <na>(c)</na> mindful of thy congregation, <na>(d)</na> which thou hast possessed from the beginning. Thou hast <na>(e)</na> redemed the rod of thine inheritance: mount Sion, in which thou hast dwelt.

notes.label: c
notes.text: But the stronger pray with confidence,

notes.label: d
notes.text: being assured that God who hath conserued his Church hitherto, from the beginning of the world, wil conserue it stil to the end.

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other reason why God wil conserue his Church is, because he hath deliuered it often in a strong armie; as from bondage in Ægypt, from persecution and oppression in the time of Iudges, and kings, and lastly redemed it from the tyrannie of the diuel by Christs death.

verses.text: Lift vp thy handes vpon <na>(f)</na> their prides for euer: how great things hath the enimie done malignantly in the holy place:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Thirdly the pride of the enimies moueth God to reuenge their wickednes, and so to deliuer his owne people.

verses.text: And they that hate thee haue gloried: in the middes of <na>(g)</na> thy solemnitie. They haue sette <na>(h)</na> their signes, for signes:

notes.label: g
notes.text: They pretend to kepe solemne feastes like to thyne.

notes.label: h
notes.text: They set vp altares against thyn altares, or some new deuised external shew, against the holie Rites of the Church :

verses.text: and haue not knowne, <na>(i)</na> as in the issue on high. As <na>(k)</na> in a wood of trees they haue with axes

notes.label: i
notes.text: and that in publike places, in the endes of high wayes, or portes, and pinnacles.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The prophet describeth the maner how persecutors destroy temples, and al sacred thinges.

verses.text: cut out the gates therof together: in hatchet, and chippeaxe they haue cast it downe.
They haue burnt thy sanctuarie with fire: they haue polluted the tabernacle of thy name in the earth.
Their <na>(l)</na> kinred together haue saide in their hart: Let vs make al the festiual daies of God to cease from the earth.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The whole crew, or band of persecutors.

verses.text: Our <na>(m)</na> signes we haue not seene, there is now no prophet: and he wil know vs no more.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The weake complaine that God sheweth not wonted signes, nor sendeth succourse to his people, by raising some prophet, or other meanes to helpe them.

verses.text: How long ô God shal the enimie vpbraide: the aduersarie prouoke thy name for euer?
Why doest thou turne away thy hand, and thy right hand, out of the middes of thy bosome for euer?
But <na>(n)</na> God our king before the worldes: he hath wrought saluation in the middes of the earth. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: n
notes.text: The perfect do answer, that God both hath, and wil releeue his people.

verses.text: Thou in thy strength hast confirmed <na>(o)</na> the sea: thou hast <na>(p)</na> crushed the head of Dragons in the waters.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Made the redde sea like walles.

notes.label: p
notes.text: drowned Pharao and his hoste.

verses.text: Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: thou hast giuen him for meate to the peoples <na>(q)</na> of the Æthiopians.

notes.label: q
notes.text: of blacke diuels.

verses.text: Thou hast <na>(r)</na> broken vp fountaines, and torrentes: thou hast dried the riuers <na>(s)</na> of Ethan.

notes.label: r
notes.text: geuen water out of rockes,

notes.label: s
notes.text: made passage ouer Iordan.

verses.text: The day is thine, and the night is thine: thou hast made the morning and the sunne.
Thou hast made al the coastes of the earth: the summer and the spring thou hast formed them.
Be mindeful of this, the enimie hath vpbraided our Lord: and a foolish people hath prouoked thy name.
Deliuer not to beasts the soules that confesse to thee: and the soules of thy poore forget not for euer.
Haue respect vnto thy testament: because they that are <na>(t)</na> obscure of the earth, are filled with houses of iniquities.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Ignorant, blind, and barbarous infidels, lodge al kindes of iniquitie in their consciences.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Let not the humble be turned away being confounded: the poore and needy shal praise thy name.

notes.label: v
notes.text: And therfore it is vnmeete, that faithful people should be in bondage vnder them.

verses.text: Arise God, iudge thy cause: be mindful of those thy reproches, that are <na>(w)</na> from the foolish man al the day.

notes.label: w
notes.text: These foolish audacious men do continually blaspheme al holie thinges.

verses.text: <na>(x)</na> Forget not the voices of thine enimies: the <na>(y)</na> pride of them that hate thee, hath ascended alwaies.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Omitte not to punish them,

notes.label: y
notes.text: seing they are obstinate and obdurate in pride, and in hatred.

chapters.summary: Faithful people pressed with persecution lamentably complayning, besecheth God to respect his owne inheritance, cruelly afflicted; 10. and leift long without helpe, 12. wheras heretofore he releeued his people in like distresses. 18. And therfore confidently hopeth he wil renenge the blasphemers of his name, <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in long affliction.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> Corrupt not, a Psalme of Canticle to Asaph.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Either this was the beginning of a songue, to the tune wherof this Psalme was song; as some Hebrew Rabbins testifie; or, as S. Augustin and other fathers explicate, the Septuagint do admonish vs, by occasion of this Psalme, not to faile in our hope, for that God wil in no case violate his promise nor purpose, but wil render to euerie one in the day of Iudgement, as they deserue.

verses.text: We <na>(b)</na> wil confesse to thee ô God: <na>(c)</na> we wil confesse, and wil inuocate thy name. We wil tel thy meruelouse workes:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Christ with his Apostles, and other assessorie iudges, wil praise and thanke God, for his admirable good prouidence, and gouernement of this world.

notes.label: c
notes.text: This duplication of the same word, confirmeth vs of the assured performance of that, which is here prophecied.

verses.text: when <na>(d)</na> I shal take a time, I wil iudge iustices.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Christ our singular, principal, and proper Iudge only, and no mere creature, knoweth the determinate time of general iudgement.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> The earth is melted, and al that dwel in it: <na>(f)</na> I haue confirmed the pillers thereof.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The earth at that time shal be purged with flaming fire :

notes.label: f
notes.text: yet shal not be destroyed, but changed in qualities.

verses.text: I said to the wicked: <na>(g)</na> doe not wickedly: and to them that offend: <na>(h)</na> Exalt not the horne.

notes.label: g
notes.text: An epitome, or briefe summe of Christs doctrine, to flee from sinne.

notes.label: h
notes.text: be not proud, abuse not the powre you haue, to do what you please.

verses.text: Exalt not your horne on high: speake not iniquitie aganst God.
For neither from the East, nor from the West, nor from the desert mountanes:
<na>(i)</na> because God is Iudge. <na>(k)</na> This man he humbleth, and him he exalteth,

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVhen other Iudges sitte on tribunales, some may be absent, or escape from their sentences : but al without exception shal be brought in persons, when Christ God and Man shal iudge.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Some shal haue sentence of eternal paine in hel; some of eternal reward in glorie,

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> because there is a cuppe in the hand of our Lord <na>(m)</na> of mere wine ful of mixture. And he hath powred it out <na>(n)</na> of this into that, but yet the dregges therof are not emptied: al the sinners of the earth shal drinke.

notes.label: l
notes.text: though (partly in this world, partly in particular iudgement of euerie soule) God hath alreadie, and wil before the last day punish sinners, yet there resteth more punishment, and no impenitent sinners shal escape, but al shal drinke of the bitter cuppe of eternal damnation.

notes.label: m
notes.text: strong wine not delayde with water, but mingled with bitter sharpe thinges, as gal, vinegre, brimstone &c. and so powred into festered woundes, so they shal suffer vntolerable endles paine, mixed with the worme of conscience, losse of glorie, rancor of hart, and eternal desperation.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Varietie of hellish torments, from one extreme to another : as from snowwaters to exceeding heate. Iob. 24.

verses.text: But I wil shewforth for euer: I wil sing to the God of Iacob.
And I wil breake al the hornes of sinners: and <na>(o)</na> the hornes of the iust shal be exalted.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The iust for wel vsing their powre of freewil, and of al powre geuen them in this life, are rewarded in heauen.

chapters.summary: Christ (with his Assessors) wil iudge the whole world, at the last day: in the meane time exhorteth sinners to amend their life; 7. for none shal escape iust iudgement. 11. The wicked shal be punished, and the good rewarded. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
General iudgement.
The 9. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, in prayses, a Psalme <na>(a)</na> to Asaph, a Canticle to <na>(b)</na> the Assirians.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For the congregation of faithful and godlie people.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Amongst others, one notorious example of Gods prouidence is recorded of an hundred fourescore & fiue thousand Assirians, slaine in one night by an Angel. 4.Reg.19.

verses.text: God is knowne <na>(c)</na> in Iewrie: in Israel his name is great.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God was not only knowen in general, as to pagane Philosophers, and some others, but more particularly to the Iewes, the issue of Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob, by his special benefites towards them.

verses.text: And <na>(d)</na> his place is made in peace: and <na>(e)</na> his habitation in Sion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: God suffering al other nations to erre for their sinnes, in their fond phantesies of false goddes, reserued the Israelites for his Church,

notes.label: e
notes.text: establishing the principalitie therof in Sion.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> There he brake the powres of bowes, the shilde, the sword, and the battle.

notes.label: f
notes.text: For obtaining and conseruing of Sion from wicked Infidels, God ouerthrewe al sortes of contrarie forces.

verses.text: Thou <na>(g)</na> doest illuminate meruelousely from the eternal mountaynes:

notes.label: g
notes.text: God not only gaue his people temporal victories ouer their enimies, but also illuminated their mindes with knowlege of true religion:

verses.text: al the foolish of hart <na>(h)</na> were trubled. They <na>(i)</na> slept their sleepe: and al the men of riches found nothing in their handes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: others are often trubled in mind, hearing the truth, but are not conuerted through their obstinate follie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: VVorldlie men in supine carelesnes as in a sleepe, passe ouer this life, and afterwards find themselues excluded from heauen, for lacke of merites, and good workes, with the foolish virgins.

verses.text: At <na>(k)</na> thy reprehension ô God of Iacob, they <na>(l)</na> haue al slumbered that mounted on horses.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God vndertaking the defence of his people, and threatning the aduerse part,

notes.label: l
notes.text: they failed in courage, as men ouercome with drowsines of sleepe.

verses.text: Thou art terrible, and who shal resist thee? <na>(m)</na> from that time thy wrath.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Euen from the first notice of thy wil, the aduersaries were deiected, fearing thy potent wrath.

verses.text: From <na>(n)</na> heauen thou <na>[1]</na> hast made thy iudgement hearde: <na>(o)</na> the earth trembled and was quiet.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Terrible signes from the firmament appearing before the day of iudgement,

notes.label: o
notes.text: persecutors and others being terrified shal be astonied and silent.
The Prophetes do often speake in the preter-tence, for the assurance of the thinges to come.

verses.text: When God arose vnto iudgement, <na>(p)</na> that he might saue al the meeke of the earth.

notes.label: p
notes.text: God wil come to iudge the world, more especially for the iusts sake.

verses.text: Because <na>(q)</na> the cogitation of man shal confesse to thee: and <na>(r)</na> the remanes of the cogitation shal keepe festiual day to thee.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Men that shal seriously thinke and meditate vpon these thinges, wil praise and thanke God for them:

notes.label: r
notes.text: and the effect, and sweete repast of such meditation, shal make as it were a great festiual day, in the deuout soule spiritually ioyned with God.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Vowe ye, and <na>(t)</na> render to our Lord your God: al ye that round about him bring <na>(v)</na> giftes.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The soule thus inflamed with Gods loue, is then apt of gratitude, for his goodnes towardes man, to make vowes of thinges wherto we are not obliged,

notes.label: t
notes.text: but most necessarie it is to be maturely aduised, and not rashly, nor lightly to vow; for being once vowed, we are strictly bound to whatsoeuer we haue lawfully promised. And it is great sinne to vow vndiscretly.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Remembring that for vowes, and al other workes we must answer to God, who is a terrible iudge, readie to punish in bodie and soule, sparing none for their greatnes, not princes, nor kinges, nor vulgar sorte, for al are to him alike.

verses.text: To vthe terrible, and him that taketh away the spirite of princes, terrible to the kinges of the earth.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet singeth Gods praises, for his particular prouidence towards the Iewes: 10. further to be extended to al the meeke of the whole earth. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence towards his people.
The 3. key.

verses.text: and therefore he still reneweth his purpose to serve God sincerely, 15. particularly remembering the delivery of Israel from Ægypt. [1]

notes.text: Gods special protection of the Iewes. the 4. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Idithun, a psalme <na>(b)</na> to Asaph.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For Idithun to sing, or to make tune for it.

notes.label: b
notes.text: For the faithful congregation to consider Gods benefites.

verses.text: With <na>(c)</na> my voice I haue cried to our Lord: with my voice to God <na>(d)</na> and he attended to me. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: Hauing heretofore prayed,

notes.label: d
notes.text: I haue obtayned.

verses.text: In the day of my tribulation I sought God, with my handes <na>(e)</na> in the night before him: and I <na>(f)</na> was not deceiued. My <na>(g)</na> soule refused to be comforted,

notes.label: e
notes.text: Especially being in tribulation, and praying with hart and handes lifted vp, as wel in the night as day:

notes.label: f
notes.text: I was not frustrate of my prayer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: I was sometimes in such anguish that nothing semed comfortable,

verses.text: I <na>(h)</na> was mindeful of God, and was delighted, and was exercised: and <na>(i)</na> my spirite fainted.

notes.label: h
notes.text: but I relied vpon God so firmly,

notes.label: i
notes.text: that my spirite came into an extasie, or traunce.

verses.text: Myne eies <na>(k)</na> preuented the watches: I was <na>(l)</na> trubled, & spake not.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I arose early before the ordinarie time of awayking,

notes.label: l
notes.text: my hart being attentiue inwardly, I vttered nothing with my tongue.

verses.text: I thought vpon old daies: and the eternal yeares I had in minde.
And I meditated in the night with my hart, and I was exercised, and I <na>(m)</na> swept my spirite.

notes.label: m
notes.text: I diligently examined my conscience.

verses.text: Why, <na>(n)</na> wil God reiect for euer: or wil he not adde to be better pleased as yet?

notes.label: n
notes.text: Assuredly God wil not reiect for euer, but he wil be pleased with his Church.

verses.text: Or wil he cutte of his mercie for euer, from generation vnto generation?
Or wil God forget to haue mercie? or wil he in his wrath keepe in his mercies?
And I sayde: <na>(o)</na> Now haue I begune: <na>(p)</na> this is the change of the right hand of the Highest.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Whiles I thus thought, I erred greatly, now I see and confesse that God suffereth al calamities for the good of his seruantes:

notes.label: p
notes.text: and this I knew not by my selfe, but by the inspiration of God, making this change in me by his gracious hand.

verses.text: I haue bene mindful of the workes of our Lord: because I wil be mindful, from the beginning of thy meruelous workes.
And I wil meditate in al thy workes: and in thy inuentions I wil be exercised.
O God in the holie is thy way: what God is great as our God?
thou art the God that doest meruelous thinges. Thou hast made thy powre knowne among peoples:
thou hast with thine arme redemed thy people, the children of <na>(q)</na> Iacob, and Ioseph.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The progenie of Iacob, receiued and nourished in Ægypt for Iosephs sake, as his adopted children.

verses.text: The waters <na>(r)</na> saw thee ô God, the waters saw thee: and they were afrayd, and the depthes were trubled.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The read sea, and Iordan felt thy diuine powre, and obeyed thy wil.

verses.text: A <na>(s)</na> multitude of the sounding of waters: the cloudes gaue a voice. For in deede arrowes doe passe:

notes.label: s
notes.text: Noise of waters meeting after the Israelites were passed, thunders and lightninges also hapened, to the terror of the persecutors, though not mentioned in Exodus.

verses.text: the voice of thy thunder in a wheele. Thy lightenings shined to the rounde world: the earth was moued and trubled.
Thy way in the sea, and thy pathes in many waters: and thy steppes shal not be knowne. <cr>[1]</cr>
Thou hast conducted thy people as sheepe: <na>(t)</na> in the hand of moyses and Aaron.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Exo. 14 · By the ministerie of Moyses and Aaron.

chapters.summary: Anie faithful deuout person meditating Gods benefites, 7. examineth his cõscience, that nothing be in his soule, that may offend God. Who is alwayes readie to forgeue: 11. and therfore he stil reneweth his purpose to serue God sincerly, 15. particularly remembring the deliuerie of Israel from Ægypt.

verses.text: Vnderstanding <na>(a)</na> to Asaph. MY people attend ye to <na>(b)</na> my law: incline your eare vnto the wordes of my mouth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Commended to Asaph a chiefe musitian, that the people might vnderstand and consider Gods benefites.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither the law, nor the people was Dauids, but presenting Gods person, he speaketh in his name or authoritie, with whose inspiration he was replenished. S. Greg. Præfat. in Iob. c. 2.

verses.text: I wil open my mouth in <na>(c)</na> parables: I wil speake <na>(d)</na> propositions from the beginning.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Albeit the prophet reciteth historically thinges donne, yet the same were parables, similitudes, and figures of other thinges:

notes.label: d
notes.text: yea of secret hidden Mysteries, obscurly signified in the old Testament, and reueled in the new.

verses.text: How great thinges haue we heard and <na>(e)</na> haue knowne them, and <na>(f)</na> our fathers haue told vs.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Which partly we know by written holie Sriptures:

notes.label: f
notes.text: partly by Traditions.

verses.text: They were not hid from their children, in an other generation. Telling the prayses of our Lord, and his powers, and his meruelous workes which he hath done.
And he <na>(g)</na> raised vp a testimonie in Iacob: and <na>(h)</na> made a law in Israel. How great thinges he commanded our fathers, <na>(i)</na> to make

notes.label: g
notes.text: God of his mercie without precedent merite, raised vp a peculiar people of Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and gaue them a particular law, first of Circuncision, & more largely by Moyses.

notes.label: i
notes.text: So Abraham instructed his children and his house after him, Gen. 18.

verses.text: the same knowne to their children: that <na>(k)</na> an other generation may know. The children that shal be borne, and shal rise vp, and shal tel their children.

notes.label: k
notes.text: in like sorte others taught their children.

verses.text: That they may <na>(l)</na> put their hope in God, and may <na>(m)</na> not forget the workes of God: and may <na>(n)</na> seeke after his commandmentes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For three causes God gaue his law, that his people may haue confidence in him, he shewing his care to instruct and gouerne them;

notes.label: m
notes.text: that they remember his benefites;

notes.label: n
notes.text: and kepe his commandmentes.

verses.text: That they become not as their fathers: <na>(o)</na> a peruerse generation and exasperating. A generation, that hath not directed their hart, their spirit hath not bene faithful towards God. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: o
notes.text: The Iewish nation very often, and in great numbers murmured, rebelled, and committed other great sinnes, and therfore Dauid exhorted the people of his time, not to do the like. And this exhortation perteyneth more especially to Christianes. as S. Paul teacheth. 1. Cor. 10.

verses.text: The <na>(p)</na> children of Ephrem bending, and shooting with bow: were turned in the day of battel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: They first (trusting in their owne strength) without Gods commandment (Num. 14.) went forth to batle and were ouerthrowne. 1. Par 7. v. 11.

verses.text: They kept not the testament of God: and in his law they would not walke.
And they forgate his benefites, and his meruelous workes, which he shewed them.
Before their fathers he did meruelous thinges in the land of Ægypt, in the filde <na>(q)</na> of Tanis.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Tanis the principal citie in Ægypt nere the riuer Nilus, where Moyses wrought his great miracles.

verses.text: He diuided the sea & brought them through: and he made the waters to stand as in a bottle. <cr>[1]</cr>
And he <na>(r)</na> conducted them in a cloude by day: and al the night by light of fire.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This cloude shadowed them from the heate of the sunne in the day, and the fire shined in the night, al the time that they were in the desert.

verses.text: He stroke the rocke in <na>(s)</na> the desert: and gaue them water to drinke as in a great depth.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In mount Horeb: and there was continual water in al the campe, which occupied nere foure miles in length and breadth.

verses.text: And he brought forth water out of the rocke: and made waters runne downe as riuers.
And they added as yet to sinne vnto him: they prouoked the Highest to wrath in the place <na>(t)</na> without water.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Which naturally wanted water: but by miracle had abundance.

verses.text: And they tempted God in their hartes: so that they asked <na>(v)</na> meats for their liues.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Not content with Manna, they demanded to haue flesh.

verses.text: And they spake euil of God: they saide: Can God prepare a table in the desert?
Because he stroke the rocke and waters ranne, & torrentes flowed: <na>(w)</na> Can he also giue <na>(x)</na> bread, or prepare a table for his people?

notes.label: w
notes.text: Stil incredulous, not beleuing Gods omnipotencie, they thought that, albeit he had geuen them manna, and water, yet he could not geue them flesh.

notes.label: x
notes.text: By bread in general is vnderstood al competent meate vsual for a table.

verses.text: Therfore our Lord heard, and <na>(y)</na> made delay: and <na>(z)</na> fire was kindled in Iacob, and wrath ascended vpon Israel.

notes.label: y
notes.text: For this incredulitie, murmuring, and other sinnes God kept the children of Israel fourtie yares in the desert, til al that were of age, when they came from Ægypt, were dead, except only Iosue and Caleb.

notes.label: z
notes.text: In the meane time amongst other punishments, manie murmurers were burnt to death with strange fire. Num. 11.

verses.text: Because they beleued not in God, nor hoped in his saluation.
And he commanded the cloudes from aboue, and opened the gates of heauen.
And he rayned them Manna to eate, and bread of heauen he gaue to them.
Bread <na>(a)</na> of Angels did man eate: he sent them victuals in abundance.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Manna made by Angels.

verses.text: He <na>(b)</na> transported the Southwinde from heauen: and in his powre he brought in the Southwest winde.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God so changed the wind, that it brought abundance of quailes and other birdes, into their campe. Exo. 16. Nu. 11.

verses.text: And he rayned vpon them flesh as dust: and as the sand of the sea fethered fowles.
And they fel in the middes of their campe: about their tabernacles.
And they did eate and were filled excedingly, and their desire he brought to them:
They were not defrauded of their desire. <na>(c)</na> As yet their meats were in their mouth:

notes.label: c
notes.text: Immediatly after a moneth (for so long they had abundance of these birdes ibid. v. 20,) they were striken with a plague, and manie died, for their concupiscence.

verses.text: And the wrath of God ascended vpon them. And he killed their fat ones, and <na>(d)</na> the chosen of Israel he hindered.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The most fresh strong men died, and so were hindered from possessing the promised land of Chanaan.

verses.text: In al these things they sinned as yet: and they beleued not in his meruelous workes.
And their daies failed in vanitie: and their years <na>(e)</na> in hast.

notes.label: e
notes.text: In fourtie yeares aboue six hundred thousand died.

verses.text: When he slew them, they sought him: and they returned, and <na>(f)</na> early they came to him.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They offered morning sacrifice.

verses.text: And they remembred that God is their helper: and the high God is their redemer.
And they loued him <na>(g)</na> with their mouth, and with their tongue they did lie to him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: But were not sincere in their hartes.

verses.text: But their hart was not right with him: neither were they counted faithful in his testament.
<na>(h)</na> But he is merciful, and wil be propicious to their sinnes: and he wil not destroy them. And he abunded to turne away his wrath: and he kindled not al his wrath.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Howsoeuer multitudes of people committe great sinnes, and are seuerely punished, yet Gods mercie preserueth some by his effectual grace, and neuer suffereth the whole Church to faile, nor to be destroyed.

verses.text: And he remembred that they are flesh: <na>(i)</na> spirit going, and not returning.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Mans life is like the winde, that stil passeth, and the same returneth not. As Aristotel teacheth. Here the Hebrewes note the middes of the Psalter, in 1263. verses. and so manie in the rest.

verses.text: How <na>(k)</na> often haue they exasperated him in the desert: prouoked him to wrath in the place without water.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The people of Israel murmured so often in the desert, that it was not easie to tel how often. See the Annotation.

verses.text: And <na>(l)</na> they returned, and tempted God: and the holie one of Israel they exasperaed.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For efsoones repenting they offended God againe and againe.

verses.text: They did not remember his hand: in the day that he redemed them from the hand of the afflicter.
As he put <na>(m)</na> his signes in Ægypt, and his wonders in the filde of Tanis.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The first signe was in turning a rodde into a serpent, which was a miracle, but no plague, the other signes were also plagnes to the Ægyptians.

verses.text: And he turned <na>(n)</na> their riuers into bloude, & their <na>(o)</na> showers that they might not drinke.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The first plague.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Pooles, lakes, and al sortes of water, yea showers, or raine water, which seldome happeneth in Ægypt.

verses.text: He sent vpon them <na>(p)</na> a swarme of flies, and it eate them: and <na>(q)</na> the frogge, and it destroyed them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: p
notes.text: The fourth plague, in order as they are recited in Exodus.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The second plague.
* Coenomyiam.

verses.text: And he gaue their fruites to <na>(r)</na> the blast, and their labors to <na>(s)</na> the locuste.

notes.label: r
notes.text: This was ∷ lesse plague, not mentioned in with the greater.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The eight plague.

verses.text: And he killed their vineyeardes with <na>(t)</na> haile: and their mulberie trees with <na>(v)</na> horefrost.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The seuenth plague.

notes.label: v
notes.text: This also is omitted in. · Exodus.

verses.text: And he deliuered <na>(w)</na> their beast to haile: and their possession <na>(x)</na> to fire.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Not only al trees, and plantes, but also beastes were subiect to the haile.

notes.label: x
notes.text: and to firie leghtnings.

verses.text: He sent vpon them <na>(y)</na> the wrath of his indignation: indignation, & wrath, and tribulation: immissions <na>(z)</na> by euil angels.

notes.label: y
notes.text: In these general termes, of wrath, indignation, and tribulation, the Prophet comprehendeth al the other plagues, to witte, the third of scinies, the fifth of pestilence, the sixt of boyles in men and beastes, the ninth of darknes three dayes together.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Al which God sent by the ministerie of diuels, euil angels.

verses.text: He made a way to the path of his wrath, he spared not their liues from death: and their cattel he shut vp in death.
And <na>(a)</na> he stroke al the firstborne in the land of Ægypt: the first fruites of al their labors in the tabernacles <na>(b)</na> of Cham.

notes.label: a
notes.text: a The tenth and greatest plague, 11. v. 5. & c. 12. v. 29.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Egyptians also descended from cham, by his sonne Mesraim. Gen. 10. v. 6.

verses.text: And he <na>(c)</na> tooke away his people as sheepe: and led them as a flock in the desert.

notes.label: c
notes.text: After that Ægypt was thus plagued, God brought Israel out of their seruitude, as a shepheard leddeth his sheepe, and defendeth them.

verses.text: And he brought them forth in hope, and they feared not: and the sea couered their enemies.

And he brought them into <na>(d)</na> the mount of his <na>(e)</na> sanctification, the mount, which his right hand purchased. And he cast <na>(f)</na> out the gentiles from their face: and by lot he diuided the land of them in a corde of distribution:

notes.label: d
notes.text: Iudea a hillie countrie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Into that countrie which God chose, and endewed with manie blessinges.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As is written in Iosue.

verses.text: And he made the tribes of Israel to dwel in their tabernacles.
And <na>(g)</na> they tempted, and exasperated God the highest, and they kept not his testimonies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: After the conquest and quiet possession, the Israelites often fel into grosse sinnes, especially in the time of Iudges.

verses.text: And they turned away themselues, & kept not the couenant: euen as their fathers, they were turned as a <na>(h)</na> crooked bow.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A croked bow deceiueth the archer, so this people failed to serue God, and deceiued themselues.

verses.text: They incensed him to wrath in their <na>(i)</na> hilles: and in their <na>[1]</na> grauens they prouoked him <na>(k)</na> to emulation.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In their altares erected in hilles to Idoles.

notes.label: k
notes.text: By grauen imagies of Idoles, they prouoked God to indignation.
* Sculptilibus.

verses.text: God heard, and contemned: and he brought Israel to nothing <na>(l)</na> excedingly.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Not absolutely to nothing, but punished them exceedingly, til they repented, and then spared and deliuered them from tribulation, as appeareth in the booke of Iudges.

verses.text: And he reiected the tabernacle <na>(m)</na> of Silo, his tabernacle, <na>(n)</na> where he dwelt among men.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The Arke of God sometime kept in Silo, Iosue 18. in the tribe of Ephraim, was taken by the Philistims. 1. Keg. 4. and neuer returned thither agane.

notes.label: n
notes.text: but whersoeuer the Arke was, there God more especially heard their petitions, and gaue answers.

verses.text: And he deliuered <na>(o)</na> their force into captiuitie: and their beautie into the hands of the enemie.

notes.label: o
notes.text: For their sinnes God suffered the Arke to be taken.

verses.text: And he <na>(p)</na> shut vp his people in the sword: and he dispised his inheritance.

notes.label: p
notes.text: And the Israelites to be sore afflicted by their enimies.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Fyre deuoured their young men: and their virgins were not lamented.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The zele, and iust wrath of God suffered these calamities to happen.

verses.text: Their <na>(r)</na> Priestes fel by the sworde: and their widowes were not wept for.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Ophni and Phinees the sonnes of Heli slaine and Heli himselfe hearing that the Arke was taken fel from his stoole and broke his neck. 1. Reg 4.

verses.text: And <na>(s)</na> our Lord was raised vp as one that sleepeth: as a mightie man hauing surfited of wine.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Neuertheles God plagued the infidels, and conserued his Church. 1. Reg. 5.

verses.text: And he stroke his enimies on the hinder partes: an euerlasting reproch he gaue to them.
And he reiected the tabernacle <na>(t)</na> of Ioseph: and the tribe of Ephraim he chose not.

notes.label: t
notes.text: As before. v. 60.

verses.text: But he chose the tribe <na>(v)</na> of Iuda, mount Sion which he loued.

notes.label: v
notes.text: After a time the Arke was brought into the tribe of Iuda.

verses.text: And he built <na>(w)</na> his sanctuarie as of vnicornes in the land, which he hath founded for euer.

notes.label: w
notes.text: The Church was firme, and euer preserued in the old testament til Christ, and from Christs time to the end of the world.

verses.text: And <na>(x)</na> he chose Dauid his seruant, and tooke him from the flockes of sheepe: from after the ewes with yong he tooke him.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Gods particular grace in choosing, and exalting Dauid, was a special benefite to the Israelites.

verses.text: To <na>(y)</na> feede Iacob his seruant, and Israel his inheritance.

notes.label: y
notes.text: To rule and gouerne the people of Israel.

verses.text: And he fedde them in the innocencie of his hart: and in the vnderstandings of <na>(z)</na> his hands he conducted them.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Prudently vsing his powre and authoritie.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet exhorting the people to attend, 5. reciteth manie great benefites of God towards their forefathers (whose ingratitude, often rebellion, and chatisement he stil noteth) 9. 11 in their entrance into the land of Chanaan: 12. also before the same in Ægypt, and in the desert. 42. How God plagued the Ægyptians: 52. protected, and conducted his people into the promised land. 56. where likewise they often offended, were punished: 65. yet were stil conserued: 69. and the tribe of Iuda exalted in king Dauid. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's great Benefits bestowed upon the Jews, and their ingratitude.
The 4. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> to Asaph. O God <na>(b)</na> the Gentiles are come into thine inheritance, they <na>(c)</na> haue polluted thy holie temple: they haue made Ierusalem <na>(d)</na> as a watch toure of fruits.

notes.label: a
notes.text: to be sungue by Asaph and his companie, in the behalfe of people vnited in faith.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Cruel infidels haue inuaded those thinges, which perteyne to thy Church:

notes.label: c
notes.text: euen possessed and prophaned the holie temple of the Iewes, and Churches of Catholique Christians. Fulfilled by Antiochus, in Ierusalem; by the Vandals in Afrike, by Protestants, and Puritanes, in diuers partes of Europe, and wil be more vniuersally by Antichrist in al Christendom.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In steed of great and faire Churches, Gods seruantes are fane to vse meane houses, yea poore cotages.

verses.text: They haue made <na>(e)</na> the carcases of thy seruants, meats for the foules of the aire: the flesh of thy sainctes for the beastes of the land.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some persecutors suffer not Martyrs bodies to be buried, but hang them on polles, and pinnacles, where birdes may eate them.

verses.text: They haue poured out their bloude as water round about Ierusalem: and there was none to burie them.
We are <na>(f)</na> become a reproch to our neighboures: a scorne and mocke to them that are round about vs.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Christianes Gallileans, Catholiques Homousians, and now Papistes, in spite and reproch.

verses.text: How long ô Lord wilt thou <na>(g)</na> be angrie for euer: shal thy zele be kindled as a fire?

notes.label: g
notes.text: Sinnes prouoking Gods wrath, are one cause why he suffereth his people to be persecuted.

verses.text: Poure out thy wrath vpon the Gentiles, <na>(h)</na> that haue not knowne thee: & vpon the kingdomes, that haue not inuocated thy name.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Though the faithful committe some sinnes, yet in respect that they beleue righly, haue zele in Gods cause, and denie not God, they are nerer to grace and fauour.

verses.text: Because they haue deuoured Iacob: and his place they haue made desolate.
<na>(i)</na> Remember not our old iniquities, let thy mercies quickly preuent vs: because we are become exceding <na>(k)</na> poore.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Especially when they repent, and confesse their sinnes, then those that neither know nor wil know God; but obstinatly impugne and resist the truth,

notes.label: k
notes.text: so much afflicted, and despised, that none wil regard the truth which we professe.

verses.text: Help vs ô God our sauiour: and for the glorie of thy name ô Lord deliuer vs: and be propicious to our sinnes for thy names sake.

Lest they say perhaps amongst the Gentiles: <na>(l)</na> where is their God? and <na>(m)</na> be notified in the nations before our eies. The reuenge of the bloud of thy seruants, which hath benne shed:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Albeit ô Lord, thou suffer vs to be punished, yet suffer not thyn enimies to insult, as though thou were not our God; and consequently thou haddest no people at al in the world.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Therfore we pray, that the reuenge of thy seruantes bloud may be so notified, that it can not be denied, nor doubted of. Which is also here prophesied, that it wil so come to passe in the end.

verses.text: let the groning of the fettered enter in thy sight. According to the greatnes of thine arme, possesse thou <na>(n)</na> the children of them that are put to death.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Preserue also, ô God, the reliques of thy seruantes, the successors of thy Martyrs.

verses.text: And <na>(o)</na> tender to our neighboures seuenfold in their bosome: their reproch wherewith they haue reproched thee ô Lord.

notes.label: o
notes.text: This also is a prophesie, that God wil most seuerely reuenge the blasphemie of persecutors.

verses.text: But <na>(p)</na> we thy people, and the sheepe of thy pasture, wil confesse to thee for euer: Vnto generation and generation we wil shew forth thy praise.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Gods people deliuered from persecution, and perpetually conserued, wil alwayes praise God for the same.

chapters.summary: The Prophet, in person of the Church, lamenteth the crueltie of persecutors (both in the old and new testament) 5. prayeth for release, with iust reuenge against Gods enimies, that blaspheme his name, 3. and promiseth to be gratful in diuine praises. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church suffereth very great persecutions.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for <na>(b)</na> them, that shal be changed, testimonie to <na>(c)</na> Asaph, a Psalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Perteyning to the new Testament,

notes.label: b
notes.text: especially to Gentiles, that shal be conuerted to Christ.

notes.label: c
notes.text: for perpetual memorie to the congregation of faithful.

verses.text: Thou that rulest Israel, attend: that <na>(d)</na> conductest Ioseph as a sheepe. Which sittest vpon the cherubs <na>(e)</na> be manifest <na>(f)</na>

notes.label: d
notes.text: By Ioseph the prophet vnderstandeth al Israel; because the first birthright being taken from Ruben was geuen to him, to witte duble portion of enheritance, two tribes of twelue.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Appeare, and shew thy mightie hand before thy people:

notes.label: f
notes.text: wherof Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manasses folowing the Arke, when they marched or camped, should most directly see what appeared therin, the other nine tribes being placed before it, and on both sides. Num. 2.

verses.text: before Ephraim, Beniamin, and Manasses. Raise vp <na>(g)</na> thy might, and come, to saue vs.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Thou which alwayes can helpe vs, now vse thy powre in deliuering vs from this temporal miserie.

verses.text: O God <na>(h)</na> conuert vs: and shew <na>(i)</na> thy face, & we shal be saued.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Set vs in a better state.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Shew thy benigne countenance and fauoure, Mystically, send the promised Messias, Christ, the essential Image of God. 1. Cor. 4. v. 4. Collos. 1. v. 15.

verses.text: O Lord the God of hostes, how long wilt thou be angrie <na>(k)</na> vpon the prayer of thy seruant?

notes.label: k
notes.text: How long wilt thou differre to heare our prayer?

verses.text: Thou wilt feede vs with the bread of teares: and giue vs drinke with teares <na>(l)</na> in mesure.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Thou dost iustly punish vs, but thou temperest the same with measure, that it exceede not to our ruines.

verses.text: Thou hast made vs to be a contradiction to our neighboures and our enimies haue scorned vs.
O God of hosts <na>(m)</na> conuert vs: and shew thy face, and we <na>(n)</na> shal be saued.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God first preuenting with his grace,

notes.label: n
notes.text: man may cooperate therwith to his iustification, and saluation.

verses.text: Thou didst transport <na>(o)</na> the vineyeard out of Ægypt: thou didst cast out <na>(p)</na> the Gentiles, and plantedst it.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Thy Church and people,

notes.label: p
notes.text: the Chananites.

verses.text: Thou wast the guide of the way <na>(q)</na> in the sight therof: thou didst plant the rootes therof, and it <na>(r)</na> filled the earth.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The cloude, and piller of fire were visible guides.

notes.label: r
notes.text: and it multiplied mightely.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> The shadow of it couered the mountanes: and the bowghes of it the ceders of God.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Hyperbolical speach to signifie the great multiplication of the Israelites.

verses.text: It extended her branches euen to <na>(t)</na> the sea; and her boughes vnto <na>(v)</na> the riuer.

notes.label: t
notes.text: from the mediterranean sea of Palestin,

notes.label: v
notes.text: to the riuer Euphrates. Exo. 23. v. 31. Deut. 11. v. 24.

verses.text: Why hast thou destroyed the hedge therof: and al that passe by the way doe plucke it.
The <na>(w)</na> boare of the wood hath destroyed it: and <na>(x)</na> the singular wilde beest hath eaten it.

notes.label: w
notes.text: cruel enimies more like to most cruel beastes then to men.

notes.label: x
notes.text: yea so cruel, as none els in the world are like vnto them.

verses.text: O God of hoasts returne: regard <na>(y)</na> from heauen, and see, and visite this vineyeard.

notes.label: y
notes.text: The Prophet now prayeth for the coming of Christ, which he saw in spirite.

verses.text: And <na>(z)</na> perfite it, which thy right hand hath planted: and vpon <na>(a)</na> the sonne of man whom thou hast confirmed to thee.

notes.label: z
notes.text: The Church of the old testament, in her best state, wanted the perfection, which the Church of Christ hath.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Christ our Messias most commonly calleth by this title: The Sonne of man.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Thinges burnt with fyre, and digged doune at the increpation of thy countenance shal perish.

notes.label: b
notes.text: So thy vinyard can not indure if it be stil afflicted, and trodden downe.

verses.text: Let <na>(c)</na> thy hand be vpon the man of thy right hand: and vpon the sonne of man, whom thou hast confirmed to thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Christ working by Gods powre redresseth al miseries.

verses.text: And we depart not from thee, thou wilt quicken vs: and we wil inuocate thy name.
<na>(d)</na> O Lord the God of hoastes conuert vs: and shew thy face, and we shal be saued.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The same is the 8. and the 15 verse (with litle alteration) and here repeted the third time, In which we also pray for three thinges first to be purged, and conuerted from sinne, second to be illuminated by Christ, the Image of God, Thirdly to be sanctified, and saued in eternal glorie to haue the fruition of the most blessed Trinitie.

chapters.summary: The Prophet prayeth for the release of Israel in great tribulation. 15. forsheweth the coming of Christ to redeme man from sinne, and from thraldome of the diuel. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ our Redeemer from sin and captivity.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, for <na>(b)</na> wine presses, a Psalme to <na>(c)</na> Asaph him selfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme perteyneth not only to the old testament, but also to the new,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Gods seruants oppressed with tribulations,

notes.label: c
notes.text: to be songue by Asaph a chief master of musike.

verses.text: Reioice to God our helper: make Iubilation to the God of Iacob.
Take ye Psalme, and <na>(d)</na> giue timbrel: pleasant Psalter with the harpe.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Make readie al these musical instruments.

verses.text: Sound ye with trumpet in <na>(e)</na> the <na>[1]</na> new moone, in <na>(f)</na> the <na>[2]</na> notable day of your solemnitie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: In the Calendes, or first day of euerie moneth, in remembrance of Gods prouidence, and perpetual gouernment of al creatures:

notes.label: f
notes.text: and most especial solemnitie in the first day of the seuenth moneth, in memorie of Isaac conserued from death, in whom God promised Abraham, to multiplie his seede, and to blesse al nations. Gen. 17. v. 21. c. 21. v. 12. c. 22. v. 18.
The feast of Neomenia.
Feast of trumpetes.

verses.text: Because it is a precept in Israel, and iudgement to the God of Iacob.
He put it for a testimonie in <na>(g)</na> Ioseph, when he came out of the Land of Ægypt: he heard a tongue which he knew not.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The people of Israel signified by Ioseph, as Psal. 79. v. 2.

verses.text: He <na>[1]</na> turned away his backe <na>(h)</na> from burdens: his handes serued in baskettes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God deliuered the same people from their vntolerable bondage of carying burdens in baskettes, from geathering straw, making brickes, and other seruitude. Exo. 1. v. 14. c. 5. v. 7.
In memorie of this benefite Pasch was instituted.

verses.text: In <na>(i)</na> tribulation thou didest inuocate me, and I heard thee: I heard thee in the secret of the tempest: I <na>(k)</na> proued thee at the water of contradiction.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The admonition of God to the people:

notes.label: k
notes.text: yet after so great benefites thou didest murmure, and contradict me. Exo. 17. Num. 20.

verses.text: Heare ô my people: and I <na>(l)</na> wil contest thee: Israel <na>(m)</na> if thou wilt heare me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seriously admonish thee.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Man by free wil may choose whether he wil obey or no.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> There shal be <na>(n)</na> no new God in thee, neither shalt thou adore a strange God.

notes.label: n
notes.text: This was an other great benefite, to geue an expresse law, for their instruction.
The feast of Pentecost in memorie of the lawe.

verses.text: For I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Ægypt: <na>(o)</na> dilate thy mouth and I wil fil it.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Obseruing my commandments, aske what thou wilt, and I wil geue it thee.

verses.text: And my People heard not my voice: and Israel attended not to me.
And I let them alone, according to the desires of their hart, they shal goe in their owne inuentions. <cr>[1]</cr>
If my people had heard me: if Israel had walked in my wayes:
I had <na>(p)</na> for nothing, <na>(q)</na> perhaps humbled their enimies: and had laide my hand vpon those that afflict them.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Very easely.

notes.label: q
notes.text: of my freewil and liberalitie, without necessitie or obligation.

verses.text: The enimies of our Lord haue lied to him: and <na>(r)</na> their time shal be for euer.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The wicked that promise to serue God, and do it not shal be in eternal torments:

verses.text: And <na>(s)</na> he fedde them of the fatte of corne: and out of the rocke, with honie he filled them.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In the meane time God bestowed these benefites vpon them, for the iusts sake.

chapters.summary: Al men are inuited to celebrate festiual dayes, 6. which were instituted in memorie of benefites receiued. 9. the deuont shal be protected, and the negligent leift in distresse. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Invitation to celebrate festival days devoutly.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Psalme to Asaph. God stood in the assemblie <na>(a)</na> of goddes, and in the middes he <na>(b)</na> iudgeth goddes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wordes of the prophet, admonishing al magistrates, that when they sitte in iudgement, or determine anie cause, God who is there, and euerie where present,

notes.label: b
notes.text: attendeth their processe: and therfore it behoueth them to be aduised what they doe: euen as if they heard God speaking as here foloweth:

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> How long iudge ye iniquitie: and accept ye the persons of sinners.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The wordes of God, though not vttered sensibly, yet in effect intimated by his law, according:· wherto he wil procede in iudgement against vniust Iudges.

verses.text: Iudge ye for the needie and the pupil: iustifie ye the humble, and the poore.
Take away the poore: and deliuer the needie from the hand of the sinner.
They <na>(d)</na> knew not, neither did they vnderstand, they walke in darkenesse: <na>(e)</na> al the fundations of the earth shal be moued.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Such iudges procede in grosse ignorance, not caring to vnderstand, but content to walke in darknes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Ye are so euil disposed, that you would turne al vpside downe, iustifying the wicked, and condemning the iust.

verses.text: I saide: Yow are <na>(f)</na> goddes, and the sonnes of the highest al.

notes.label: f
notes.text: For your office which you participate of me, you are certaine goddes vpon earth:

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> But you shal die as men: and fal <na>(h)</na> as one of the princes. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: But when you die you shal find that you are men, subiect to Gods iudgement.

notes.label: h
notes.text: yea your punishment wil be greuous, and importable: for the mightie shal mightely suffer torments. sap.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Arise ô God, iudge the earth: <na>(k)</na> because thou shalt inherite in al the Gentiles.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Againe the wordes of the prophet praying God,

notes.label: k
notes.text: that eing he is Lord of al he wil iudge al.

chapters.summary: The Prophet declareth, 2. that God reprehendeth vniust Iudges and Magistrates: premonisheth them of his seuere & eternal punishment: 8. Wherto the prophet conforming his wil prayeth for the same. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Admonition to Magistrates.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Canticle of Psalme to Asaph.
O God <na>(a)</na> who shal be like to thee? <na>(b)</na> hold not thy peace, <na>(c)</na> neither be thou appeased ô God:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Seing none is like to thee ô God,

notes.label: b
notes.text: shew thy powre and maiestie,

notes.label: c
notes.text: be not silent.

verses.text: For behold <na>(d)</na> thine enimies haue made a sound: they that hate thee, <na>(e)</na> haue lifted vp the head.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The cruel persecuters are most insolent,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and proud.

verses.text: They haue taken malignant counsel vpon thy people: and they haue deuised against thy saincts.
They haue saide: Come, and let vs destroy them out of <na>(f)</na> the nation: and let <na>(g)</na> the name of Israel be remembred no more.

notes.label: f
notes.text: That there be no more anie faithful people,

notes.label: g
notes.text: anie Catholiques left aliue.

verses.text: Because they haue deuised with one consent: they haue together made a couenant against thee.
The tabernacles of <na>(h)</na> the Idumeians, and <na>(i)</na> the Ismahelites <na>(k)</na> Moab, and <na>(l)</na> the Agarens.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The progenie of Esau,

notes.label: i
notes.text: the seede of Ismael.

notes.label: k
notes.text: descending from the elder sonne of Lot.

notes.label: l
notes.text: the issue of Abraham by Agar, who falsly cal themselues Sarascens, as if they were of Sara.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Gebal, and <na>(n)</na> Ammon, and <na>(o)</na> Amalec: <na>(p)</na> the foreners, with <na>(q)</na> the inhabitantes of Tyre.

notes.label: m
notes.text: People of Gebal à citie of Syria,

notes.label: n
notes.text: of the other sonne of Lot.

notes.label: o
notes.text: those that first oppugned the Israelites, after they were parted from Ægypt. Exo. 17.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The Philistians,

notes.label: q
notes.text: and Tyrians, al nere neighboures, and some of them nere akine to the Israelites, were their great enimies.

verses.text: Yea and <na>(r)</na> Assur also is come with them: they are made an aide to the children of Lot.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Others also coming further of, ioyned against Gods people, in figure that al heretikes, and other infidels conspire together against Catholiques.

verses.text: Doe to them as <na>(s)</na> to Madian, and <na>(t)</na> Sisara: as to <na>(v)</na> Iabin in the torrent Cisson.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The Psalmist therfore prayeth (and withal prophecieth) that God wil at last destroy them, as he did Madian. Num 31. Iudic. 6. & 7.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Sisara captaine general,

notes.label: v
notes.text: for Iabin king of Asor nere Cisson. Iudic. 4. v. 7. & 23.

verses.text: They perished <na>(w)</na> in Endor: they were made as <na>(x)</na> the dung of the earth.

notes.label: w
notes.text: Within the territorie of Manasses (Ios. 17.) which they inuaded.

notes.label: x
notes.text: slaine and not buried.

verses.text: Put their princes as <na>(y)</na> Oreb, and Zeb, and Zebee, and Salmana.

notes.label: y
notes.text: These foure princes of the Madianites were slaine by Gedeons forces Iudic. 7. & 8.

verses.text: Al their princes: which haue saide: Let vs possesse the Sanctuarie of God for an inheritance.
My God put them <na>(z)</na> as a wheele: and as stubble before the face of the winde.

notes.label: z
notes.text: By foure similitudes the prophet describeth the punishment that shal fal vpon persecuters.
