verses.text: Euen as fire that burneth a wood: & as a flame that burneth the mountaines:
So shalt thou pursew them in thy tempest: and in thy wrath thou shalt truble them.
Fil their faces with ignominie: and <na>(a)</na> they wil seeke thy name, ô Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God by punishing seeketh the conuersion of sinners, not their eternal death.

verses.text: Let <na>(b)</na> them be ashamed, and trubled for euer and euer: and let them be confounded, and perish.

notes.label: b
notes.text: But such as be stil obstinate, and finally impenitent do perish for euer.

verses.text: And let them know that <na>(c)</na> Lord is thy name, thou onlie the Highest in al the earth.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God only the creator of heauen and earth is properly called LORD: VVhose essential, and incommunicable name is VVHICH IS. Exo. 3. v. 14. & 6. v. 3.

chapters.summary: The Church impugned by al sortes of enimies 10. prayeth God to confound them, as she hath donne diuers the like, 17. wherby some shal be conuerted. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Persecuters of the Church confounded or converted.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, <na>(a)</na> for wine presses, <na>(b)</na> the children of Core, a Psalme.

notes.label: a
notes.text: For men afflicted in this vale of miserie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: By the children of Core not being musitians (but porters in the temple, 1. Par. 26.) S. Augustin here and in other titles of Psalmes, vnderstandeth the faithful children of Christ.

verses.text: How beloued are <na>(c)</na> thy tabernacles ô Lord of hoastes!

notes.label: c
notes.text: The glorious mansions in heauen, which God hath prepared for the iust.

verses.text: My soule coueteth, and <na>(d)</na> fainteth vnto the courtes of our Lord. My hart, and <na>(e)</na> my flesh haue reioyced toward the liuing God.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Vehement desires do sometimes depriue vs of external sense.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The mind reioycing in hope, the bodie is also recreated, releeued, and reuiued, which before was dulle and heauie.

verses.text: For <na>(f)</na> the sparow also hath found her an house: and <na>(g)</na> the turtledoue a nest for her selfe, where she may lay her young ones. Thine <na>(h)</na> altars ô Lord of hoastes: my King, and my God.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As sparowes by natural instinct seeking habitations, finde houses to dwel in,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and turtles haue nestes, wherin to lay their young ones: so faithful soules seeke to dwel in heauen, and in the meane time to lay vp good workes within the Catholique Church; out of which (sayth S. Augustin in this place) how good soeuer workes do seme (as when paganes, and heretikes feede the hungrie, cloth the naked, receiue strangers into their houses, visite the sicke, comforte prisoners) being not laid in the nest, conculcabuntur, & conterentur: non seruabuntur, non custodientur: they shal be trodde vnder foote, they shal be bruised in peeces: they shal not be conserued, they shal not be kept: but (that such workes may be profitable and be conserued) they must be donne in true faith, in the Catholique faith, in societie of the vnitie of the Church.

notes.label: h
notes.text: VVorkes are good, and rightly laide vp when they are donne in vnitie, and participation of Gods Altares, the most proper places of Diuine Seruice, of external Sacrifice in this life, and spiritual sacrifice of perfect praises in eternal glorie; where al Sainctes without ceasing sing: Holie, holie, holie, Lord God of hoastes. Isaiæ 6. Apoc. 4.

verses.text: Blessed are they, that dwel in <na>(i)</na> thy house ô Lord: for euer and euer they shal praise thee.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The Catholique Church.

verses.text: Blessed is the man, whose helpe is from thee: he <na>(k)</na> hath disposed ascension in his hart,

notes.label: k
notes.text: The iust by Gods grace and helpe, may resolue to ascend by steppes and degrees, from vertue to vertue (v. 8.) euen to heauen,

verses.text: in <na>(l)</na> the vaile of teares, in the place, which he hath appointed.

notes.label: l
notes.text: though he be now in this vaile of teares, by reason of mans sinne, who otherwise was before sinne in paradise, a place of delight.

verses.text: For <na>(m)</na> the lawgeuer shal geue <na>(n)</na> blessing, they shal goe <na>(o)</na> from vertue into vertue: <na>(p)</na> the God of goddes shal be seene in Sion.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Christ our lawgeuer,

notes.label: n
notes.text: geueth abundance of graces,

notes.label: o
notes.text: with continual increase.

notes.label: p
notes.text: but our only omnipotent God, is to be senne by this effect of his grace, in the Church and not elswhere.

verses.text: Lord God of hoastes heare my prayer: receiue with thine eare ô God of Iacob.
Behold ô God our protectour: and <na>(q)</na> looke vpon the face of thy Christ.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Agreably to this the Church maketh al her petitions, concluding al prayers; By Christ our Lord.

verses.text: Because <na>(r)</na> better is one day in thy courtes, aboue thousands. I haue chosen to be <na>(s)</na> an abiect in the house of my God: rather then to dwel <na>(t)</na> in the tabernacles of sinners.

notes.label: r
notes.text: In respect of the future retribution, which euerie one shal receiue according to their desertes, one day in Gods Church is better then thousands out of it.

notes.label: s
notes.text: And better to be in the poorest state of Catholique Christians,

notes.label: t
notes.text: then in greatest palaces or hieghest dignities amongst sinners.

verses.text: Because God <na>(v)</na> loueth mercie and truth: our Lord wil geue <na>(w)</na> grace, <na>(x)</na> and glorie.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The Diuine wisdom so vseth mercie, and veritie, that neither may preiudice the other:

notes.label: w
notes.text: and so geueth grace in this life,

notes.label: x
notes.text: and glorie in the next.

verses.text: He wil not depriue them of good thinges, that <na>(y)</na> walke in innocencie: ô Lord of hoastes blessed is the man, that hopeth in thee.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Besides innocencie conserued without sinne, there is also innocencie after remission of sinne, of which the prophet here speaketh.

chapters.summary: Deuout persons feruently desire eternal glorie, 6. accounting it, in the meane time, a happie state to be in the militant Church, 12. where God first geuing grace, wil geue glorie in the triumphant. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal glory.
The 10. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, to the children of Core, a Psalme.
O Lord thou <na>(a)</na> hast blessed thy land: thou <na>(b)</na> hast turned away the captiuitie of Iacob.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God bestowed manie great benefites vpon the people of Israel:

notes.label: b
notes.text: he brought them out of the bondage of Ægypt.

verses.text: Thou <na>(c)</na> hast forgeuen the iniquitie of thy people: thou <na>(d)</na> hast couered al their sinnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Remitted their manifold sinnes:

notes.label: d
notes.text: pardoned also a great part of due punishment.

verses.text: Thou hast mitigated al thy wrath: thou hast turned away from the wrath of thine indignation.
<na>(e)</na> Conuert vs ô God our sauiour: and <na>(f)</na> auert thy wrath from vs.

notes.label: e
notes.text: As thou hast spared thy peculiar people, so we besech thee ô God creator and general Sauiour of al mankind,

notes.label: f
notes.text: mitigate thy wrath towards vs al.

verses.text: Wilt thou be wrath with vs for euer? or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation vnto generation?
O God thou <na>(g)</na> being turned shalt quicken vs: and thy people <na>(h)</na> shal reioyce in thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Til God first shew his mercie, sinners lye dead in guilt of sinne, but by his grace they are sturred vp, and quickned:

notes.label: h
notes.text: and ioyfully retutne to God.

verses.text: Shew vs ô Lord thy mercie and giue vs thy saluation.

I wil <na>(i)</na> heare what our Lord God wil speake in me: <na>(k)</na> because he wil speake peace vpon his people. And vpon <na>(l)</na> his sainctes: and vpon them, that are conuerted to the hart.

notes.label: i
notes.text: The wordes of the prophet,

notes.label: k
notes.text: signifying that God had reueled vnto him the redemption of mankind.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Not al men are iustified, and saued, but those that are hartely and sincerely conuerted.

verses.text: But yet his saluation is nigh to them that <na>(m)</na> feare him: that glorie may inhabite in our land.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Though al be not saued (because manie wil not cooperate to Gods grace) yet very manie hauing the feare of God, which is the beginning of godlie wisdom, freely accept of Gods mercie, and so the Church is gloriously propagated.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Mercie and truth haue met each other: <na>(o)</na> iustice and peace haue kissed.

notes.label: n
notes.text: VVheras Gods mercie would saue al, and his truth, or iustice requireth that sinnes be duly punished, by Christs Passion and death, sufficient satisfaction is offered for al sinnes, and those that wil be partakers by penance, and conformitie to Gods law, may haue remission,

notes.label: o
notes.text: and so iustice is obserued, and peace made betwen God and his subiects.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> Truth is risen out of the earth: <na>(q)</na> and iustice hath looked downe from heauen.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Integritie of conscience reigneth in good men,

notes.label: q
notes.text: God sending iust meanes from heauen to saue them.

verses.text: For <na>(r)</na> our Lord certes wil geue benignitie: and <na>(s)</na> our land shal giue her fruite.

notes.label: r
notes.text: God geueth grace,

notes.label: s
notes.text: and so men yeld fruict.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Iustice shal walke before him: and shal set his steppes in the way.

notes.label: t
notes.text: Yea they walke in iustice, and right path of Gods law.

chapters.summary: With commemoration of Gods former benefites, 5. Christs Incarnation is prophecied, 9. bringing peace and saluation, 11. mercie and iustice concurring together. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Incarnation of Christ.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A praier <na>(a)</na> to Dauid him selfe. Incline thine eare ô Lord, and <na>(b)</na> heare me: <na>(c)</na> because I am needie and poore.

notes.label: a
notes.text: A forme of prayer for king Dauid, and for anie faithful person.

notes.label: b
notes.text: There be sundrie iust causes which moue God to heare our prayers:

notes.label: c
notes.text: first our necessitie requireth Gods helpe.

verses.text: Keepe my soule, because <na>(d)</na> I am holie: saue thy seruant my God, that <na>(e)</na> hopeth in thee.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Secondly because we professe, and promise to lead a holie life.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Thirdly, because we trust and hope in God.

verses.text: Haue mercie on me ô Lord, because I haue cried to thee <na>(f)</na> al the day:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Fourtly, because we perseuere in prayer.

verses.text: make ioyful the soule of thy seruant, because to thee ô Lord haue I <na>(g)</na> lifted vp my soule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Fiftly, if we pray with attention of mind.

verses.text: Because thou ô Lord art <na>(h)</na> swete, and <na>(i)</na> milde: and <na>(k)</na> of so much mercie to al that inuocate thee. <na>(l)</na>

notes.label: h
notes.text: Sixtly because God of his owne nature is benigne, readie to bestow benefites.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Seuently, he is meeke to remitte offences.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Eighily, he is merciful to mitigate the punishment, to those that make recourse vnto him.

notes.label: l
notes.text: For these causes we pray as foloweth.

verses.text: Receiue ô Lord my praier with thine eares: and attend to the voice of my petition.
In the day of my tribulation I haue called to thee: because thou hast heard me.
There is not the like to thee amongst goddes ô Lord: and there is not according to thy workes.
<na>(m)</na> Al nations whatsoeuer thou hast made, shal <na>(n)</na> come, and shal adore before thee ô Lord: and they shal <na>(o)</na> glorifie thy name.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Vocation of Gentiles.

notes.label: n
notes.text: They shal come by faith.

notes.label: o
notes.text: and glorifie God by good workes. Mat. 5.v.17.

verses.text: Because thou art great and doing meruelous thinges: thou onlie art God.
Conduct me ô Lord in thy way, and I wil walke in thy truth: let my hart reioyce that it may feare thy name.
I wil <na>(p)</na> confesse to thee ô Lord my God with al my hart, and wil glorifie thy name for euer:

notes.label: p
notes.text: Cofession of praise.

verses.text: Because thy mercie is great vpon me: and thou hast deliuered my soule out of <na>(q)</na> the lower hel.

notes.label: q
notes.text: From the state of eternal damnation.

verses.text: O God the wicked are risen vp vpon me, and the synagogue of the mightie haue sought my soule: and they haue not set thee in their sight.
And thou ô Lord the God of compassion and merciful, patient, and of much mercie, and <na>(r)</na> true.

notes.label: r
notes.text: In performing al promises.

verses.text: Haue respect to me, and haue mercie on me, <na>(s)</na> giue thine empire to thy seruant: and saue the sonne of thy handmaide.

notes.label: s
notes.text: A digression (vsual to prophetes) of Christs Empyre and Kingdom the Church, geuen to him, being the sonne of an immaculate virgin, the handmaide of God.

verses.text: Make with me <na>(t)</na> a signe vnto God, that they may see which hate me, and may be confounded: <na>(v)</na> because thou ô Lord hast holpen me.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The chief and principal signe of Christs, and his Churches glorie, is his Resurrection, præfigured in Ionas.

notes.label: v
notes.text: VVhereby al enimies are confounded, either to their conuersion, or to eternal damnation. See 6. Augustin.

chapters.summary: In consideration of his owne imperfections, the royal prophet, or other faithful person prayeth God, 5. according to his mercie and goodnes, 9. shewed in conuerting Gentiles, 13. and in deliuering the supplicant him self from the state of damnation, 16. that he wil stil direct and defend him against al enimies. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for continual grace.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To the children of Core, a Psalme of Canticle. THE fundations thereof in the holie <na>(a)</na> mountaynes:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Christs Church was first founded in Ierusalem on whitsunday, Act 2 in mount Sion, which hath two coppes, in one of which the Temple stood, in the other Dauids towre or palace.

verses.text: our Lord loueth the gates of Sion, aboue al the tabernacles of Iacob.
Glorious thinges are saide of thee, ô cittie of God.
<na>(b)</na> I wil be mindeful of <na>(c)</na> Raab, and Babylon knowing me. Behold <na>(d)</na> the foreners, and Tyre, & the people of the Æthiopians, these <na>(e)</na> were there.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Prophet in the person of Christ, saith he wil commend vnto his Apostles, and other Apostolical men, that they conuert al nations (as our Sauiour gaue expresse commission and commandment. Math. 28. Luc. 24. v. 47. Act. 1. v. 8.)

notes.label: c
notes.text: naming here Raab (which is Ægypt) and Babylon:

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Philistims, Tyrians, Æthiopians,

notes.label: e
notes.text: & the rest, shal be regenerate in this Church, which for the assured certaintie therof (after the prophets maner of speaking) is affirmed in the pretertence, as if it were then donne.

verses.text: Shal it not be said of Sion <na>(f)</na> Man and man, is borne in her; and <na>(g)</na> the Highest himselfe founded her?

notes.label: f
notes.text: It shal be reported, or one shal say to an other: Loe this and that man, al these and al these men are regenerate by Baptisme in the Church of Christ.

notes.label: g
notes.text: God himselfe, Christ God and Man, founded this Church.

verses.text: Our Lord wil declare <na>(h)</na> in scriptures of peoples, and <na>(i)</na> of princes: of those that haue bene in her.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The multitude of the elect is so great, that only God knoweth the number,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and the qualities of al sortes, of Princes, Prelates, and Peoples.

verses.text: The <na>(k)</na> habitation in thee, is as it were of al reioycing.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Great spiritual ioy with peace of conscience, is in true Christian Catholiques in the militant Church; but the blessed haue the most absolute & secure ioy of al, in the Church triumphant.

chapters.summary: The Church of Christ beginning in Ierusalem, 3. is extended to al Nations, 5. glorious, 6. and permanent, 7. in holie ioy. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer for continual grace.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A Canticle of a Psalme, to the children of Core, vnto the end, for <na>(a)</na> Maheleth <na>(b)</na> to answer, <na>(c)</na> of vnderstanding to Eman the Ezrahite.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An instrument of musike apt for lamentable songues. Not expressed in the title of anie other Psalme. Perhaps because this Psalme mixeth not anie consolation with mourning, as other Psalmes do, which are also prayers in affliction. As the 30. 33. 63. 73.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Neither is this word in anie other title. It is added here to admonish vs, that as this Psalme, and some others were songue by two quires, one answering the other, so we must in answer and imitation of Christ, suffer long and great afflictions with patience, seeing he in his passion was leift without ordinarie côsolation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: By some interpreted [his bretheren] For Christ (saith S. Augustin) vouchsasseth to make them his bretheren, which vnderstand the mysterie of his Crosse, and not only are not ashamed therof, but also faithfully glorie therin.

verses.text: O Lord the God of my saluation: <na>(d)</na> in the day haue I cried, and in the night before thee.

notes.label: d
notes.text: I haue cried to thee very often both by day, and by night.

verses.text: Let my prayer enter in thy sight: incline thine eare to my petition.
Because my soule is replenished with euils: and <na>(e)</na> my life hath approched to hel.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I am almost dead.

verses.text: I <na>(f)</na> am accounted with them that descend into the lake. I am become as a man without helpe,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Accounted as dead, and readie to be buried.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> free among the dead, as the wounded sleeping in the sepulchres, of whom thou art mindeful no more: and they are cast of from thy hand.

notes.label: g
notes.text: If I were dead, I should be free from these afflictions. Especially it agreeth to Christ, who was free, yea of infinite powre amongst the dead.

verses.text: They haue put me in <na>(h)</na> the lower lake: in the darke places, and in the shadowe of death.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Myn enimies haue endeuored not only to bereue me of temporal life, wherby I should goe into limbus, but also to kil my soule spiritually, wherby I should descend into the lower hel of the damned.

verses.text: Thy <na>(i)</na> furie is confirmed vpon me: and al thy waues thou hast brought in vpon me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thy iust wrath also ô God hath excedingly afflicted me.

verses.text: Thou hast made my familiars far from me: they haue put me abomination to themselues. I was deliuered and came not forth:
myne eies languished for pouertie. I cried to thee ô Lord al the day: I stretched out my handes to thee.
Wilt thou <na>(k)</na> doe meruels to the dead: or shal phisicians raise to life, and they confesse to thee?

notes.label: k
notes.text: O God deliuer me whiles I am yet liuing, for I may not looke for extraordinarie, and miraculous helpe, as to be raised againe after death:

verses.text: Shal any <na>(l)</na> in the sepulchre declare thy mercie, and thy truth in perdition?

notes.label: l
notes.text: when I shal be dead & buried, I can not denounce thy praises as now I can to mortal men.

verses.text: Shal thy meruelous workes be knowne <na>(m)</na> in darkenes: and thy iustice in the land of obliuion.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Much lesse shal the damned praise thee in eternal perdition.

verses.text: And I ô Lord haue cried to thee: and in the morning shal my praier preuent thee.
Why doest thou o Lord reiect my prayer: turnest away thy face from me?
I am poore, and in labours <na>(n)</na> from my youth: and being <na>(o)</na> exalted, humbled and troubled.

notes.label: n
notes.text: As wel young,

notes.label: o
notes.text: as waxing elder I haue bene stil afflicted.

verses.text: Thy wrathes haue passed vpon me: and thy terrouts haue trubled me.
They haue compassed me as water al the day: they compassed me together.
Thou <na>(p)</na> hast made frend, and neighboure far from me: and my familiars because of miserie.

notes.label: p
notes.text: My miserable estate hath alienated al freindes, neighbours, & acquantances from me.

chapters.summary: A faithful person sore and long afflicted, lamentably complaineth, praying God, 15. not stil to repel him, being leift desolate, 19. without al consolation of freindes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: A prayer in long affliction. The 7 key.

verses.text: Of vnderstanding <na>(a)</na> to Ethan the Ezrahite.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Otherwise called Idithun. 1. Paral. 25. or rather Ethan, who was very wise, mentioned with others, to whom Salomon is preferred for wisdom. 3. Reg. 4. v. 31, and signifieth strong, applied here to those that are strong in assured hope of Christs promises, notwithstanding it semeth sometimes to the weake, that his promises are not performed.

verses.text: THE mercies of our Lord I wil sing for euer. In generation <na>(b)</na> and generation I wil shewe forth thy truth, in my mouth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In al generations.

verses.text: Because thou saidst: Mercie shal be built vp for euer <na>(c)</na> in the heauens: thy truth shal be prepared in them.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The heauens shal rather fal, then Gods truth faile. Mystically, in the Apostles, and by their preaching, the Church of Christ is built for euer.

verses.text: I haue ordained a testament with mine elect, I haue sworne to Dauid my seruant:
<na>(d)</na> for ever wil I prepare thy seede. And I wil build thy seat vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Dauids seede conserued til Christ was borne of his virgin mother: and in his spiritual seede, his kingdom the Church is for euer conserued. Otherwise not verified of Dauids temporal kingdom, which decayed in the captiuitie of Babylon, and is now wholly destroyed.

verses.text: The heauens shal confesse thy meruelous workes ô Lord: yea and thy truth in the church of saintes.
For who in the cloudes shal be equal to our Lord: shal be like to God among <na>(e)</na> the sonnes of God?

notes.label: e
notes.text: The Angels.

verses.text: God, who is glorified in the counsel of saintes: great and terrible ouer al that are round about him.
O Lord God of hoastes who is like to thee? thou art mightie ô Lord, and thy truth round about thee.
Thou rulest ouer the powre of the sea: and the mouing of the waues therof thou doest mitigate.
Thou <na>(f)</na> humbledst the proud one, as one wounded: in the arme of thy strength thou hast dispersed thine enimies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The prophet aludeth to the plagues and miracles in Ægypt, and in other enimes.

verses.text: The heauens are thine, and the earth is thine, the round earth, and the fulnes therof thou hast founded:
the north, and the sea thou hast created. <na>(g)</na> Thabor and Hermon shal reioice in thy name:

notes.label: g
notes.text: Conuersion of Gentiles.

verses.text: thy arme is with might. Let <na>(h)</na> thy hand be confirmed, and thy <na>(i)</na> righthand exalted:

notes.label: h
notes.text: VVhether God punish, as with the left hand,

notes.label: i
notes.text: or bestow benefites, as with the right hand, al is to his glorie, and according to mercie, and truth.

verses.text: iustice and iudgement is the preparation of thy seat. Mercie and truth shal goe before thy face:
<na>(k)</na> blessed is the people that knoweth iubilation. Lord they shal walke in the light of thy countinance,

notes.label: k
notes.text: They are spiritually happie, that do thus consider of Gods meruelous procedings, praise the same, and reioyce therin.

verses.text: and in thy name they shal reioyce al the day: and in thy iustice they shal be exalted.
Because thou art the glorie of their streingth: and in thy good pleasure shal our <na>(l)</na> horne be exalted.

notes.label: l
notes.text: powre, and kingdom.

verses.text: Because our protection is of our Lord: and of the holie one of Israel our king.
Then didst thou speake in vision to thy saintes, and saidst <na>[1]</na> I haue put helpe on the mightie one: and haue exalted an elect one of my people.

notes.text: Thus God promised to establish the kingdom of the Iewes in Dauid and his familie. 1. Reg. 16. 2. Reg. 5. and other places. which was performed as in a figure but more fully in Christ. Act. 13. v. 22.

verses.text: I haue found Dauid my seruant: with myne holie oyle haue I anointed him.
For mine hand shal helpe him: and myne arme shal strengthen him.
The enimie shal nothing preuale in him: and the sonne of iniquitie shal not adde to hurt him.
And I wil cut downe his enimies before his face: and them that hate him I wil put to flight.
And my truth, and my mercie with him: and in my name shal his horne be exalted.
And I wil put his hand in the sea: and his righthand in the riuers.
He shal inuocate me: Thou art my Father: my God, and the protector of my saluation.
And I wil put him the firstbegotten, high aboue the kings of the earth.
I wil kepe my mercie vnto him for euer: and my testament faithful to him.
I wil put his seed for euer and euer: and his throne as the daies of heauen.
But if his children shal forsake my lawe: and wil not walke in my Iudgementes:
If they shal profane my iustices: and not kepe my commandmentes:
I wil visite their iniquities with a rod: and their sinnes with stripes:
But, my mercie I wil not take away from him: neither wil I hurt in my truth:
Neither wil I profane my testament: and the words that procede from my mouth I wil not make frustrate.
Once I haue sworne in my holie, if I lie to Dauid:
his seede shal continewe for euer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: I wil not lie.

verses.text: And <na>(m)</na> his throne as the Sunne in my sight, and as the <na>(n)</na> Moone perfect for euer: and a faithful witnesse in heauen.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Christian iust soules as the sunne,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and as the perfect, or full moone. See the first Tome. page 716. S. Augustin also expoundeth this verse in the Anagogical sense, of the iust after the Resurrection in glorie, where the soule shal be like the sunne, and the bodie, which now is mutable, shal be like the moone, not as now alwayes changing, but as the ful moone, alwayes perfect.

verses.text: But <na>[1]</na> thou hast repelled and dispised: thou <na>(o)</na> hast differred thy Christ.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Amongst manie pensiue thinges, this one word doth comforte vs, thy promise remaineth, thou hast not denied to send Christ, but differred him,

God hauing promised al the aforsaide the prophet in the person of the weake, lamenteth that the contrarie shal happen as wel in the temporal kingdom oppressed by the Assirians Babylonians, Persians, Grecians, and Romanes: as in the Church impugned by innumerable sortes of Heretikes and other Infidels.

verses.text: Thou hast ouerthrowne the testament of thy seruant: thou hast profaned his sanctuarie on the earth.
Thou hast destroyed al the hedges therof: thou hast made the firmament therof feare.
Al that passe by the way haue spoiled him: he is become a reproch to his neighbours.
Thou hast exalted the righthand of them that oppresse him: thou hast made al his enimies ioyful.
Thou hast turned away the helpe of his sword: and hast not holpen him in battel.
Thou hast destroied him from <na>(p)</na> emundation: and his seat thou hast broken downe to the ground.

notes.label: p
notes.text: From the vse of Sacrifice and Sacraments, wherby sinners were wount to be cleansed.

verses.text: Thou hast lessened the daies of his time: thou hast ouerwhelmed him with confusion.
<na>[1]</na> How long ô Lord doest thou turne away for euer: shal thy wrath burne as a fire?

notes.text: The Psalmist prayeth and prophecieth that God wil respect the weaknes of man, maintaine his Church in manie natiôs, & saue manie soules.

verses.text: Remember what my substance is: for hast thou made al the children of men in vaine?
Who is the man that shal liue, and shal not see death: shal deliuer his soule from the hand of hel?
Where are thyne old mercies ô Lord, as thou swarest to Dauid in thy truth?
Be mindeful ô Lord of the aeproch of thy seruantes (which I haue held in my bosome) of manie nations.
Which thine enimies haue reproched ô Lord, which they haue reproched <na>(q)</na> the commutation of thy Christ.

notes.label: q
notes.text: As though Christ were changed and turned from vs.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord for euer: <na>(r)</na> Be it, be it.

notes.label: r
notes.text: So we wish and pray that al may blesse and praise thee. Amen.

chapters.summary: Gods mercie and truth, with his great promises to Dauid, 6. his powre in the whole world, and iust iudgements, are the true ioy of his seruantes. 20. Christs kingdom shal remaine for euer: 31. yea manie offending yet al shal not perish, 39. but after great affliction, 47. God wil respect mans infirmitie, 50. his owne promise, and the enimies reproching his seruantes and himselfe: 53. who is blessed for euer. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Christ never faileth.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A prayer <na>(a)</na> of Moyses the man of God. Lord, thou art made a refuge for vs: <na>(b)</na> from generation vnto generation.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Some Expositors thincke Moyses was the author of this Psalme, and of the tenne next folowing. But others hold that Dauid was author of al, and that Moyses his name is here put in the title by Esdras, because this Psalme is like to the prayer of Moyses, when the people prouoked Gods wrath by their sinnes in the desert. And because mans creation, fal, punishmẽt, and Gods mercie towards him, are here described: which Moyses first writte, as going before the written law. And that Moyses made not this Psalme is probably gethered by the 10. verse, where the ordinarie age of men is described to be (in streingth and vigore) seuentie yeares, or of some fourscore: and the greater part (of the one or the other) is in labour and sorow. And it is euident ( Deut. 34. ) that Moyses liued in al an hundred and twentie yeares, and his eye was not dimme, neither were his teeth moued. So Aaron, Iosue, and others commonly liued longer then is here mentioned. But Dauid was old and impotent at seuentie yeares. 3. Reg. 1. S. Hilarion, liuing neere seuentie yeares in his heremitage, S. Remigius gouerning the Church of Rhemes, seuentie yeares, and the like are accounted to haue bene ful of dayes, and such as liued longer are reputed extraordinarie. Agane it is more euidenly proued that Moyses was not author of the 94. and 95. Psalmes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Alwayes from the beginning of the world to the end.

verses.text: Before <na>(c)</na> the mountaines were made, or the earth and the world formed: <na>(d)</na> from euerlasting euen vnto euerlasting thou art God.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Prophet sheweth that the world was created in and with time, not eternal.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And that only God is eternal.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Turne not away man into humiliation: thou saidst: Be conuerted ye children of men.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath often saide, that he would not the death of sinners, but rather that they be conuerted and liue for euer.

verses.text: Because <na>(f)</na> a thousand years before thine eies, are as yesterday, that is past. And as a watch in the night,

notes.label: f
notes.text: Though some liued long ( none for al that did reach to a thousand yeares ) yet it is nothing before God, and in respect of eternitie.

verses.text: thinges that are counted nothing shal their years be.
In <na>(g)</na> the morning as an herbe he shal passe, in the morning he shal florish, and passe: in <na>(h)</na> the euening he shal fal, be hardened, and withered.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The youth of man quickly passeth:

notes.label: h
notes.text: old age can not last long: wherof cometh our English prouerb: A young man may dye sowne, an old man can not liue long.

verses.text: Because we haue faynted in thy wrath, and in thy furie we are trubled.
Thou hast put <na>(i)</na> our iniquities in thy sight: our age in the light of thy countinance. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: i
notes.text: Sinne the cause of shortnes of mans life.
Sæculum.

verses.text: Because al our daies haue failed: and in thy wrath we haue failed. Our yeares shal be considered <na>(k)</na> as a spyder:

notes.label: k
notes.text: spider. Man's life as brittle as a spider's web: or man's life wasteth continually, as a spider wasteth herself by spinning, and consuming her own substance.

verses.text: the daies of our yeares in them, are <na>(l)</na> seuentie yeares. And if in strong ones <na>(m)</na> eightie years: and the more of them, labour and sorrow. Because <na>(n)</na> mildnes is come vpon vs: and we shal be chastised.

notes.label: l
notes.text: These numbers literarly shew the shortnes of the longer sorte of mens liues. Mystically, seuen signifie the rest after laboures of this world, and perteyn to the old testament: eight signifie the reward in the resurrection, perteyning to the new testament. VVhich multiplied by tenne, a perfect number, make seuentie and eightie. VVhich ioyned together make an hundred and fiftie. The number of al these Psalmes.

notes.label: m
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: n
notes.text: It is of Gods milde prouidence, that mans life is short, for that manie if they were sure, or had probabilitie to liue long, would presume to sinne more.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> Who knoweth the powre of thy wrath: and for feare

notes.label: o
notes.text: Seing God of his iustice punished al mankind, for one sinne of our first parente, his wrath must nedes be very great to euerie sinner, for his owne proper sinnes.

verses.text: to number thy wrath? So make thy righthand knowne: and men learned in hart, in wisedome.
Turne ô Lord, how long? and be intreated for thy seruants.
<na>(p)</na> We are replenished in the morning with thy mercie: and we haue reioyced, and are delighted al our daies.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The hope of glorious resurrection turneth our calamities into spiritual ioy.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> We haue reioyced for the daies wherin thou hast humbled vs: the yeares, wherin we haue seene euils.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Yea the more we suffer in this life for the truth, the greater is our comforth in hope of reward.

verses.text: Looke vpon <na>(r)</na> thy seruants, and vpon thy workes: and <na>(s)</na> direct their children.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Not only in that we are thy creatures, but also in that we are thy seruants, we are thy proper worke, therfore in both these respectes, ô God looke vpon vs with clemencie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: lead also our posteritie into the right way, and make them thy seruantes.

verses.text: And <na>(t)</na> let the brightnes of our Lord God be vpon vs, and <na>(v)</na> direct thou the workes of our handes ouer vs: and <na>(w)</na> the worke of our handes doe thou direct.

notes.label: t
notes.text: O God illuminate our vnderstanding,

notes.label: v
notes.text: make our actions by thy grace profitable to vs:

notes.label: w
notes.text: and make perfect in vs the worke of charitie. In which one worke, al good workes are included and to which al other are directed. For then workes are right ( sayth S. Augustin ) when they are directed to this one end.

chapters.summary: Vnder the forme of prayer, the Psalmist describeth the shortnes of mans life and other calamites. 7. Gods strict iudgement. 13. but first his comfortable mercie: 16. and perpetual regard of his owne worke. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Man rightly created fell by sin into miseries.
The 6. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Prayse of a <na>(b)</na> Canticle to Dauid. He <na>(c)</na> that dwelleth in the helpe of the Highest, shal abide in the protection of the God of heauen.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praise of Gods prouidence, with thankes,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Which Dauid songe with voice.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that firmely relieth and resteth vpon Gods prouidence, is assuredly protected by him.

verses.text: He shal say to our Lord: Thou art my protectour, and my refuge: my God I wil hope in him.
Because he hath deliuered me from <na>(d)</na> the snare of the hunters, and from <na>(e)</na> the sharpe word.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al secret and sutle machinations :

notes.label: e
notes.text: and from al crueltie of tyrants.

verses.text: With his shoulders shal he ouershadowe thee: and vnder his winges thou shalt hope.
With shilde shal his truth compasse thee: thou shalt not be afrayed <na>(f)</na> of the feare in the night.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Terrors obscurly suggested by euil men or spirites, with erronious conceipte that men are not bond in time of temporal dangers, to confesse the truth.

verses.text: Of <na>(g)</na> the arrow flying in the day, <na>(h)</na> of busines walking in darkenes: <na>(i)</na> of inuasion, and the midday diuel.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Open persecution threatning present death, except men denie the truth which they know.

notes.label: h
notes.text: circumuention of craftie enimies by sutle arguing, and drawing men into error, and so to decline from Catholique Religion,

notes.label: i
notes.text: long torments, euen to death, except Gods seruants wil relent, and denie the truth, which they assuredly beleue, and know in their conscience, that they are bond to professe it.

verses.text: A <na>(k)</na> thousand shal fal on thy syde, & <na>(l)</na> ten thousand: on thy righthand: but to thee it shal not approch.

notes.label: k
notes.text: On thy left side, in aduersitie manie fal from God,

notes.label: l
notes.text: & on thy right side, in prosperitie manie more forgete, and forsake God.

verses.text: But thou shalt consider with thine eies: and shalt see the retribution of sinners.
Because <na>(m)</na> thou ô Lord art my hope: thou hast made the Highest thy refuge.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In sincerely saying thou art my hope: thou makest God thy refuge.

verses.text: There shal no euil come to thee: and scourge shal not approch to thy tabernacle.
Because he hath geuen <na>(n)</na> his Angels charge of thee: <na>(o)</na> that they keepe thee in al thy waies.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Angels haue protection of men by Gods ordinance .

notes.label: o
notes.text: The diuel corruptly alleageth this scripture (Mat. 4) omitting the latter part of this verse: which sheweth when Angels protect iust men, to witte, when they walke in a right path, obseruing ordinarie course in their actions, not in geuing themselues headlong into needles danger, as the same diuel proposed to our Sauiour, to cast himself downe from the pinnacle of the temple. Such falling is not the way of the iust, but of Lucifer, that fel from heauen. So S. Bernard noteth Ser. 15. in hunc Psal.

verses.text: In their handes they shal beare thee: lest perhaps thou knocke thy foote against a stone.
Vpon the aspe, and the basiliscus thou shalt walke: & thou shalt tread vpon the lion, and the dragon.
<na>(p)</na> Because he hath hoped in me, I wil deliuer him: I wil protect him, because he hath knowne my name.

notes.label: p
notes.text: God speaketh the rest that foloweth in this Psalme.

verses.text: He shal crie to me, and I wil heare him: with him I am in tribulation: I wil deliuer him, and <na>(q)</na> wil glorifie him.

notes.label: q
notes.text: In eternal saluation.

verses.text: With length of daies I wil replenish him: and I wil shew him my saluation.

chapters.summary: Whosoeuer faithfully and firmly trusteth in Gods prouidence, is secure from al dangers of secrete, sutle, and open enimies. 7. his aduersaries shal come to ruine. 11. Angels shal defend him. 13. no kind of serpent, nor beast shal hurt him. 14. God himself assureth him of his protection, and of eternal saluation. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> in the sabbath day.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Voices beginning instrumentes prosecute this song:

notes.label: b
notes.text: when we rest from worke then especially vve ought to thincke vpon Gods vvorkes, praise and thanke him for the same.

verses.text: IT is good <na>(c)</na> to confesse to our Lord; and to sing to thy name ô Highest.

notes.label: c
notes.text: To geue thankes.

verses.text: To shewforth thy mercie in <na>(d)</na> the morning: and thy truth in <na>(e)</na> the night.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In prosperitie,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in aduersitie.

verses.text: In <na>(f)</na> the instrument of tenstrings, in <na>(g)</na> Psalter: with Canticle, on <na>(h)</na> the Harpe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: On euerie instrument of tenne stringes, signifying the obseruation of the tenne commandments:

notes.label: g
notes.text: namely on the Psalter.

notes.label: h
notes.text: also on the harpe, which signifieth mortification.

verses.text: Because thou hast delighted me ô Lord in thy workemanship: and in the workes of thy handes I wil reioyce.
How are thy workes magnified ô Lord! thy cogitations are made very profounde.
The <na>(i)</na> vnwise man wil not know; and the <na>(k)</na> foule wil not vnderstand these thinges.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Carnal and sensual man,

notes.label: k
notes.text: he that thinketh only of present thinges, not of future.

verses.text: When sinners shal spring vp as grasse: and al that worke iniquitie shal appeare. That they may perish for euer:
but thou the Highest for euer ô Lord.
Because loe thine enimies ô Lord, because loe thine enimies shal perish: and al that worke iniquitie shal be dispersed.
And <na>(l)</na> my horne shal be exalted, as the vnicorns: <na>(m)</na> and my old age in plentiful mercie.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The iust in confidence of a good conscience, expect exaltation of their powre:

notes.label: m
notes.text: and great consolation in the end of their life.

verses.text: And <na>(n)</na> mine eie hath looked vpon mine enimies: and the malignant rysing vp against me, mine ears shal heare.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Then shal the iust see their enimies depressed: and themselues florish, like the palme, and ceder trees as folovveth.

verses.text: The iust, shal florish as a palme tree: as the ceder of Libanus shal he be multiplied.
They that are planted in <na>(o)</na> the house of our Lord, shal florish in <na>(p)</na> the courtes of the house of our God.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Militant Church:

notes.label: p
notes.text: triumphant.

verses.text: As yet shal they be multiplied in plentiful old age: and they shal be wel affected,
that they <na>(q)</na> may shewforth: That the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquitie in him.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Publikly professe Gods praises, as in the wordes folowing:

chapters.summary: God is by al maner of voices and instruments to be praised in his admirable workes. 7. which the foolish not doing are punished; 11. and the wise are rewarded. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The works of God admirable.
The 2. key.

verses.text: Prayse <na>(a)</na> of Canticle <na>(b)</na> to Dauid himselfe, in <na>(c)</na> the day before the sabbath, <na>(d)</na> when the earth was founded. OVr Lord <na>(e)</na> hath reigned, he <na>(f)</na> hath put on beutie: our Lord hath <na>(g)</na> put on strength, and hath girded him selfe. For he hath established <na>(h)</na> the round world, which <na>(i)</na> shal not be moued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praise to be songue vvith voice:

notes.label: b
notes.text: composed by Dauid:

notes.label: c
notes.text: the sixth day of the weeke, vvhich is our friday,

notes.label: d
notes.text: in vvhich day the Church of Christ vvas founded, by his bloud shed on the crosse.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Our Sauiour founding his Church by his death begane then to reigne therin:

notes.label: f
notes.text: gloriosly descending a soule into limbus, and in bodie to his graue:

notes.label: g
notes.text: he then put on al armour of strength to reforme the world, and to inlarge his kingdom, according to his owne prediction where he saide: If I be exalted from the earth, I wil draw al thinges vnto myselfe. Ioan. 12. v. 31.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Not only in Iurie and Samaria, but the whole earth:

notes.label: i
notes.text: and the same Church shal not be destroyed.

verses.text: Thy seat is prepared from that time: thou <na>(k)</na> art from euerlasting.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Christ being eternal, hath an euerlasting Church.

verses.text: The <na>(l)</na> riuers ô Lord haue lifted vp: the riuers haue lifted vp their voice. The riuers haue lifted vp their waues,

notes.label: l
notes.text: Al sortes of persecuters, the High priestes (who sometimes vvatered the spiritual land, like riuers) vvith Scribes, Pharises, and other incredulous Ievves, also Paganes, Turkes, and Heretikes haue oppugned the Church.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> aboue the voices of manie waters. The surges of the sea are meruelous; <na>(n)</na> meruelous is our Lord on high.

notes.label: m
notes.text: With more force then anie persecutions in the old Testament.

notes.label: n
notes.text: but though al these assaultes be great, and meruelous, yet Christ in protecting his Church, is more meruelous.

verses.text: Thy testimonies are made <na>(o)</na> credible exceedingly: <na>(p)</na> holines becometh thy house ô Lord <na>(q)</na> for length of daies.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Articles of faith are not euidently apparent to knovvlege, but euident to credibilitie, to those that are disposed by Gods grace, illuminating their vnderstanding, and mouing their free vvil, to geue consent of beleefe if they vvil

notes.label: p
notes.text: It behoueth therfore al members of the Church to conuerse piously, and religiously in this life, seing she hath so excellent a spouse, protector, and instructor,

notes.label: q
notes.text: euen to the end of the vvorld.

chapters.summary: Christ reigneth for euer in his Church: 3. notwithstanding manie and great persecution against the faithful. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Perpetuitie of the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himselfe, in <na>(b)</na> the fourth of the sabbath. OVr Lord God of reuenges: the God <na>(c)</na> of reuenges hath done <na>(d)</na> freely.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Hebrevv letter Lamed, vvhich ordinarily is prefixed to the datiue case, or signifieth to, being set before proper names, is a signe of the genetiue case. Yet the Septuagint, expresse it by the datiue, and so doth the latin, ipsi Dauid, and consequently our English hath, to Dauid himselfe, to shevv a difference betvven sacred and profane vvriters. For in humane bookes the vvriter and auctor is al one; but in diuine, the Holie Ghost is the proper auctor, and a man is the vvriter. To signifie therfore the principal auctor, Dauid is sometimes named as the instrumental cause, to vvhom the Holie Ghost inspired this, and other Psalmes, and by vvhom they vvere vvritten. And vvhen the titles expresse othervvise: A Psalme of Dauid, yet it is so to be vnderstood, that the Holie Ghost is alvvayes the principal auctor, and Dauid the instrumental, ministerial, or secondarie auctor. But vvhen other names are expressed, either in the genetiue or datiue case, or hovvsoeuer, it proueth not that those men vvere the vvriters of the same Psalmes, but importeth some other thing, as by S. Augustins iudgement, vve noted in the proemial Annotations page 3. & 4. vvherby is proued that this Psalme vvas not vvritten, nor composed by Moyses, as Hebrevv Rabbins suppose, but by the Royal Psalmist Dauid.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Made and ordinarily songue in the fourth day of the vveke, our vvenesday, in vvhich day Iudas the traitor sold our Sauiour Christ to his enimies. The reuenge of vvhich vvickednes, and of al other sinnes, is here prophecied.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God more commonly called the God of mercie (vvhich vertue in him is aboue al his vvorkes, Psal. 144) is also the God of reuenges, according to his iustice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: He proceedeth in iudgement resolutly, not depending, nor fearing, not respecting anie person, povvre, dignitie, vvisdome or other like qualitie, but their iust merites.

verses.text: Be <na>[1]</na> exalted thou that iudgest the earth: render retribution to the proude.

notes.text: A prayer of iust zele,

verses.text: How long shal sinners ô Lord: how long shal sinners glorie?
Shal they vtter, and speake iniquitie? shal al they speake, <na>(e)</na> that worke iniustice?

notes.label: e
notes.text: Shal most wicked men stil be suffered to speake so insolently?

verses.text: Thy <na>[1]</na> people ô Lord they haue humbled: and thine inheritance they haue vexed.

notes.text: A description of heathnish and heretical crueltie.

verses.text: The widow, and the stranger they haue slaine: and the pupilles they haue killed.
And <na>[1]</na> they haue saide: The Lord shal not see, neither shal the God of Iacob vnderstand.

notes.text: Scarse anie Atheistes are so blind, as thus to thinke but manie sinners so behaue themselues, as if God saw not, knew nor, or at least cared not vvhat they do.

verses.text: Vnderstand ye foolish in the people: and ye fooles be wise at sometime.
He that planted the eare, shal he not heare? Or he that made the eie doth he not consider?
He that chastiseth nations, shal he not rebuke: he that teacheth man knowledge?
Our Lord knoweth <na>(f)</na> the cogitations of men: that they be vaine.

notes.label: f
notes.text: So vnpossible is it that God should be ignorant, or careles vvhat men do, that he also knovveth and obserueth most secret thoughtes.

verses.text: Blessed is the man, whom thou shalt instruct ô Lord: and shalt teach out of thy lawe.
That thou maist <na>(g)</na> geue him quietnes from the euil daies: til a pitte be digged for the sinner.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Mitigate and temper his afflictions, that by patience and fortitude, the iust may perseuere, and not be ouervvhelmed.

verses.text: Because our Lord <na>(h)</na> wil not reiect his people: and his inheritance he wil not forsake.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The vvhole Church shal neuer be reiected, nor forsaken.

verses.text: Vntil iustice <na>(i)</na> be turned into iudgement: and <na>(k)</na> they who are neere it, are al that are right of hart.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Iustice is conuerted into iudgement, vvhen iust meaning is put in vvorke and practise, that it may appeare in iudgement. Also God vvho doth & suffereth al iustly, vvil conserue his inheritance the Church, euen vnto the day of iudgement.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The sense is easie by transposing the vvordes: al that are right of hart, are nere it, that is, shal like and approue Gods iustice, vvhen the vvicked shal repine, and blaspheme it.

verses.text: Who shal rise for me against the malignant? or who shal stand with me against them that worke iniquitie?
But that our Lord hath holpen me: within very litle my soule had dwelt in hel.
If I said: <na>(l)</na> My foote is moued: thy mercie ô Lord did help me

notes.label: l
notes.text: When I felt, and complained that I was in danger, thou didst assist me.

verses.text: According to the multitude of my sorrowes in my hart: thy consolations haue made my soule ioyful.
Doth the seat of iniquitie cleaue to thee: which makest <na>(m)</na> labour in precept?

notes.label: m
notes.text: Onlie faith sufficeth not, but careful laboure, in keping Gods commandmnts is required.

verses.text: They wil hunt after the soule of the iust: and wil condemne innocent bloud.
And our Lord became my refuge: and my God the helpe <na>(n)</na> of my hope.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The iust do hope for eternal saluation, to vvhich God vvil bring them.

verses.text: And he <na>(o)</na> wil repay them their iniquitie: and in their malice he wil destroy them: the Lord our God wil destroy them.

notes.label: o
notes.text: And God, the reuenger of vvronges, vvil at last cast the vvicked into eternal torments.

chapters.summary: The faithful seruant of God assuredly professeth, that al the pride, 5. crueltie, 7. foolish imaginations, and secret thoughts of the wicked are manifest to God, 12. acknowlegeth himself happie, that he is better instructed of God: wheras he had otherwise bene damned. 20. sharply reprehendeth those that consider not of Gods iudgements: concluding that the iust shal be glorified, and the wicked damned. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal salvation and damnation.
The 10. key.

verses.text: Praise <na>(a)</na> of Canticle, <na>(b)</na> to Dauid him selfe. COME, <na>[1]</na> let vs <na>(c)</na> reioyce to our Lord: let vs make iubilation to God <na>(d)</na> our sauiour.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praise songue with voices:

notes.label: b
notes.text: inspired to Dauid, & written by him.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVith great and solemne exultation:

notes.label: d
notes.text: God our Creator, is also our Protector & Sauiour.
This Inuitation is most fitly ordayned by the Church for the proeme or beginning of Mattins.

verses.text: Let vs <na>(e)</na> preuent his face in confession: and <na>(f)</na> in Psalmes let vs make iubilation to him.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Let vs be more diligent, and preuent our accustomed time. For no man can preuent Gods grace with anie good worke, who first preuenteth vs; els we can neither doe, nor thincke anie good thing.

notes.label: f
notes.text: not only in singing his praise with voice, but also with musical instruments.

verses.text: Because our Lord is a great God: and a great King aboue al goddes.
Because in his hand are the endes of the earth: and the heightes of the mountaines be his.
Because the sea is his, and he made it: and his handes formed the drie land.
Come let vs adore, <na>(g)</na> and fal downe: and wepe before our Lord, that made vs.

notes.label: g
notes.text: So also Isaias (c. 45. v. 23.) and S. Paul (Philip. 2.) teach that kneeling or bowing the knees, as an external religious ceremonie, is acceptable to God.

verses.text: Because he is the Lord <na>(h)</na> our God; and we the people of his pasture, and the shepe <na>(i)</na> of his hand.

notes.label: h
notes.text: It is most iust and necessarie that we adore God, because he made vs, and al this world for vs, hath also redemed vs, and made vs his people, as shepe of his pasture, and as a Pastor feedeth and gouerneth vs.

notes.label: i
notes.text: of his making.

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> To day if ye shal heare his voice, harden not your hartes;

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though some haue often repelled, and resisted Gods grace, yet if they receiue it being offered againe, it wil auaile them to remission of sinnes.

verses.text: As in the prouocation according to the day <na>(l)</na> of the tentation in the desert: where your fathers tempted me, proued me, and saw my workes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The Israelites in the desert tempted God, by desiring water, and flesh, of voluptuous concupiscence without necessitie. For Manna did both extinguish their thirst, and tasted vnto them, whatsoeuer they desired: Exo. 16. That also which was left vngathered when the sunne waxed hotte, melted (v. 21.) and serued their cattel for drincke. So this tentation was a figure of those, which require to communicate vnder both kindes, as if one did not conteine as much as both.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Fourtie years was I <na>(n)</na> offended with that generation, and said: These alwaies erre in hart.

notes.label: m
notes.text: By this mention of the offence of fourtie yeares, as long before passed, is conuinced that Moyses writte not this Psalme, who died in the very fourtith yeare of their abode in the desert. And S. Paul citing the wordes of this Psalme. (Heb. 4.) manifestly acknowlegeth Dauid the writer therof, and that it was written long after Moyses time in these wordes: (v. 7.) Againe he limiteth a certaine day; To day, in Dauid saying after so long time, s is aboue saide. To day if you shal heare his voice, do not obdurate your hartes. For if Iesus (that is Iosue) had geuen them rest, he would neuer speake of an other day afterward.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Being greatly offended, I approched nere vnto them, in punishing the offenders.

verses.text: And these haue not knowne my waies: as I sware in my wrath: <na>(o)</na> if they shal enter into my rest.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Those that murmured died in the desert, and entered not into the promised land, euen so those that finally offend Christ, shal not enter into euerlasting rest: Heb. 3. & 4.

chapters.summary: An inuitation to serue and adore Christ our Lord and Messias, 3. aswel for the benefites of creating al thinges, 7. as for his Incarnation, and not to harden our hartes as the Iewes did. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ our Lord and King.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Canticle <na>(a)</na> to Dauid <cr>[1]</cr> himselfe, <na>(b)</na> when the house was built after the captiuitie. SING ye to our Lord <na>(c)</na> a new song: sing to our Lord al the earth.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Inspired to Dauid, and written by him:

notes.label: b
notes.text: prophecying the restauration of the temple, after the future captiuitie. And that in figure of the vniuersal redemption of mankind by Christ, from the captiuitie of the diuel.

notes.label: c
notes.text: For a new benefite, farre greater then the deliuerie of Israel from Ægypt.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Sing ye to our Lord, and blesse his name: shewforth his saluation from day to day.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The same wordes [Sing to our Lord] thrise repeted, signifie the Blessed Trinitie, as some Fathers note. Likewise v. 7. and 8. Bring ye to our Lord, &c. in both places concluding in the singular number, blesse his name, bring to his name, importing one God.

verses.text: Shewforth his glorie among the Gentiles, his meruelous workes in al peoples.
Because our Lord is great, and exceeding laudable: he is terrible aboue al goddes.
Because al the goddes of the Gentiles are <na>(e)</na> diuels, but our Lord <na>(f)</na> made the heauens.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhat creatures soeuer spiritual or corporal, visible or inuisible the paganes serue for goddes, stil they be diuels that deceiue them, and diuers wayes vsurpe diuine honour, making such idolaters to thinke, that there is diuine powre, where none is.

notes.label: f
notes.text: He only is true God, who is Creator of heauen, and of al creatures. For no creature can create anie thing at al, that is, make anie thing of nothing but only God.

verses.text: Confession, and beauty in his sight: holinesse, and magnificence in his sanctification.
Bring to our Lord ye families of Gentiles, bring ye to our Lord glorie and honour:
bring to our Lord glorie vnto his name. Take vp hoastes, and enter into his courtes:
adore ye our Lord in his holie court. Let al the earth be moued before his face:
say ye among the Gentiles that our Lord <na>(g)</na> hath reigned. For he hath corrected the round world which shal not be moued: he wil iudge peoples in equitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Diuers ancient Doctors read more in this place: Our Lord hath reigned from the wood, to witte, Christ by his death on the crosse conquered the diuel, sinne, and death, and thence begane to reigne. S. Iustinus Martyr, dialogo aduers. Triphonem. Tertullian li. aduers. Iudæos. c. 9. & 13 & aduers Marcionem. li 1. c. 19. & 21. S. Augustin in this place, according to the old Roman Psalter Before him Arnobius, and after him Cassiadorus and others, wherby it is probable, that it was sometimes in the Hebrew text, and blotted out by the Iewes.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Let the heauens be glad, and the earth reioyce, the sea be moued, and the fulnesse therof:

notes.label: h
notes.text: The Psalmist in abundance of spirite inuiteth al creatures to praise God, as Daniel in his Canticle. c. 3.

verses.text: the fieldes shal be glad, and al things, that are in them. Then shal the trees of the woodes reioyce
before the face of our Lord, because he cometh: because he cometh to iudge the earth. He <na>(i)</na> wil iudge the round world in equitie, and peoples in his truth.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Christ iudgeth now in the world by his ministers discerning and deciding causes, rewarding and punishing, but especially he wil iudge al in the last day.

chapters.summary: Al peoples & nations are inuited to praise the blessed Trinitie, 3. for Christs Incarnation, and spiritual kingdom in al the world. 10. euen sensles creatures acknowledging his maiestie, 13. and iudicial powre. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's divine power.
The 5. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> this Dauid, <na>(b)</na> when his land was restored agane to him. OVr Lord hath reigned, let the earth reioyce: let <na>(c)</na> manie Ilands be glad.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In figure of Christ,

notes.label: b
notes.text: whose bodie rose the third day after his death: to whom manie returned beleuing in him after his resurrection, which fel from him in his passion: and to whom al thinges shal be subdued, as to their true Lord, in the day of iudgement.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Holie Dauid, and other Prophetes hauing great ioy to see long before in spirite only, Christs kingdom extended in the whole earth, yea to the Ilandes, we Ilanders haue great cause to be gladde, that God hath not only so blessed vs long since, but as yet conserueth seede, wherby we trust the whole Iland shal be againe restored vnto him.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Cloude, and mist round about him: iustice, and iudgement <na>(e)</na> the correction of his seat.

notes.label: d
notes.text: As in a cloud with terror God gaue his law to the Iewes: so in a cloud with greater terror and maiestie, he wil iudge the world;

notes.label: e
notes.text: not as manie corrupted seates of iudgement, in this world, but as a corrected tribunal, where iustice and right iudgement shal be practised.

verses.text: Fire shal goe before him, and shal inflame his enimies round about.
His lightninges <na>[1]</na> shined to the round world, the earth sawe, and was moued,

notes.text: These thinges are denounced as if they were alredy donne, for the assured certaintie therof.

verses.text: The mountaines melted as waxe, before the face of our Lord: before the face of our Lord al the earth.
The heauens haue shewed forth his iustice: and al peoples haue seene his glorie.
Let them al be confounded, that adore <na>(f)</na> sculptils: and that glorie in their idoles. Adore him al ye his Angels:

notes.label: f
notes.text: As wel the worshippers of grauen, or painted images of Iupiter, Mars, Bacchus and the like, as the worshippers of the same imagined false goddes shal be confounded.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Sion heard, and was glad. And <na>(h)</na> the daughters of Iuda reioyced, because of thy iudgements ô Lord.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The Catholique Church.

notes.label: h
notes.text: And al particular Churches, members of the vniuersal.

verses.text: Because thou Lord most high ouer al the earth: thou art exalted excedingly aboue al goddes.
You that loue our Lord, hate ye euil: our Lord keepeth the soules of his saintes, out of the hand of the sinner he wil deliuer them.
Light is risen to the iust, and ioy to the right of hart.
Be glad ye iust in our Lord: and confesse ye to the memorie <na>(i)</na> of his sanctification.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Praise our Lord Christ who is sanctitie it selfe, and sanctifieth others.

chapters.summary: Al the earth is inuited to reioyce in Christs kingdom, 3. with description of the signes coming before the day of Iudgement. 7. Idolaters shal be confounded. 8. Holie Angels and iust men shal adore Christ, and reioyce. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The last iudgement,
The 9. key.

verses.text: his coming to iudge the world. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: The Church in al nations. The 6. key.

verses.text: A psalme <na>(a)</na> to Dauid himselfe. SING ye to our Lord <na>(b)</na> a new song: because he hath done meruelous thinges. His righthand hath wrought saluation <na>(c)</na> to himselfe: and his arme is holie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Prefiguring Christ, who hath made his saluation knowen in al nations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: A new benefite of grace, making men new in spirite, requireth a new songue of gratitude.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Raised vp himselfe from death.

verses.text: Our Lord hath <na>(d)</na> made knowne his saluation: in the sight of the Gentiles he hath reueled his iustice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Made his grace effectually knowen by raising men from sinne, and deliuering them from the powre of the diuel.

verses.text: He hath remembred his mercie, and his truth to <na>(e)</na> the house of Israel. Al the ends of the earth haue seene the saluation of our God.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Some of the Iewes conuerted to Christianitie. Rom. 11.

verses.text: Make ye iubilation to God al the earth: <na>(f)</na> chaunt, and <na>(g)</na> reioyce, and <na>(h)</na> sing. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: f
notes.text: In voice.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: In instruments.
Cantate, exultate, psallite.

verses.text: Sing to our Lord on harpe, on harpe and voice of psalme:
on long drawen trumpets, and voice of cornet of horne. Make iubilation in the sight of the king our Lord:
let the sea be moued, and the fulnes therof: the round world, and they that dwel therin:
The riuers shal clappe with hand, the mountaynes together shal reioyce
at the sight of our Lord: <na>(i)</na> because he cometh to iudge the earth. <na>(k)</na> He wil iudge the round earth in iustice, and the peoples in equitie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Christ directeth and disposeth al thinges rightly in this world.

notes.label: k
notes.text: And wil accordingly geue iust sentence in the end.

chapters.summary: Al men are againe inuited ioyfully to celebrate the meruelous conquest of Christ in al nations, 4. with hart, voice, and instruments. 8. al creatures acknowledging

verses.text: A Psalme to Dauid himselfe. OVr Lord hath reigned, <na>(a)</na> let peoples be angrie: he that sitteth vpon the Cherubs, let <na>(b)</na> the earth be moued.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Though manie enimies do rage, and impugne Christ:

notes.label: b
notes.text: though the whole earth be trubled thervvith, yet Christ vvho sitteth Lord ouer the highest Angels, Cherubins and Seraphins, obteyneth the victorie, reigneth, and doth his vvil in al the earth.

verses.text: Our Lord great in Sion: and high aboue al peoples.
Let them confesse to thy great name: because it is terrible, and holie.
And the honour of the king <na>(c)</na> loueth iudgement. Thou hast prepared directions: thou hast done iudgement and iustice <na>(d)</na> in Iacob.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Requireth discretion.

notes.label: d
notes.text: in fauour of thyn elect people.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore <na>(e)</na> his footstoole: because it is holie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Hebrevv Doctors expound this of the Arke in the old testament, but the Doctors of the Church vnderstand Christs humanitie, in the holie Eucharist.

verses.text: Moyses, and Aaron in his <na>(f)</na> priestes: and Samuel among them, that inuocate his name: They inuocated our Lord <na>(g)</na> and he heard them:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Here it is euident (and S. Augustin sayth this place taketh avvay al doubt) that Moyses vvas a Priest, against those that for maintaining the heresie of Laicheadshippe, denie it.
q. 23. in Levit.

notes.label: g
notes.text: By example of their praying and obtaining, the Psalmist confirmeth his prophecie, that Priestes of the new Testament shal pray, and obtaine mercie of Christ for the Church.

verses.text: in a piller of a cloud he spake to them. They kept his testimonies, & the precept which he gaue them.
O Lord our God thou heardest them: God thou wast propitious to them, and taking vengeance vpon al <na>(h)</na> their inuentions.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God reuenged the machinations made against them, punishing the rebellion of chore, Dathan and Abyron. Num. 16.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore ye in his holie mount: because the Lord our God is holie.

chapters.summary: Christ reigneth, notwithstanding his enimies repine, is adored (5. also his footestoole) 6. whom ancient Prophetes did inuocate. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ our Messias.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A Psalme <na>(a)</na> in confession.

notes.label: a
notes.text: of praise.

verses.text: MAKE ye iubilation to God <na>(b)</na> al the earth: serue ye our Lord in gladnesse. Enter ye in <na>(c)</na> before his sight, in exulration.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not only Iewes, but also al Gentiles.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God eueryvvhere present, yet more peculiarly heareth his suppliants, praying in the temple, or place dedicated to his seruice.

verses.text: Know ye that our Lord <na>(d)</na> he is God: he made vs, and not we ourselues. His people, and the sheepe of his pasture:

notes.label: d
notes.text: He only whom we serue as our Lord is the only God, and there is no other.

verses.text: enter ye into <na>(e)</na> his gates in confession, his courtes in hymnes: confesse ye to him. Praise ye his name:

notes.label: e
notes.text: Peculiar dedicated place, as v. 2.

verses.text: because our Lord is sweete, his <na>(f)</na> mercie for euer, and <na>(g)</na> his truth euen vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As God is alwayes merciful in geuing, and promising:

notes.label: g
notes.text: so he is euer faithful in performing.

chapters.summary: Al are inuited to reioyce in God, Creator of al. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
One Creator of all things.
The 1. key.

verses.text: A Psalme to Dauid himselfe. MERCIE <na>(a)</na> and iudgement I wil sing to thee ô Lord: I wil sing,

notes.label: a
notes.text: These two capital diuine vertues are euer ioyned in al Gods workes, for both which experienced towards him selfe, the Psalmist rendereth thankes and praises.

verses.text: and I <na>(b)</na> shal vnderstand in the immaculate way, <na>(c)</na> when thou shalt come to me. I walked through in the inocencie of my hart, in the middes of my house.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I wil do myn endeuoure to know the immaculate way,

notes.label: c
notes.text: which I can not do, but by thy grace coming vnto me. For by helpe therof I did as followeth.

verses.text: I did not propose before mine eies any vniust thing: I hated them that do preuarication.
A peruerse hart hath not cleaued to me: the malignant declining from me I knew not.
<na>(d)</na> One secretly detracting from his neighbour, him did I persecute. One of a proud eye, and vnsatiable hart, with him I did not eate.

notes.label: d
notes.text: That is, al and euerie one thus wickedly disposed I abhorred.

verses.text: Mine eies are towards the faithful of the earth that they may sit with me. A man that walketh in the immaculate way, <na>(e)</na> he did minister to me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I kept such vnder, as a seruant or slaue.

verses.text: He that doth proudly shal not dwel in the middes of my house: he that speaketh vniust thinges, hath <na>(f)</na> not directed in the sight of mine eies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Prospered not, gotte no benefite by me.

verses.text: In <na>(g)</na> the morning did I kil al the sinners of the earth: that I might destroy <na>(h)</na> out of the citie of our Lord, al those that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Speedely and without delay I cutte of al disordered people:

notes.label: h
notes.text: that others might not be corrupted by them.

chapters.summary: King Dauid gratfully celebrateth the two general diuine vertues, Mercie and Iustice: 2. by his owne example exhorteth al, especially Superiors, to direct their wayes in sinceritie, 4. and to seperate the wicked from conuersation of the good. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Instruction to gouerne.
The 7. key.

verses.text: The prayer of the poore, when he shal be anxious, and shal make his petition before our Lord.
LORD heare my <na>(a)</na> prayer: and let my <na>(b)</na> crie come to thee.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Euerie petition is a prayer,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and that which proceedeth from more feruent affection, is called a crie, though it burst not out into clamoure, nor perhaps into anie voice at al. For God saide to Moyses, praying in mere silence, but with vehemencie of spirite (Exod. 14) Why criest thou to me?

verses.text: Turne <na>(c)</na> not away thy face from me: in what day soeuer I am in tribulation, incline thine eare to me. In what day soeuer I shal inuocate thee, heare me speedely.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though sinne prouoke Gods wrath, because we by sinning turne from him, and not he first from vs: yet we pray God not so to leaue vs, but to geue vs new grace, that by humilitie, and penance we may returne to him, and not dye in sinne.

verses.text: Because my dayes haue vanished as <na>(d)</na> smoke: and my <na>(e)</na> bones are withered as <na>(f)</na> a drie burnt firebrand.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Mans dayes, and al his workes are nothing worth, but vanish like smoke, so long as he is in mortal sinne:

notes.label: e
notes.text: yea his best workes, as if he geue almose, fast, pray, and dye for the truth, yet al those auaile nothing (1. Cor. 13.) but are

notes.label: f
notes.text: like dryed stickes, or chippes, sitte to kindle the fire.

verses.text: I <na>(g)</na> am striken as grasse, and my hart is withered: because <na>(h)</na> I haue forgotten to eate my bread.

notes.label: g
notes.text: My soule separated by sinne from God, withereth as grasse, that is cutte from the roote:

notes.label: h
notes.text: because I haue lost al sauour and appetite to spiritual meate.

verses.text: For <na>(i)</na> the voyce of my groning, my <na>(k)</na> bone hath cleaued to my flesh.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In this miserable state.

notes.label: k
notes.text: I am as bones and flesh cleauing together without moysture, or radical humour.

verses.text: I am become like <na>(l)</na> a pellicane of the wildernes: I am become as <na>(m)</na> a nightcrow in the house.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I fled from conuersation of men for sorow, and shame of my sinnes:

notes.label: m
notes.text: as a crow that only flieth by night: or as an owle, or batte.

verses.text: I haue watched, and am become as <na>(n)</na> a sparow solitarie in the housetoppe.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Also as a sparow hauing lost her mate, remaineth mourning and solitarie in the accustomed nest, or mere vnto it,

verses.text: Al the day did mine enemies vpbrayde me: and they <na>(o)</na> that praised me, sware against me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Those that were wont to praise or flatter me, now are as sworne enimies against me.

verses.text: Because I did <na>(p)</na> eate ashes as bread, & mingled <na>(q)</na> my drinke with weeping.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Bread sauoured to me no better then ashes.

notes.label: q
notes.text: and drinke gaue me no comfort, but stil I wept.

verses.text: At <na>(r)</na> the face of thy wrath and indignation: because <na>(s)</na> lifting me vp thou hast throwne me <na>(t)</na> downe.

notes.label: r
notes.text: I am most especially afflicted, because thou art angrie.

notes.label: s
notes.text: In that thou didst sometime aduance me in prosperitie,

notes.label: t
notes.text: my fall is so much greater, and more grieuous.

verses.text: My daies haue declined <na>(v)</na> as a shadow: and I am withered <na>(w)</na> as grasse.

notes.label: v
notes.text: As a shadow declineth to nothing, and al becometh darknes, when the sunne, and other light departeth, euen so I, that am but a shadow, decline to mere darknes, when thy fauoure parteth from me.

notes.label: w
notes.text: and I lose my beautie, as grasse cutte from the ground withereth.

verses.text: <na>(x)</na> But thou ô Lord endurest for euer: and <na>(y)</na> thy memorial in generation and generation.

notes.label: x
notes.text: But I am meruelously comforted, considering that thou our Messias, the Sonne of God, art immutable for euer:

notes.label: y
notes.text: and thy memorable promise of redeeming mankind, wil haue effect in al generations.

verses.text: Thou <na>(z)</na> rysing vp shal haue mercie on Sion: because it is <na>(a)</na> time to haue mercie on it, because <na>(b)</na> the time cometh.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Thou rising to helpe, who semedst to haue forgote, wilt protect the Church, and euerie faithful soule.

notes.label: a
notes.text: because thou hast differred long:

notes.label: b
notes.text: and because the time by thee designed semeth to approch

verses.text: Because <na>(c)</na> the stones therof haue pleased thy seruantes: and they shal haue pittie on <na>(d)</na> the earth <na>(e)</na> therof.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Men that shal heare thyn Apostles preach, shal proue good and fitte matter, for the building of thy Church:

notes.label: d
notes.text: and the simplest poore people, as it were, the earth or dust;

notes.label: e
notes.text: shal participate of this mercie.

verses.text: And <na>(f)</na> the Gentiles shal feare thy name ô Lord, and al <na>(g)</na> the kinges of the earth thy glorie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Besides those Iewes that shal beleue in Christ, much more the Gentiles shal feare and serue him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: His glorie is so euident that al kinges know it, though al be not conuerted.

verses.text: Because our Lord hath built Sion: and he shal be seene in his glorie.
He hath had respect to the prayer <na>(h)</na> of the humble: and he hath not despised their petition.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Of holie Patriarches, Priestes, Prophetes, and of al true penitents,

verses.text: Let these thinges be written vnto an other generation: and the people, that shal <na>(i)</na> be created, shal praise our Lord.

notes.label: i
notes.text: That shal be made a new creature in Christ.

verses.text: Because he hath lookedforth from his high holie place: our Lord from heauen hath looked vpon the earth.
That he might heare the gronings of the fettered: that he might loose the children of them that are slayne:
That they may <na>(k)</na> shewforth the name of our Lord in Sion: and his praise in Ierusalem.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The faithful people of the Church, according to their habilitie endeuour to serue Christ.

verses.text: In the assembling of the people together in one, and kinges to serue our Lord.
He answered him in the way of his strength: Shew me the fewnes of my daies.
