Cal me not backe <na>(l)</na> in the halfe of my daies: thy yeares are vnto generation and generation.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Grant me time and meanes to be mature in vertue in this life.

verses.text: In the beginning ô Lord thou didst found the earth: and the heauens are the workes of thy hands.
They <na>(m)</na> shal perish, but thou art permanent: and they shal al waxe old as a garment. <cr>[1]</cr> And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shal be changed:

notes.label: m
notes.text: Be changed in qualitie.

verses.text: but thou art the selfe same, and thy yeares shal not faile.
The children of thy seruantes shal inhabite: and <na>(n)</na> their seede shal be directed for euer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The Church of Christ perpetual.

chapters.summary: A sinner in affliction of mind prayeth God to deliuer him, 10. desolate of al other helpe. 13. conceiueth comforth in Gods eternal goodnes, and singular mercie, in redeming mankind, and propagating the Church. 24. Prayeth to be made mature in vertue before he dye, that he may liue with God: 26. who only and wholly being immutable, establisheth his seruantes for euer. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The fifth penitential Psalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid himself. MY soule <na>(b)</na> blesse thou our Lord: and <na>(c)</na> al thinges, that are within me, his holie name.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Inspired to Dauid, and written by him.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Shew forth praises, and thankes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: al my cogitations, affections, senses, and powres.

verses.text: My soule blesse thou our Lord: and forget not al his retributions.
Who is <na>(d)</na> propitious to al thine iniquities: who <na>(e)</na> healeth al thine infirmities.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The first benefite of grace is remission of sinnes:

notes.label: e
notes.text: the second, is curing euil habites, or dispositions.

verses.text: Who <na>(f)</na> redemeth thy life from deadly falling: who <na>(g)</na> crowneth thee in mercie and commiserations.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The third, to conserue from falling againe:

notes.label: g
notes.text: the fourth, to geue victorie and reward in abundant measure.

verses.text: Who <na>(h)</na> replenisheth thy desire in good thinges: thy youth <na>(i)</na> shal be rewed as the eagles.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The fifth, to grant al lawful petitions temporal and spiritual, which are good for the soule,

notes.label: i
notes.text: the sixth, resurrection of flesh in glorie.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(k)</na> doth mercies: and <na>(l)</na> iudgement to al that suffer wrong.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Our Lord, whose special propertie is to shew mercie,

notes.label: l
notes.text: when the same is neglected, he reuengeth the wrongs, deliuering the oppressed, and punishing the oppressors.

verses.text: He made his waies <na>(m)</na> knowne to Moyses, his willes to the children of Israel.

notes.label: m
notes.text: By geuing them a written law.

verses.text: Our Lord is <na>(n)</na> pitieful, and <na>(o)</na> merciful: <na>(p)</na> long suffering, and very merciful.

notes.label: n
notes.text: God is naturally pittiful, to releeue the afflicted.

notes.label: o
notes.text: merciful towards sinners.

notes.label: p
notes.text: loath to be angrie, or to punish.

verses.text: He wil <na>(q)</na> not be angrie alwayes: neither wil he threaten for euer.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God punisheth not penitents with eternal paine, but with temporal: for though (as in the next verse) our sinnes of their owne nature, deserue eternal punishment, yet Christ paying our ransome, true penitents are only punished temporally.

verses.text: He hath not done to vs according to our sinnes: neither according to our iniquities hath he rewarded vs.
For according to the height of heauen from the earth: hath he strengthned his mercie vpon them that feare him.
As far <na>(r)</na> as the East is distant from the West: hath he made our iniquities far from vs.

notes.label: r
notes.text: See here the perfect washing away, and separation of sinnes.

verses.text: As a father hath compassion of his children, so hath our Lord compassion on them that feare him:
because he hath knowen <na>(s)</na> our making. He remembred that we are dust:

notes.label: s
notes.text: In reguard of our frailtie he hath compassion: yet his mercie only auaileth to them that feare him: as in the next wordes before, and v. 17.

verses.text: man, his daies are as grasse, as the floure of the filde so shal he florish.
Because the spirit shal passe in him, and he shal not stand: and he shal know his place no more.
But the mercie of our Lord from euerlasting, and vnto euerlasting vpon them that feare him. And his iustice is vpon the childrens children, to them that keepe his testament.
And are mindful of his commandmentes, to <na>(t)</na> doe them.

notes.label: t
notes.text: A iust man not only knoweth, and remembreth, but also doth the commandments.

verses.text: Our Lord hath prepared his seate in heauen: and his kindom shal haue dominion ouer al.
Blesse our Lord al ye his Angels: mightie in powre, doing his word, that feare the voice of his wordes.
Blesse our Lord al ye his hoastes: you his ministers, that doe his wil.
Blesse ye our Lord <na>(v)</na> al his workes: in euerie place <na>(w)</na> of his dominion, my soule blesse thou our Lord.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Al creatures, though naturally senseles, yet praise God, because they are his worke,

notes.label: w
notes.text: and because they are in his dominion.

chapters.summary: Thankes to God for priuate, 6. and publike benefites. 17. His mercie, iustice, and other proprieties are immutable. 20. Angels, and al other creatures are inuited to praise him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gratitude for God's benefits.
The 7. key.

verses.text: To Dauid him self. MY soule blesse thou our Lord: ô Lord my God thou art magnified excedingly.
Thou hast put on <na>(a)</na> confession and beautie: being clothed with light as with a garment: Stretching out the heauen as a skinne:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Thou possessest al maiestie, and matter of praise.

verses.text: which couerest the higher partes therof <na>(b)</na> with waters. Which <na>(c)</na> makest the cloude for thee to ascend on: which walkest vpon the winges of windes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Thou hast compassed the sphere of the fixed starres, with a sphere of christalline substance which is as water congeled.

notes.label: c
notes.text: According to our capacitie the prophet describeth the speedie coming, or working of God as if he came in a swift cloud, or with winges of the wind, to signifie that he worketh wel and when he pleaseth without delay: He saide, and thinges were made: he commanded and they were created, Psal. 32.

verses.text: Which makest spirites thine <na>(d)</na> Angels: and thy <na>(e)</na> ministers a burning fyre.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Thy messengers to execute thy wil:

notes.label: e
notes.text: & the same Angels are as a burning fire in operation yea they dispatch more easily, and more spedely then we can conceiue,

verses.text: Which hast founded the earth vpon <na>(f)</na> the stabilitie therof: it shal not be inclined for euer and euer

notes.label: f
notes.text: Most firmly established by natural weight, in the center of the world:

verses.text: The <na>(g)</na> depth, <na>(h)</na> as a garment, is his clothing: vpon the mountaines shal waters stand.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The water hi

notes.label: h
notes.text: should naturally couer al the earth:

verses.text: At <na>(i)</na> thy reprehention they shal flee: at the voice of thy thunder they shal feare.

notes.label: i
notes.text: But by thy commandment the waters are conteined in their limited places.

verses.text: The <na>(k)</na> mountaines ascend: and the plaine fildes descend into the place, which thou hast founded for them.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The waters being conteyned in their appointed chanels, both hilles and fieldes appeare which otherwise would be couered.

verses.text: Thou hast set a bound, which <na>(l)</na> they shal not passe ouer: neither shal they returne to couer the earth.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The wate…

verses.text: Which sendestforth fontaines in the valles: betwen the middest of mountaines shal waters passe.
Al the beastes of the filde shal drinke: the wilde asses shal <na>(m)</na> expect in their thirst.

notes.label: m
notes.text: hope for and receiue

verses.text: Ouer them shal the foules of the ayre inhabite: out of the middes of rockes they shal geueforth voices.
Watering the mountaines from his higher places: of the fruite of thy worke shal the earth be filled:
Bringing forth grasse for beastes, and herbe for the seruice of men. That thou mayst bring forth <na>(n)</na> bread out of the earth:

notes.label: n
notes.text: By these three principal kindes of foode, breade, wine, and oyl, al sortes of nutriment are vnderstood.

verses.text: and <na>(o)</na> wine may make the hart of man ioyful: That he may make the face chereful with <na>(p)</na> oile: and bread may confirme the hart of man.

notes.label: o
notes.text: See previous note

notes.label: p
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: The trees of the filde shal be filled, and the ceders of Libanus, which he hath planted:
there sparowes shal make their nest. The house of the hearne is the leader of them:
the high mountaines for hartes: the rocke a refuge for the Irchins.
He made the moone for seasons: the sunne knoweth his going downe.
Thou didst appoint darkenes, and night was made: in it shal al the beastes of the wood passe.
The whelpes of lions roaring, to rauen, and to seeke of God meate for themselues.
The sunne is risen, and they are gathered together: and in their couches they shal be placed.
Man shal goe forth to his worke: and to his working vntil euening.
How magnified are thy workes ô Lord! thou hast made al thinges in wisedom: the earth is filled with <na>(q)</na> thy possession.

notes.label: q
notes.text: VVith thy creatures.

verses.text: This great sea, and very large, there are <na>(r)</na> creeping beastes, wherof <na>(s)</na> there is no number. Litle beastes with great:

notes.label: r
notes.text: Fishes, serpents, wormes, and al liuing creatures that lacke feete.

notes.label: s
notes.text: No kind of liuing creatures multiplieth so much as fishes Aristotel li. 9. Animal. c. 17.

verses.text: there ships shall pass. This <na>(t)</na> dragon, whom thou madest to <na>(v)</na> delude:

notes.label: t
notes.text: A most huge fish called Leuiathan. Iob. 40. v. 20.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Albeit in the water he passeth mans streingth, yet depriued of water he is not able to defend himselfe. v. 19.

verses.text: al expect of thee that thou geue them meate in season.
Thou geuing vnto them, they shal gather it: thou opening thy hand, al shal be filled with bountie.
But thou turning away the face, they shal be trubled: thou shalt take away their spirite, and they shal faile, and shal returne into their dust.
Thou shalt sendforth thy spirit, and they shal be created: and thou shalt renewe the face of the earth.
Be the glorie of our Lord for euer: our Lord wil reioice in his workes:
Who looketh vpon the earth, & maketh it to tremble: who toucheth the mountaines, and they smoke.
I wil chaunte to our Lord in my life: I wil sing to my God as long as I am.
Let my speach be acceptable to him: but I wil take delight in our Lord.
<na>(w)</na> Let sinners faile from the earth, and the vniust, so that they be not: my soule blesse thou our Lord.

notes.label: w
notes.text: A prediction that impenitent sinners shal be damned, wherin the Prophet conforming his wil to Gods, vttereth it in forme of a prayer.

chapters.summary: The Psalmist inuiteth himself and others to praise God, for his meruelous workes in the heauens, 5. the earth, and water, 9. limiting their bondes, producing al thinges necessarie for al liuing creatures, in conuenient seasons. 27. with continual prouidence of al. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's works marvelous.
The 2. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Alleluia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord, and inuocate his name: <na>(b)</na> shew forth his workes among the Gentiles. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Alleluia signifieth more then Laudate Dominum, Praise ye our Lord. For by these two hebrew wordes, Allelu a, the Prophet inuiteth al men to praise God, with gladnes, and iubilation, with hart, voice, and gesture, with instruments, and howsoeuer we are able. And therfore S Ierom, S. Augustin, and al Catholique writers kepe the same worde, and translate it not, neither in the titles of Psalmes, not ordinarily in anie place of holie Scripture. This is the first Psalme thus titled, and is the same Psalme in sense, and in good part of the wordes, which the royal Prophet made, and caused to be songue, when he brought the Arke of God from the house of Obededom into his owne house. 1. Par. 16. v. 8.

notes.label: b
notes.text: How much more gratful is it now to God, that we celebrate the greater mysteries of the new Testament.
For an exposition of this Psalme read the places quoted in the inner margen.

verses.text: Chaunt to him, and sing to him: tel ye al his meruelous workes.
Prayse ye him in his holie name: let the hart of them reioice that seeke our Lord.
Seeke ye our Lord, and be confirmed: seeke <na>(c)</na> his face alwayes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: His present helpe.

verses.text: Remember ye his meruelous workes, which he hath done: his wonders, and the iudgments of his mouth.
The seede of Abraham, his seruantes: the children of Iacob his elect.
He is the Lord our God: in <na>(d)</na> al the earth are his iudgementes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: not only in Israel, but in al the world.

verses.text: He hath bene mindeful for euer of his testament: of the word, which he commanded <na>(e)</na> vnto a thousand generations. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: e
notes.text: For euer, to the end of the world.

verses.text: Which he disposed to Abraham: and of his oath to Isaac.
And he appointed it to Iacob for a precept: and to Israel for an eternal testament.
Saying: To thee wil I geue the land of Chanaan, the corde of your inheritance.
When they were <na>(f)</na> of smal number, very few and seiourners therof:

notes.label: f
notes.text: But 70. persons.

verses.text: And they passed from nation into nation, & from kingdom to an other people.
He leift not a man to hurt them: and he rebuked kings for their sake.
Touch not my annointed, and toward my prophetes be not malignant.
And <na>(g)</na> he called a famine vpon the land: and he destroyed al the strength of bread. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: By his prouidence suffered.

verses.text: He sent a man before them: Ioseph was sold to be a seruant.
They humbled his feete in fetters, yron passed through his soule, <cr>[1]</cr>
vntil his word came. The word of our Lord inflamed him:
the king sent, and loosed him; the prince of the people, and released him.
He appointed him lord of his house: and prince of al his possession.
That he might instruct his princes as himselfe: and might teach his ancientes wisedom.
And Israel entered into Ægypt, and Iacob was a seiourner in the land <na>(h)</na> of Cham. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: h
notes.text: Ægypt, possessed by Mesraim Chams second sonne. Gen. 10. v. 13.
Gen 46.

verses.text: And he increased his people excedingly: and strengthned them ouer their enemies. <cr>[1]</cr>
He <na>(i)</na> turned their hart, that they hated his people: and to worke guile toward his seruantes.

notes.label: i
notes.text: May it be vnderstood, or beleued (saith S. Augustin) that God turneth the hart of man to committe sinnes? Or is it no sinne, or is it a smal sinne, to hate the people of God? Or to worke guile towards his seruants? VVho wil say this? VVhat then, is God author of these so greeuous sinnes, who is not to be supposed the author of a most smal sinne? This lerned Father therfore answereth, that God peruerted not a right hart, but turned that was of it selfe peruerse, to the hatred of his people, where he might vse that euil wel, not by making them euil, but by bestowing vpon his owne people good thinges, which the euil might easily enuie. VVhich hatred of theirs how God vsed both to the exercise of his people (which is profitable to vs) & to the glorie of his owne name, the thinges that folow do teach vs, which are here remembred to his praise.

verses.text: He sent Moyses his seruant: Aaron, <na>(k)</na> him selfe whom he chose. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: k
notes.text: In whom God established the Priesthood of Moyses law.

verses.text: He did put in them the wordes of his signes, and of his wonders in the Land of Cham.
He sent <na>(l)</na> darkenes, and obscured: and did <na>(m)</na> not exasperate his wordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: The ninth plague of the Ægyptians.

notes.label: m
notes.text: God willingly, not as one loath or vnwilling, performed al that he threatned.

verses.text: He turned their <na>(n)</na> waters into bloud: and killed their fishes.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The first plague.

verses.text: Their land broughtforth <na>(o)</na> frogges in <na>[1]</na> the inner chambers of their kinges.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The second plague.
Dauid knew this by reuelation, or by tradition for it is not in Exodus.

verses.text: He sayd, and <na>(p)</na> the <na>[1]</na> cænomyia came: and the <na>(q)</na> cinises in al their coastes.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The fourth plague.

notes.label: q
notes.text: The third plague.
p A swarme of flies.

verses.text: He made theyr raynes <na>(r)</na> haile: fire burning in their land.

notes.label: r
notes.text: The seuenth plague.

verses.text: And he stroke their vines, and their figtrees: and he destroyed the wood of their coastes.
He said, & <na>(s)</na> the locust came, and the <na>(t)</na> bruchus wherof there was no number.

notes.label: s
notes.text: The eight plague.

notes.label: t
notes.text: A worme that spoyleth corne, grasse, and fruict.

verses.text: And it did eate al the grasse in their land: and it did eate al the fruicte of their land.
And he stroke euerie <na>(v)</na> first begotten in their land: the first fruictes of al their labour.

notes.label: v
notes.text: The tenth plague. · The fifth & sixt of pestilence and boyles are omitted.

verses.text: And he brought them forth with gold and siluer, and there was not in their tribes a feeble person.
Ægypt was glad at their departure: because the feare of them lay vpon them.
He spred a cloude for their protection, and fire to shine vnto them by night. <cr>[1]</cr>

cross_refs.text: Exod. 13. v. 21. Exod. 16. v. 13. Exod. 17. v. 6. Gen. 12.

verses.text: They made petition, and the quaile came: and he filled them with the bread of heauen.
He diuided the rocke, and waters flowed: riuers ranne in the drie ground.
Because he was mindful of his holie word, which he had vttered to Abraham his seruant.
And he broughtforth his people in exultation, and his elect in ioy.
And he gaue them the countries of the Nations: and they possessed the labours of peoples: <cr>[1]</cr>
That they might keepe his iustifications, and seeke after his lawe.

chapters.summary: The Israelites are exhorted to sing praises to God, 5. for his meruelous benefites towards Abraham, Isaac, and Iacob. 11. whose particular familie, being then smal, went from Chanaan into Ægypt (17. Whither Ioseph by Gods prouidence was caried before) there increased in number, was persecuted, 26. deliuered by Moyses and Aaron, working manie great miracles, 36. protected, and fedde in the desert, 44. and finally possessed Chanaan. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's special benefits towards the Jews.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord <na>(a)</na> because he is good: because his mercie is for euer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: God is of himselfe and essentially good, al other goodnes is participated of him.
Iudith. v. 21.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Who shal speake the powers of our Lord, shal make al his praises to be heard?

notes.label: b
notes.text: No creature can fully expresse Gods perfections.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Blessed are they, that keepe iudgement, and <na>(d)</na> doe iustice at al time.

notes.label: c
notes.text: It is a happie state in this life, either to kepe Gods law :

notes.label: d
notes.text: or to repent and do worthie penance for transgressing.

verses.text: Remember vs ô Lord <na>(e)</na> in the good pleasure of thy people: visite vs in thy saluation:

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy wonted beneuolence, promised to thy people.

verses.text: To <na>(f)</na> see in the goodnes of thyne elect, to reioyce in the ioy of thy nation: that thou maist be praised with thine inheritance.

notes.label: f
notes.text: That we may see, and enioy the benefites promised to thyne elect.

verses.text: We haue <na>(g)</na> sinned with our fathers: we haue <na>(h)</na> dealt vniustly, we haue <na>(i)</na> done iniquitie.

notes.label: g
notes.text: We haue erred and hurt ourselues :

notes.label: h
notes.text: we haue wronged our neighboures :

notes.label: i
notes.text: we haue offended against God.

verses.text: Our fathers in Ægypt did not vnderstand thy meruelous workes: they were not mindeful of the multitude of thy mercie. And they prouoked thee to wrath going vp vnto the sea, the Read sea.
And he saued them <na>(k)</na> for his name sake; that he might make his power knowen. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: k
notes.text: Albeit the people by their murmuring deserued more punishment, yet God for the glorie of his owne name saued them from vtter destruction.

verses.text: And he rebuked the Read sea, and it was made drie: and he led them in the depths as in a desert.
And he saued them from the hand of them that hated them: and he redemed them out of the hand of the enemie.
And water ouerwhelmed those that afflicted them: there did not one of them remaine.
And they beleued his wordes: and they sang his praise.
They had <na>(l)</na> quickly donne, they forgot his workes: and they <na>(m)</na> expected not his counsel.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They perseuered not long in their dutie towards God, seing his omnipotent powre by his meruelous workes :

notes.label: m
notes.text: nor were content with his prouidence, but carnally coueted thinges, not necessarie.

verses.text: And they coueted concupiscence in the desert: and tempted God in the place without water. <cr>[1]</cr>
He gaue them their petition: and sent saturitie into their <na>(n)</na> soules. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: n
notes.text: According to their carnal desires.

verses.text: And they prouoked Moyses in the campe: Aaron the <na>(o)</na> holie of our Lord.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Holie by his function.

verses.text: The earth was opened, and swalowed Dathan: and ouerwhelmed the congregation of Abiron.
And a fire flamed vp in their sinagogue: the flame burnt the sinners.
And they made a calfe in Horeb: and they adored <na>(p)</na> the sculptil. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: p
notes.text: They adored the image that represented a calf, not God.

verses.text: And they <na>(q)</na> changed their glorie into the similitude of a calfe that eateth grasse.

notes.label: q
notes.text: God being their true glorie, they changed him, for a false god of the Ægyptians (who especially honoured a calfe called Apis) making an image therof, and attributed their deliuerie from Ægypt to this imagined god. Exo. 32. v. 4. 8. Of which and the like foolish, and abominable idolatrie S. Paul writeth, Rom. 1. v. 23. They changed the glorie of the incorruptible God, into a similitude of the image of a corruptible man, and of foules, and of foure footed beastes, and of them that crepe : where we see what maner of imagies holie Scriptures condemne, and not the imagies of Christ and his Sainctes.

verses.text: They forgat God, which saued them, which did great thinges in Ægypt,
meruelous thinges in the land of Cham, terrible thinges in the Read sea.
And <na>(r)</na> he sayd to destroy them: if Moyses his elect had not stood in the way before him: <cr>[1]</cr>To turne away his wrath that he should not destroy them:

notes.label: r
notes.text: He sayd, he would destroy them, but for Moyses prayer spared them.

verses.text: and they estemed for naught the land that was to be desired. <cr>[1]</cr> They did not beleue his word,
and they murmured in their tabernacles: they heard not the voice of our Lord.
And he lifted vp his hand ouer them: to ouerthrowe them in the desert: <cr>[1]</cr>
And to cast doune their seede among the Nations: and to disperse them in the countries.
And they were professed to <na>(s)</na> Beelphegor: and they did eate the sacrifices <na>(t)</na> of the dead. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: s
notes.text: The Idol of Moabites, and Madianitees,

notes.label: t
notes.text: As God is in deede the liuing God, that liueth of himselfe, and geueth life to others : so false goddes are called dead goddes, that can not geue life to anie, but doe kil al that serue them at least spiritually, and often corporally.

verses.text: And they prouoked him in their inuentions: and ruine was multiplied on them.
And Phinees stood, and <na>(v)</na> pacified: and the slaughter ceased.

notes.label: v
notes.text: Phinees moued by the zele of God (as the holie text witnesseth. Nu. 25. v. 11.) in killing the adulterers pleased God, and merited reward.

verses.text: And it was reputed to him vnto iustice, in generation and generation euen for euer.
And they prouoked him at the waters of contradiction: and <na>(w)</na> Moyses was vexed for them: <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: w
notes.text: Moyses afflicted in spirite, by the enormious murmuring of the people, doubted whether God would geue them water out of the rocke or no, not doubting of his powre, but of his wil : and so when he should haue spoken to the rocke, Num. 20. v. 8. he spoke to the incredulous people. v. 10. and therin offended God. for which he was temporally punished. v. 12. Deut. 1. v. 37. & c. 3. v. 26. c. 4. v. 21.

verses.text: because they exasperated his spirit. And he plainly affirmed in his lips:
they destroyed not the nations, of which our Lord spake to them.
And they were mingled among the nations, and learned their workes: <cr>[1]</cr>
and they serued their sculptils: and it became a scandal to them.
And they immolated their sonnes, and their daughters to diuels.
And <na>(x)</na> they shed innocent bloud: the bloud of their sonnes and of their daughters, which they sacrificed to the sculptils of Chanaan. And the land was infected with bloud,

notes.label: x
notes.text: Some Iewes offered these most cruel, vnnatural, and abominable sacrifices ; perhaps in the times of Iudges, when they were mingled with idolatrous people, and serued their goddes ; Iud. 2. v. 11. c. 3. v. 6. But it is more expresse after Dauids time, wherof he here prophecieth, and was verified by Achaz. 4. Reg. 16 v. 3. and by Manasses. 4. Reg. 21. v. 6. VVhich with other idolatrie king Iosias destroyed. 4. Reg. 23. v. 10.

verses.text: and was contaminated in their workes: and they did fornicat in their inuentions.
And our Lord was wrath with furie vpon his people: and he abhorred his inheritance.
And he deliuered them into the handes of the nations: and they that hated them, had the dominion of them.
And their enimies afflicted them: and they were humbled vnder their handes:
he did often deliuer them. But they exasperated him in their counsel: and they were humbled in their iniquities.
And he <na>(y)</na> saw when they were afflicted: and he heard their prayer.

notes.label: y
notes.text: God respected them with his merciful eye, and gaue them grace to repent.

verses.text: And he was mindeful of his testament: and it repented him according to the multitude of his mercie.
And he gaue them into mercies in the sight of al, that had taken them. <na>(z)</na>

notes.label: z
notes.text: Here the Psalmist concludeth both the historie and prophecie of this Psalme, with prayer and praise, as foloweth :

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Saue vs ô Lord our God: and geather vs out of the Nations: That we may confesse to thy holie name: & may glorie in thy prayse.

notes.text: A verie fitte prayer in time of schisme.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord the God of Israel from euerlasting vnto euerlasting: and al the people shal say: Be it, be it.

chapters.summary: The prophet exhorteth the people to render thankes and praises to God, 6. for remitting their manifold sinnes, in the desert. 34. and in the conquered land : 38. foreshewing like sinnes to come, Gods wrath and punishment for the same. 44. and that he wil geue grace of repentance : to some 47. for which he prayeth, and praiseth God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Israelites often sinned, and were mercifully punished.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. CONFESSE <na>(a)</na> ye to our Lord because he is good: because his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Praise God by confessing his mercie, prouidence, and goodnes.

verses.text: Let them say that are <na>(b)</na> redemed of our Lord, whom he redemed out of the hand of the enemie: and out of the countries he gathered them:

notes.label: b
notes.text: God of his mercie promised the Redemer of mankind streight after Adams fal.

verses.text: From <na>(c)</na> the rising of the sunne, and the going downe: from the north, and the sea.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVhich redemption was intended for al, and faileth not of Gods part in anie, but of mens owne wilful refusing to be duly penitent, and to kepe Gods precepts.

verses.text: They <na>(d)</na> wandered in the wildernes, in a place without water: the way of citie for habitation they found not.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Literally of such as wander in this world, hauing no setled place to dwel in : spiritually of al mankind after his fal.

verses.text: Hungrie, and thirstie: their soule fainted in them.
And <na>(e)</na> they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their necessities.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhensoeuer they cal vpon God, he helpeth them, as is best for their spiritual health.

verses.text: And he conducted them into the right way: to goe into a citie of habitation.
Let <na>(f)</na> the mercies of our Lord confesse to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al Gods benefites, which are of his mercie, not of mans deserte, are iust matter of praising God.

verses.text: Because he hath filled the emptie soule: and the hungrie soule he hath filled with good thinges.
Them that sate in darkenes, and in the shadow of death: bound in needines, and yron.
Because they <na>(g)</na> exasperated the wordes of God: and they prouoked the counsel of the Highest.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Calamities in this world are commonly inflicted for sinnes.

verses.text: And their hart was humbled in labours: they were weakened, neither was there anie to helpe.
And they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their necessities.
And he brought them out of darkenes, and the shadow of death: and brake their bondes asunder.
Let the mercies of our Lord confesse to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.
Because he hath destroyed the gates of brasse: and the barres of yron he hath broken.
He hath receiued them out of the way of their iniquitie: for they were humbled for their iniustices.
Their soule did abhorre al meate: & they approched euen to the gates of death.
And they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation: and he deliuered them out of their necessities.
He sent his word, and healed them: and deliuered them out of their destructions.
Let the mercies of our Lord confesse to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.
And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise: and shew forth his workes in exulation.
They that goe downe into the sea in shippes, making trafike in the great waters.
They haue sene the workes of our Lord, and his meruelous thinges in the depth.
He sayd, and the blast of the storme stood: and the waues therof were exalted.
They ascend euen to the heauens, and they descend euen to the depthes: their soule pyned away in euils.
They were trubled, and were moued as a drunken man: and al their wisedom was deuoured.
And <na>(h)</na> they cried to our Lord when they were in tribulation, and he brought them out of their necessities.

notes.label: h
notes.text: As before in the 6, 13, and 19, verses,

verses.text: And he turned his storme into calme: and the waues therof were quiet.
And they reioyced because they were quiet: and he conducted them into the hauen of their wil.
Let <na>(i)</na> the mercies of our Lord confesse to him: and his meruelous workes to the children of men.

notes.label: i
notes.text: This verse also is foure times in this Psalme. v. 8. 15. 21. and 31. to admonish vs, that as there is one meanes to escape from al dangers by crying to God, as v. 6. 13. 19. and 28 : with mourning and penance : so there is one cause of praise and thankes for our deliuerie, which is Gods mercie and grace.

verses.text: And let them exalt him in the church of the people: and the chayre of the ancientes let them praise him.
<na>(k)</na> He turned <na>(l)</na> the riuers into a desert: and the issues of waters into drinesse.

notes.label: k
notes.text: God to shew sometimes his powre, also to benefite some, and to punish others, changeth the accustomed course of thinges, and states of men, at his diuine pleasure : as here the Royal prophet reciteth some examples. And some others are recorded in diuers times and places.

notes.label: l
notes.text: No doubt much change was made in the earth by Noes flood. And manie thincke that the land of Chanaan, was made more fruictful in the time of the Iewes inhabiting, and now is more barrane againe.

verses.text: The <na>(m)</na> fruiteful land into a salt ground, for the malice of them that inhabite it.

notes.label: m
notes.text: He alludeth to the countrie about Sodome, and Gomorre, which was most fruictful, and most pleasant, Gen. 13. v. 10, but shortly after vvas burnt vvith fire and brimston, Gen. 19, v. 24, subuerted, and turned into a dead and salt sea.

verses.text: He turned the desert into pooles of waters: and the land without water into issues of waters.
And he placed the hungrie there, and they built a citie of habitation.
And they sowed fildes, and planted vineyardes: and they made fruicte <na>(n)</na> of natiuitie.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Made abundance of fruict to grow.

verses.text: And he blessed them, and they were multiplied excedingly: and their beastes he lessened not.
And <na>(o)</na> they were made fewe: and were vexed by the tribulation of euiles, and with sorow.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Againe some countries punished for sinnes.

verses.text: Contempt was powred out vpon princes: and he made them wander where was no way, and not in the way.
And he <na>(p)</na> did helpe the poore out of pouertie: and made families as sheepe.

notes.label: p
notes.text: An other change in releeuing the poore being humbled.

verses.text: The iust shal see, and shal reioyce: & al iniquitie shal stoppe her mouth.
Who is wise and wil keepe these thinges? and wil vnderstand the mercies of our Lord?

chapters.summary: Againe the Psalmist inuiteth al men to render thankes to God for their deliuerie from dangers, or euils in general : 4. particularly from dangers in iorney, 10. in prison, or captiuitie, 17. in sicknes spiritual and corporal, 23. in nauigation, 33. describing the changeable course of thinges in this world, 38. especially of mens states, 42. for al which the iust wil praise God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: God's perpetual providence towards all men.

verses.text: A Canticle <na>(a)</na> of Psalme, to Dauid himselfe.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme was songue with instruments beginning the musike, and voices folowing.

verses.text: MY HART is readie ô God, my hart is readie: <cr>[1]</cr> I wil chaunte, and wil sing in my glorie. <na>[2]</na>

notes.text: The former part of this Psalme to the 7. verse, is the same in sense, and almost in wordes, with the latter part of the 56 from the 8. verse.

verses.text: Arise my glorie, arise psalter, and harpe: I wil arise early.
I <na>(b)</na> wil confesse to thee in peoples ô Lord: and I wil sing to thee <na>(c)</na> in the Nations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: King Dauid subdued not only some partes of Chanaan, not subiect to the Iewes before ( 2. Reg. 5. 1. Par. 11. ) but also brought the Philistims, Moabites, Ammonites, Idumeans, Amalechites, the kinges of Soba, Syria, and Emath, to pay tribute, 2. Reg. 8. 1. Par. 18.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yet al these victories and conquestes were but a figure of Christs powre and dominion in al nations. And therfore, the rest of this Psalme, by S. Augustin, and other fathers iudgement, was rather prophetically vttered by Dauid, in the person of Christ, and more perfectly performed by Christ in his Church, then historically suffered of Dauid himselfe.

verses.text: Because thy mercie is great aboue the heauens: and thy truth euen to the cloudes.
Be exalted aboue the heauens ô God, and thy glorie ouer al the earth: <cr>[1]</cr>
<na>[1]</na> that thy beloued may be deliuered. Saue with thy righthand; and heare me:

notes.text: The rest of this Psalme is the same with the latter part of the 59 from the 7. verse.

verses.text: God spake in his holie: I wil reioyce, and wil diuide Sichem; and I wil mesure the vale of tabernacles.
Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: and Ephraim the protection of my head.
Iuda is my king: Moab the potte of my hope. Vpon Idumea I wil extend my shoe: the strangers are made my freindes.
Who wil conduct me into a fensed citie? who wil conduct me into Idumea?
Wilt not thou ô God, which hast repelled vs, and wilt not thou goeforth ô God in our hoastes?
Geue vs helpe out of tribulation: because mans saluation is vayne.
In God we shal doe strength: and he wil bring our enemies to nothing.

chapters.summary: The royal prophet promiseth, 5. and rendereth praises to God, 7. for his deliuerie from trubles, and aduancement in the kingdom, 13. praying God stil to helpe mans infirmitie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
David singeth praises for benefits received.
The 8. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Psalme of Dauid.
O <na>(a)</na> God conceale not my prayse: because the mouth of the sinner, and the mouth of <na>(b)</na> the deceitful man is open vpon me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wordes of Christ.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Pharisees and Herodians ( Mat. 22. ) with their mouth acknowleged Christ a true speaker, and a teacher of the way of God in truth, therby to draw him into danger, and to sheede his bloud.

verses.text: They <na>(c)</na> haue spoken against me with deceitful tongue, and with wordes of hatred they haue compassed me: and they haue impugned me without cause.

notes.label: c
notes.text: At other times they accused him of great crimes, lastly of treason against Cæsar.

verses.text: For that they should loue me, they backbited me: but I prayed.
And they set against me euil thinges for good: and hatred for my loue.
Appoint <na>(d)</na> a sinner ouer him: and <na>(e)</na> let the diuel stand on his righthand.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A prediction that Iudas would not make recourse to anie good counseller, but complaine of his miserable tormented conscience to the wicked, who gaue him no comfort at al,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and so desparing, the diuel perswaded him to hang himselfe.

verses.text: When he is iudged, let him comeforth condemned: and let his prayer be turned into sinne.
Let his dayes be made fewe: and let an other take his <na>(f)</na> bishopricke. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: f
notes.text: The office of Apostleshippe.

verses.text: Let <na>(g)</na> his children be made orphans: and his wife a widow.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The poste title, or successors of wicked persecuters prosper not long in this world.

verses.text: Let his children be transported wandering, and let them begge: and let them be cast out of their habitations.
Let the vsurer search al his substance: and let strangers spoile his labours.
Let there be none to helpe him: neither let there be anie to haue pittie on his pupilles.
Let his children come to destruction: in <na>(h)</na> one generation let his name be cleane put out.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Arch heretikes that deuise newe opinions, are shortly forsaken, their followers stil coining new heresies of their owne, differing from their false masters.

verses.text: Let the iniquitie of his fathers returne to memorie in the sight of our Lord: and let not the sinne of his mother be blotted out.
Let them be before our Lord alwayes, and let the memorie of them perish out of the earth:
For that he remembred not to doe mercie.
And he persecuted the poore, and needie man, and the compunct in hart to kil him.

And he <na>(i)</na> loued cursing, and it shal come to him: and he would not blessing, and it shal be far from him. And he put on cursing as a garment, and it entred as water into his inner partes, and as oile in his bones.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Let them obserue this, that vse more swearing and blaspheming, then praying or meditating.

verses.text: Be it to him as a garment, wherwith he is couered: and as a girdle, wherwith he is alwayes girded.
This is the worke of them, that detract from me before our Lord: and that speake euils against my soule.
And thou Lord, Lord, doe with me for thy names sake: because thy mercie is swete.
Deliuer me because I am needie, and poore: and <na>(k)</na> my hart is trubled within me.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Christs soule was pensiue when he prayed in the garden, and he did workes of penance for our sinnes al his life.

verses.text: As a shadow when it declineth, am I taken away: and I am shaken as locustes.
My knees are weakened with fasting: and my flesh is changed by reason of oile.
And I am made a reproch to them: they saw me, and wagged their heades.
Helpe me ô Lord my God: <na>(l)</na> saue me according to thy mercie.

notes.label: l
notes.text: He prayed also for his resurrection, and glorification.

verses.text: And let them know that this is thy hand: and thou ô Lord hast done it.
They wil curse, and thou shalt blesse: let them that rise vp against me, be confounded: but thy seruant shal reioyce.
Let them that detract from me, be clothed with shame: and let them be couered with their confusion, as with a <na>(m)</na> duble patched cloke.

notes.label: m
notes.text: With al possible confusion.

verses.text: I wil confesse to our Lord excedingly with my mouth: and in the middes of manie I wil prayse him:
Because he hath stood on the righthand of the poore, that he might saue my soule from the persecutors.

chapters.summary: Christ ( by the mouth of Dauid ) requesteth of God to be iustly declared innocent, and his enimies punished, 6. particularly describing Iudas the traitors malice, 21. and his owne temporal afflictions, 26. prayeth, 30. and praiseth God for his deliuerie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ persecuted & his enemies punished.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A psalme of Dauid. OVR <na>(a)</na> Lord sayd <na>(b)</na> to my Lord: Sitte on my right hand: <na>(c)</na> til I make thine enemies, thy footestoole of thy feete. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: God the Father.

notes.label: b
notes.text: To God the Sonne, the Lord of Dauid; and of al mankind, yet the sonne of Dauid, according to his humanitie.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He limiteth not the time, but excludeth al time, wherin the enimie might imagine, that Christs kingdom should cease : signifying that Christ shal reigne, til al his enimies be subdued, much more afterwards in al eternitie.

verses.text: Our Lord wil sendforth the rod of thy strength <na>(d)</na> from Sion: rule thou in the middes of thine enemies.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Church of Christ beginning in Ierusalem on whitsunday, the fiftith day from his Resurrection, continueth euer more.

verses.text: With thee <na>(e)</na> the beginning in the day <na>(f)</na> of thy strength, in <na>(g)</na> the brightnes of holie thinges: from the wombe <na>(h)</na> before the day starre I begat thee.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Thou shalt haue principalitie,

notes.label: f
notes.text: in the day of thy powrful conquest, and rising from death.

notes.label: g
notes.text: in excellencie of al holie spiritual mysteries and graces :

notes.label: h
notes.text: because, I God the Father of my substance begate thee, God the Sonne in eternitie. The same which Micheas saith ( c. 5. v. 2. ) His comingforth from the beginning, from the dayes of eternitie.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(i)</na> sware, and it shal not repent him: Thou art a Priest <na>(k)</na> for euer according to <na>(l)</na> the order of Melchisedech. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: i
notes.text: God most firmly, and vnchangeably affirmed : that thou ( Christ our Messias ) art not only a King, but also a Priest :

notes.label: k
notes.text: not for a time, as Aaron was, but for euer,

notes.label: l
notes.text: neither of Aarons order, but according to the Order of Melchisedec.

verses.text: Our Lord on thy righthand, <na>(m)</na> hath broken kinges in the day of his wrath.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Kinges that sometimes persecute Christians, are subdued with other people to Christ.

verses.text: He <na>(n)</na> shal iudge in nations, he <na>(o)</na> shal fil ruines, he <na>(p)</na> shal crush the heads in the land of manie.

notes.label: n
notes.text: He shal iudge and punish the incredulous people,

notes.label: o
notes.text: make great slaghters amongst those that resist :

notes.label: p
notes.text: and bring princes with their populous kingdoms to nothing.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Of the torrent in the way he shal drinke: <na>(r)</na> therfore shal he exalt the head.

notes.label: q
notes.text: He shal in the meane time (and also his best seruants) suffer much tribulation in this life :

notes.label: r
notes.text: and for the same be highly exalted in life euerlasting.

chapters.summary: Christ rising and ascending into heauen sitteth on the right hand of God: 2. beginning in Ierusalem reigneth in the Church of the whole earth. 4. vseth the Priesthood of Melchisedechs order to the end of the world. 6. and shal iudge the world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's exaltation.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. I wil confesse to thee ô Lord with al my hart: in <na>(a)</na> the counsel of the iust, and <na>(b)</na> the congregation. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: I wil praise God both in secret for discharge of myn owne conscience;

notes.label: b
notes.text: and in publique for edification of others.
This Psalme in the Hebrew is composed with euerie verse and midle of verse, beginning with a distinct letter, in order of the Alphabet.

verses.text: The workes of our Lord are great: exquisite according <na>(c)</na> to al his willes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Gods wil is the whole cause of al his workes.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Confession and magnificence his worke: and his iustice continueth for euer and euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Euerie worke of his is praise worthie, and magnifical.

verses.text: He hath made <na>(e)</na> a memorie of his meruelous workes; merciful and pittiful Lord:

notes.label: e
notes.text: God hath leift one most special and beneficial memorie of al other benefites, his owne bodie and bloud, in memorie of his Passion, and our redemption,

verses.text: he hath geuen <na>(f)</na> meate to them that feare him. He wil be mindful for euer <na>(g)</na> of his testament:

notes.label: f
notes.text: the spiritual foode and sustinance of al the soules that rightly feare him.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Of his promise to conserue his Church perpetually.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> the force of his workes he wil shew forth to his people:

notes.label: h
notes.text: the powrable operation of his death, and of al his mysteries.

verses.text: To geue them the inheritance of the gentiles: the workes of his handes truth, and iudgement.
Al his commandmentes <na>(i)</na> are faithful: confirmed for euer and euer, made in truth and equitie.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Gods commandments do iustifie al that kepe them.

verses.text: He sent <na>(k)</na> redemption to his people: he commanded his testament for euer. Holie, and terrible is his name:

notes.label: k
notes.text: He also of his mercie redemed man; that he might be able to kepe his precepts.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> the feare of our Lord is the beginning of wisedom. Vnderstanding is good to al that doe it: his prayse remaineth for euer and euer.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Begingning with feare of God, bringeth at last by other degrees to true wisdom, which two are the first and last of the seuen giftes of the Holie Ghost.

chapters.summary: Praise of God for benefites, 4. especially for the B. Sacrament of the Eucharist, 6. with other graces imperted to the Catholique Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Graces given to the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Alleluia, <na>(a)</na> Of the returne of Aggeus, and Zacharie. <cr>[1]</cr> BLESSED is the man that feareth our Lord: <na>(b)</na> he shal haue great delight in his commandmentes. <na>[2]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Septuagint Interpreters added this mention of Aggeus and Zacharie, returning from captiuitie, to signifie that this Psalme was very proper, & meete to be comended to the people at that time, wherby they might lerne, that their sinnes were the cause of their captiuitie, and of al their miseries: and if they desired temporal, or spiritual prosperitie, they must obserue the meanes here prescribed to obtayne the same.

notes.label: b
notes.text: He that sincerly feareth God, wil take great delight in keping his commandments.
This Psalme is also composed by the Alphabet, as the next before.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> His seede shal be mightie in the earth: the generation of the righteous shal be blessed,

notes.label: c
notes.text: So doing he and his shal prosper.

verses.text: Glorie, and riches in his house: and <na>(d)</na> his iustice abideth for euer and euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The iust shal not only prosper in this world but also in the next.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Light is risen vp in darkenes to the righteous: he is merciful, and pitiful, and iust.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God wil also comfort the iust in tribulations.

verses.text: Acceptable is the man, that is merciful and lendeth, that <na>(f)</na> shal dispose his wordes in iudgement:

notes.label: f
notes.text: That shal geue discrete and wholsome counsel to the afflicted.

verses.text: Because he shal not be moued for euer.
The iust shal be in eternal memorie: he shal not feare at the hearing of euil.
His hart is readie to hope in our Lord, his hart is confirmed:
he shal not be moued til he looke ouer his enemies.
He distributed, he gaue to the poore: <na>(g)</na> his iustice remaineth for euer and euer <na>(h)</na> his horne shal be exalted in glorie. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: g
notes.text: Workes of mercie are also called iustice, because they concurre to mans iustification,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and to his saluation.

verses.text: The sinner shal see, and wil be angrie, he shal gnash his teeth and pine away: the desire of sinners shal perish.

chapters.summary: True happines consisteth in fearing God, keping his commandments, 5. and in doing workes of mercie. 10. The contrarie bringeth to miserie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The meanes to be happie.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. PRAYSE our Lord ye <na>(a)</na> children: praise ye the name of our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Al Gods seruants.

verses.text: Be the name of our Lord blessed, from henceforth now and for euer.
From the rising of the sunne vnto the going downe, the name of our Lord is laudable.
Our Lord is high aboue al nations, and his glorie aboue the heauens.
Who is as the Lord our God, that dwelleth on high,
and beholdeth the low thinges <na>(b)</na> in heauen and in earth?

notes.label: b
notes.text: In respect of God al creatures are low, though they be in heauen.

verses.text: Raising vp the needie from the earth, and lifting vp the poore out of the dung:
<na>(c)</na> To place him with princes, with the princes of his people.

notes.label: c
notes.text: See the example of Ioseph so aduanced

verses.text: Who maketh the <na>(d)</na> barren woman to dwel in a house, a ioyful mother of children.

notes.label: d
notes.text: of Sara, Rebecca, Rachael, and other wemen made fruitful.

chapters.summary: God is to be praised, who being hiegh regardeth, and prouideth for the needie in this world. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. IN the comming forth of Israel out of Ægypt, of the house of Iacob from <na>(a)</na> the barbarous people.

notes.label: a
notes.text: People of false religion counted barbarous, especially such as also persecute the true Religion; for otherwise the Ægyptians were both ciuil in maners, and lerned in manie sciences.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Iewrie was made his sanctification, Israel his dominion.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The people of Iewes were more notoriously renowmed in the world from the time of their deliuerie out of Ægypt, for the peculiar people, whom God sanctified, and in whom, as in his elected enheritance or dominion, he dwelled and reigned.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> sea saw, and <na>(d)</na> fled: Iordan <na>(e)</na> was turned backeward. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Psalmist writing in verse doth often describe thinges in poetical maner, but more truly then prophane poetes: for that in very dede, al creatures otherwise sensles, as the sea, do in a sorte feele the powre of their Creator, & obey his wil,

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVhen the Israelites went forth of Ægypt,

notes.label: e
notes.text: when they entred into Chanaan,

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> The mountaines leaped as rammes: and the litle hilles as the lambes of sheepe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Either there was an earthquake, or some other mouing of hilles not mentioned by Moyses, or els the Psalmist speaketh of the rockes of the torrentes which bowed, that the Israelites might rest in Ar, and lie in the borders of the Moabites, Num, 21, v, 15,

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> What ayleth thee ô sea that thou didst flee: and thou ô Iordan, that thou wast turned backeward?

notes.label: g
notes.text: By the figure Apostrophe he speaketh to the sea, riuer, and hilles : vsing also Prosopopœia: as if sensles thinges, vnderstood, and should answer.

verses.text: Ye mountaines leaped as rammes, and ye litle hilles as the lambes of shepe.
At the face of our Lord was the earth moued, at the face of the God of Iacob.
Who turned <na>(h)</na> the rocke into pooles of waters, and stonie hil into fountaines of waters.

notes.label: h
notes.text: An other miraculous benefite, that the rocke yelded them water in their necessitie.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> <sc>NOT TO VS O LORD, NOT</sc> TO VS: but to thy name geue the glorie.

notes.text: Here some Hebrewe Rabbins beginne an other Psalme, but by the coherence of the matter, S. Augustin proueth that it is but one Psalme, where is shewed that the true inuisible God is knowen by such workes as are here recited: and contrariwise, that the Gentils idoles are not goddes, because they are made of siluer, gold, or other matter, by mens handes, hauing resemblance of liuing thinges are altogether sensles.

verses.text: For <na>(i)</na> thy mercie, and <na>(k)</na> thy truth: lest at any time <na>(l)</na> the Gentiles say: Where is their God?

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thou didst al this ô God, of mere mercie towards thy people :

notes.label: k
notes.text: for thy truths sake, seing thou didst promise to protect them :

notes.label: l
notes.text: that the Gentiles should not take occasion to blaspheme.

verses.text: But our God is in heauen: he hath done al thinges whatsoeuer he would.
The idols of the gentiles are siluer, and gold, the workes of mens handes.
They haue mouth, and shal not speake: they haue eies, and shal not see.
They haue eares, and shal not heare: they haue nosthrels and shal not smel.
They haue handes, and shal not handle: they haue feete, and shal not walke: they shal not crie in their throte.
<na>(m)</na> Let them that make them become like to them: and al that haue confidence in them.

notes.label: m
notes.text: This is a iust prayer of the zelous, conforming their desires to Gods wil But if God geue idolaters grace to amend, then al the iust wil also reioice in their conuersion.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> The house of Israel hath hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Though manie Iewes fel to idolatrie, yet there alwayes remained so manie in Gods true seruice, that it might stil be truly saide : The house of Israel hath hoped in our Lord, as is here auerred.

verses.text: The house of Aaron hath hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
They that feare our Lord, haue hoped in our Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
Our Lord hath beene mindful of vs: and hath blessed vs: He hath blessed the house of Israel: he hath blessed the house of Aaron.
He hath blessed al, that feare our Lord, the litle with the great.
Our Lord adde vpon you: vpon you, & vpon your children.
Blessed be you of our Lord, which made heauen, and earth.
<na>(o)</na> The heauen of heauen is to our Lord: but <na>(p)</na> the earth he hath geuen to the children of men.

notes.label: o
notes.text: This in effect al worldlie politikes say in their hartes : as it were quitting their interest of heauen to God,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and contenting themselues with earthlie possessions.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> The dead shal not prayse thee ô Lord: nor al they, <na>(r)</na> that goe downe hel.

notes.label: q
notes.text: But when such prophane men are dead, they make no shew at al of praising God :

notes.label: r
notes.text: for parting from the earth, they descend into hel, and there eternally blaspheme God.

verses.text: But we <na>(s)</na> that liue, doe blesse our Lord, from this time, and for euer.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Contrariwise the iust, aspiring to heauen, which is the proper kingdom of God, & vsing this world as they ought to do, for a meanes to ascend into heauen, shal blesse and praise God for euermore.

chapters.summary: For the meruelous passage of Israel out of Ægypt, 3. the red sea, the riuer of Iordan, 7. and the hilles geuing them place, 8. the rockes yelding them water, 9. God, not themselues, is to be praised. 12. Idoles and Idolaters are vaine, and shal be confounded: 17. the faithful trust in God, 20. are blessed, and for euer praise God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The marvelous passage of Israel from Ægypt.
The 4. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. I <na>(a)</na> haue loued, because our Lord <na>(b)</na> wil heare the voice of my prayer.

notes.label: a
notes.text: I am induced to loue God,

notes.label: b
notes.text: because he alwayes heareth my prayers.

verses.text: Because he hath inclined his eare to me: and <na>(c)</na> in my daies I wil inuocate.

notes.label: c
notes.text: So long as I shal liue.

verses.text: The sorowes <na>(d)</na> of death haue compassed me: and <na>(e)</na> the perils of hel haue found me. <na>(f)</na> I haue found tribulation and sorow:

notes.label: d
notes.text: VVhen I erred like a stray sheepe from thee, the paines of death,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and the danger of hel-torments, both due for sinne, inuironed me, and I was not ware therof:

notes.label: f
notes.text: But by tribulation falling vpon me, I came to knowe my dangerous estate :

verses.text: and I <na>(g)</na> inuocated the name of our Lord. O Lord deliuer my soule:

notes.label: g
notes.text: turned to thee, and prayed as foloweth :

verses.text: our Lord is merciful, and iust, and our God doth mercie.
Our Lord kepeth litle ones: <na>(h)</na> I was humbled, and he hath deliuered me.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Afflicted with tribulations.

verses.text: Turne ô my soule into thy rest: because our Lord hath done good to thee.
Because he hath deliuered my soule from death: mine eies from teares, my feete from sliding.
I <na>(i)</na> wil please our Lord in the countrie of the liuing.

notes.label: i
notes.text: I wil endeuoure to please God, in the congregation of those that liue here in grace, and in heauen in glorie.

chapters.summary: The prayer of a iust man in tribulation, with confidence and gratitude towards God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer, with praise of God.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. I <na>(a)</na> beleued, <na>(b)</na> for which cause I spake: but I <na>(c)</na> was humbled excedingly. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: I beleued that God would helpe me:

notes.label: b
notes.text: therfore I freely professed that I trusted in him. For then in dede faith is perfect, when we confesse with mouth, that which we beleue in hart:

notes.label: c
notes.text: I was vehemently afflicted in tribulations.
This in the Hebrew is ioyned to the next Psalme before.

verses.text: I said <na>(d)</na> in mine excesse: Euerie man is a lyer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: In the middes of my great affliction I professed, that al mans helpe is vaine, false, deceipful, and defectiue, and therfore our trust must be in God only.

verses.text: What <na>(e)</na> shal I render to our Lord, for al thinges that he <na>(f)</na> hath rendred to me?

notes.label: e
notes.text: Considering that God hath not only geuen, and bestowed manie great benefites vpon me, and al mankind, but also hath rendered good for euil, mercie for our sinnes, we hauing rendered euil for good : what now shal I render, sayth a true penitent, for al that he hath thus rendered to me, deseruing so euil?

notes.label: f
notes.text: See previous note

verses.text: I <na>(g)</na> wil take the chalice of saluation: and <na>(h)</na> I wil inuocat the name of our Lord.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Seing I am not able to render anie thing worthie of Gods fauoure to me, yet I wil do that I can : I wil gratfully accept his great benefite. the cuppe of Christs passion, which he druunke for mankind,

notes.label: h
notes.text: and wil praise, and cal vpon his name.

verses.text: I wil <na>(i)</na> render my vowes to our Lord <na>(k)</na> before al his people:

notes.label: i
notes.text: I wil pay voluntarie vowes,

notes.label: k
notes.text: for Gods glorie, and edification of others.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> precious in the sight of our Lord is the death of his Sainctes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: yea I wil offer my life, and suffer death, when Gods glorie shal require it, in whose sight, the death of Sainctes is precious, and most highly esteemed.

verses.text: O Lord because <na>(m)</na> I am thy seruant: I am thy seruant, and <na>(n)</na> the sonne of thy handmaide. Thou hast <na>(o)</na> broken my bondes:

notes.label: m
notes.text: Alvvayes vnderstood, that such as suffer persecution, be in good state of their soules, the true seruantes of God,

notes.label: n
notes.text: the children of the Church his handmaide.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Deliuered me from captiuitie of sinne.

verses.text: I wil sacrifice to thee the hoast of praise, and I wil inuocate the name of our Lord.
I wil render my vowes to our Lord in the sight of al his people:
in the courtes of the house of our Lord, in the middes of <na>(p)</na> thee ô Ierusalem.

notes.label: p
notes.text: In the Church of the faithful.

chapters.summary: A iust man acknowledging that spiritual life beginneth by faith, and by publique profession therof, 4. gratfully accepteth of Christs Redemption, 5. dedicateth his life, and al he hath to Gods seruice. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Thanks-giving for our Redeemer.
The 5. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. PRAYSE our Lord <na>(a)</na> al ye Gentiles: prayse him <na>(b)</na> al ye peoples. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Not only some, but al nations of the Gentiles :

notes.label: b
notes.text: and al Ievves, (Christs Redemption being abundantly sufficient for al) are inuited to praise God.

verses.text: Because <na>(c)</na> his mercie is confirmed vpon vs: and his <na>(d)</na> truth remaineth for euer.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Because he hath multiplied his mercie to vs Gentiles, to vvhom he made no promise :

notes.label: d
notes.text: and most truly performed his promise made to the Ievves,

chapters.summary: Gods mercie is largely extended to al Gentiles by Christ, and his promise withal is performed to the Iewes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church of Christ in al nations.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord because he is <na>(a)</na> good: because <na>(b)</na> his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Let vs praise God, for his goodnes, in making vs of nothing, geuing vs manie benefites,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and remitting our sinnes.

verses.text: Let Israel <na>(c)</na> now say that he is good: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Let the Church of the new testament especially confesse his goodnes, which hath receiued more mercie and grace.

verses.text: Let the house of Aaron <na>(d)</na> now say: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Let al the Clergie praise God now in the time of more grace, and of greater spiritual functions.

verses.text: Let them now say <na>(e)</na> which feare our Lord: that his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Yea let the whole bodie of the Church, al that feare, and serue God praise his mercie.

verses.text: From <na>(f)</na> tribulation I inuocated our Lord: and our Lord heard me in largenes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: As wel spiritual as temporal.

verses.text: Our Lord is my helper: I wil not feare what man can doe to me.
Our Lord is my helper: and I wil looke ouer mine enemies.
It is good to hope in our Lord, rather then to hope in man.
It is good to hope in our Lord, rather then to hope in princes.
<na>(g)</na> Al nations haue compassed me: and in the name of our Lord am I <na>(h)</na> reuenged on them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Though innumerable oppose, and endeuour to hurt me (saith the Church, or anie iust person)

notes.label: h
notes.text: yet by Gods powre, not by myn owne, I am defended, and they punished, and so the iust hath the victorie, and triumpheth,

verses.text: Compassing they haue compassed me: and in the name of our Lord I was reuenged on them.
They compassed me as <na>(i)</na> bees, and were inflamed as <na>(k)</na> fyre in thornes: and in the name of our Lord I was reuenged on them.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In great trooper, and furie,

notes.label: k
notes.text: with sharpe though shorte force, and with special noise, to terrifie me, but in God I ouercame al.

verses.text: Being thrust <na>(l)</na> I was ouerturned to fal: and our Lord <na>(m)</na> receiued me.

notes.label: l
notes.text: I was sometimes by vehemencie of tentation, declining to sinne :

notes.label: m
notes.text: but Gods grace assisted and strengthned me.

verses.text: Our Lord is my strength, and my prayse: and he is made my saluation.
The voice of exultation, and of saluation in the tabernacles of the iust.
The right hand of our Lord hath wrought strength: the right hand of our Lord hath exalted me, <na>(n)</na> the right hand of our Lord hath wrought strength.

notes.label: n
notes.text: The same word [ right hand ] thrise mentioned, signifieth the B. Trinitie. Also [ Our Lord] signifying Christ in his humanitie the chief instrument of God, is here often repeted, to signifie the singular efficacie therof.

verses.text: I shal not die, but shal liue: and I wil tel the workes of our Lord.
Our Lord <na>(o)</na> chastising hath chastised me: and <na>(p)</na> to death he hath not deliuered me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God chastiseth his children,

notes.label: p
notes.text: because he would not that they should dye eternally. So he punisheth as a father, not as an enimie.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> Open ye the gates of iustice to me, being entred into them I wil confesse to our Lord:

notes.label: q
notes.text: The Prophet now speaketh in the person of iust soules, requiring spiritual doctrin, and foode,

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> this is the gate of our Lord, the iust shal enter into it.

notes.label: r
notes.text: and promising to serue God.

verses.text: I wil confesse to thee because thou hast heard me: and art become my saluation.
<na>(s)</na> The stone, which the builders reiected: the same is made into the head of the corner.

notes.label: s
notes.text: An euident prophecie of Christ vttered by the Royal Psalmist, and now confessed by euerie Christian, that our Sauiour reiected by the Iewes, is neuertheles the builder of his Church, by ioyning the two peoples of Iewes and Gentiles, as two walles into one house.

verses.text: This was done by our Lord: and it is meruelous in our eies.
This <na>(t)</na> is the day, which our Lord made: let vs reioice, and be glad therein.

notes.label: t
notes.text: God ordayned this acceptable time of grace. · Mat. 21. Luc. 10. Act. 4. Rom. 9. 1. Pet. 2.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> O Lord saue me, ô Lord geue good successe: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of our Lord. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: v
notes.text: The tongue of the Hebrew children, when Christ entered Ierusalem with palmes of triumph, and acclamations.

verses.text: <na>(w)</na> We haue blessed you of the house of our Lord:

notes.label: w
notes.text: The voice of Christ, and his Apostles and other Clergie blessing the people as they desire.

verses.text: Our Lord is God, and he hath geuen light to vs. Appoint a solemne day with <na>(x)</na> thicke bowes, euen to <na>(y)</na> the horne of the altar.

notes.label: x
notes.text: This was fulfilled when Christ was brought with bowes of palme, and other signes of triumph, from Bethania,

notes.label: y
notes.text: through the whole citie, euen into the Temple and vnto the Altar : Mat. 21.

verses.text: Thou art my God, and I wil confesse to thee: thou art my God, and I wil exalt thee. I wil confesse to thee because thou hast heard me: and art become my saluation.
<na>(z)</na> Confesse ye to our Lord because he is good: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: z
notes.text: Our first, chiefe, and final dutie is to praise God. v. 1. & vlt.

chapters.summary: Faithful people collected in the Church of Christ, exhorte each other to render thankes to God, for their deliuerie from spiritual and temporal tribulations. 16. The Laitie demand participation of Christs Mysteries, promising to serue him duly: 25. Which the Pastors freely impert, and together with the people, solemnely celebrate Gods praise. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ beneficial Mysteries are celebrated by his Church.
The 6. key.

verses.heading: Aleph. Doctrine.
verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Allelu ia. BLESSED <na>(a)</na> are <na>(b)</na> the immaculate in the way: which <na>(c)</na> walke in the law of our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Whereas al, without exception, desire to be happie and blessed ;

notes.label: b
notes.text: they are in dede happie (according to the perfectest happines of this life) that are immaculate :

notes.label: c
notes.text: and they are immaculate, that walke in the law of God. Where the holie Psalmist presupposeth, that some can and do kepe the law of God, and so are immaculate, and blessed in the way of this life.
This title was added by the Septuagint, to admonish vs that this Psalme conteyneth that singular maner of praising God, signified by the two Hebrew wordes Alleluia, as before. Psal 104.

verses.text: Blessed are they, <na>(d)</na> that search his testimonies: that <na>(e)</na> seeke after him with al their hart.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Those that are immaculate, are againe blessed, by searching Gods testimonies, that is, his law testifying that the good shal be rewarded, and the wicked punished, but searching these testimonies, whiles one is contaminate with sinnes against Gods law, maketh not blessed :

notes.label: e
notes.text: neither doth euerie superficial careles search bring this blessing, but searching with true affection of the hart.

verses.text: For <na>(f)</na> they that worke iniquitie, haue not walked in his <na>(g)</na> waies.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Contrariwise they that worke iniquitie are not blessed ;

notes.label: g
notes.text: because they haue not walked in the wayes of God, towitte, not kept his commamdments and law, which are the way to happines.

verses.text: Thou hast <na>(h)</na> very much commanded thy commandmentes to be kept.

notes.label: h
notes.text: For mans owne good, that he may come to true happines, God hath most seriously commanded vs to kepe his commandments, that is, to obserue his Law commanded by most souueraine diuine authoritie.

verses.text: Would God my waies <na>(i)</na> might be directed, to keepe thy <na>(k)</na> iustifications.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Therfore the faithful seruant of God, knowing his owne insufficiencie, desireth that God by his grace wil direct and streingthen him,

notes.label: k
notes.text: to kepe his law, called Iustifications, because therby man is made iust.

verses.text: Then shal I <na>(l)</na> not be confounded, when I shal looke throughly in al thy commandmentes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They shal be safe from eternal confusion, when they shal kepe not only part, but al thy commandments, because breach of anie bringeth confusion.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> I wil confesse to thee <na>(n)</na> in direction of hart: in that I haue lerned the <na>(o)</na> iudgements of thy iustice.

notes.label: m
notes.text: So shal I praise thee, and render thankes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: with sincere not fayned affection,

notes.label: o
notes.text: for this great benefite, that I haue lerned, that thy law is according to most iust iudgement.

verses.text: <na>(p)</na> I wil keepe thy iustifications: <na>(q)</na> forsake me not wholy.

notes.label: p
notes.text: I haue therfore a firme purpose, & do faithfully promise to kepe thy law, which maketh the keper therof iust.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Albeit thou suffer me sometimes to be in tribulation, or in tentation, yet forsake me not wholy. The Psalmist knew wel (saith S. Gregorie) that he might be profitably leist a while, who prayed, that he should not be wholy forsaken.

verses.heading: Beth. House.
verses.text: Wherein <na>(a)</na> doth a yongman correct his way? <na>(b)</na> in keeping thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In this second Octonarie, as also in al the rest, the Holie Ghost by the prophets penne teacheth the meanes how to come to perfection & happines. Here by way of interrogation, as it were demanding how a youngman, that is euerie man prone to worldlie pleasure, & slow in Gods seruice, shal beginne to correct his course ?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Wherto the same Holie Ghost answereth, that he must kepe Gods law, called here his wordes. For al the wordes which God vttereth, are lawes to his seruants.
sermones.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> With my whole hart I haue sought after thee: <na>(d)</na> repel me not from thy commandmentes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The Psalmist now speaketh in the person of perfect iust men, or of the whole Church in general. Whose common spirite seeketh God intyrely.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And considering that this perfect good wil is the gift of God, prayeth that he wil conserue the same, and not suffer it to be altered, or to erre from his commandments.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> In my hart I haue hid thy <na>[1]</na> wordes: that I may not sinne to thee.

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other sincere profession of a resolute good purpose not to sinne.
eloquia.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Blessed art thou o Lord: <na>(g)</na> teach me thy iustifications.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A gratful aspiration praising God.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Againe the iust prayeth to be more and more instructed in iustifications : that which S. Iohn exhorteth vnto : He that is iust, let him yet be iustified. Apoc. 22.

verses.text: In my lippes, I haue pronounced al the <na>(h)</na> iudgementes of thy mouth.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Gods law is also called his Iudgements, because sitting in iudgement he geueth sentence according to his Law.

verses.text: I am <na>(i)</na> delighted in the way of thy testimonies, as in al riches.

notes.label: i
notes.text: As the iust professeth by mouth, so he delighteth in hart.

verses.text: I <na>(k)</na> wil be exercised in thy commandmentes: and I wil consider thy waies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: practiseth in worke :

verses.text: I <na>(l)</na> wil meditate in thy iustifications: I wil not forget thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: and diligently meditateth Gods law.
sermones.

verses.heading: Gimel. Fulnes.
verses.text: Render <na>(a)</na> to thy seruant, <na>(b)</na> quicken me: <na>(c)</na> and I shal keepe thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: O Lord liberally geue me that which I here craue,

notes.label: b
notes.text: quicken me with spiritual life, thy grace.

notes.label: c
notes.text: so I shal kepe thy law, which otherwise I can not.
sermones.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Reuele mine eies: <na>(e)</na> and I shal consider the meruelous thinges of thy law.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Illuminate myn vnderstanding, by thy grace,

notes.label: e
notes.text: that I may be able to see the meruelous great and iust reasons of thy law, instructing al, threatning the peruerse, encoreging the wel disposed, punishing the wicked, rewarding the good, doing right to al.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> I am a seiourner in the land, <na>(g)</na> hide not thy commandmentes from me.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I that haue but a smal time in this world,

notes.label: g
notes.text: desire to be instructed in thy law, what is therein commanded.

verses.text: My soule hath coueted to desire thy iustifications, at al time.
Thou hast <na>(h)</na> rebuked the prowde: <na>(i)</na> cursed are they that decline from thy commandmentes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: I consider that thou o God, dost sharply reproue the prowd contemners of thy commandments :

notes.label: i
notes.text: laying curses vpon them for declining from thyn obedience.

verses.text: Take from me reproch, and contempt: because I haue sought after thy testimonies.
For <na>(k)</na> princes sate, and they spake against me: but <na>(l)</na> thy seruant was exercised in thy iustifications.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Though persecutors were very potent,

notes.label: l
notes.text: yet the faithful seruant of God perseuered in his seruice.

verses.text: For both <na>(m)</na> thy testimonies are my meditation: and <na>(n)</na> thy iustifications my counsel.

notes.label: m
notes.text: In time of persecution and tentation we must thincke and meditate, that Gods law testifieth eternal reward, or punishment,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and in our deliberation or consultation, we must consider that keping Gods law maketh iust : and consequently meriteth reward.

verses.heading: Daleth. Of Tables.
verses.text: My soule <na>(a)</na> hath cleaued to the pauement: <na>(b)</na> quicken me according to thy word.

notes.label: a
