notes.text: This also is vttered in the person of the iust, who is often brought to great distresse : as it were, euen nere to death,

notes.label: b
notes.text: in which case he confidently prayeth to be relieued, according to Gods word, law, and promise.

verses.text: I haue vttered my wayes, and thou hast heard me: teach me thy iustifications.
Instruct me the way of thy iustifications: and I shal be exercised in thy meruelous workes.
My soule <na>(c)</na> hath slumbered for tediousnes: <na>(d)</na> confirme me in thy wordes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Being in so great anxietie that my minde is almost distracted, or ouercome,

notes.label: d
notes.text: I cal to thee o God, that thou wilt conserue me, that I stil kepe thy law, vttered by thy wordes.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Remoue from me the way of iniquitie: and according to thy law, <na>(f)</na> haue mercie on me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Protect me that I fal not to iniquitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: And of thy mercie conserue me in state of grace.

verses.text: I haue chosen the way of truth: I haue not forgotten thy iudgements.
I haue cleaued to thy testimonies o Lord: <na>(g)</na> do not confound me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Suffer me not to be confounded.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> I ranne the way of thy commandments: <na>(i)</na> when thou didst dilate my hart.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Man is able, and doth runne in the right way of Gods commandments,

notes.label: i
notes.text: yet not of himselfe, but when God replenisheth his hart with grace.

verses.heading: He. This thing.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Set me a law o Lord the way of thy iustifications: <na>(b)</na> and I wil seeke after it alwayes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Impresse o God thy law in myn affection, make me to loue it, and to desire to be iustified,

notes.label: b
notes.text: so shal I hartely and alwayes seeke it.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Geue me vnderstanding, <na>(d)</na> and I wil search thy law: and I wil keepe it with my whole hart.

notes.label: c
notes.text: After thou hast geuen me a desire to kepe thy law, geue me also vnderstanding.

notes.label: d
notes.text: then shal I fruictfully search it. For this is the right order (as before in the first and second verses) first to loue Gods lawe, to be iustified, and to become immaculate ; and then to search to know the lawe, and so it is more easily lerned.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Conduct me into the path of thy commandments: <na>(f)</na> because I would it.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods grace first draweth and leadeth,

notes.label: f
notes.text: then freewil inflamed with desire effectually concurreth.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Incline my hart into thy testimonies: and <na>(h)</na> not into auarice.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Stil the Prophet inculcateth the necessitie of Gods grace, as wel to make vs desire that is good,

notes.label: h
notes.text: as to flee from euil.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Turne away mine eies that they see not vanitie: <na>(k)</na> in thy way quicken me.

notes.label: i
notes.text: It is necessarie also to pray that God wil take away occasions, which might moue to sinne :

notes.label: k
notes.text: and stil to grant his helping grace in progresse of vertue.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Establish thy <na>[1]</na> word to thy seruant, in thy feare.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Againe the iust prayeth for confirmation in grace, to be established in the feare of God.
eloquium.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> Take away my reproch, which I haue feared: <na>(n)</na> because thy iudgements are pleasant.

notes.label: m
notes.text: To be deliuered also from al the effectes of former sinnes,

notes.label: n
notes.text: for sinne is therfore reprochful and odious, because it is contrarie to Gods law, and true iudgements, which are most pleasant.

verses.text: Behold I haue coueted thy commandments: in thine equitie <na>(o)</na> quicken me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Being thus affected with desire to kepe the commandments, the soule prayeth to be stil quickned, more and more with good spirite, and so to perseuere to the end.

verses.heading: Vau. And.
verses.text: And <na>(a)</na> let thy mercie come vpon me o Lord: <na>(b)</na> thy saluation according to thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Againe considering that without Gods grace preuenting, man can not do anie good thing, the prophet reneweth his prayer, requesting Gods mercie,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and his helpe freely promised to al that aske it.
eloquium.

verses.text: And <na>(c)</na> I shal answer a word to them that vpbrayde me: <na>(d)</na> because I haue hoped in thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Wherwith being assisted and streingthned, he that before was weake wil boldly answer al calumniators ; that reprochfully say : God wil not helpe him :

notes.label: d
notes.text: that in dede he hath not in vaine trusted in Gods promised helpe.
sermonibus.

verses.text: And <na>(e)</na> take not away out of my mouth the word of truth vtterly: <na>(f)</na> because I haue much hoped in thy iudgementes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: He also prayeth, though he be sometimes fearful, that God wil not suffer him wholly to omitte manifest profession of faith and true religion,

notes.label: f
notes.text: seing by thy former grace I haue already reposed my trust in thy promises, made to them that are resolued to kepe thy law.

verses.text: And <na>(g)</na> I wil keepe thy law alwayes: for euer, and for euer and euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: For I do firmly purpose euer and alwayes to kepe thy law.

verses.text: And <na>(h)</na> I walked in largenesse: <na>(i)</na> because I haue sought after thy commandments.

notes.label: h
notes.text: In this I haue had great ioy and comforte of mind :

notes.label: i
notes.text: because I did in dede seeke after thy commandements, which is specially vttered (as also the three next verses) in the person of those, that are in trial of persecution for their faith :

verses.text: And <na>(k)</na> I spake of thy testimonies in the sight of kinges: and was not confounded.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Who boldly in time of persecution, euen before persecuting Kinges and Emperors, professe Christs true Religion. Verified in innumerable glorious Martyrs, yea also of the fraile sexe, in S Catharin, S. Cecilie, S. Lucie, S. Margaret, S. Wenefrede, S. Vrsula, and her felowes, and manie more, most constantly answering al wordes of reproch obiected, as if it were a base or contemtible thing to be Christians, to be Catholiques, to be Papistes No, al these and the like, are honorable and glorious titles ; importing the true seruice of Christ ; in vnitie of the Catholique Church ; and spiritual participation with the visible head therof, Christs Vicar in earth.

verses.text: And <na>(l)</na> I meditated in thy commandments, which I loued.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Such confessors as yet mortal, reioyce in that they haue meditated in Gods commandments, which they haue feruently loued.

verses.text: And <na>(m)</na> I haue lifted vp my handes to thy commandments, which I loued: and <na>(n)</na> I was exercised in thy iustifications.

notes.label: m
notes.text: Also shewed the same in external worke, not dissembling by silence, by word, nor fact.

notes.label: n
notes.text: euerie way exercising Gods law, which maketh the obseruers iust.

verses.heading: Zain. This.
verses.text: Be <na>(a)</na> mindeful of thy word to thy seruant, wherein thou hast geuen me hope.

notes.label: a
notes.text: That which God hath decreed, and promised, being in itselfe most certaine and assured, yet includeth the meanes, wherby it shal be put in execution : and therfore the iust, his elect, do pray for the performance of his wil.

verses.text: This hath comforted me in my humiliation: because <na>(b)</na> thy <na>[1]</na> word hath quickened me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Expectation of thy promise hath geuen me corege.
eloquium.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> prowd did vniustly exceedingly: <na>(d)</na> but I declined not from thy law.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Prowde contemners of Gods law, haue euerie way molested me, by detracting, deriding, calumniating, and violently persecuting me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al which I haue borne patiently, and not declined from thy law.

verses.text: I <na>(e)</na> haue bene mindful of thy iudgements from <na>(f)</na> euerlasting o Lord: <na>(g)</na> and was comforted.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I remembred and considered thy iust punishments inflicted vpon the impious,

notes.label: f
notes.text: euen from the beginning of the world (both vpon the diuels, and wicked men) and that thou wilt exercise the like hereafter,

notes.label: g
notes.text: which consideration of thy iustice comforted me.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Faynting possessed me, because of sinners forsaking thy law.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Otherwise if I had not sene thy iustice, my zele against contemners of thy law, would haue killed me.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Thy iustifications were songue by me, in the place of my peregrination.

notes.label: i
notes.text: In this place of my perigrination from heauen, I am comforted by remembring, celebrating, and singing thy iust commandments and lawe, which make thy seruant iust.

verses.text: I haue bene mindful in <na>(k)</na> the night of thy name o Lord: and haue kept thy law.

notes.label: k
notes.text: In persecution, and in al tribulation, I kept thy law because I would not dishonour thy name.

verses.text: This was done to me: <na>(l)</na> because I sought after thy iustifications.

notes.label: l
notes.text: And my tribulation especially fel vpon me, because I sought to be iustified by keping thy law.

verses.heading: Heth. Life.
verses.text: My <na>(a)</na> portion o Lord, I sayd to keepe thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Prophet procedeth speaking in the person of the iust tending to perfection, and saying : This is my happie choise, that I desire no other enheritance, nor possession, but to kepe Gods Law.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> I besought thy face, with al my hart: haue mercie on me according to thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: b
notes.text: And seeing this excedeth my proper streingth, I prayed God of his mercie to make me able to kepe it.
eloquium.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> thought vpon my wayes: and conuerted my feete vnto thy testimonies.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Pondering my former actions, I turned my pathes to obserue more perfectly the Law, which God hath testified to be the right way.

verses.text: I <na>(d)</na> am prepared, and am not trubled: to keepe thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: With prompnes of mind, and without hesitation I resolued to kepe the commandments.

verses.text: The <na>(e)</na> cordes of sinners haue wrapped me round about: and <na>(f)</na> I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The wicked laide cordes, nettes, or snares to intrappe, and hinder me,

notes.label: f
notes.text: but I kept thy law fresh in memorie.

verses.text: At <na>(g)</na> midnight I rose to confesse to thee; for the iudgements of thy iustification.

notes.label: g
notes.text: That this is not vnderstood only mystically in time of affliction, but also literally and prophetically, that some special seruantes of God, should obserue a godlie profession of praying at midnight, the word [I rose] maketh it probable. S. Paul & Silas, either of a holie custome, or at least vpon special occasion (and such occasions were to them, and others frequent) prayed, and praised God at midnight. And now in the Church of Christ some religions men pray, and praise God continually at midnight ; besides other houres, mentioned more distinctly v. 164.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> I am partaker of al that feare thee: and that keepe thy commandments.

notes.label: h
notes.text: A great benefite, and a singular consolation, that al true liuing members of Christ, are partakers of al the prayers, good workes, and merites, of the whole Church militant and triumphant. Which in our Crede is called, The Communion of Sainctes.

verses.text: The <na>(i)</na> earth o Lord is ful of thy mercie: <na>(k)</na> teach me thy iustifications.

notes.label: i
notes.text: So great is the mercie of God, extended, communicated, and multiplied in the whole earth :

notes.label: k
notes.text: Instruct me, and direct me therfore o God, that I may lerne and obserue thy law, and so be iustified, and made participant of so great mercie.

verses.heading: Teth. Good.
verses.text: Thou hast <na>(a)</na> done bountie with thy seruant o Lord: <na>(b)</na> according to thy word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dealt very bountifully

notes.label: b
notes.text: as thou didst promise.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Teach me goodnesse, <na>(d)</na> and discipline, and <na>(e)</na> knowledge: <na>(f)</na> because I haue beleued thy commandments.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He that hath bountifully receiued grace at Gods hand, prayeth for more grace, that he may be beneficial to others in releuing the needie ;

notes.label: d
notes.text: in instructing the ignorant,

notes.label: e
notes.text: in perswading to kepe the law of God :

notes.label: f
notes.text: because he hath lerned and beleueth the commandments, by which he is bond to loue, and haue care of his neighbour.

verses.text: Before I <na>(g)</na> was humbled I offended: <na>(h)</na> therfore haue I kept thy <na>[1]</na> word.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Before I was afflicted, I often fel into sinne :

notes.label: h
notes.text: but vexation gaue me vnderstanding, therfore now I kepe thy law.
eloquium.

verses.text: Thou art good: and in thy goodnesse teach me thy iustifications.
The iniquitie of <na>(i)</na> the prowd is multiplied vpon me: <na>(k)</na> but I in al my hart wil search thy commandments.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Contemners of thy law haue endeuored to intangle me,

notes.label: k
notes.text: but I persist in keping thy commandments. As before. v. 51. 61.

verses.text: Their hart is <na>(l)</na> crudded together as milke: <na>(m)</na> but I haue meditated thy law.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Though the wicked combine themselues together against me,

notes.label: m
notes.text: yet I consider, that it is necessarie to perseuer in thy law.

verses.text: It is good for me that thou hast humbled me: that I may learne thy iustifications.
The law of thy mouth is <na>(n)</na> good vnto me, aboue thousands of gold, and siluer.

notes.label: n
notes.text: A clere comparison, that it is better to kepe Gods law, which bringeth life euerlasting, then to haue al the riches & kingdoms of this world.

verses.heading: Iod. Beginning.
verses.text: Thy handes haue made me, and formed me: <na>(a)</na> geue me vnderstanding, and I wil learne thy commandmentes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God being our Creator, we may with confidence pray him to illuminate our mindes, that we may lerne what is his pleasure, and so endeuour to fulfil it.

verses.text: They that feare thee <na>(b)</na> shal see me, & shal reioyce: because I haue much hoped in thy wordes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Others that loue God wil be gladde to see me also serue him.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> I know o Lord that thy iudgements are equitie: and in thy truth thou hast humbled me. <na>(d)</na>

notes.label: c
notes.text: The iust being afflicted, and not seing the particular cause therof, yet knoweth and confesseth, that God doth it for most iust cause.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And therfore with patience prayeth for comforth, as foloweth :

verses.text: Let thy mercie be done to comfort me, according to thy <na>[1]</na> word vnto thy seruant.

notes.text: eloquium.

verses.text: Let thy commiserations come to me, and I <na>(e)</na> shal liue: because thy law is my meditation.

notes.label: e
notes.text: who am almost dead in tribulation.

verses.text: Let the prowde <na>(f)</na> be confounded, because they haue done vniustly toward me: but I wil be exercised in thy commandments.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The iust also prayeth that the wicked may be ashamed, and conuerted, for so the hebrew word here signifieth, though it is also lawful to desire tho iust punishment of obstinate sinners.

verses.text: Let them <na>(g)</na> be conuerted to me that feare thee: and that know thy testimonies.

notes.label: g
notes.text: He prayeth againe for conuersion of the wicked, and to haue peace with them.

verses.text: Let my hart be made immaculate in thy iustifications, that I be not confounded.

verses.heading: Caph. Hand, or Palme of the hand.
verses.text: My soule hath fainted for <na>(a)</na> thy saluation: and I haue much hoped in thy word.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Manie iust of the old testament most feruently desired the coming of Christ our Sauiour, as our Lord himselfe testifieth, Mat. 13. v. 17. And now the iust desire his coming in glorie, 2. Tim. 4. v. 8.

verses.text: Myne eies haue fayled for thy <na>[1]</na> word, saying: <na>(b)</na> When wilt thou comfort me?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Delayed hope afflicteth.
eloquium.

verses.text: Because I am made <na>(c)</na> as a bottel in the hoare frost: I haue not forgotten thy iustifications.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As a leather bottel made of a beasts skinne, congeled with the frost, and after partched in smoke, so is the bodie of the iust mortified by diuers sortes of afflictions, made a new bottel fitte to receiue new wine, that is, perfect doctrin of Christian life, as of fasting, and other austeritie, wherof our Sauiour speaketh, Mat. 9. v. 17.

verses.text: How manie are <na>(d)</na> the daies of thy seruant: when wilt thou doe iudgement on them that persecute me?

notes.label: d
notes.text: Such is mans infirmitie, yea of the iust, that he apprehendeth tribulations to be very long, and therfore desireth consummation ; and that without sinne, so he stil submitte his wil to Gods wil.

verses.text: The vniust haue told me <na>(e)</na> fables: but not as thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Friuolous idle tailes, which are not according to Gods law.

verses.text: Al thy commandmentes are truth: they haue vniustly persecuted me, helpe me.
They haue welnere <na>(f)</na> made an end of me in the earth: but I haue not forsaken thy commandments.

notes.label: f
notes.text: I was in great danger, but am not ouerthrowne.

verses.text: According to <na>(g)</na> thy mercie quicken me: and I shal keepe the testimonies of thy mouth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: And by thy merciful grace shal persist.

verses.heading: Lamed. Discipline.
verses.text: For euer Lord <na>(a)</na> thy word is permanent in heauen.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The praise of Gods workes ; which are firme and parmanent in the order, wherin he set them.

verses.text: Thy truth in generation and generation: thou hast founded the earth, and it is permanent.
By thy ordinance the day contineweth: because <na>(b)</na> al thinges serue thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al thinges of this world, man excepted, do Gods wil.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> But that thy law is my meditation: I had then <na>(d)</na> perhaps perished in my humiliation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Man, except he meditate Gods law, and therby be holden vp, is in danger,

notes.label: d
notes.text: perhaps in eternal tentation to perish eternally. For he can neuer rise out of mortal sinne, by his owne powre, and al should perish, if Gods mercie did not spare some, and geue them new effectual grace to repent.

verses.text: I wil not forget thy iustifications for euer: because in them thou hast quickned me.
I am thine, saue me: because <na>(e)</na> I haue sought out thy iustifications.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Alwayes vnderstood, that Gods grace preuented, els no man can seeke to obserue the commandments.

verses.text: Sinners haue expected me to destroy me: I vnderstood thy testimonies.
<na>(f)</na> Of al consummation I haue sene the end: <na>(g)</na> thy commandment is exceding large.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al worldlie thinges haue their consummation and end :

notes.label: g
notes.text: Gods commandment continueth euer. For we are perpetually bond, to loue and serue God : to loue our neighboures, yea and enimies. The reward also for keping Gods commandments, & punishment for breaking them, are eternal without end.

verses.heading: Mem. Of them.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> How haue I loued thy law ô Lord! al the day it is my meditation.

notes.label: a
notes.text: It is meruel to a perfect iust man, that he hath so much loued, and obserued Gods law. By acknowleging wherof, he yeldeth praise and thankes to God, whose gift it is.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Aboue mine enemies thou hast made me wise by thy commaundment: because it is to me for euer.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The fruictes of obseruing Gods law are manie and great. Amongst others, it maketh the obseruer, wiser then his enimies.

verses.text: Aboue <na>(c)</na> al that taught me haue I vnderstood: because thy testimonies are my meditation.

notes.label: c
notes.text: It maketh the obseruer wiser, then his temporal maisters, that taught him, towit, then those that teach wel, and do not performe the same.

verses.text: Aboue <na>(d)</na> ancientes haue I vnderstood: because I haue sought thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Yonger in yeares that kepe Gods commandments, are wiser then the more ancient that kepe them not.

verses.text: I haue staied my feete from al euil way: that I may keepe thy wordes.
I haue not declined from thy iudgements: because thou hast set me a law.
<na>(e)</na> How sweete are thy <na>[1]</na> wordes to my iawes, more then honie to my mouth!

notes.label: e
notes.text: An other fruict is the swetnes, which the iust feeleth in his owne soule.
eloquia.

verses.text: By thy commandments I haue vnderstood: therfore haue I <na>(f)</na> hated al the way of iniquitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: It brideth also iust hatred to sinne.

verses.heading: Nun. Euerlasting.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Thy word is a lampe to my feete, and a light to my pathes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The word or law of God declared by Prophets, Pastors, or other Preachers is the ordinarie meanes for others to lerne, how to direct their wayes, and actions.

verses.text: I <na>(b)</na> sware, and haue determined to keepe the iudgements of thy iustice.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Such profession Gods people made in the old law, in Circumcision, or at other times : Christians make it in Baptisme.

verses.text: I am <na>(c)</na> humbled exceedingly ô Lord: quicken me according to thy word.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al that wil liue godly in Christ Iesus, shal suffer persecution. 2. Tim. 3. v. 12.

verses.text: The <na>(d)</na> voluntaries of my mouth make acceptable ô Lord: and teach me thy iudgementes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Besides the commandments, the iust also offer voluntarie workes of supererogation, acceptable to God.

verses.text: My <na>(e)</na> soule is in my handes alwaies: and I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: By this Hebrew prouerb is signified, that a iust mans temporal life is in continual danger, as the thing that is in ones hand, is readie to be laide by, put out of his hand, or to be by and by disposed of, or may forthwith fal from his hand.

verses.text: Sinners laid a snare for me: and I haue not erred from thy commandments.
For inheritance I haue purchased thy testimonies for euer: because they are the ioy of my hart.
I haue inclined my hart to doe thy iustifications for euer, <na>(f)</na> for reward.

notes.label: f
notes.text: A most euident place, that the keping of Gods commandments merite reward, and are rightly obserued in respect of reward.

verses.heading: Samech. Helpe.
verses.text: I haue <na>(a)</na> hated the vniust: and I haue <na>(b)</na> loued thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Not anie mortal man is to be hated, in his person, but his iniquitie, by which he is an enimie to Gods law,

notes.label: b
notes.text: which euerie iust man loueth.

verses.text: Thou art my helper, and protectour: and vpon thy word I haue much hoped.
<na>(c)</na> Depart from me ye malignant: and I wil search the commandmentes of my God.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Whosoeuer wil seriously and securely search the law of God, must auoide the conuersation of euil men.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Recciue me according to thy <na>[1]</na> word, <na>(e)</na> and I shal liue: and <na>(f)</na> confound me not of myn expectation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A general and very fitte prayer, when we addict ourselues by a firme resolution to serue God, beseching him to receiue vs into his protection :

notes.label: e
notes.text: wherby spiritual life is conserued :

notes.label: f
notes.text: which we pray with great confidence, because he hath promised to heare those that seeke, aske, and knocke at the dore of his grace.
eloquium.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Helpe me, and I shal be saued: and I wil meditate in thy iustifications alwayes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: We must pray also that he suffer vs not to be confounded, or made frustrate of the reward which we expect ; for hope confoundeth not, if charitie be powred in our hartes, by the Holie Ghost, which is geuen vs. Rom. 5. v. 5.

verses.text: Thou hast <na>(h)</na> despised al that reuolt from thy iudgementes: <na>(i)</na> because their cogitation is vniust.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God reiecteth sinners :

notes.label: i
notes.text: so long as they thincke peruersly : that is, vntil by his grace, some returne to a better mind, which of themselues they can neuer do.

verses.text: Al the sinners of the earth I <na>(k)</na> haue reputed preuaricatours: therfore haue I loued thy testimonies.

notes.label: k
notes.text: As God accounteth of sinners, so the iust also estemeth them, conforming his iudgement to Gods.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Pearse my flesh with thy feare: for I am afrayd of thy iudgementes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Seruil feare is profitable as this place maketh euident : though perfect charitie afterwards succeding, expelleth that feare, and moueth to do wel for the loue of God, not for feare of punishment. 1. Ioan. 4.

verses.heading: Ain. A fountaine, or an eye.
verses.text: I <na>(a)</na> haue done iudgement and iustice: <na>(b)</na> deliuer me not to them that calumniate me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The iust againe in feruent zele, not arrogantly, but confidently professing his innocencie,

notes.label: b
notes.text: prayeth to be defended from calumniators.

verses.text: Recciue thy seruant <na>(c)</na> vnto good: let not the prowde calumniate me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Grant therfore o God the good, and lawful request which I demand.

verses.text: Mine eies haue fayled. <na>(d)</na> after thy saluation: and for the <na>[1]</na> word of thy iustice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: By long expecting to be deliuered, and saued from tribulation.
eloquium.

verses.text: Doe with thy seruant according to thy mercie: and teache me thy iustifications.
I am thy seruant: geue me vnderstanding, that I may know thy testimonies.
<na>(e)</na> It is time to doe ô Lord: <na>(f)</na> they haue dissipated thy law.

notes.label: e
notes.text: It is time, and hiegh time, saith feruent zele of the iust man, that God deliuer the innocent :

notes.label: f
notes.text: when the wicked haue not only persecuted the good, but haue also contemptuously made hauooke of Gods law, and true religion.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Therfore haue I loued thy commandementes, aboue gold and topazius:

notes.label: g
notes.text: For this zele of Gods law so despised, and disputed, the iust more and more loueth, that which the wicked so deadly hate.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Therfore was I directed to al thy commandementes: <na>(i)</na> al wicked way I haue hated.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Euen by the mortal hate of the wicked I saw, that Gods law is most excellent, and therfore addicted myselfe so much the more to loue it,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and to hate al wicked wayes.

verses.heading: Phe. Mouth.
verses.text: Thy <na>(a)</na> testimonies are meruelous: <na>(b)</na> therfore hath my soule searched them.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Gods meruelous powre and wisdom, testified by his workes and commandments,

notes.label: b
notes.text: worthely inuite iust soules, to meditate and contemplate the same.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> declaration of thy <na>[1]</na> wordes doth illuminate: and geueth vnderstanding to litle ones.

notes.label: c
notes.text: First entrance into knowlege of holie Scripture, illuminateth the vnderstanding of the humble, wherby they procede to know more.
sermonum.

verses.text: I <na>(d)</na> opened my mouth, and drew breath: because I desired thy commandments.

notes.label: d
notes.text: By this Metaphor, of gaping, or wide opening the mouth, and drawing breath, the Prophet describeth the great desire of the iust, to know and kepe Gods commandments.

verses.text: Looke vpon me, and haue mercie on me, according to <na>(e)</na> the iudgement of them that loue thy name.

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy accustomed equitie, in shewing mercie to them that loue thy name.

verses.text: Direct my steppes according to thy <na>[1]</na> word: and let not anie iniustice haue domination ouer me.

notes.text: eloquium.

verses.text: Redeme me from the calumnies of men: that I may kepe thy commondmentes.
Illuminate <na>(f)</na> thy face vpon thy seruant: and teach me thy iustifications.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Let thy diuine Maiestie looke vpon me with fauorable countenance.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Mine eies haue gushed forth issues of waters: because they haue not kept thy law.

notes.label: g
notes.text: True repentance consisteth not only in purpose to auoide sinne hereafter, which in dede is first required, but also in sorow and lamentation for sinnes past.

verses.heading: Sade. Iustice.
verses.text: Thou art iust ô Lord: and <na>(a)</na> thy iudgement is right.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God being essentially iust of himselfe, maketh men iust according to right iudgement, by geuing them grace of mercie, wherwith they cooperating, are iust by iustice in dede inherent in their soules, not by imputation only : for it were not right iudgement to impute, or account man iust, who is not so in dede.

verses.text: Thou hast commanded <na>(b)</na> iustice thy testimonies: and thy veritie excedingly.

notes.label: b
notes.text: The same is more confirmed, by these three synonyma, Iustice, Testimonies, Veritie, signifying the law of God, most earnestly commanded.

verses.text: My Zele hath made me to pine away: because mine enimies haue forgotten thy wordes.
Thy <na>[1]</na> word is <na>(c)</na> fired excedingly: and thy seruant hath loued it.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Gods law is as pure as anie thing purged by fire.
eloquia.

verses.text: I am <na>(d)</na> a yongman, and contemned: I <na>(e)</na> haue not forgotten thy iustifications.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A iust man is often iudged ignorant, immature, vnexperienced, by the worldlie wise ;

notes.label: e
notes.text: but in dede is wise, in that he forgetteth not to kepe the law, which maketh him iust.

verses.text: Thy iustice, is iustice for euer: and thy law is veritie.
Tribulation, and distresse haue found me: thy commandments are my meditation.
Thy testimonies are equitie for euer <na>(f)</na> geue me vnderstanding, and I shal liue.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Hauing professed the necessitie of perfect iustice, he concludeth this Octonarie, praying to be illuminated in his vnderstanding, that so he may attaine iustice, and liue therby.

verses.heading: Coph. Vocation.
verses.text: I <na>(a)</na> haue cried in my whole hart, heare me ô Lord: I wil seeke after thy iustifications.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Most precious and feruent inuocation of God for his grace, is necessarie, to the fulfilling of his law.

verses.text: I haue cried to thee, saue me: that I may keepe thy commandmentes.
I haue preuented in <na>(b)</na> maturitie, and <na>(c)</na> haue cried: because I hoped much in thy wordes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I haue preuented the mature, and ordinarie time of the night, and haue prayed

notes.label: c
notes.text: very attentiuely.

verses.text: Mine eies <na>(d)</na> haue preuented early vnto thee: that I might meditate thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Againe in the morning I haue preuented the accustomed time of prayer.
eloquia.

verses.text: Heare my voice according to thy mercie ô Lord: and according to <na>(e)</na> thy iudgement quicken me.

notes.label: e
notes.text: According to thy accustomed maner of shewing mercie, shew it me, that therby I may liue.

verses.text: They that persecute me haue approched to iniquitie: but from thy law they are made far of.
Thou art <na>(f)</na> nigh ô Lord: and al thy wayes are truth.

notes.label: f
notes.text: God is alwayes readie to heare al that sincerly inuocate him.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> From the beginning I knewe of thy testimonies: that thou hast founded them for euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Gods law is the same in substance from the beginning of the world, and wil be for euer.

verses.heading: Res. Head.
verses.text: See <na>(a)</na> my humiliation, and deliuer me: because I haue not forgotten thy law.

notes.label: a
notes.text: An other prayer of the iust in affliction.

verses.text: Iudge my iudgement, & redeme me: for thy <na>[1]</na> word <na>(b)</na> quicken thou me.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Conserue me in thy grace.
eloquium.

verses.text: Saluation is far from sinners: because they haue not sought after thy iustifications.
Thy mercies are manie ô Lord: <na>(c)</na> according to thy iudgement quicken me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As before v. 149.

verses.text: There are manie that persecute me, and afflict me: I haue not declined from thy testimonies.
I saw the preuaricatours, and I pyned away: because they kept not thy <na>[1]</na> wordes.

notes.text: eloquia.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> See that I haue loued thy commandmentes ô Lord: in thy mercie quicken me.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Sincere profession of innocencie is no arrogancy.

verses.text: The <na>(e)</na> beginning of thy wordes is truth: <na>(f)</na> al the iudgementes of thy iustice are for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Gods essencial veritie is the beginning from whence, as from the fountaine al other truthes are deriued :

notes.label: f
notes.text: And al commandments proceding from this first truth, are for euer immutable.

verses.heading: Sin. Tooth.
verses.text: Princes haue persecuted me <na>(a)</na> without cause: and my <na>(b)</na> hart hath bene afrayd of thy wordes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Potent wicked men persecute the godlie without cause, that is, without anie iust reason mouing them ; & without the effect intended by them, which is to drawe Gods seruants from truth, and equitie ;

notes.label: b
notes.text: whose hart being possessed with the true feare of God, they persist in keping Gods commandments.

verses.text: I <na>(c)</na> wil reioyce at thy <na>[1]</na> wordes: as he that findeth manie spoyles.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Yea they also reioyce in keping the commandments, with such difficultie, as those doe, that gaining the victorie ouer their enimies, carie away great and rich spoyles.
eloquia.

verses.text: I haue hated iniquitie, and abhorred it: but thy law I haue loued.
<na>(d)</na> Seuentimes in the day. I haue sayd praise to thee, for the iudgements of thy iustice.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Euerie day the iust praise God often, signified by the number of seuen. From hence also the Church of Christ tooke example to institute the seuen Canonical Houres, which is the ordinarie Ecclesiastical Office ; consisting, as S. Isidorus, and manie other Fathers testifie, of Hymnes, Psalmes, Canticles, Antiphones, Lessons, Responsories, & other Prayers & Praises, distributed into distinct times, beginning in the night, wherof that part is called the Nocturne (one or three according to the diuersitie of the Office) and perteineth to one or more of the foure Vigiles, into which souldiars diuide the whole night. Whereto also the Laudes are added. Then Prime, in the morning. Afterwards, the Third houre, Sixt, Ninth ; and in the euening, Euensongue, and Compline. Against which most ancient and religious Constitution, especially against the part called Vigiles, or Nocturnes, certaine Heretikes repined, and calumniated the Churches custome, as superfluous and vnfructful to spiritual worke, violating of Gods ordinance, who made the night for rest, and the day for laboure. For which cause they were called Nyctazontes, Somnicolosi, Drowsy heretikes, As the same S. Isidorus testifieth li. 1. c. 22. de Offic. Eccles. S. Ierom Epist. ad Riparium, noteth the same heresie in Vigilantius, calling him Dormitantius, because he reprehended holie Vigiles, as if it were better to sleepe, then wake in time of Diuine seruice. Wiclif also raised vp the same heresie, as witnesseth Thomas Waldensis. To. 3. Tit. 3. c. 21. Lastly Luther and al his broode. But the holie obseruation of Canonical Houres is proued, by manie ancient Fathers to be altogether agreable to the holie Scriptures, both of the old and new Testament. So S. Beda. in 18. Luc. & li. 4. c. 7. Hist. Angl. S. Gregorie the Great li. 3. Dialogi. c. 14. S. Augustin (Ser. 55. de temp.) exhorting the people to rise early to the Vigiles (or Nocturnes) and in aniewise to come to the Third houre, Sixt, and Ninth. Let none (saith he) withdraw himselfe from the holie worke, but whom either sicknes, or publique vtilitie, or perhaps some great necessitie holdeth backe. S. Ierom. Epist. 22. ad Eustoch. & in Epitaph. Paule. c. 10. maketh expresse mention of the Third houre. Sixt, Ninth, Morning, and Euening ; also of Midnight, adding that no Religious is ignorant that sometimes they must rise to Diuine Seruice, twise, yea thrise in the night. S. Basil, in Regulis fusius disput. ad Interrog 37. & de Instit. Monachorum. first. sheweth this ordinance to be agreable to the holie Scriptures, and namely to this place of the Psalmist. S. Cyprian in fine exposit. Orat. Domini. affirmeth that besides the three houres in which Daniel and his felowes prayed, the Church of Christ hath added more. And (as manie suppose) S. Clement li. 8. Constitut. Apostol c. 40. sheweth the sette Houres of prayers, and the reasons therof : Make your prayers Early in the morning, at the Third houre ; Sixt, Ninth ; Euening ; and at the Time of cocke crowing. Early geuing thankes because our Lord hath illuminated vs, the night being passed, & the day coming in ; the Third, because that houre our Lord receiued Pilats sentence ; the Sixt houre, because then he was Crucified ; the Ninth, because al thinges were moued, when our Lord was crucified, abhorring the audacitie of the wicked, & not bearing the ignominie of our Lord ; at Euening, geuing thankes, for that God hath geuen vs the night for rest of dayes labours : at the Cocke crowing, because at that time the coming of the day is denounced, to exercise the workes of light, thus S. Clement. Touching the distinct and sette times of publique prayer, the continual practise by tradition teacheth, that Mattines with Laudes were said in the night, about the first Cockcrowing. Prime early in the morning. The other partes in the day time : At euening Euensongue, and last of al Compline. And touching the place : If for the infidels (saith the same holie Father) there be not accesse to the Church, the Bishop must geather the Assemblie at home, that the godlie may not enter into the Church of the wicked : for the place doth not sanctifie man, but man the place. Wherfore if the wicked occupie the place, that place is to be shunned, because it is prophaned by them : for as Priestes do sanctifie holie thinges, so the wicked do contaminate them. If neither at home, nor in the Church Assemblies can be celebrated, let euerie one by himselfe sing, read, pray, or twoo or three be geathered together. For where twoo or three are geathered in my name (saith Christ) there am I, in the middes of them. Let not the godlie pray with an heretike, no not at home. For what societie is there of light with darknes ?

verses.text: There is <na>(e)</na> much peace to them that loue thy law: & <na>(f)</na> there is no scandal to them.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Amongst other benefites, it is a special commoditie, that those which perfectly loue Gods law, haue alwayes peace in their owne conscience :

notes.label: f
notes.text: and are neuer scandalized, that is, do not fal nor committe sinne, by anie occasion whatsoeuer geuen them by others. For it is a general assured doctrine, that the perfect are not scandalized, because they are constant in vertue, and not moued by anie example, perswasion, prouocation, or other meanes to offend God : but only the weake and vnperfect are moued, and drawne to sinne by occasions geuen them, who otherwise would not haue sinned. Neither is he excused that falleth by such occasions, because he ought to be constant.

verses.text: I expected thy saluation ô Lord: and haue loued thy commandmentes.
My soule hath kept thy testimonies: and <na>(g)</na> hath loued them excedindgly.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Not of seruile feare, but of true charitie & filial loue.

verses.text: I haue kept thy commandmentes, and thy testimonies: <na>(h)</na> because al my waies are in thy sight.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Because whatsoeuer I do is in thy sight, whom i wil in no case offend.

verses.heading: Tau. Signe.
verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Let my petition approch in thy sight ô Lord: according to thy word giue me <na>(b)</na> vnderstanding.

notes.label: a
notes.text: In this last Octonarie, and conclusion of this Psalme, the faithful seruant of God prayeth,

notes.label: b
notes.text: not for humane knowlege, or other temporal thinges, but to vnderstand Gods law.

verses.text: Let my request enter in thy sight: <na>(c)</na> according to thy word <na>(d)</na> deliuer me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Thou that hast promised to heare al that inuocate thee,

notes.label: d
notes.text: voutsaffe to deliuer me in time of tribulations and tentations.

verses.text: My lippes shal vtter an hymne, when thou shalt teach me thy iustifications.
My tongue shal pronounce thy <na>[1]</na> word: <na>(e)</na> because al thy commandmentes are equitie.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God geuing grace, it behoueth his seruants thankefully to serue, and praise him.
Why the 15 Psalms following are called Gradual Canticles. Here follow in order fifteen Psalms entitle Gradual Canticles.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Let thy hand be to saue me: because I haue chosen thy commandmentes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Though man be indued with grace, yet he nedeth more grace, that by Gods hand and powre, not by his owne, he may resist tentations.

verses.text: I haue coueted thy saluation ô Lord: and thy law is my meditation.
<na>(g)</na> My soule shal liue, and shal prayse thee: and thy iudgementes shal helpe me.

notes.label: g
notes.text: By this assistance of grace, the soule continueth in spiritual life, and praiseth God.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> I haue strayed, as a sheepe, that is lost: <na>(i)</na> seeke thy seruant, <na>(k)</na> because I haue not forgotten thy commandmentes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Al mankind, and vniuersally euerie one hath bene as a lost sheepe,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and Christ came into this world to seeke and saue al :

notes.label: k
notes.text: but effectually findeth and saueth those only, that forgete not to kepe his commandments.

chapters.summary: A perpetual recommendation of the singular excellencie, absolute necessitie, and eternal heauenlie profite of Gods law : with frequent aspirations to perfection, hatred of sinne, loue of vertue, and feruent desire to rest in God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Perfect justice is in keeping God's law.
The 7. key.

articles.title: GENERAL ANNOTATIONS UPON THIS CXVIII. PSALM.
articles.text:
As this Psalm is the longest in the whole Psalter, so it seemeth to the ancient Fathers most profound in sense. And so much the harder to be understood, because also the very hardness <mn>[1]</mn> thereof lieth hidden, which in diverse other Psalms and parts of holy Scripture, easily appeareth to the reader. But here the words being clear, and the sense also plain and easy in some points of doctrine, yet the more diligence is employed, the more difficulty is found in searching the whole sense and meaning of every word and sentence, with the manner observed in composing it, and the frequent repetition of the same or like words. All which maturely considered caused that great Clerk, and light of the Church Saint Augustin, to omit this Psalm, when he explicated all the <mn>[2]</mn> rest. And when at last he added also this, he wittingly omitted one special difficulty, which he doubted not to be contained in the manner of composing it, not only by order of the Hebrew Alphabet, as diverse more Psalms, and some other parts of holy Scripture, but more artificially than any other, the first eight verses all beginning with the first letter Aleph; the next eight, with the second letter Beth: and so to the last of the two and twenty letters. Of which omission he yieldeth this only reason, because he found nothing (as he humbly affirmeth) that might properly pertain thereunto. Confessing also expressly, that whensoever he applied his cogitations to expound the text it-self, it always exceeded his hability. But finally to satisfy the often and earnest request of his brethren and friends, trusting (as always) in God's special help, he largely expoundeth it, in thirty two distinct Sermons. <mn>[3]</mn>

S. Ambrose, also moved with like piety, made two and twenty Sermons in exposition of this <mn>[4]</mn> Psalm. Affirming in his Prologue, that amongst other Psalms, especially this sheweth how great a master King David was of moral good life. For all Moral doctrine, being of his own nature sweet, yet most delighteth the ears, and gently toucheth the mind, being uttered, as here it is, with pleasantness of verse, and sweetness of song. Again whereas this Royal Prophet in many places of this book poureth out sentences of moral Psalms or songs, as bright stars, that shine and <mn>[5]</mn> glister to all the world, here most excellently he produceth a more singular mirror, as the sun, of full light, burning with meridian heat. And for the profit of all, the better to draw our <mn>[6]</mn> attentions, to learn that we may, though we cannot attain to all that we would, he disposed this Psalm through all the Alphabet: that as children beginning with the first letters, make entrance to further knowledge; so by the same beginnings we should lay the first foundation, and thereupon proceed in our spiritual building, towards perfection in good life, the true service of God. Which is yet further insinuated (as the same Doctor teacheth) by the eight verses continually beginning with the same letter, and so other eight in order through the whole Alphabet, to signify that <mn>[7]</mn> after seven days travail in this temporal life, we may come to that unity, which we expected in the eighth day of resurrection, when we hope to rise revived in our Lord Jesus, in newness of eternal life.

Likewise Saint Basil in the Argument of this Psalm admonisheth, that whereas holy David, <mn>◦</mn> according to diverse states, which he passed, writ diverse Psalms: as when he fled from his enemies, when he lamented his distresses, mourned in pensiveness, enjoyed peace and comfort, ran a right course of virtue, fell from God by sin, & again returning observed God's laws; in this one Psalm he comprehendeth all his prayers made to God at sundry times, & here proposeth the same, a certain profitable moral doctrine, to all sorts and states of men. Neither doth he pretermit doctrinal points of faith, but interposeth them also with moral documents, in such sort, that this one Psalm may suffice to teach the well disposed, how to attain to perfection in virtue, to stir up the slothful unto diligent care of their souls, to recreate the desolate with spiritual consolations, & briefly it administereth all kind of medicine to the diverse passions of mortal men.

For the like judgements of other Fathers we remit the learned reader, to Saint Hilary, <mn>[8]</mn> Theodoret, Prosper, Arnobius, Cassiodorus, Beda, Euthymius, and others, but cannot well omit a brief instruction of S. Jerome. Who in his Epistle to Paula Urbica: not only sheweth the interpretation of the two and twenty letters, but also explicateth their sense in this place, by connecting them into certain short sentences, in this manner: <mn>[9]</mn>



Which is the first connection, signifying that the doctrine of the house, that is the Church of God, is found in the fullness of divine books.
The second connection is:



For what other life can there be without knowledge of Scriptures? Whereby also Christ is known, who is the life of them that believe in him.
The third connection is: <mn>◦</mn>



Albeit we now could know all things which are written, yet we know but in part, and in part we prophesy: for we see now by a glass, in a dark sort, but when we shall be worthy to be with <mn>[10]</mn> Christ, and shall be like to Angels, then doctrine of books shall cease, & then we shall see face to face the Good Beginning, even as he is. <mn>[11]</mn>

The fourth connection is: <mn>◦</mn>



The hands are understood in work, heart and discipline are understood in sense or meaning, because we cannot rightly do any thing, unless we first know what things are to be done. The fifth connection is:



This needeth not explication, for it is manifest as the light, that from Scriptures are eternal helps. The sixth connection is:



According to that which we have expounded in the fourth connection: that deeds & intention must concur.
The seventh connection which is last, in which number of seven is also mystical understanding:



Distinct voice is produced by the teeth, & in these signs we come to the Head of all which is Christ, by whom we have access to the everlasting Kingdom.
Or thus (not transposing the words) By vocation of Christ the Head, through distinct voice of signs (for words are signs shewing the mind) we are conducted to the eternal Kingdom, the happiness which all men desire.
What I pray thee (saith this holy Doctor) is more sacred than this mystery, what more pleasant than this delight? What meat, & what honey are sweeter, than to know God's wisdom; to enter into his secret closet; to behold the sense of our Creator; and to teach the words of thy Lord God, full of spiritual wisdom, which are derided by the wise of this world.
We must also advertise the reader of the like discourses of ancient Fathers (over long to be here recited) concerning the manifold high praises of God's Law, contained in this Psalm, with <mn>[12]</mn> frequent repetition of certain Synonyma words signifying the same thing, in all fourteen, to wit: The Law of God, his Ways, Testimonies, Commandments, Precepts, Statutes, Justifications, <mn>[13]</mn> Judgements, Justice, Equity, Verity, Words, Speeches, & Sermons: of which there is commonly one, in every verse, & sometimes two or three in the same verse. But our English tongue hardly sufficing rightly, to distinguish the three last, which in Latin are Verba, Eloquia, Sermones, we translate WORDS only, adding in the margin, Eloquia, and Sermones, when they occur.

Leaving therefore larger commentaries to others; we shall prosecute our wonted manner of brief glosses. Only here premonishing the diligent readers, especially Clergyman (ourselves and our brethren) who every day sing or read this whole Psalm in the Canonical hours, to observe two particular points of Christian doctrine, evidently proved by many places of this Psalm. The one against the Pelagians' heresy, denying the necessity of God's special grace in meritorious works. For the Psalmist often here inculcateth man's insufficiency, that of himself, and by natural <mn>[14]</mn> forces, he cannot keep the commandments of God, but needeth always the particular grace of God, as well to believe in him, to repent for sins, and to begin good works; as to proceed, and persevere in good state to the end. The other against the heresy of our time, denying merit by grace & freewill. For here it is also manifest, that God's grace maketh man able, to keep his <mn>[15]</mn> commandments, and by keeping them to become just in this life, and so to merit eternal glory. Sundry other principal Articles of Christian Catholic Religion are likewise comprised in this one Psalm: but especially Moral doctrine.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. WHEN I was in tribulation I cried to our Lord: and <na>(a)</na> he heard me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Former experience of Gods mercie in hearing the prayers of those that inuocated him, geueth hope that he wil heare in like case.

verses.text: O Lord deliuer my soule from <na>(b)</na> vniust lippes, and from a deceiptful tongue.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Nothing is more dangerous then vntrue and deceiptful tongues, nothing more damage then to diminish, and detract from the good fame of the iust : and therfore this is a most necessarie prayer, that God wil deliuer vs, from the wicked tongues of Turkes, Heretikes, and other wicked men.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> What may be geuen thee, or what may be added vnto thee, to a deceiptful tongue?

notes.label: c
notes.text: What punishment is great ynough for wicked tongues?

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> The sharpe arrowes of the mightie, with coales of desolation.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Surely the malice of wicked tongues deserueth sharpest punishments to be afflicted by strong handes.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Woe is to me, that my seiourning is prolonged: I haue dwelte with the <na>(f)</na> inhabitantes of Cedar:

notes.label: e
notes.text: Iewes lamented their long absence from the holie land, especially from Ierusalem, and the Temple. Christians mourne for their restraint from Gods Seruice, and long perigrination from heauen.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Of Cedar the sonne of Ismael, came Mahomet, the Turkes false prophet, whose tyrannie is great and long. The name Cedar is interpreted, blackenes, and obscuritie, which signifieth darkenes of error, and sinne.

verses.text: My soule hath bene long a seiourner.
With them, that hated peace, I was peaceable: when I spake to them, they impugned me <na>(g)</na> without cause.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The wicked afflict those that geue no cause of offence.

chapters.summary: The Iewes in captiuitie of Babylon, Christians in persecution, or other great tribulation, pray with confidence to be deliuered from danger, and slander of wicked tongues, 5. lamenting their long indurance. <na>[1]</na>

articles.title: A BRIEF NOTE CONCERNING the Gradual Psalms.
articles.text: Here follow in order fifteen Psalms entitle Gradual Canticles. The Hebrew word Mahaloth <mn>[1]</mn> signifieth Steps, or Ascensions. The reason whereof Aadias, and some other Rabbins yield, for that they were sung with highest elevated notes, that can be in Music. The Talmud saith they are so called, because they were sung in the fifteen steps going up into the Temple. But S. Augustin, S. Basil, and other Christian Fathers expound them according to the history, and immediate prophetical sense, of the delivery of the Jews from captivity of Babylon, ascending into <mn>[2]</mn> Jerusalem: which is so situated on mountains, that the way from all parts was by ascending unto it. According to the Mystical sense, of ascending spiritually by virtues to perfection, and to <mn>[3]</mn> eternal felicity. For the way tending to virtue (saith S. Basil) is like to certain steps (or degrees) by little and little bringing the man that loveth wisdom unto heaven. These Canticles therefore are prayers, mixed with consolations, for the joyful delivery of God's people, from that great captivity in Babylon, which the Psalmist King David saw in prophetical spirit, and which his posterity felt, and sometime endured. Which again as a figure signifieth the return and ascending of mankind from sin to grace, and from the miserable state of this world into heaven. Whereupon S. Augustine interpreteth this prophecy of the ascension, or elevation of the heart, from the vale of tears. In <mn>[4]</mn> the mean time, whiles we are in this world, these Psalms are consolatory prayers, and prophetical assurance, that God's people, Catholic Christians, shall be delivered from the thraldom and persecution of Pagans, Turks, and Heretics. As partly we see by the delivery from the Roman persecuting Emperors, from the Vandals, Goths, and Huns: & therefore with assured confidence we hope and expect the like delivery from Turks, and all Heretics of Luther's brood.

The historical sense.

summary_notes.text:
Prayer in tribulation.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. I HAVE lifted vp mine eies vnto <na>(a)</na> the mountaines, <na>(b)</na> from whence helpe shal come to me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Towardes Ierusalem, and towards heauen.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al helpe cometh from heauen, that is, from God, who of his diuine ordinance especially heareth prayers made in holie places. 3. Reg. 7.

verses.text: My helpe is from our Lord, who made heauen and earth.
Geue he not <na>(c)</na> thy foote to be moued: neither doe he slumber that keepeth thee.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The iust speaketh and wisheth wel to his owne soule. Especially the whole Church reioyceth in Gods assured protection.

verses.text: Loe he shal not slumber nor sleepe, that kepeth <na>(d)</na> Israel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The militant Church.

verses.text: Our lord kepeth thee, our Lord is thy protection, vpon thy right hand.
By day <na>(e)</na> the sunne shal not burne thee: nor <na>(f)</na> the moone by night.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Prosperitie,

notes.label: f
notes.text: nor aduersitie can ouerthrow the Church.

verses.text: Our Lord doth kepe thee from al euil: our Lord kepe <na>(g)</na> thy soule.

notes.label: g
notes.text: spiritual life.

verses.text: Our Lord kepe thy coming in, and thy going out: from hence forth now, and for euer.

chapters.summary: The iust reioyce that their prayer is heard, and that God continually protecteth them. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's protection.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. I REIOYCED in these thinges, which <na>(a)</na> were sayd to me: We shal goe into the house of our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Diuers Prophetes told the Iewes in captiuitie, that they should returne to Ierusalem. Al Prophetes, Christ also, and his Apostles, and Priestes preach the entrance, and ioyes of heauen to the iust. Al which the Psalmist saw in propheticall spirite, and reioyced.

verses.text: <na>(b)</na> Our feete were standing, in thy courtes ô Ierusalem

notes.label: b
notes.text: The Iewes consider that sometimes they were ioyful in the Temple of Ierusalem : Christians reioyce in the comforte they haue in the militant Church.

verses.text: Ierusalem, which is built as a citie: whose <na>(c)</na> participation is together in it self.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Communitie and participation of spirituall graces, is a great ioy to Catholiques, wherof the same Prophet speaketh, Psal 118. v. 6, and often els where.

verses.text: For <na>(d)</na> thither did the tribes ascend, <na>(e)</na> the tribes of our Lord: the testimonie of Israel to confesse vnto the name of our Lord.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al the twelue Tribes frequented Ierusalem,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and al nations of the world do come to the Catholique Church.

verses.text: Because seates <na>(f)</na> sate there in iudgement, <na>(g)</na> seates vpon the house <na>(h)</na> of Dauid.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Seates of Iudgement vvere placed in Ierusalem,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and seates of Iudgement in the Catholique Church

notes.label: h
notes.text: of Christ.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Aske ye the thinges that are for the peace of Ierusalem: and <na>(k)</na> abundance to them that loue thee.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Christ exhorteth to aske,

notes.label: k
notes.text: and promiseth to geue that is rightly asked ; Christians also inuite each other to pray for the Church.

verses.text: Peace be made in thy strength: and abundance in thy towers.
<na>(l)</na> For my bretheren, and my neigbours sakes, <na>(m)</na> I spake peace of thee:

notes.label: l
notes.text: Christ prayeth for his Church,

notes.label: m
notes.text: and gaue his peace to the Apostles, and in them to their successors.

verses.text: For the house of our Lord God, I haue sought <na>(n)</na> good thinges to thee.

notes.label: n
notes.text: For in heauenlie Ierusalem, al good thinges are prepared, & are geuen to Sainctes reigning there for euer.

chapters.summary: Vnder the figure of returne to Ierusalem, vehemently desired by the Iewes in captiuitie, the Psalmist describeth the desire, and hope of the iust to possesse heauen. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Ioyes of heauen promised to the iust.
The 10. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. TO thee haue I lifted vp mine eies, which dwellest in the heauens.

Behold as the eies <na>(a)</na> of seruantes, are on the handes of their masters, As the eies <na>(b)</na> of the handmaide on the handes of her mistresse: so are our eies to our Lord God vntil he haue mercie on vs.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Seruantes expecting necessaries at their masters handes, are commonly very attentiue to receiue that which they hope for : so must the faithful praying God, be very attentiue, and not distracted in their prayers.

notes.label: b
notes.text: An other example of handmaides, who generally are more diligent then men.

verses.text: Haue mercie on vs ô Lord, haue mercie on vs: because we are <na>(c)</na> much replenished with contempt.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Though God suffer his seruantes to sustaine some affliction and reproch, yet he heareth and deliuereth them before they be oppressed.

verses.text: Because our soule is <na>(d)</na> much replenished: reproch to them that abund, and contempt to the prowde.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Seing persecution stil increase, or continew long, the faithful are then specially to conceiue hope of speedie reliefe.

chapters.summary: A feruent and attentiue prayer, to be deliuered from captiuitie, or anie other affliction. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
A prayer in affliction.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. BVt that our Lord <na>(a)</na> was in vs, let Israel now say:

notes.label: a
notes.text: If God had not sent his helpe, and defence to vs,

verses.text: but that our Lord was in us. <na>(b)</na> When men rose up against us,

notes.label: b
notes.text: we could not haue escaped the force of our enimies.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> perhaps they had swalowed vs <na>(d)</na> aliue: When their furie was angrie against vs,

notes.label: c
notes.text: The word [perhaps] doth not here import a doubt, or vncertaintie, but in modest maner of asseueration, leaueth the iudgement of the euent that should hapen (if God did not protect his seruantes) to their owne consideration : which is an vsual phrase in most langnages.

notes.label: d
notes.text: So sudainly should the weake, without Gods protection, be destroyed, as men are deuoured & swalowed vp by rauening wild beastes, euen before they be throughly dead. So was Ionas swalowed into the whales bellie.

verses.text: perhaps <na>(e)</na> water had swalowed vs.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Furious persecution.

verses.text: Our soule hath passed through <na>(f)</na> a torrent: perhaps our soule had passed through an intolerable water.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Suddaine great trubles.

verses.text: Blessed be our Lord which hath not geuen vs, for a pray to their teeth.
Our soule as a sparow is deliuered from the snare of the fowlers: The snare is <na>(g)</na> broken, and we are deliuered.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Mans subtelue often deceiueth an other man, but there is no counsel able to circumuent God.

verses.text: Our helpe is in the name of our Lord, who made heauen and earth.

chapters.summary: The whole Church, and euerie iust person, gratfully confesseth, that by Gods protection they are secure, without which none could escape ruine. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Gods protection.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. THEY <na>(a)</na> that trust in our Lord, as mount Sion: he shal not be moued for euer, <na>(b)</na> that dwelleth in Ierusalem.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Those that confidently trust in God, are in such securitie as is mount Sion, which is a hil, defended also with other hilles round about.

notes.label: b
notes.text: An other thing required to this securitie, is to dwel within Ierusalem, not the terrestrial citie, for (as S. Augustin obserueth) the Iewes that dwelt therin are destroyed or made captiues, and hitherto reiected of God, but in the Catholique Church.

verses.text: Mountaines round about it: and our Lord round about his people, from hence forth now and for euer.
Because our Lord <na>(c)</na> wil not leaue the rod of sinners vpon the lote of the iust: that the iust reach not their handes to iniquitie.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God wil not alwayes, nor finally leaue his seruants in tribulation, but only a while for their good.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Doe wel ô Lord to the good, and right of hart.

notes.label: d
notes.text: This prayer is also an asseueration, for it is certaine that God wil defend, and reward the good, and right of hart:

verses.text: But <na>(e)</na> those that decline into obligations, our Lord wil bring with them that worke iniquitie: <na>(f)</na> peace vpon Israel.

notes.label: e
notes.text: And no lesse assuredly God wil punish not only the notorious wicked, and principal auctors of wickednes, but also al those that for feare or for commoditie, or for anie other cause, decline into obligations, bondes, couenants, or anie way consent, in external shew with the wicked against God, as in outward profession of Heresie, or Schisme, though such temporizers do not thinke in their hart, that the pretended religion is true, wherto they are drawe to yeld external conformitie. For, as the Psalmist here teacheth, our Lord wil bring al such accessarie offenders, to the same iudgement and punishment, with the principal workers of iniquitie.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Al which being punished, then Ierusalem, the Catholique Church, shal haue peace.

chapters.summary: The Church, and holie members therof, are alwayes protected by God: 5. The wicked being suffered for a while, are at last punished. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's protection.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. WHEN our Lord turned the captiuitie of Sion: we were made as <na>(a)</na> men comforted.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Iewes released from captiuitie, were exceedingly, and almost incredibly comforted, as men for great, and vnexpected sundaine ioy thinke it rather a dreame, then a truth that they are deliuered from miseries. So S. Peter when he was deliuered out of prison by an Angel. Act. 12. thought it rather a vision, then a true deliuerie. Such spiritual ioy deuoute soules haue when they are deliuered from sinne.

verses.text: Then was our mouth replenished with ioy: and our tongue with exultation. Then <na>(b)</na> shal they say among the Gentiles: Our Lord hath done magnifically with them.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Wheras in the two former verses (and very commonly) the Prophet speaketh in the preter tense, for the assurance of that he foresheweth, as if it were already donne, yet here he vttereth his prophecie in the future tense, that the Gentiles wil confesse that God dealeth magnifically with his people.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> Our Lord hath done magnifically with vs: we are made ioyful.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The people also themselues gratfully confesse that God dealeth magnifically with them.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Turne our captiuitie ô Lord, <na>(e)</na> as a torrent in the South.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The Prophet forseing al this in spirit, prayeth for the performance hereof.

notes.label: e
notes.text: And that it may spedely be done, as a torrent that runneth in the south part of the world. is commonly very great, much desired, but scarse expected.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> They that sow in teares, <na>(g)</na> shal reape in ioyfulnesse.

notes.label: f
notes.text: This is the ordinarie disposition of God, that his seruants shal make their seeding, which is, doe good workes (saith S. Augustin) with teares, in tribulation vpon earth:

notes.label: g
notes.text: and reape a plentiful haruest, the reward of their suffering and wel working, in the next life. In assured hope wherof the Psalmist, and the whole Church ioyfully conclude this Psalme with the two verses folowing.

verses.text: Going they went and wept, casting their seedes.
But coming they shal come with exultation, carying their sheaues.

chapters.summary: Isralites released from captiuitie of Babylon, much more the blessed both of the old and new testament deliuered by Christ from captiuitie of sinne, do reioyce: 5. Who neuertheles must passe through tribulation to eternal felicitie. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The deliuered from captiuitie reioyce.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle <na>(a)</na> of Salomon: VNLESSE <na>(b)</na> our Lord build the house, they haue laboured in vayne that build it. Vnlesse our Lord kepe the citie, he watcheth in vayne that kepeth it.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God not permitting Dauid to build the Temple, promised that his sonne should build it, and therfore besides other good admonitions, geuen to his sonne Salomon, he directeth this Psalme to him, to be songue with others in the dedication of the Temple. 3. Reg. 8. 1. Par. 5.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Vnlesse God be the principal Agent, no worke can prosper.

verses.text: It is vaine for you to rise <na>(c)</na> before light: <na>(d)</na> rise ye after ye haue sitten, which eate <na>(e)</na> the bread of sorow.

notes.label: c
notes.text: It is vaine to atempt anie thing without Gods grace assisting:

notes.label: d
notes.text: they that so doing, & thincking they haue done something, rest

notes.label: e
notes.text: after their painful trauel, must rise againe & beginne anew, because that which they seme to haue done wel, is nothing worth, nor shal haue reward.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> When he shal giue <na>(g)</na> sleepe to his beloued: behold <na>(h)</na> the inheritance of our Lord <na>(i)</na> are children: <na>(k)</na> the reward, the fruite of the wombe.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Contrariwise where God geuing grace, those that truly loue him, do good workes,

notes.label: g
notes.text: with great ease, and dilight, as they take their sleepe,

notes.label: h
notes.text: they merite inheritance in heauen,

notes.label: i
notes.text: for their good workes.

notes.label: k
notes.text: the reward is promised to the true children of God, borne to him in the wombe of the Catholique Church.

verses.text: As <na>(l)</na> arrowes in the hand of the mightie: so are the <na>(m)</na> children of them that are shaken.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Moreouer as a strong archer striketh deepe with his arrowes; so they that patiently suffer much in this world,

notes.label: m
notes.text: do multiplie good workes.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Blessed is the man that hath filled his desire of them: he shal <na>(o)</na> not be confounded when he shal speake to his enemies <na>(p)</na> in the gate.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Such shal be very happie,

notes.label: o
notes.text: & very easily answer al that can be obiected against them

notes.label: p
notes.text: in the day of Iudgement.

chapters.summary: Neither house nor citie can be built, or kept without Gods special prouidence and helpe, 3. those that trust in him shal prosper in their endeuours. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's help in all good works.
The 3. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. BLESSED are al that feare our Lord, that walke in his wayes.
Because thou shalt eate the labours of thy handes: blessed art thou, and it shal be wel with thee.
Thy <na>(a)</na> wife as a fruitful vine, in <na>(b)</na> the sides of thy house. <na>(c)</na> Thy children as young plantes of oliuetrees, round about thy table.

notes.label: a
notes.text: If such seruants of God be maried, they shal ordinarily haue issue, and succession in their familie: but especially the soules of such shal bring forth manie meritorious workes,

notes.label: b
notes.text: in the bosome of the Catholique Church, which was founded in Christs side.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Children also signifie good workes.

verses.text: Behold so shal the man be blessed, that feareth our Lord.
Our Lord out of Sion blesse thee: and that thou mayst see the good thinges of Ierusalem al the dayes of thy life.
And that thou mayst see thy <na>(d)</na> children's children, peace upon Israel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Reward in heauen for good workes in earth.

chapters.summary: Happines both of this life and of the next, is obtayned by fearing, and sincerely seruing God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Feare of God the way to happines.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. <na>(a)</na> OFTEN haue they impugned me <na>(b)</na> from my youth, let Israel now say:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Israel which is the Church of God, reioycing saith: that enimies haue often,

notes.label: b
notes.text: euen from the beginning of the world, persecuted me, as when Cain persecuted Abel, other wicked persecuted Seth, Enoch, Noe: the Chaldeis persecuted Abraham: the Ægyptians persecuted the Israelites: and so in other generations.

verses.text: Often haue they impugned me from my youth: <na>(c)</na> but they haue not preuailed against me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: But they haue neuer ouercome me. So the Psalmist testifieth for al times past, & prophecieth the same for times to come.

verses.text: Sinners <na>(d)</na> haue builded vpon my backe: they haue <na>(e)</na> prolonged their iniquitie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Persecuters not being able to ouerthrow, or suppresse the Church, haue laide great weightie burdens of tribulations vpon her backe, which she hath patiently and strongly borne,

notes.label: e
notes.text: they haue stil persisted, one sorte after an other, but with longanimitie the Church hath stood fast, and constantly passed through al distresses. In moral sense sinners build iniquitie vpon the back of the Church, yea and vpon Gods back, when they presume to sinne, trusting in the end to be absolued by vertue of holie Sacraments leift in the Church. Likewise when they excuse their sinnes, imputing the cause to other creatures of God, wherby they are allured. which is in effect ( saith S. Augustin) to accuse God, and to build iniquities on Gods back, who made those creatures.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Our iust Lord wil cut the neckes of sinners:

notes.label: f
notes.text: God therfore who is iust, wil at last cast such presumptuous sinners from his back, and breake their stiffe neckes:

verses.text: let them al <na>(g)</na> be confounded and <na>(h)</na> turned backward, that hate Sion.

notes.label: g
notes.text: then shal they be confounded,

notes.label: h
notes.text: separated eternally from God, become like fruitles, and withered grasse, cast away, despised, yea cursed of al, and blessed by none, as the Prophet denounceth in the next verses.

verses.text: Let them be made as grasse in the toppes of houses: which is withered before it be plucked vp.
Wherof the reaper hath not filled his hand, and he that gathereth the sheaues his bosome.
And they sayd not that passed by: The blessing of our Lord be vpon you: we haue blessed you in the name of our Lord.

chapters.summary: The Church often (3. and much) impugned, is not ouercome. 4. Her persecuters are destroyed, 6. contemned, 8. and cursed. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church still firm in persecution.
The 6. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. From <na>(a)</na> the depths I have cried to thee, o Lord:

notes.label: a
notes.text: This prayer agreeth to al true penitents, crying to God for helpe, being either in depth of sorovv for sinne, and so it is one of the Penitential Psalmes. or the depth of feruent desire to ascend towards perfection in vertue, and from this vaile of miserie into heauen. and so it is a Gradual Psalme. or in the depth of temporal paines, and so it is a special prayer for soules in Purgatorie, offered by the Church in their behalfe.

verses.text: Lord heare my voice: Let thine eares be intent, to the voice of my petition.
If thou shalt obserue iniquities ô Lord: Lord <na>(b)</na> who shal susteyne it?

notes.label: b
notes.text: None is able to abide the rigour of Gods iustice.

verses.text: Because with thee there is <na>(c)</na> propiciation: and for <na>(d)</na> thy law I haue expected thee ô Lord. My soule hath expected in his word:

notes.label: c
notes.text: But al must relie vpon his mercie.

notes.label: d
notes.text: For thy promises made in the law, that thou wilt remitte sinnes to the penitent, geue more grace to them that seeke it, and mitigate also the paines due for sinnes.

verses.text: my soule hath hoped in our Lord.
From <na>(e)</na> the morning watch euen vntil night: let Israel hope in our Lord.

notes.label: e
notes.text: The hope of penitents is like to the watches of the day time, from morning vntil night, which are more comfortable, then watches of the night:

verses.text: Because with our Lord there is mercie: and with him <na>(f)</na> plenteous redemption.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The greatest comforth is in Christ our Redemer, whose plentiful Redemption bringeth more abundance of grace.

verses.text: And he shal redeme <na>(g)</na> Israel, from al his iniquities.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Christs Redemption being sufficient for al the world, is effectual only to true liuing members of the Catholique Church.

chapters.summary: The Iewes, or other people in tribulation for sinne, or temporal captiuitie, crie to God to be deliuered: 4. trusting, and encoreging ech other in Gods accustomed mercie, assuredly hoping that he wil redeme & deliuer them. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The sixth penitential Psalm.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle of <na>(a)</na> Dauid. LORD my hart is not exalted: <na>(b)</na> neither are mine eies loftie. Neither haue I walked in great matters: nor in meruelous thinges aboue me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dauid by Gods special grace hauing a sincere minde towards al men, euen towards his enimies, and an humble hart, not desiring anie thing ambiciously, but al to the honour of God, proposeth his owne example, for others to imitate: that they may with him offer the sacrifice of humilitie, and innocencie vnto God, from whom al good thinges procede.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al this with a thankful mind to God who gaue this grace.

verses.text: If I was not humbly mynded: but exalted my soule: As <na>(c)</na> the weaned childe is toward his mother, <na>(d)</na> so retribution in my soule.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As children after they are weaned come stil willingly to their mother, so doth the childe of God relie vpon Gods helpe, though he alwayes feele not the same swetnes:

notes.label: d
notes.text: & according to his demeanur herein, he expecteth reward.
