verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Let Israel hope in our Lord, from henceforth now and for euer.

notes.label: e
notes.text: King Dauid, or anie other being for his vertue aduanced, and rewarded by God, is a good example to moue others to do the like, so shal they receiue like reward.

chapters.summary: Anie iust soule in humble confidence offereth his innocencie, as a spiritual and gratful sacrifice to God, 3. exhorting al Gods seruants euer to hope in him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Confidence of innocencie.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. REMEMBER <na>(a)</na> Dauid ô Lord, and al his meekenes:

notes.label: a
notes.text: It is an vsual thing that Dauid, Moyses, & other Prophetes speake of themselues in the third person.

verses.text: As he sware to our Lord, <na>(b)</na> vowed a vowe to the God of Iacob.

notes.label: b
notes.text: King Dauid desiring, and so farre as lay in him, promising to build a Temple to God, with great instance prayed that he might performe the same. But God disposing otherwise, that not he, but his sonne should build it, he neuertheles prepared the matter, workemen, and money, shewed the forme, and disposed the Leuites how to serue therin.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> If I shal enter into the tabernacle of my house, if I shal ascend into the bed of my couch.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Moreouer by vow depriued himself of entering into his owne house, or taking his ordinarie rest, til he might (if it so pleased God) know the place where it should be built.

verses.text: If I shal geue sleepe to mine eies, and slumbering to mine eie liddes:
And rest to my temples: vntil I finde a place for our Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Iacob.
Behold we haue heard of it <na>(d)</na> in Ephrata: we haue found it in <na>(e)</na> the fildes of the wood.

notes.label: d
notes.text: It was reueled to Dauid, that the Temple should be built, in that part of Ierusalem, which looketh towards Bethleem (otherwise called Ephrata) where our Sauiour was borne.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Within Ierusalem, which is compassed with woodes. In this vision also the whole forme of the Temple was reueled vnto him, as he testifieth. 1. Par. 28. v. 19. Al thinges, quoth he, came written with the hand of our Lord vnto me: that I might vnderstand al the workes of the paterne.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> We wil enter into his tabernacle: we wil <na>(g)</na> adore in the place where his feete stood.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Holie Dauid moued with exceding deuotion, repared to the place, where Gods Temple should be built:

notes.label: g
notes.text: & adored God, where the Propitiatorie, as a footstoole representing Gods presence, should stand. What meruel then if deuotion moue Christians, to visite the holie places, where our Sauiour, God and Man was Incarnate, was borne, suffered death, was buried, ascended into heauen, or anie other place where his feete stood.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Arise Lord into thy rest, thou and <na>(i)</na> the arke of thy sanctification.

notes.label: h
notes.text: O God, leauing Silo, Gabaon, and the like places, come into thy holie Temple.

notes.label: i
notes.text: With the Arke of conenant, where thou sanctifiest thy people. And here againe the Prophet illuminated with a higher Mysterie, and inflamed with more deuotion, prayeth for Christes coming into the world, and that after his Passion he wil rise, not only in glorie of soule, but also of bodie, prefigured by the Arke of testimonie, which was in the tabernacle, and after in the Temple.

verses.text: Let thy Priestes be clothed with <na>(k)</na> iustice: & let thy <na>(l)</na> sainctes reioyce.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Grant therfore that thy Priestes, which must offer sacrifice in this sacred place, be indued with vertues, and good life worthie of their degree:

notes.label: l
notes.text: and the Leuites who are ordained to serue there, be likewise made fitte for their diuers functions, both in the old and new Testament.

verses.text: <na>(m)</na> For Dauid thy seruants sake, <na>(n)</na> turne not away the face of thy Christ.

notes.label: m
notes.text: And seing thou hast geuen such meeknes, deuotion, zele, sinceritie, and other vertues making him a man according to thyne owne hart, and therupon promised to establish his sede,

notes.label: n
notes.text: differ not to send thy promised Messias, Christ our Redemer.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(o)</na> hath sworne truth to Dauid, and <na>(p)</na> he wil not disapoint it: <na>(q)</na> Of the fruite of thy wombe I wil set vpon thy seate.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Henceforth to the end of this Psalme, the Prophet relateth Gods reuelation to him: That he hath truly promised with an oath,

notes.label: p
notes.text: and wil performe,

notes.label: q
notes.text: to sette one of Dauids sonnes vpon his Throne: which was not only fulfilled in Salomon, who reigned in great peace, and builded the Temple, but especially in Christ the Sonne of Dauid, to whom our Lord God gaue the seate of Dauid his father, & he shal reigne in the house of Iacob for euer, and of his kingdom there shal be no end. Luc. 1. v. 32. 33. By this promise S. Peter also proueth Christs Resurrection. Act. 1. v. 30.

verses.text: <na>(r)</na> If thy children shal keepe my testament, and these my testimonies which I wil teach them: Their children also euen for euer, shal sit vpon thy seate.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Concerning the children of Christ, members of his kingdom the Church, the promise is conditional, if they obserue Gods commandments, they shal sit vpon his seate: be coheyres of his kingdom. Rom. 8. v. 17.

verses.text: Because our Lord hath chosen Sion: he hath chosen it for an habitation to himself.
This is my <na>(s)</na> rest for euer and euer: here wil I dwel because I haue chosen it.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Sion, the Catholique Church, is a perpetual place where God dwelleth.

verses.text: Blessing I wil blesse her <na>(t)</na> widow: her <na>(v)</na> poore I wil fil with breades.

notes.label: t
notes.text: The Church wanting Christs visible presence, is replenished with manie blessinges,

notes.label: v
notes.text: and al her humble children are releeued with holie Sacraments.

verses.text: Her <na>(w)</na> Priestes I wil clothe with saluation: and her <na>(x)</na> sainctes shal reioyce with ioyfulnes.

notes.label: w
notes.text: The Church hath alwayes some holie Priestes,

notes.label: x
notes.text: and some holie people.

verses.text: <na>(y)</na> Thither wil I bring forth a horne to Dauid, I haue prepared <na>(z)</na> a lampe to my Christ.

notes.label: y
notes.text: Of this Church, elected by God, Christ is the Protector, and strong defence.

notes.label: z
notes.text: and the same Church shal be a perpetual lampe, wherby others may come to him.

verses.text: His enemies I wil clothe with confusion: but vpon him shal my sanctification florish.

chapters.summary: The Psalmist earnestly prayeth God to geue him leaue, & to shew him where, to build a Temple. But more especially prayeth for, and prophecieth the coming of Christ, the promised Sonne of Dauid, 14. signifying Gods promise therof, and of establishing his Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Christ's coming to restore man.
The 5. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle <na>(a)</na> of Dauid. BEHOLD <na>(b)</na> how good, and how pleasant a thing it is, for brethren to dwel in one:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Dauid being a most peaceable man, euen toward his enimies, is added by Esdras in this title, as an example for others to imitate.

notes.label: b
notes.text: That concord is both good and pleasant, nedeth no other proofe, but only to consider, & to behold the fruict therof in euerie communitie, and especially in the Church of God.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> As oyntement on <na>(d)</na> the head, which ranne downe vpon the beard, <na>(e)</na> the beard of Aaron, which ranne downe vnto <na>(f)</na> the hemme of his garment:

notes.label: c
notes.text: The ointment, wherwith Aaron, and other High Priestes were consecrated, was precious, and most odoriferous, signifying grace bought by Christs blood, and producing vertues, which make swete sauoure:

notes.label: d
notes.text: was powred vpon the High Priests head, who being head of the Church,

notes.label: e
notes.text: vnitie and concord descended from him to other Priestes,

notes.label: f
notes.text: and so to the people, euen to the lowest, and meanest in Gods Church.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> As the dew of Hermon, which runneth downe vpon mount Sion. Because <na>(h)</na> there hath our Lord commanded blessing, and life euen for euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: An other similitude to declare the excellencie of concord: As the dew of mount Hermon, which is perpetually couered with snow, that falleth from the heauen, thence descending refresheth & fructifieth the hil of Sion: so mutual concord, and fraternal charitie amongst the faithful, nourisheth each other, making them fructful in al good workes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Where there is vnitie God geueth abundance of grace, as where the Apostles with other faithful were geathered, and continued in prayer, the Holie Ghost came vpon them al. And the multitude of beleuers [then increasing] had one hart and one soule. Act. 2. &. 4. v. 32.

chapters.summary: Fraternal concord is commended to al in the Church, as necessarie and delectable in it self, and blessed of God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Fraternal concord.
The 7. key.

verses.text: A gradual Canticle. LOE <na>(a)</na> now blesse our Lord, al ye the seruantes of our Lord: which stand in the house of our Lord, in the courtes of the house of our God.

notes.label: a
notes.text: This last Gradual Psalme, as a conclusion exhorteth al to praise God:

verses.text: In the nightes lift vp your handes vnto the holie places, and blesse ye our Lord.
Our Lord out of Sion blesse thee, who <na>(b)</na> made heauen and earth.

notes.label: b
notes.text: for to this end he made al creatures in heauen & in earth.

chapters.summary: Al, and especially clergie men that serue the Church, are inuited to prayse God by day and by night, so shal they be blessed of God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God continually to be praised.
The 1. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. PRAYSE ye the name of our Lord, <na>(a)</na> ye seruantes prayse our Lord.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Gods seruantes.

verses.text: Ye <na>(b)</na> that stand in the house of our Lord, in <na>(c)</na> the courtes of the house of our God.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Clergie that serue in the Temple,

notes.label: c
notes.text: and ye Leuite that attend to his seruice, must praise him for these causes.

verses.text: Prayse ye our Lord, because our Lord is <na>(d)</na> good: sing ye to his name, because it is <na>(e)</na> sweete.

notes.label: d
notes.text: his goodnes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: his benignitie.

verses.text: Because our Lord <na>(f)</na> hath chosen Iacob to himself, Israel for his owne possession.

notes.label: f
notes.text: he hath adopted vs his children.

verses.text: Because I haue knowne that our Lord is <na>(g)</na> great, and our God aboue al goddes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: he is omnipotent, as appeareth by his workes, here and elsvvhere recited : and manie wayes knovvne to the vvorld.

verses.text: Al thinges whatsoeuer our Lord would he hath done, in heauen, in earth, in the sea, and in al the depthes.
Bringing forth clowdes from the vttermost of the earth: lightenings he hath turned into rayne. Who bringeth forth the windes out of his treasures:
who stroke the first begotten of Ægypt from man euen to beast.
He sent forth signes, and wonders in the middes of thee ô Ægypt: vpon Pharao, and vpon al his seruantes. <cr>[1]</cr>
Who stroke manie nations: and slew strong kinges:
Sehon the king of the Amorrheites, & Og the king of Basan, and al the kingdomes of Chanaan. <cr>[1]</cr>
And he gaue their land for inheritance, for an inheritance to Israel his people.
Lord thy name is for euer: Lord thy memorial is vnto generation and generation.
Because our Lord shal iudge his people: and wil be intreated toward his seruantes.
The idoles of the Gentiles are siluer, and gold, the workes of mens handes.
They haue mouth, and shal not speake: they haue eies, and shal not see.
They haue eares, and shal not heare: for neither is there breath in their mouth.
Let them that make them become like to them: and al that haue confidence in them.
Ye house of Israel blesse our Lord: ye house of Aaron blesse our Lord.
Ye house of Leui blesse our Lord: you that feare our Lord, blesse ye our Lord.
Blessed be our Lord out of Sion, who dwelleth in Ierusalem.

chapters.summary: God who only is omnipotent, and fountaine of al goodnes, is of al to be praised, 3. He is the special protector of his elected people. 15. Contrariwise false goddes are impotent, vaine, and can not helpe those that serue them. 19. Only the Church doth rightly praise him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's perfection and goodness.
The 1. key.

verses.text: Allelu ia. CONFESSE ye to our Lord <na>(a)</na> because he is good: <na>(b)</na> because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: a
notes.text: VVhose goodnes is incomparable.

notes.label: b
notes.text: This second part of euerie verse, first pronounced by the Priestes, confessing & praising Gods mercie aboue al his workes, was stil repeted by musicians, or other assistants, in maner as now in Litanies [ ô Lord deliuer vs ] and [ VVe besech thee to heare vs ] And as Gloria Patri &c. is added in the end of Psalmes, and our Lords prayer, and the Angelical salutation are often repeted in diuers Offices, and in the Rosarie.

verses.text: Confesse ye to <na>(c)</na> the God of goddes: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: c
notes.text: VVhose diuine powre created al other thinges.

verses.text: <na>(d)</na> Confesse ye to <na>(e)</na> the Lord of lordes: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: d
notes.text: By this inuitation to praise our Lord God, thrise repeted, we professe the Blessed Trinitie, who is one God in substance, and three Diuine Persons.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhose dominion is ouer al the world.

verses.text: Who <na>(f)</na> onlie doth great meruels: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Only God can do true miracles ; to wit, workes aboue the course of al nature.

verses.text: Who made the heauen <na>(g)</na> in vnderstanding: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In admirable wisdom.

verses.text: Who established <na>(h)</na> the earth ouer the waters: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Made the waters aboue nature to remaine vvithin their bondes, & not to couer the earth.

verses.text: Who made the great lightes: because his mercie is for euer.
The sunne to rule the day: because his mercie is for euer.
The moone, and starres to rule the night: because his mercie is for euer.
Who stroke Ægypt with their firstbegotten: because his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>
Who brought forth Israel out of the middes of them: because his mercie is for euer.
In a mightie hand, and loftie arme: because his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>
Who diuided the Read sea into diuisions: because his mercie is for euer.
And brought forth Israel through the middes therof: because his mercie is for euer.
And he ouerthrew Pharao, and his host in the Read sea: because his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>
Who led his people through the desert: because his mercie is for euer. <cr>[1]</cr>
Who stroke great kinges: because his mercie is for euer.
And slewe strong kinges: because his mercie is for euer.
Sehon the king of the Amorrheites: because his mercie is for euer.
And Og the king of Basan: because his mercie is for euer.
And he gaue their land for an inheritance: because his mercie is for euer.
For an inheritance to Israel his seruant: because his mercie is for euer.
For in our humiliation he was mindful of vs: because his mercie is for euer.
And he redemed vs from our enemies: because his mercie is for euer.
Who geueth foode to <na>(i)</na> al fleshe: because his mercie is for euer.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Al Gods benignitie, as wel of particular benefites towards his people, as general to them and al others procedeth from his mercie.

verses.text: Confesse ye to the God of heauen: because his mercie is for euer. Confesse ye to the Lord of lordes: because his mercie is for euer.

chapters.summary: God being meruelous in himself, 4. hath shewed his powre and goodnes in his workes, as wel in general to al the world, 10. as in particular towards his elected people. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's marvelous works.
The 2. key.

verses.text: A Psalme of Dauid <na>(a)</na> for Ieremie. VPON the riuers <na>(b)</na> of Babylon, there we <na>(c)</na> sate and wept: whiles we <na>(d)</na> remembred Sion.

notes.label: a
notes.text: By adding to this title [ for Ieremie ] the Septuagint Interpreters signifie that this Psalme treateth of the same captiuitie, in which Ieremias writte his Lamentations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Nere the riuers in Chaldea ; wherof Babylon was the head citie,

notes.label: c
notes.text: the Iewes remained mourning,

notes.label: d
notes.text: remembring the holie rites and seruice of God, which had bene in Sion, wherof they were depriued in the captiuitie.

verses.text: On the willowes in the middes therof, we hanged vp <na>(e)</na> our instrumentes.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Al their musical instruments, as hauing no vse of them.

verses.text: Because there they that led vs captiue, <na>(f)</na> demanded of vs wordes of songes. And they that led vs away: Sing ye an hymne to vs of the songes of Sion.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Either in earnest, or in scorne the Chaldees willed them to sing, as they were accustomed in their countrie.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> How shal we sing the song of our Lord in a strange land?

notes.label: g
notes.text: They excused themselues, and refused to sing sacred Psalmes before prophane people, neither had they mind to sing in that mourning state of captiuitie.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> If I shal forget thee ô Ierusalem, let my right hand be forgotten.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The people shew not only their feruent present desire to serue God in Ierusalem, but also their firme purpose stil to desire the same, wishing that if they forget it, or lose this affection, their right handes, or whatsoeuer is most deare, or necessarie for them, may be forgotten, not conserued, but suffered to perish,

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> Let my tongue cleaue to my iawes, if I doe not remember thee: If I shal not set Ierusalem in the beginning of my ioy.

notes.label: i
notes.text: If I lose this affection, let me also lose the vse of my tongue.

verses.text: Be mindful ô Lord of <na>(k)</na> the childrem of Edom, in <na>(l)</na> the day of Ierusalem: <na>(m)</na> That say: Rase it, rase it, euen vnto the foundation therof.

notes.label: k
notes.text: The Idomeans incensed the Chaldees to be cruel against the Iewes, wherof they pray for iust reuenge, and withal the Psalmist prophecieth that it wil be reuenged, which Isaias also prophecieth, c. 21. v. 11.

notes.label: l
notes.text: for their reioycing in Ierusalems miserie.

notes.label: m
notes.text: The voice of the Idumeans, inciting the Babylonians vtterly to destroy Ierusalem.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> Daugther of Babylon miserable: blessed is he, that shal repay thee thy payment, which thou hast payed vs.

notes.label: n
notes.text: A prophecie that the people of Babylon should also be punished, for their crueltie against the Iewes, wherof Isaias likewise prophecieth c. 13.

verses.text: Blessed is he, <na>(o)</na> that shal hold, and <na>(p)</na> shal dash thy litle ones against the rocke.

notes.label: o
notes.text: God wil blesse, or reward them that shal seuerly afflict the Babylonians,

notes.label: p
notes.text: not sparing their children. Morally he is blessed, that mortifieth his owne passions, cutteth of first il motions, or punisheth venial sinnes, that they grow not strong within his soule, and so draw it to committe mortal sinne. S. Aug. hic. & S. Greg in fine expos. Psal. 4. pænit.

chapters.summary: The Prophet describeth how lamentably the people in captiuitie of Babylon, wil bewaile the want of meanes to serue God, and of their natiue soyle : 7. with iust desire of their enimies punishment. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Jews' lamentation in captivity.
The 4. key.

verses.text: To <na>(a)</na> Dauid him self. I wil <na>(b)</na> confesse to thee ô Lord in my whole hart: <na>(c)</na> because thou hast heard the wordes of my mouth. In <na>(d)</na> the sight of Angels I wil sing to thee:

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme is a fitte forme of thankes for Dauid, or anie other seruant of God.

notes.label: b
notes.text: I wil render thankes and praise.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God euer heareth the prayer that is rightly made, for which the supplicant is therfore to geue thankes.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Angels are present where the faithful pray, obserue our prayers, and offer them to God, if they be sincere, as the prayers of Tobias, and Cornelius.

verses.text: I wil adore <na>(e)</na> toward thy holie temple, and wil confesse to thy name. <na>[1]</na> For thy mercie, and thy truth: because thou hast magnified aboue euerie thing <na>(f)</na> thy holie name.

notes.label: e
notes.text: VVhen there was not accesse to the Temple, yet the Iewes praying in captiuitie, turned themselues towards the Temple.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The Name and Maiestie of GOD, The VVord (which is the Sonne of God) also the name of IESVS, is magnified aboue al names, or temporal thinges :

verses.text: In what day soeuer I shal inuocate thee, heare me: thou wilt multiplie strength in my soule.
Let <na>(g)</na> al the kinges of the earth ô Lord confesse to thee: because they haue heard al the wordes of thy mouth:

notes.label: g
notes.text: Sowner or later Kinges and Princes of al kingdomes and nations, haue bene or shal be conuerted to Christ.

verses.text: And let them sing in the wayes of our Lord: because great is the glorie of our Lord.
Because our Lord is high, and he beholdeth low thinges: and high thinges he knoweth <na>(h)</na> far of.

notes.label: h
notes.text: God knoweth proud men, not as his freindes or seruantes, but farre of, as strangers and enimies.

verses.text: If I shal walke in the middes of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: and vpon the wrath of mine enimies thou hast extended thy hand, and thy right hand hath saued me.
Our Lord wil repay for me: ô Lord thy mercie is for euer: despise not the workes of thy handes.

chapters.summary: The whole Church, or anie iust person, rendreth thankes to God for his benefites 4. praying that al kinges and kingdomes may do the same, 6. because God being high respecteth, and aduanceth the humble. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Thankes to God for benefites.
The 7. key.

verses.text: Vnto <na>(a)</na> the end, a Psalme of Dauid. LORD thou <na>(b)</na> hast proued me, and hast knowen me:

notes.label: a
notes.text: By this part of the title [to the end] is signified (as is noted Psal. 4.) that the matter conteined in the Psalme, perteyneth to the newe Testament.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God who knoweth al thinges most absolutly and perfectly, without discourse or searching, yet, as it were, maketh experimental trial of his seruants, to make them in some sorte to know him, and to know themselues. And so here, holie Dauid or other faithful man, acknowlegeth Gods Omniscience, that is, perfect knowlege of al thinges, without exception, past, present, & to come : al workes, wordes, thoughtes, and whatsoeuer can be, though it neuer was nor shal be, in general and in particular.

verses.text: thou hast knowen my sitting downe, and my rising vp.
Thou hast vnderstood my cogitations far of: my path, and <na>(c)</na> my corde thou hast searched out.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The vttermost measure and reach of myne intention.

verses.text: And thou hast foresene al my wayes: because there is not a word in my <na>(d)</na> tongue.

notes.label: d
notes.text: The word holden in by the tongue, and not vttered by mouth, is not hidden from God.

verses.text: Behold ô Lord thou hast knowen al the last thinges, & them of old: thou hast formed me, and hast put thy hand vpon me.
Thy knowledge is <na>(e)</na> become meruelous of me: it is made great, and I can not reach to it.

notes.label: e
notes.text: By experiece we see that Gods knowlege exceedeth our reach.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Whither shal I goe from thy spirit? and whither shal I flee from thy face?

notes.label: f
notes.text: As Gods knowlege comprehendeth al thinges, so his presence extendeth it selfe to al places, neither is conteined in place, but excedeth al place, in his diuine immensitie.

verses.text: If I shal ascend into heauen, thou art there: if I descend into hel, thou art present.
If I shal take my winges early, and dwel in the extreme partes of the sea:
Certes thither also shal thy hand conduct me: and thy right hand shal hold me.
<na>(g)</na> And I sayd: Perhaps darknes shal treade ouer me: and the night is mine illumination in my delightes.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The Prophet also in the person of anie curious imaginatiue man, examineth and findeth that no darknes, nor couer can hide anie thing from God.

verses.text: For darkenes shal not be darkened from thee, and the night shal be lightened as the day: as the darkenes therof, so also the light therof.
Because thou hast possessed <na>(h)</na> my reynes: thou hast receiued me from <na>(i)</na> my mothers wombe.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Nothing semeth more hidden, then a mans entrals.

notes.label: i
notes.text: or a child in the mothers wombe.

verses.text: I wil confesse to thee, because thou art terribly magnified: thy workes are meruelous, & my soule knoweth excedingly.
My <na>(k)</na> bone is not hid from thee, which thou madest in secrete: and my substance in the lower partes of the earth.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Or bones in the flesh.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Mine <na>[1]</na> imperfection thine eies haue sene, & in thy booke <na>[2]</na> al shal be written: <na>(m)</na> daies shal be formed, & no man in them.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Or mans bodilie imperfection before his birth,

notes.label: m
notes.text: dayly formed by God, not by man. Iob. 10. v. 8. 2. Mac. 7. v. 21, 23.
Colem, Embryonem.
Of knowlege.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> But to me thy <na>[1]</na> frendes ô God are become honorable exceedingly: their principalitie is exceedingly strengthned.

notes.label: n
notes.text: Aboue al considerations it most excedeth, that God so high and infinite, honoreth his humble poore seruants so exceedingly, that it semeth to themselues, farre more then can be due. For he rewardeth euen ouer & aboue merites ; which merites also are founded in Gods mercie geuen without merite.

Newe translaters peruert this place, translating [thoughts] for [frendes] contrarie to the Hebrew, Greke, and Latin, and al ancient Fathers, only pretending, that the same word in the Chaldee tongue also signifieth thoughts.

verses.text: <na>(o)</na> I wil number them, and they shal be multiplied aboue the sand: <na>(p)</na> I rose vp and I am yet with thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: The number also of Sainctes whom God hath chosen, called, iustified and wil glorifie, excede mans conceipt. Apoc 7.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Incensed with this excellent glorie, and desiring to be of this innumerable multitude, by thy grace I haue risen from sinne, and in confidence of thy perpetual helpe, I stand and hope to perseuere in thy seruice.

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> If thou shalt kil sinners ô God: <na>(r)</na> ye men of blood depart from me.

notes.label: q
notes.text: And if it be so, yea seing it is so, that as thou ô God doest exalt thy Sainctes, to exceeding and vnspeakable honour : so thou hast also decreed to punish obstinate sinners, with eternal death and damnation :

notes.label: r
notes.text: I renounce al wicked association, gette ye away from me al cruel bloudie men, that would drawe me into euerlasting torments.

verses.text: <na>(s)</na> Because you say in thought: they <na>(t)</na> shal receiue thy cities in vayne.

notes.label: s
notes.text: Away from me, you that thinke,

notes.label: t
notes.text: the glorious mansions in heauen, prepared and promised to the iust, are vaine hopes, and in vaine expected.

verses.text: <na>(v)</na> Did not I hate them, that hate thee ô Lord: and <na>(w)</na> pyned away because of thine enemies?

notes.label: v
notes.text: This hate of such sinners the iust shal confidently plead, and happie are they that shal be able truly to alleage for themselues in the day of iudgement, that they hated al, whom God hateth,

notes.label: w
notes.text: yea hated them with feruent zele, that are Gods enimies.

verses.text: <na>(x)</na> with perfect hatred did I hate them: they are become <na>(y)</na> enemies to me.

notes.label: x
notes.text: Stil the Prophet inculcateth this necessarie perfect hatred,

notes.label: y
notes.text: and enmitie towards Gods enimies.

verses.text: <na>(z)</na> Proue me ô God, and know my hart: examine me, and know my pathes.

notes.label: z
notes.text: For that none in this life (without special and extraordinarie reuelation) knoweth certainly their owne state, whether they be worthie of Gods loue or hatred (Eccle. 9.) the iust submitte themselues to Gods examination of their hart and actions :

verses.text: And <na>(a)</na> see, if the way of iniquitie be in me: <na>(b)</na> and conduct me in the euerlasting way.

notes.label: a
notes.text: humbly praing God, that if they be in the way of iniquitie,

notes.label: b
notes.text: he wil voutsafe to reduce and guid them into the right way of euerlasting life.

chapters.summary: Gods knowlege, 7. and presence (10. without the helpe, or hinderance anie thing) extendeth to al thinges, times, and places. 17. he geueth exceeding great honour to his sainctes, 20. the wicked, as enimies to God are iustly hated, 23. the iust pray for Gods perpetual direction. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's special providence of his servants.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Vnto the end, a Psalme of Dauid.
DELIVER me ô Lord from the euil man: from the vniust man rescue me.
Which <na>(a)</na> haue deuised iniquitie in their hart: <na>(b)</na> al the day they did appoint battels. They haue whet their tongues as that of a serpent:

notes.label: a
notes.text: Vnquiet euil disposed men stil deuise wicked plottes,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and neuer cease to make discord, and debates.

verses.text: the venome of aspes is vnder their lippes.
Kepe me ô Lord from the hand of the sinner: and from vniust men deliuer me.
Who haue deuised to supplant my steppes: the proude haue hid a snare for me: And they haue streched out ropes for a snare: they haue layd <na>[1]</na> a stumbling blocke for me nere the way.

notes.text: scandalum.

verses.text: <na>(c)</na> I sayd to our Lord: Thou art my God: heare ô Lord the voice of my petition.

notes.label: c
notes.text: In time of tentation prayer is most necessarie.

verses.text: O Lord, Lord <na>(d)</na> the strength of my saluation: <na>(e)</na> thou hast ouershadowed my head in the day of battel.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Man is not able to resist temptations,

notes.label: e
notes.text: vnlesse God by his grace, as by a helmet, defend him from yelding consent.

verses.text: Yeld me not ô Lord from <na>(f)</na> my desire, to the sinner: they haue deuised against me, forsake me not, <na>(g)</na> lest they perhaps be proude.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Suffer me not to fal from that which I now desire (which is to be constant in vertue) not to consent to sinners perswasions.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Who then would triumph ouer me.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> The head of their compasse: <na>(i)</na> the labour of their lippes <na>(k)</na> shal couer them.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The summe of their mischeuous deuises,

notes.label: i
notes.text: consisting in their subtle persuasions with swete wordes,

notes.label: k
notes.text: shal ouerwhelme, and bring themselues to perdition.

verses.text: <na>(l)</na> Coales shal fal vpon them, <na>(m)</na> thou shalt cast them downe into fyre: in miseries <na>(n)</na> they shal not stand vp.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Hel fire shal be their lotes ;

notes.label: m
notes.text: into which they shal fal,

notes.label: n
notes.text: & euer be in intolerable torments.

verses.text: A man ful of tongue shal not be directed in the earth: euils shal take the vniust man into destruction.
<na>(o)</na> I haue knowne that our Lord wil do the iudgement of the needie: and the reuenge of the poore.

notes.label: o
notes.text: I haue learned by good instructions, and by experience, that in the end thou ô God wilt comfort the iust, who are now afflicted, and punish the vniust, that liue in temporal delightes, as it happened to Lazarus, and the glutton.

verses.text: But as for the iust, they shal confesse to thy name: and the righteous shal dwel with <na>(p)</na> thy countenance.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Eternal glorie consisteth in seeing God.

chapters.summary: The iust diuersly afflicted by the wicked, pray to be defended, 7. repose their confidence in God, 10. who wil adiudge the reprobate to eternal punishment, 13. and reward the good with the fruition of himself. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Eternal pain of the wicked, and joy of the blessed.
The 10. key.

verses.text: A Psalme of Dauid. LORD I haue cried to thee, heare me: attend to my voice, when I shal crie to thee.
<na>[1]</na> Let my prayer be directed as <na>(a)</na> incense in thy sight: the eleuation of my handes as <na>(b)</na> euening sacrifice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: As the sume of incense is swete and ascendeth vpwards : so the Church prayeth that her petitions may be gratful, and ascend to God.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In the old testament morning sacrifice was rather more solemne, and more frequent, but the Prophet semeth to allude vnto Christs Sacrifice, which he was to offer towards euening on the Crosse ; and the same also in vnbloudie maner, the euening before his Passion, in the Eucharist.
In these wordes the Church prayeth, offering incense in her solemne Offices.

verses.text: Set ô Lord <na>(c)</na> a watch to my mouth: and <na>(d)</na> a doore round about to my lippes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: A iust care and consideration what to speake, before the mouth be opened.

notes.label: d
notes.text: lippes must not be alwayes stopt, for it is a sinne sometimes not to speake, but as a dore that is to be opened, and shut at due seasons, for example ; opened to confesse our sinnes, and Gods truth :

verses.text: Decline not my hart <na>(e)</na> into wordes of malice, to make excuses in sinnes. With men that worke iniquitie: and I wil not communicate with the chiefe of them.

notes.label: e
notes.text: shutte from wordes of malice, and from excusing sinnes committed.

verses.text: The iust shal rebuke me in mercie, and <na>(f)</na> shal reprehend me: but let not the oyle of a sinner <na>(g)</na> fatte my head. Because, <na>(h)</na> yet also my prayer is in their <na>(i)</na> good pleasures:

notes.label: f
notes.text: Admonition of the iust, is a profitable reprehension,

notes.label: g
notes.text: but the fawning of flatterers is pernicious.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The Church ceaseth not to pray for sinners,

notes.label: i
notes.text: though as yet they take pleasure in their sinnes,

verses.text: <na>(k)</na> their Iudges are swalowed vp ioyned to the rocke. <na>(l)</na> They shal heare my wordes <na>(m)</na> because they haue preuailed:

notes.label: k
notes.text: but the very chiefest of them, which seme most potent, if they remaine obstinate to their death, shal then perish, as men throwne against rockes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: They shal then heare and vnderstand, that the prayers of the Church

notes.label: m
notes.text: are effectual, obtaining grace of constancie to her children, not to feare anie persecution, nor anie kind of death ; obtayning also iustificatiô of their cause, when the persecuters shal see that the wordes, and doctrin of the Church are true, and preuaile in true iudgement, as true, modest, peaceable, not seditious, turbulent, nor against the commonwealth.

verses.text: <na>(n)</na> as the grossenes of the earth is broken out vpon the earth. Our <na>(o)</na> bones are dissipated <na>(p)</na> nere to hel:

notes.label: n
notes.text: As much earth sticking together is made fructful, by breaking it into smal mould, so the children of the Church by persecution, bring forth more fruict then before. S. Aug.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Some persecuters are so cruel as to rage against the bones, and other reliques of Martyrs,

notes.label: p
notes.text: casting them into the vilest places they can, willing if they could, to throw them into hel,

verses.text: <na>(q)</na> for to thee ô Lord, Lord are mine eies; in thee haue I hoped, take not away my <na>[1]</na> soule.

notes.label: q
notes.text: but the Church and al her members repose confidence in God.
life.

verses.text: Keepe me from <na>(r)</na> the snare, which they haue set for me: and from <na>(s)</na> the scandals of them that worke iniquitie.

notes.label: r
notes.text: Therefore she prayeth that her children be not entrapped by guilful deceiptes,

notes.label: s
notes.text: nor ouerthrowne by anie stumbling blocke cast in their way.

verses.text: <na>(t)</na> Sinners shal fal in his net: <na>(v)</na> I am alone vntil I passe.

notes.label: t
notes.text: In the end, al persecuters and other wicked shal be caught in their owne nette of perdition,

notes.label: v
notes.text: the Church is singularly protected euen to the end.

chapters.summary: The Church prayeth that her children may auoide sinful wordes, 4. not make excuses of sinnes committed, not communicate with others in sinne, nor to harken to flatterers : 6. but to pray that they may amend ( the Psalmist by the way prophecieth that manie shal be conuerted) 8. though sometimes persecution be great, the Church faileth not. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church prayeth and prevaileth.
The 6. key.

verses.text: OF <na>(a)</na> vnderstanding to Dauid, when he was in the caue, a prayer. 1. Reg. 24. <cr>[1]</cr>

notes.label: a
notes.text: This Psalme in forme of a prayer, sheweth what cogitations Dauid had in extreme danger.

verses.text: VVIth my voice I <na>(b)</na> haue cried to our Lord: with my voice I haue prayed to our Lord:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not with exterior voice, for so he should haue detected himselfe, but with feruour of spirite.

verses.text: I powre out my prayer in his sight, and I pronounce my tribulation before him.
<na>(c)</na> When my spirit faileth of my self, and <na>(d)</na> thou hast knowne my pathes. In this way, which I walked, they hid a snare for me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: When by reason of extremitie, I was not able to thinke how to helpe my selfe,

notes.label: d
notes.text: thou ô God knowing my actions and demeanour, didst deliuer me.

verses.text: I looked toward <na>(e)</na> the right hand, and <na>(f)</na> saw: and <na>(g)</na> there was none that would know me. <na>(h)</na> Flight hath failed me: and there is none to require my soule.

notes.label: e
notes.text: I looked for helpe :

notes.label: f
notes.text: and diligently looked about me,

notes.label: g
notes.text: but none would seme to know me, when I required their helpe.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Endeuoring to saue my self by flight, I found no secure place, for being in a caue or hole of a montaine, the whole armie beseeged me ; al seeke to take away my life, none to saue it.

verses.text: <na>(i)</na> I haue cried to thee ô Lord, I haue sayd: Thou art <na>(k)</na> my hope, <na>(l)</na> my portion <na>(m)</na> in the land of the liuing.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Thus left desolate of al mans helpe, and destitute of al worldlie shift, I cried to thee ô Lord,

notes.label: k
notes.text: my only hopeful refuge,

notes.label: l
notes.text: neither do I desire to liue for anie worldlie respect, but hauing chosen thee ô God for my portion, and inheritance,

notes.label: m
notes.text: I desire to be out of this desert place, and to be in the land, where is right vse of religious diuine seruice.

verses.text: Attend to my petition: because I am <na>(n)</na> humbled exceedingly. Deliuer me from them that persecute me: because they are made strong ouer me.

notes.label: n
notes.text: afflicted.

verses.text: Bring forth my soule out of prison, <na>(o)</na> to confesse vnto thy name: <na>(p)</na> the iust expect me; <na>(q)</na> til thou reward me.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Dauids desire of libertie, was especially to this end, that he might haue conuenient place, and other meanes to serue and praise God :

notes.label: p
notes.text: the good, and wel disposed people of Israel, can not now serue thee as they desire, but expect me,

notes.label: q
notes.text: whom thou ô Lord, vvilt aduance to the kingdom, that then vve may serue thee, more freely and more commodiously.

chapters.summary: Holie Dauid being fled into a caue, and beseeged round about by Sauls armie, explicating his distresse, 6. prayeth to be deliuered: <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Dauids prayer in extreme distresse.
The 8. key.

articles.title: The prophetical sense of this Psalme.
articles.text: Al this happened in figure of Christ, of vvhom prophetically S. Augustin S. Hilarie, Cassiams, Cassiodorus, and others expound the vvhole Psalme. Amongst others S. Beda briefly in these vvordes. VVheras in the title, Vnderstanding is premised to Prayer, therby is signified, that Dauid in his distresses, and in the denne whither he fled, vnderstood vvhat our Lord should suffer of the Ievves, and hovv he vvould pray to his Father. In the first part our Lord crieth to his Father, complaining of the detestable deceiptes of Iudas the persecutor. In the second he prayeth to be deliuered from the prison of hel (Limbus, vvhere he vvas free) because the faith of al the Sainctes depended on his Resurrection.

verses.text: to be spedely deliuered; 11. and confidently assureth himselfe therof. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: The seuenth penitential Psalme. the 7. key.

verses.text: A Psalme of Dauid, when Absalom his sonne persecuted him. 2. Reg. <cr>[1]</cr> LORD heare my prayer: with thine eares receiue my petition in <na>(a)</na> thy truth: heare me in <na>(b)</na> thy iustice.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God hauing so promised is bond by his truth,

notes.label: b
notes.text: and his iustice, to heare penitents praying for remission of sinnes.

verses.text: And <na>(c)</na> enter not into iudgement with thy seruant: <na>(d)</na> because no man liuing shal be iustified in thy sight.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Deale not vvith me in rigour of iustice,

notes.label: d
notes.text: for no mortal man is able of himselfe to be iustified, abstracting from Gods mercie.

verses.text: Because the enemie <na>(e)</na> hath persecuted my soule: he <na>(f)</na> hath humbled my life in the earth. <na>(g)</na> He hath set me in obscure places as the dead of the world:

notes.label: e
notes.text: sought my life,

notes.label: f
notes.text: and brought it into great danger. Spiritually, the diuel as a roring lion stil seeking vvhom he may deuour, hath tempted me vehemently.

notes.label: g
notes.text: I am pressed vvith great calamities, temporal or spiritual.

verses.text: and my spirit is in anguish vpon me, within me my hart is trubled.
<na>(h)</na> I was mindful of old dayes, I haue meditated in al thy workes: in the factes of thy handes did I meditate.

notes.label: h
notes.text: In this case I consider, how God hath hertofore shewed his goodnes towards me, and others.

verses.text: I haue <na>(i)</na> stretched forth my handes to thee: my soule is <na>(k)</na> as earth without water vnto thee.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Stretching forth handes a ceremonie in prayer, vvherby the supplicant is made more attentiue, and also indureth some paine for part of satisfaction.

notes.label: k
notes.text: mans mind vvithout Gods illumination is drie and barren.

verses.text: Heare me <na>(l)</na> quickly ô Lord: my spirite hath faynted. Turne not away thy face from me: <na>(m)</na> and I shal be like to them that descend into <na>(n)</na> the lake.

notes.label: l
notes.text: In great tentations Gods grace and helpe is more presently nedeful to preuent our weaknes, lest vve yeld consent.

notes.label: m
notes.text: If God leaue man vvithout special and continual grace, he vvil fal,

notes.label: n
notes.text: into sinne, as into a deepe lake, from vvhence vvithout helpe he can not rise vp againe.

verses.text: Make me heare thy mercie <na>(o)</na> in the morning: because I haue hoped in thee. Make the way knowen to me, wherein I may walke: <na>(p)</na> because I haue lifted vp my soule to thee.

notes.label: o
notes.text: In the first assault of tentation.

notes.label: p
notes.text: Seing by thy grace I haue begunne to pray vnto thee.

verses.text: Deliuer me from mine enemies ô Lord, to thee I haue fled:
teach me to doe thy wil, because thou art my God: Thy <na>(q)</na> good spirite wil conduct me into the right way:

notes.label: q
notes.text: The penitent thus humbling himselfe, and praying may assuredly trust that God doth remitte his sinnes by the holie Sacraments, and iustifieth him, protecteth him, and wil bring him out of al dangers of spiritual or temporal enemies.

verses.text: for thy name sake ô Lord thou wilt quicken me, in thine equitie. Thou wilt bring forth my soule out of tribulation:
and in thy mercie thou wilt destroy mine enemies. And thou wilt destroy al, that afflict my soule: because I am thy seruant.

chapters.summary: King Dauid (or anie other) in spiritual or temporal tribulation, not trusting in his owne iustice, layeth open his calamitie, 5. considering Gods benignitie, 6. prayeth

verses.text: A Psalme of Dauid, <na>(a)</na> against Goliath. BLESSED be our Lord my God, who <na>(b)</na> teacheth my handes to battel; and my fingers to warre.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Because this vvas Dauids first, and a very notable victorie, the Septuagint Interpreters make mention of Goliath in this title.

notes.label: b
notes.text: God made Dauid a warier, and victorer against Goliath, without anie former training in armes.

verses.text: My mercie, and my refuge: my defender, and my deliuerer. My protectour, and I haue hoped in him, who <na>(c)</na> subdeweth my people vnder me.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Made him afterwards king of a great people.

verses.text: Lord <na>(d)</na> what is man, that thou art <na>(e)</na> made knowne to him? or the sonne of man; <na>(f)</na> that thou estemest him?

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al mankind was vnvvorthie before Christ,

notes.label: e
notes.text: that God should be reueled vnto them,

notes.label: f
notes.text: especially that he should haue care of the progenie of men, after their sinne.

verses.text: <na>(g)</na> Man is made like to vanitie: his dayes passe as a shadow.

notes.label: g
notes.text: In dede man in himself, in his ovvne nature and frailtie, is but a vaine and transitorie creature, passing from life to death, as a shadovv that can not consist of it selfe, neither can man vvithout God.

verses.text: <na>(h)</na> Lord incline thy heauens, and descend: touch the mountaynes, and they wil smoke.

notes.label: h
notes.text: By a poetical description he prayeth for Gods helpe, as if God should make the heauens to bovv, and so descend; or make the montaines smoke, as vvhen Moyses receiued the lavv; or declare himself by Meteors, as folovveth:

verses.text: Lighten lightening, and thou shalt disperse them: shoote out thine arrowes, and thou shalt destroy them.
Send forth thy hand from on high, take me out, and deliuer me from manie <na>(i)</na> waters: from the hand <na>(k)</na> of children <na>(l)</na> strangers.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Tribulations or tentations.

notes.label: k
notes.text: Children of the Church,

notes.label: l
notes.text: but of euil life.

verses.text: Whose mouth hath spoken <na>(m)</na> vanitie: and their right hand is the right hand of iniquitie.

notes.label: m
notes.text: They speake in vanitie that promise to kepe Gods law, and performe it not.

verses.text: O God I wil sing to thee a new song: in <na>(n)</na> the psalter of ten stringes, I wil sing to thee.

notes.label: n
notes.text: In that principal instrument, apt for a new songue, and for extraordinarie benefites.

verses.text: Who geuest saluation to kinges: who hast redemed Dauid thy seruant from the malignant sword:
deliuer me, And rescue me out of the hand of <na>(o)</na> children strangers, whose mouth hath spoken vanitie: and their right hand, is the right hand of iniquitie.

notes.label: o
notes.text: Both Ievves & Christians that liue not vvel, are as strangers that frame to themselues such a false felicite, as is here described : making riches or vvorldlie pleasures their God.

verses.text: Whose sonnes, are as new plantes in their youth. Their daughters comly trimmed: decked about after the similitude of a temple.
Their storehouses ful, flowing out of this into that. Their ewes ful of yong, abunding in their going forth:
their oxen are fatte. There is no ruine of wal, nor <na>[1]</na> passage, nor crie in their streates.

notes.text: transmigration

verses.text: They haue said, that it is a happie people, which hath these things: <na>(p)</na> blessed is the people, whose <na>(q)</na> God is our Lord.

notes.label: p
notes.text: True happines consisteth not in vvorldlie things.

notes.label: q
notes.text: But in preferring God before al.

chapters.summary: The royal Prophet thanketh God, for al his victories, and possession of the kingdom. 3. Admiring Gods benignitie towards man, 5. prayeth to be stil defended from al enimies, 9. promiseth a new songue of prayse, 11. describeth the vanitie of worldlie men, 15. concluding that true felicitie is in seruing God. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
King David praiseth God for his victories.
The 8. key.

verses.text: <na>(a)</na> Praysing, to Dauid himselfe. I Wil exalt thee my God <na>(b)</na> the king: and I wil blesse thy name <na>(c)</na> for euer, and <na>(d)</na> for euer and euer.

notes.label: a
notes.text: By this title, Eldras signifieth that the Holie Ghost, vvho indited al the Psalmes to Gods praise, more specially in these seuen last suggested to Dauid, and by him to al Gods seruants, that al their other seruice must tend, and be directed to the praise of God : and that therin vve must continevv, and finally rest, as in the sabbath of the seuenth day, signified (as S. Beda supposeth) by these seuen last Psalmes of praise, eternally praising our Lord God. For vvhich principal end both Angels and Men, yea and al other creatures vvere made.

notes.label: b
notes.text: King, is the proper epitheton of Christ, the Sonne of God, to vvhom, in his humanitie, God the Father promised the Church of al nations for his kingdom. Psal. 2. in vvhom also the vvhole Blessed Trinitie is praised.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al the time of this vvorld they praise God,

notes.label: d
notes.text: & after in eternitie.

verses.text: Euerie day wil I blesse thee: and wil praise thy name, for euer, and for euer and euer.
Great is our Lord and exceding laudable, and of his greatnes there is no end.
Generation and generation shal praise thy workes: and they shal pronounce thy powre.
They shal speake the magnificence of the glorie of thy holines: and shal tel thy meruelous workes.
And they shal tel the force of thy <na>(e)</na> terrible thinges: and shal declare thy greatnes:

notes.label: e
notes.text: Of vvonderful and miraculous thinges, vvhich strike terrour into mens mindes.

verses.text: They shal vtter the memorie of the abundance of thy swetnes: and in thy iustice they shal reioyce.
Our Lord is pitiful and merciful: patient and very merciful.
Our Lord is sweete to al: and his <na>(f)</na> commiserations are ouer al his workes.

notes.label: f
notes.text: The effectes of Gods mercie in redeming, and recalling sinners, are eminent aboue al other vvorkes.

verses.text: Let al thy workes o Lord confesse to thee: and let thy <na>(g)</na> sainctes blesse thee.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Therfore the sanctified haue special cause to praise God.

verses.text: They shal tel the glorie of thy kingdom: and shal speake thy might.
That they may make thy might knowne to the children of men: and the glorie of the magnificence of thy kingdom.
Thy kingdom is a kingdom <na>(h)</na> of al worldes: and thy dominion in al generation and generation. Our Lord is faithful in al his wordes: and holie in al his workes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Christs kingdom the militant Church is signfical, but much more the triumphant vvhich is eternal.

verses.text: Our Lord <na>(i)</na> lifteth vp al that fal: and setteth vp al that are bruised.

notes.label: i
notes.text: God is readie of his part to lift vp al.

verses.text: The eies of al hope in thee ô Lord: and thou geuest their meate in time conuenient.
Thou openest thy hand: and fillest <na>(k)</na> euerie liuing creature with blessing.

notes.label: k
notes.text: He geueth necessarie thinges to al liuing creatures, euen to brute beastes.

verses.text: Our Lord is iust in al his wayes: and holie in al his workes.
Our Lord is neere to al that inuocate him: to al that inuocate him in truth.
He wil doe the wil of them that feare him, and wil heare their prayer; and saue them.
Our Lord keepeth al that loue him: and he wil destroy al sinners.
My mouth shal speake the prayse of our Lord: and let al flesh blesse his holie name for euer, and for euer and euer.

chapters.summary: God is, and for euer ough̄ to be praised, 3. for his immensiue, infinite, glorious Maiestie, meruelous workes, merciful benefites; for his powre, wisdom, iustice, 19. who wil reward the good, and destroy the wicked. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's Majesty excelleth all things.
The 1. key.

verses.text: Alleluia, <na>(a)</na> of Aggæus, and Zacharie.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The Septuagint added the names of these two Prophetes, for the like reason as they added Ieremie, Psal. 136. because Aggæus and Zacharias prophecying in the reduction of the people from captiuitie, exhorted them, as here the Psalmist doth, to trust in Gods prouidence, and preferre his seruice before vvorldlie cares.

verses.text: MY soule prayse thou our Lord, I wil praise our Lord in my life: I wil sing to my God as long as I shal be. Put not confidence in princes:
in <na>(b)</na> the sonnes of men, in whom there is no saluation.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In one Sonne of Man [Christ] is saluation (saith S. Augustin) and in him, not because he is the sonne of man, but because he is the Sonne of God.

verses.text: His spirit shal goe forth, and he shal returne into <na>(c)</na> his earth: in that day al their cogitations shal perish.

notes.label: c
notes.text: He saith not, that the spirit or soule shal turne into the earth, but the soule shal depart from the bodie, and so euerie one (in whom worldlie men put their trust) shal according to the bodie, returne into his earth.

verses.text: Blessed is he, whose helper is the God of Iacob, his hope in our Lord his God:
who made heauen and earth, the sea, and al thinges, that are in them.
Which keepeth truth for euer, doth iudgement for them that suffer wrong: geueth foode to the hungrie. Our Lord looseth the fettered:
our Lord illuminateth the blind. Our Lord lifteth vp the bruised, our Lord loueth the iust.
Our Lord keepeth strangers, the pupil, and widow he wil receiue: and the wayes of sinners he wil destroy.
Our Lord wil reigne for euer thy God ô Sion, in generation and generation.

chapters.summary: The Psalmist exciteth himself, and al others to praise God for his singular regard, and prouidence of al that trust in him: 3. shewing that neither princes, nor other men are able to helpe, 5. but God can and doth continually releue al sortes of necessities. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Al are exhorted to praise God and trust in his assured prouidence.
The 3. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. PRAYSE ye our Lord because Psalme <na>(a)</na> is good: to our God let there be pleasant, and comelie praise.

notes.label: a
notes.text: It is good to sing Psalmes of praise to God.

verses.text: Our Lord building vp Ierusalem: <na>(b)</na> wil gather together the dispersions of Israel.

notes.label: b
notes.text: A prophecie of the restauration of Ierusalem after the captiuitie.

verses.text: Who <na>(c)</na> healeth the contrite of hart: and bindeth vp their sores.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Remitteth sinnes to the penitent.

verses.text: Who <na>(d)</na> numbereth the multitude of starres: and <na>(e)</na> geueth names to them al.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Besides experience of euerie one, that shal behold the firmament in a clere night, the holie Scripture (Gen. 15. v. 5.) sheweth, that the starres are innumerable to man. For albeit Ptolomæy and other Astronomers numbereth certaine more notorious starres, which serue especially for some knowlege in the science of Astronomie, numbering 349. such in the Zodiach; 316. in the South part therof; and 360. on the North part, which are in al 1025. Yet al acknowlege that no man can come nere to anie probable coniecture of the whole number, nor is able to attaine anie perfect knowlege of their natural influences, and special proprietes. And therfore the Psalmist proposeth here the admirable, and vnsearchable knowlege of God : who both most exactly knoweth the number,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and so perfectly their nature, that his diuine Omniscience geueth to euerie starre a proper name, according to their singular differences and proprieties.

verses.text: Great is our Lord, and great is his strength: and of his <na>(f)</na> wisdom there is no number.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Thinges subiect to Gods knowlege and wisdom are innumerable.

verses.text: Our Lord receiuing the meeke: & humbling sinners euen to the ground.
Sing ye to our Lord in confession: sing ye to our God on harpe.
Who <na>(g)</na> couereth the heauen with cloudes: and prepareth rayne for the earth. Who bringeth forth grasse in the mountaines: and herbe for the seruice of men.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Al these and the like benefites do shew Gods incomparable greatnes, wisdom, and goodnes.

verses.text: Who geueth to beastes their foode: and to <na>(h)</na> the young rauens that cal vpon him.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Both sacred and prophane auctors testifie, that rauens seing their yong ones, either without fethers, or to haue whitish, vnlike to theirs, as suspecting that they are not their owne birdes, but of some other kinde, leaue them destitute of meate; therfore God the auctor of nature, and conseruer of al kindes of creatures, by his special prouidence, feedeth them : either by a certaine dew hanging nere them in the ayre, as Isidorus supposeth; or by litle beastes, or flees, sent by Gods prouidence, which they catching into their mouthes, are nourished and brought vp, as S. Chrysostom teacheth, ser. in Heliam; or by what other meanes soeuer, al agree that yong rauens are neglected by their parents, and are fedde meruelously by Gods ordinance; by which example the Psalmist sheweth, that much more God hath care of men : especially of such men (saith S. Chrysostom.) as honour him with hymnes and praises, whom also he hath called to be his peculiar people, and his owne portion or inheritance.

verses.text: He shal not haue pleasure in the strength of an horse: nor in the legges of a man shal he be wel pleased.
Our Lord is wel pleased toward them that feare him: and in them, that hope vpon his mercie.

chapters.summary: God is also to be praised by his peculiar people, for particular benefites. 4. & for his omnipotent powre, wisdom, goodnes, in creating, and gouerning this whole world, 11. and most special benignitie towards those that trust in him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's excellency in creating and governing the world.
The 2. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. O <na>(a)</na> Ierusalem praise our Lord: praise thy God ô Sion. <na>[1]</na>

notes.label: a
notes.text: Ierusalem in the latter part of Dauids time, al the time of Salomon, and part of other kings reignes til the captiuitie, had peace & prospered. Againe after the captiuitie, the Citie was repared, the Temple reedified, and the whole land receiued and enioyed manie blessinges. But al this was no more then a figure of the excellent benefites here prophecied, and more euidently verified in Christs Catholique Church : partly here militant in the whole world, and especially in the glorious Ierusalem, and Sion, the perfect vision of peace, and contemplation of God, in eternal life.
The Hebrews ioyne this Psalme with the precedent.

verses.text: Because he <na>(b)</na> hath strengthened the lockes of thy gates: he <na>(c)</na> hath blessed thy children in thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: In comparison of other cities, and peoples of the world, the gates of Ierusalem were strongly fensed,

notes.label: c
notes.text: and the citizens blessed : much more the Church of Christ is built vpon a sure rock, her faithful children indued with al spiritual graces ; and most ofal, heauen it selfe is free from al danger of calamitie, and the Sainctes are most secure & most happie, enioying eternal fruition of God.

verses.text: Who <na>(d)</na> hath set thy borders peace: and filleth thee with <na>(e)</na> the fatte of corne.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Hath geuen peace in thy borders,

notes.label: e
notes.text: and the very best corne, and al other fruictes : wine, oyle, milke, honey, and the rest. Allegorically in the Church, reconciliation with God, by remission of sinnes, and peace of conscience, in the Sacraments of Baptisme & Penance ; with the most spiritual food of Christs Bodie and Bloud in the Eucharist, and graces of other Sacraments. In heauen most assured peace and ioy without end.

verses.text: Who sendeth forth <na>(f)</na> his speach to the earth: his word <na>(g)</na> runneth swiftly.

notes.label: f
notes.text: This perteyneth most specially to Euangelical doctrine, preached

notes.label: g
notes.text: and quickely receiued in al the world. Rom 10.v.18.

verses.text: Who geueth <na>(h)</na> snow as wool: scatereth <na>(i)</na> mist as ashes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Snow nourisheth the earth, making it warme by Antiperistasis, as is euident in natural Philosophie,

notes.label: i
notes.text: and noysome ayre is changed into clere weather. In the Church by penance & austere life men are purged from sinnes and vices, euil spirites are also driuen away. If your sinnes shal be as scarlet, they shal be made white as snow, and if they be redde as vermilion, they shal be white as wool. Isaie. 1. v. 18.

verses.text: He casteth <na>(k)</na> his crystal as morseles: before the face of his cold <na>(l)</na> who shal endure?

notes.label: k
notes.text: Yea some that are hardned in sinne, as yse, or chrystal, shal be melted, broken, or made fitte to be ingraffed in Gods Church. So S. Peter was admonished by a vision (Act. 10. v. 13.) to kil and eate.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Otherwise without Gods grace geuing remorse and sorow, no man can ouercome his owne vices.

verses.text: He <na>(m)</na> shal sendforth his word, and shal melt them: <na>(n)</na> his spirit shal blowe, and <na>(o)</na> waters shal flowe.

notes.label: m
notes.text: But Gods word preached,

notes.label: n
notes.text: and his grace touching mens hartes,

notes.label: o
notes.text: innumerable are conuerted.

verses.text: Who declareth his word to <na>(p)</na> Iacob: his iustices, and iudgements to Israel.

notes.label: p
notes.text: The Church only enioyeth these spiritual benefites.

verses.text: He hath <na>(q)</na> not done in like maner to anie nation: and his iudgements he hath not made manifest to them. <na>(r)</na> Allelu-ia.

notes.label: q
notes.text: Considering that al mankind was in the masse of sinne, and that God letteth manie iustly perish, those to whom he geueth his grace to iustification, are specially bond to praise him.

notes.label: r
notes.text: And therfore the Prophet concludeth this Psalme, and the rest folowing, with Alleluia.

chapters.summary: Againe God is to be praised for his goodnes towards his peculiar people, 4. yea towards al the world: 7. but most abundantly towards his Church. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
God's providence especially towards the Church.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. PRAYSE ye our Lord <na>(a)</na> from the heauens: praise ye him in the high places.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Al ye heauenlie spirites praise God for the excellencie of your nature.

verses.text: Prayse ye him al his Angels: prayse ye him <na>(b)</na> al his hostes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: And for your innumerable multitude.

verses.text: Prayse ye him <na>(c)</na> sunne and moone: prayse him al ye starres, and light.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Al creatures, wanting sense or reason, shewforth the Maiestie and excellencie of their Creator.

verses.text: Prayse him ye heauens of heauens: and the waters that are aboue the heauens,
let them praise the name of our Lord. Because he sayd, and they were made: he commanded, and they were created.
He established them for euer, and for euer and euer: he put a precept, and it shal not passe.
Prayse our Lord from the earth: ye dragons, and al depthes.
Fyre, haile, snow, yse, spirit of stormes: which doe his worde:
Mountaines, and al litle hilles: trees that beare fruite, and al ceders.
Beastes, and al cattel: serpentes, and fethered fowles:
<na>(d)</na> Kinges of the earth, and al peoples: princes, and al iudges of the earth.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Againe God is to be praised for the diuersitie of states in men, wherby the whole communitie, is conserued & gouerned.

verses.text: Yongmen, and virgins: old with yong let them prayse the name of our Lord:
because the name of him <na>(e)</na> alone is exalted.

notes.label: e
notes.text: God only, & no false imagined god made & disposed al thinges in order.

verses.text: The confession of him aboue heauen, and earth: and he hath exalted <na>(f)</na> the horne of his people. An hymne to al his <na>(g)</na> sainctes: to the children of Israel, a people <na>(h)</na> approching vnto him. <na>(i)</na> Alleluia.

notes.label: f
notes.text: More especially for that God hath so fortified his Church.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Sanctified children,

notes.label: h
notes.text: that by grace and free wil, which he geueth them, approch vnto him.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Al this considered the Psalmist concleding with Alleluia, inuiteth al to praise our Lord.

chapters.summary: Al creatures spiritual and corporal, are inuited to praise God, their Creator and Conseruer, 13. as incomparably excellent. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
Our Creator to be praised by all creatures.
The 2. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. SING ye to our Lord a new song: let his praise be in <na>(a)</na> the Church of sainctes.

notes.label: a
notes.text: God our Lord whom al creatures are bond to praise, only accepteth those mens praises, that liue in his holie Church.

verses.text: Let Israel be ioyful in him, that made him: and let the children of Sion reioyce in their king.
Let them praise his name in quire: on tymbrel, and psalter let them sing to him:
Because our Lord is wel pleased in his people: and he wil exalt the meeke vnto saluation.
The sainctes shal reioyce in glorie: they shal be ioyful in <na>(b)</na> their beddes.

notes.label: b
notes.text: eternal rest.

verses.text: The <na>(c)</na> exaltations of God in their throte: and <na>(d)</na> two edged swordes in their handes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Hieghest praises of God shal be continually vttered by Sainctes in glorie : for stil as praises passe by their tongues and mouthes, more like praises shal succede from their throte, and hartie affection, so out of the abundance of the hart their mouth shal stil speake Gods praise.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Glorified Sainctes shal also haue iudiciarie povvre. First, al in general shal like and approue Gods iustice in punishing the vvicked. Secondly the vvicked shal be iustly condemned in comparison of the blessed, vvho passed through, and ouercame the like, yea and greater tribulations and tentations then those, by vvhich the damned vvere ouercome. Thirdly, certaine more excellent Sainctes, namely the Apostles. and al those that forsaking proprietie of temporal goodes, geue that they haue to the poore, as some religious Orders doe ; or into a Communitie as the Apostles, and manie primitiue Christians did (Mat. 4. v. 20. cap. 19. v. 27. Act. 4. v. 34. 1. Cor. 6. v. 3.) shal sitte in iudgement seates, assessorie iudges with Christ, and iudge those that render account, of wel or euil spending the temporal landes or goodes, which they possessed in this vvorld. So teach S. Augustin S. Ierom. S. Beda, and others.

verses.text: To doe reuenge in the nations: chastisements among the peoples.
To binde their kinges in fetters: and their nobles in yron manicles.
That they may doe in them the iudgement that is <na>(e)</na> written: <na>(f)</na> this glorie is to al his sainctes. Alleluia.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Decreed by God.

notes.label: f
notes.text: This iudicial povvre is part of Sainctes glorie.

chapters.summary: The Church is most singularly bond to praise God, 4. for the grace, sanctitie, victorie, glorie, 7. and iudicial powre, which he geueth to his Sainctes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text:
The Church must euer praise God.
The 6. key.

verses.text: Alleluia. PRAYSE ye our Lord <na>(a)</na> in his holies: prayse ye him in <na>(b)</na> the firmament of his strength.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Al ye Angels and men that are in the holie and highest heauen praise our Lord.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Al ye creatures that are in, and vnder the first moueable firmament praise our Lord.

verses.text: Prayse ye him in <na>(c)</na> his powers: prayse ye him <na>(d)</na> according to the multitude of his greatnes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: And you especially (Gods peculiar people) amongst whom, and for whom, diuine miracles haue bene wrought praise our Lord,

notes.label: d
notes.text: with al your possible endeuoure, for though his infinite Excellencie exeedeth the powre of al creatures to praise him sufficiently, yet it resteth that you may infinitly extend your wil and desire to praise our Lord, according to the multitude of his greatnes.

verses.text: <na>(e)</na> Prayse ye him <na>(f)</na> in the sound of trumpet: prayse ye him on psalter, and harpe.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Out of this your great and infinite desire, let your tongues sound and sing diuine praises, as wel vvith voice, as musical instruments.

notes.label: f
notes.text: VVherof six most vsual in the Tabernacle and Temple vvere these : Trumpet, Psalter, Harpe, Timbrel, Organ and Cymbal.

verses.text: Prayse ye him on timbrel and <na>(g)</na> quire: prayse ye him on <na>(h)</na> stringes, and organ.

notes.label: g
notes.text: By the vvay the Psalmist interposeth agane tvvo especial thinges, vvhich make perfect harmonie, vvithout vvhich no instrument is gratful to God : Vnitie amongst his seruants, signified by the Quire of consonant voices :

notes.label: h
notes.text: and mortification of passions, signified by Stringes, vvhich are made of dead beastes bovvels.

verses.text: Prayse ye him on wel sounding cymbals: prayse ye him on cymbales of iubilation:
let every <na>(i)</na> spirit praise our Lord. Alleluia.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Man created of corruptible bodie and immortal soule, is finally admonished to praise our Lord, ouer and aboue the praises of al other corporal creatures ; vvho also is more especially bond therto then Angels, because God hath voutsaffed to make himselfe Man, to redeme man that vvas lost by sinne, and to endew him vvith nevv grace, and so bring him to euerlasting glorie, vvhere vvith holie Angels, men also for euer & euer shal praise our Lord, vvith hart, voice, and iubilation of spirite, singing as the Psalmist concludeth, Alleluia.

chapters.summary: God absolutly most excellent is to be praised, 3. with al sortes of instruments, and by al other meanes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: God most excellent and most laudable. The first key.

endMatters.title: S. Augustin in the conclusion of his Enarrations upon the Psalms.
endMatters.text: S. Augustin in the conclusion of his Enarrations or Sermons upon the Psalms, explicateth a mystery in the number of an hundred and fifty, signifying the concord of the two Testaments. For in the old testament they kept the Sabbath, which is the seventh day: in ◦ the new we keep our Lord's day, after the sabbath, that is, the eighth: which seven and eight (making fifteen) multiplied by ten, signifying the Law of ten commandments, rise unto 150. Again, seven multiplied by seven make 49. whereto one (to wit the eight) being added make fifty, which multiplied by three , signifying the B. Trinity, make 150. Neither [1] seemed it without cause to this great Doctor, that the first fifty end with a Psalm of Penance, craving mercy & remission of sins: the second with Mercy & Justice, which God joineth in the Redemption, Justification, and Salvation of men: the last with Divine Praises, signifying, that by condemning sins in ourselves, through God's mercy we may be justified, and so begin in this life, which is to be perfected in the next, to praise our Lord, as S. Paul admonisheth with Psalms, Hymns, and Spiritual Songs. Concluding with the two verses, appointed by S. Damasus Pope, to be added in the end of all Psalms, and is observed ever since his time by tradition in the whole Church. [2] Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost: As it was in the beginning, and now, and ever, into worlds of worlds. (in eternity without end.) Amen. ◦

notes.text: The number of Psalms signifieth the agreement of the old and new Testament.
Three fifties signify Penance. Mercy with justice, and Praises of God.
Colloss. 3. Circa An. Do 380.
Gloria Patri added by tradition.

intros.title: Concerning interpretation of holy Scriptures.
intros.text: As Prophecy (or other holy Scripture) was not at any time by man's will, but the (Prophets) holy men of God spake , inspired by the Holy Ghost: so no prophecy (nor explication) of Scripture, is ◦ made by private interpretation. 2. Pet. 1. but by the same Spirit wherewith it was written, which our Saviour gave to the Church, to abide for ever, the Spirit of truth, to teach all truth. Ioan. 14. 16. Neither pertaineth it to every one, to discern the true spirit, but to some. 1. Cor. 12. Holy Scriptures consist not in reading, but in understanding. S. Jerome Dialogo advers. Luciferianos. The words of holy Scripture are so to be understood , as holy men, the Saints of God, have [1] understood them , S. Aug. Ser. 18. de verb. Domini. Men must learn of men, not expect [2] knowledge immediately of God, nor only by Angels. Idem, in Prologo Doct. Christ. There be some things, mentioned in holy Scripture , which God will have hidden, and those are ◦ not to be curiously searched. S. Amb. li. 1. c. 7. de vocat. Gentium. By those things, which to us are hidden in holy Scripture, our humility is proved . S. Greg. ho. 17. ◦ super Ezech.

notes.text: Scriptures are to be expounded by the common spirit of the Church, not by private men.
They consist in understanding.
Holy Fathers do best expound them.
Some Mysteries are hidden.
They prove our humility.

intros.title: PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS UPON THE BOOK OF PSALMS.
intros.text: The authority of this Book was ever authentical, and certain, as the assured word of God, and Canonical Scripture . But concerning the Author, there be diverse opinions. For although it be [1] manifest by the testimony of Philo and Josephus, that in their time, and always before, only King David was by all Hebrew Doctors holden for Author of all the Psalms; yet after that learned [2] Origen, and other Christian Doctors, expounded many Psalms of Christ, the Jews being pressed therewith, began to deny that all were David's: alleging for their new opinion the title of diverse Psalms, and some other difficulties, ministering occasion of much needless dispute, still acknowledging the whole book to be Canonical. Whereupon S. Jerome and S. Augustine , [3] sometimes admitted those as Authors of certain Psalms, whose names are in the title thereof. S. Cyprian, S. Cyril, S. Athanasius, and others agree in general, that David writ not all: but differ much in particular, touching other supposed authors. In so much that Melchisedech, Moyses, Asaph, Eman, Idithun, The sons of Core, Salomon, Jeremie, Ezechiel, Aggaeus, and Zacharias, are all (with more or less probability) reputed Authors of several Psalms. Nevertheless it seemeth that S. [4] Jerome rather related other men's judgement, than shewed his own; as we shall note by and by. And S. Augustine (l. 17. c. 14. de civit.) maturely discussing this doubt, saith plainly, that their Judgement seemed to him more credible, who attribute all the hundred fifty Psalms to David alone. Further explicating that whereas some Psalms have David's own name in their titles, some [5] have other men's names, some none at all, this diversity importeth not diverse Authors, but signifieth other things, either pertaining to the same persons, or by interpretation of their names, belonging to the present matter, as our Lord inspired him. Likewise S. Chrysostome resolutely judgeth, that only King David was Author of this whole Book. Moved especially by this argument, for that Christ and the Apostles alleging the Psalms, do oftentimes name David as Author, and never any other . [6] Also Origen, S. Basil, Saint Ambrose, S. Hilary, Theodoretus, Cassiodorus, Beda, Eutimius, and most part of ancient and late writers, with the most common voice of Christians , call this book [7] the Psalms of David: and the General Councels of Carthage, Florence, and Trent, in the Catalogue of Canonical Scriptures recite this book by the name of David's Psalter. Moreover it is clear, Act. 2. that the second Psalm, though it want his name, is David's. And other Scriptures , 2. Paral. v. 6. and 1. Esd. 3. v. 10. say plainly, that David made the Psalms, 104. 105. [8] 106. 117. 135. beginning: Confess to our Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is for ever. Which he appointed the Levites to sing, or play on instruments, 1. Paral. 15. & 16. and yet they have not his name in their title. Again, 2. Reg. 23. David is only entitled the egregious, or excellent Psalmist of Israel. Neither were Asaph, Eman, and Idithun any where called Prophets (as are all the writers of holy Scriptures) but only masters of music, 1. Paral. 25. And the sons of Core were only porters, 1. Paral. 26. Finally, S. Jerome (whose judgement the whole Church singularly esteemeth in all questions belonging to holy Scriptures (seemeth as much inclined, that only the Royal Prophet David was Author of this whole book, as to the contrary .
